These ratings, which are determined in accordance with [REF:standard:astme413] roughly describe the noise reduction provided by the separating floor or wall, or in the case of the ASTC rating, by the system of separating and adjoining walls and floors.

Support services rendered by or through care facility management refer to services provided by the organization that is responsible for the care for a period exceeding 24 consecutive hours. They do not refer to services provided by residents of dwelling units or suites, or to services arranged directly by residents of dwelling units or suites with outside agencies.

In the context of care occupancies, these services may include a daily assessment of the resident's functioning, awareness of their whereabouts, the making of appointments for residents and reminding them of those appointments, the ability and readiness to intervene if a crisis arises for a resident, supervision in areas of nutrition or medication, and provision of transient medical services. Services may also include activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, feeding, and assistance in the use of washroom facilities, etc. No actual treatment is provided by or through care facility management.

In previous editions of the British Columbia Building Code, the terminology used to identify dangerous goods came from "Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (TDGR)." The TDGR apply solely to the adequate identification of hazards related to dangerous goods in the contexts of transportation and emergency response.

Dangerous goods in the workplace are identified in accordance with the "Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS)," established in accordance with the "Hazardous Products Act." The WHMIS identification system is specifically designed with the users of the product in mind.

This edition of the British Columbia Building Code identifies dangerous goods as products regulated by the TDGR or classified under the WHMIS. In order to harmonize these two nomenclatures for dangerous goods, class descriptors were developed taking into consideration both the TDGR and WHMIS classification systems. The NBC nomenclature uses a descriptive approach to classifying dangerous goods, which is similar to the one used by the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS) developed by the United Nations (UN). Canada has actively participated in the development of the GHS and has committed to its implementation through the TDGR and WHMIS regulations.

The British Columbia Building Code nomenclature takes a common sense approach that corresponds more closely to how people refer to dangerous goods on a daily basis, blending TDGR and WHMIS terminology without using nondescript numbers and letters as previously found in the British Columbia Building Code, TDGR and WHMIS.

content.content: Exits include doors or doorways leading directly into an exit stair or directly to the outside. In the case of an exit leading to a separate building, exits also include vestibules, walkways, bridges or balconies.

Farm buildings as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect1.art2:long] include, but are not limited to, produce storage and packing facilities, livestock and poultry housing, milking centres, manure storage facilities, grain bins, silos, feed preparation centres, farm workshops, greenhouses, farm retail centres, and horse riding, exercise and training facilities. Farm buildings may be classified as low or high human occupancy, depending on the occupant load.

Examples of farm buildings that may be classified as low human occupancy are livestock and poultry housing, manure and machinery storage facilities and horse exercise and training facilities where no bleachers or viewing area are provided.

Examples of farm buildings that may be classified as other than low human occupancy include farm retail centres for feeds, horticultural and livestock produce, auction barns and show areas where bleachers or other public facilities are provided. Farm work centres where the number of workers frequently exceeds the limit for low human occupancy will also be in this category.

It is possible to have areas of both high and low human occupancy in the same building provided that the structural safety and fire separation requirements for high human occupancy are met in the part thus designated.

It is generally understood that the term “fire” refers to all products of combustion, including heat and smoke. Although a fire separation is not always required to have a fire-resistance rating, it should act as a barrier to the spread of smoke and fire until some type of response is initiated. If the fire-resistance rating of a fire separation is permitted to be waived on the basis of the presence of an automatic sprinkler system, it is nonetheless the intent of the Code that the fire separation be constructed so that it will remain in place and act as a barrier against the spread of smoke until the sprinklers have actuated.

Localized depressions that need not be considered in the determination of the elevation of grade include such features as vehicle and pedestrian entrances and other minor depressions that do not affect accessibility for firefighting or evacuation.

The definition of this term is intended to include all types of appliances and venting systems that rely entirely on fans to evacuate the products of combustion. Systems variously referred to as “forced draft,” “power vented” and “induced draft” in standards and industry terminology may be covered by this definition. The key characteristic of such systems is that they are more resistant to depressurization-induced spillage of combustion products into the building in which they are housed because the combustion venting system downstream of the fan is “sealed,” i.e. includes no draft hood or draft control device.

There may be circumstances where the authority having jurisdiction would choose to exempt certain types of buildings or parts thereof from being designated as post-disaster buildings. Such is the case in the following examples: a volunteer paramedic's residence where an ambulance is stored, or a police station in a shopping mall or in a residential complex.

Some municipalities have emergency management plans that specify which buildings are to be used for the provision of essential services after a disaster. Municipalities normally coordinate their requirements with provincial or territorial emergency management protocols, which may or may not be mandatory. If in doubt about whether a building should be designated as a post-disaster building, designers should consult with the authority having jurisdiction.

The inclusion of control centres for natural gas distribution as examples of post-disaster buildings is intended to ensure that, following a disaster, control is maintained over large fuel distribution networks that supply a commodity essential to the health and safety of a significant proportion of the Canadian population. In contrast, the localized failure of a single fuel supply point does not jeopardize the entire fuel distribution system.
Buildings with rooftop telecommunication or cellular network equipment need not be designated as post-disaster buildings.
A covered mall is considered to be a public corridor and, as such, is subject to the same requirements as a public corridor.
In the field, rim joists may also be referred to as rim boards, headers or header joists.

A secondary suite is a self-contained dwelling unit that is part of a house containing not more than two dwelling units (including the secondary suite) and any common spaces such as common storage, common service rooms, common laundry facilities or common areas used for egress. Secondary suites are typically created within an existing single dwelling unit—commonly called a "house"—either constructed as an addition or an alteration to an existing house or incorporated during the construction of a new house. A secondary suite may have more than one storey and may be on the same level as the other dwelling unit of the house or be above or below it.

Examples of buildings where secondary suites are permitted include individual detached houses, or where the secondary suite is located in a portion of a building, semi-detached houses (half of a double and also known as a side-by-side) and row houses where a vertical fire separation separates the portion from the remainder of the building.

Where a building has multiple vertically separated occupancies, the secondary suite can only be created in a vertically separated portion of the building that is of residential occupancy. A vertical fire separation extends continuously through all crawlspaces, storeys and attic spaces of the building. Apartment buildings have dwelling units above and below others that share a horizontal assembly and are therefore not permitted to have secondary suites. Figure A-1.4.1.2.(1)-C shows building types where secondary suites are permitted as well as building types where other dwelling units or other occupancies are located above or below such that secondary suites are not permitted.

content.content: Neither the secondary suite nor the other dwelling unit in a house can be strata-titled or otherwise subdivided from the remainder of the house under provincial or territorial legislation. This means that both dwelling units are registered under the same title.

Typical examples of service rooms include boiler rooms, furnace rooms, incinerator rooms, garbage handling rooms and rooms to accommodate air-conditioning or heating appliances, pumps, compressors and electrical equipment. Rooms such as elevator machine rooms and common laundry rooms are not considered to be service rooms.

The net solid area of a masonry unit is calculated by determining the gross area of the bed face of the unit ( L × T ) and subtracting the cumulative areas of the hollow portions. As long as the total area of the hollow portions is 25% or less of the gross area, the unit is considered to be a solid masonry unit.

content.content: Entrances at which vehicles stop for a short time beneath an unenclosed canopy to pick up and drop off passengers are not considered as storage garages. As a subsidiary use, storage garages may also contain space for parking or storing other vehicles (bicycles, boat, etc.).

Tenancy in the context of the term “suite” applies to both rental and ownership tenure. In a condominium arrangement, for example, dwelling units are considered separate suites even though they are individually owned. In order to be of complementary use, a series of rooms that constitute a suite must be in reasonably close proximity to each other and have access to each other either directly by means of a common doorway or indirectly by a corridor, vestibule or other similar arrangement.

The term “suite” does not apply to rooms such as service rooms, common laundry rooms and common recreational rooms that are not leased or under a separate tenure in the context of the Code. Similarly, the term “suite” is not normally applied in the context of buildings such as schools and hospitals, since the entire building is under a single tenure. However, a room that is individually rented is considered a suite. A warehousing unit in a mini-warehouse is a suite. A rented room in a nursing home could be considered as a suite if the room was under a separate tenure. A hospital bedroom on the other hand is not considered to be under a separate tenure, since the patient has little control of that space, even though he pays the hospital a per diem rate for the privilege of using the hospital facilities, which include the sleeping areas.

For certain requirements in the Code, the expression “room or suite” is used (e.g., travel distance). This means that the requirement applies within the rooms of suites as well as to the suite itself and to rooms that may be located outside the suite. In other places the expression “suite, and rooms not located within a suite” is used (e.g., for the installation of smoke and heat detectors). This means that the requirement applies to individual suites as defined, but not to each room within the suite. The rooms “not within a suite” would include common laundry rooms, common recreational rooms and service rooms, which are not considered as tenant-occupied space.

The definition of tapered tread includes treads in curved stairs and treads in winder stairs, However, requirements for winders differ from those for other tapered treads. Requirements for tapered treads are found in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art16] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect6.art9] , and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art3] of Division B. Requirements for winders are found in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect8.subsect4.art6] of Division B.

The ability to evacuate unassisted implies that a person is capable of recognizing and responding to an emergency given their physical, cognitive and behavioural abilities, and able to move to a safe location without the assistance of another person. For example, such persons must be able to arise and walk, or transfer from a bed or chair to a means of mobility, and leave the building or move to a safe location on their own.

“Treatments” may include such things as surgery, intensive care, and emergency medical intervention. Treatment services differ from the services provided by care occupancies like personal care assistance or the administration of medication, and from those provided by business and personal services occupancies like dentistry or day procedures.

It is important to understand the difference between the functions of a vapour barrier and an air barrier. Vapour barrier materials and assemblies are intended to restrict the movement of water vapour due to vapour pressure differentials, while air barrier materials and assemblies are intended to restrict the movement of air due to air pressure differentials.
Note that a vapour barrier is also referred to as a “vapour diffusion retarder.”

Documents referenced in the British Columbia Building Code may contain provisions covering a wide range of issues, including issues that are unrelated to the objectives and functional statements stated in Parts 2 and 3 of Division A respectively; e.g. aesthetic issues such as colour-fastness or uniformity. [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] is intended to make it clear that, whereas referencing a document in the Code generally has the effect of making the provisions of that document part of the Code, provisions that are unrelated to buildings or to the objectives and functional statements attributed to the provisions in Division B where the document is referenced are excluded.

Furthermore, many documents referenced in the Code contain references to other documents, which may also, in turn, refer to other documents. These secondary and tertiary referenced documents may contain provisions that are unrelated to buildings or to the objectives and functional statements of the Code: such provisions—no matter how far down the chain of references they occur—are not included in the intent of [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] .

content.text: The objectives of this Code are as follows (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.appendix.appnote2:short] ):

objectives.title: Safety
objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design, construction or demolition of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in or adjacent to the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of injury.

sub_objectives.title: Fire Safety
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in or adjacent to the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of injury due to fire. The risks of injury due to fire addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OS1.1– fire or explosion occurring 
 OS1.2– fire or explosion impacting areas beyond its point of origin 
 OS1.3– collapse of physical elements due to a fire or explosion 
 OS1.4– fire safety systems failing to function as expected 
 OS1.5– persons being delayed in or impeded from moving to a safe place during a fire emergency

sub_objectives.title: Structural Safety
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in or adjacent to the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of injury due to structural failure. The risks of injury due to structural failure addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OS2.1– loads bearing on the [REF:term:bldng:building] elements that exceed their [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] capacity 
 OS2.2– loads bearing on the [REF:term:bldng:building] that exceed the [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] properties of the supporting medium 
 OS2.3– damage to or deterioration of [REF:term:bldng:building] elements 
 OS2.4– vibration or deflection of [REF:term:bldng:building] elements 
 OS2.5– instability of the [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof 
 OS2.6– collapse of the [REF:term:xcvtn:excavation]

sub_objectives.title: Safety in Use
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in or adjacent to the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of injury due to hazards. The risks of injury due to hazards addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OS3.1– tripping, slipping, falling, contact, drowning or collision 
 OS3.2– contact with hot surfaces or substances 
 OS3.3– contact with energized equipment 
 OS3.4– exposure to hazardous substances 
 OS3.5– exposure to high levels of sound from fire alarm systems 
 OS3.6– persons becoming trapped in confined spaces 
 OS3.7– persons being delayed in or impeded from moving to a safe place during an emergency (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.appendix.appnote2:short] )

sub_objectives.title: Resistance to Unwanted Entry
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of injury due to the [REF:term:bldng:building's] low level of resistance to unwanted entry (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent2:long] for application limitation). The risks of injury due to unwanted entry addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OS4.1– intruders being able to force their way through locked doors or windows 
 OS4.2– occupants being unable to identify potential intruders as such

sub_objectives.title: Safety at Construction and Demolition Sites
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the construction or demolition of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , the public adjacent to a construction or demolition site will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of injury due to hazards. The risks of injury due to construction and demolition hazards addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OS5.1– objects projected onto [REF:term:pblc-w:public ways]
 OS5.2– vehicular accidents on [REF:term:pblc-w:public ways]
 OS5.3– damage to or obstruction of [REF:term:pblc-w:public ways]
 OS5.4– water accumulated in [REF:term:xcvtn:excavations]
 OS5.5– entry into the site 
 OS5.6– exposure to hazardous substances and activities 
 OS5.7– loads bearing on a covered way that exceed its [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] capacity 
 OS5.8– collapse of the [REF:term:xcvtn:excavation]
 OS5.9– persons being delayed in or impeded from moving to a safe place during an emergency (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.appendix.appnote2:short] )

objectives.title: Health
objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of illness.

sub_objectives.title: Indoor Conditions
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of illness due to indoor conditions. The risks of illness due to indoor conditions addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OH1.1– inadequate indoor air quality 
 OH1.2– inadequate thermal comfort 
 OH1.3– contact with moisture

sub_objectives.title: Sanitation
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of illness due to unsanitary conditions. The risks of illness due to unsanitary conditions addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OH2.1– exposure to human or domestic waste 
 OH2.2– consumption of contaminated water 
 OH2.3– inadequate facilities for personal hygiene 
 OH2.4– contact with contaminated surfaces 
 OH2.5– contact with vermin and insects

sub_objectives.title: Noise Protection
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of illness due to high levels of sound originating in adjacent spaces in the [REF:term:bldng:building] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent3:long] for application limitation). The risks of illness due to high levels of sound addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OH3.1– exposure to airborne sound transmitted through assemblies separating [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] from adjacent spaces in the [REF:term:bldng:building]

sub_objectives.title: Vibration and Deflection Limitation
sub_objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , a person in the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of illness due to high levels of vibration or deflection of [REF:term:bldng:building] elements.

sub_objectives.title: Hazardous Substances Containment
sub_objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , the public will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of illness due to the release of hazardous substances from the [REF:term:bldng:building] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent4:long] for application limitation).

objectives.title: Accessibility
objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , [REF:term:bc-prsn-wth-dsblts:persons with disabilities] will be unacceptably impeded from accessing or using the [REF:term:bldng:building] or its facilities (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent5:long] for application limitations).

sub_objectives.title: Accessible Path of Travel
sub_objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , [REF:term:bc-prsn-wth-dsblts:persons with disabilities] will be unacceptably impeded from accessing the [REF:term:bldng:building] or circulating within it (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent5:long] for application limitations).

sub_objectives.title: Accessible Facilities
sub_objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , [REF:term:bc-prsn-wth-dsblts:persons with disabilities] will be unacceptably impeded from using the [REF:term:bldng:building's] facilities (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part2.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent5:long] for application limitations).

objectives.title: Fire and Structural Protection of Buildings
objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design, construction or demolition of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , the [REF:term:bldng:building] or adjacent [REF:term:bldng:buildings] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of damage due to fire or structural insufficiency, or the [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of loss of use also due to structural insufficiency.

sub_objectives.title: Fire Protection of the Building
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of its design or construction, the [REF:term:bldng:building] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of damage due to fire. The risks of damage due to fire addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OP1.1– fire or explosion occurring 
 OP1.2– fire or explosion impacting areas beyond its point of origin 
 OP1.3– collapse of physical elements due to a fire or explosion 
 OP1.4– fire safety systems failing to function as expected

sub_objectives.title: Structural Sufficiency of the Building
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of its design or construction, the [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of damage or loss of use due to structural failure or lack of structural serviceability. The risks of damage and of loss of use due to structural failure or lack of structural serviceability addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OP2.1– loads bearing on the [REF:term:bldng:building] elements that exceed their [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] capacity 
 OP2.2– loads bearing on the [REF:term:bldng:building] that exceed the [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] properties of the supporting medium 
 OP2.3– damage to or deterioration of [REF:term:bldng:building] elements 
 OP2.4– vibration or deflection of [REF:term:bldng:building] elements 
 OP2.5– instability of the [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof 
 OP2.6– instability or movement of the supporting medium

sub_objectives.title: Protection of Adjacent Buildings from Fire
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design or construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , adjacent [REF:term:bldng:buildings] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of damage due to fire. The risks of damage to adjacent [REF:term:bldng:buildings] due to fire addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OP3.1– fire or explosion impacting areas beyond the [REF:term:bldng:building] of origin

sub_objectives.title: Protection of Adjacent Buildings from Structural Damage
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design, construction or demolition of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , adjacent [REF:term:bldng:buildings] will be exposed to an unacceptable risk of structural damage. The risks of structural damage to adjacent [REF:term:bldng:buildings] addressed in this Code are those caused by— 
 OP4.1– settlement of the medium supporting adjacent [REF:term:bldng:buildings]
 OP4.2– collapse of the [REF:term:bldng:building] or portion thereof onto adjacent [REF:term:bldng:buildings]
 OP4.3– impact of the [REF:term:bldng:building] on adjacent [REF:term:bldng:buildings]
 OP4.4– collapse of the [REF:term:xcvtn:excavation]

objectives.title: Environment
objectives.definition: An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design, construction or renovation of the [REF:term:bldng:building] or of the [REF:term:plmbng-t:plumbing system] , the environment will be affected in an unacceptable manner.

sub_objectives.title: Energy Efficiency and Water Use
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of the design, construction or renovation of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , the use of energy will be inefficient or the use of water will be excessive. The risks of inefficient energy use or excessive water use addressed in this Code are those caused by – 
 OE1.1– inefficient energy performance of [REF:term:bldng:buildings] or [REF:term:bldng:building] components

sub_objectives.title: Greenhouse Gases
sub_objectives.definition:
An objective of this Code is to limit the probability that, as a result of design and construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , including the [REF:term:bldng:building's] systems, and the energy consumed in the operation of those systems, the production of greenhouse gases will be excessive. The risks of excessive greenhouse gas emissions addressed in this Code are those caused by- 
 OE2.1– excessive emissions as a result of the design and construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , including the [REF:term:bldng:building’s] systems, and the energy consumed in the operation of those systems

content.content: Objective OE, Environment (including its sub-objectives), is attributed to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long] , which address energy efficiency for small residential buildings and certain small non-residential and mixed-use buildings (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect1.art3:long] ). The objectives, functional statements and energy efficiency requirements for larger Part 9 residential buildings as well as for non-residential buildings whose combined total floor area exceeds 300 m^{2} and some mixed-use buildings are addressed in the National Energy Code for Buildings.

Any gaps in the numbering sequence of the objectives are due to the fact that there is a master list of objectives covering the principal Code Documents-the British Columbia Building Code Book I: General, British Columbia Building Code Book II: Plumbing Systems, and the British Columbia Fire Code-but not all objectives are pertinent to all Codes.
Where the term "the building" is used in the wording of the objectives, it refers to the building for which compliance with the British Columbia Building Code is being assessed.

The term "emergency"-in the context of safety in buildings-is often equated to the term "fire emergency;" however, the wording of objectives OS3.7 and OS5.9 makes it clear that the Code addresses any type of emergency that would require the rapid evacuation of the building, such as a bomb threat or the presence of intruders.

In the definition of Objective OS1, Fire Safety, the term “person” refers to any individual in or adjacent to the building, including the occupants, the public, and emergency responders including firefighters when performing their duties.
Certain technical requirements in the BC Codes are intended to address the safety of emergency responders, including firefighters, when performing their duties.

content.text:
The objectives of this Code are achieved by measures, such as those described in the acceptable solutions in Division B, that are intended to allow the [REF:term:bldng:building] or its elements to perform the following functions (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part3.appendix.appnote1:short] ):
<bold>F01</bold>        To minimize the risk of accidental ignition.
<bold>F02</bold>        To limit the severity and effects of fire or explosions.
<bold>F03</bold>        To retard the effects of fire on areas beyond its point of origin.
<bold>F04</bold>        To retard failure or collapse due to the effects of fire.
<bold>F05</bold>        To retard the effects of fire on emergency egress facilities.
<bold>F06</bold>        To retard the effects of fire on facilities for notification, suppression and emergency response.
<bold>F10</bold>        To facilitate the timely movement of persons to a safe place in an emergency.
<bold>F11</bold>        To notify persons, in a timely manner, of the need to take action in an emergency.
<bold>F12</bold>        To facilitate emergency response.
<bold>F13</bold>        To notify emergency responders, in a timely manner, of the need to take action in an emergency.
<bold>F20</bold>        To support and withstand expected loads and forces.
<bold>F21</bold>        To limit or accommodate dimensional change.
<bold>F22</bold>        To limit movement under expected loads and forces.
<bold>F23</bold>        To maintain equipment in place during structural movement.
<bold>F30</bold>        To minimize the risk of injury to persons as a result of tripping, slipping, falling, contact, drowning or collision.
<bold>F31</bold>        To minimize the risk of injury to persons as a result of contact with hot surfaces or substances.
<bold>F32</bold>        To minimize the risk of injury to persons as a result of contact with energized equipment.
<bold>F33</bold>        To limit the level of sound of a fire alarm system.
<bold>F34</bold>        To resist or discourage unwanted access or entry.
<bold>F35</bold>        To facilitate the identification of potential intruders.
<bold>F36</bold>        To minimize the risk that persons will be trapped in confined spaces.
<bold>F40</bold>        To limit the level of contaminants.
<bold>F41</bold>        To minimize the risk of generation of contaminants.
<bold>F42</bold>        To resist the entry of vermin and insects.
<bold>F43</bold>        To minimize the risk of release of hazardous substances.
<bold>F44</bold>        To limit the spread of hazardous substances beyond their point of release.
<bold>F46</bold>        To minimize the risk of contamination of potable water.
<bold>F50</bold>        To provide air suitable for breathing.
<bold>F51</bold>        To maintain appropriate air and surface temperatures.
<bold>F52</bold>        To maintain appropriate relative humidity.
<bold>F53</bold>        To maintain appropriate indoor/outdoor air pressure differences.
<bold>F54</bold>        To limit drafts.
<bold>F55</bold>        To resist the transfer of air through environmental separators.
<bold>F56</bold>        To limit the transmission of airborne sound into a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit ] from spaces elsewhere in the [REF:term:bldng:building] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part3.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent2:long:Sentence 3.1.1.2.(2)] for application limitation).
<bold>F60</bold>        To control the accumulation and pressure of water on and in the ground.
<bold>F61</bold>        To resist the ingress of precipitation, water or moisture from the exterior or from the ground.
<bold>F62</bold>        To facilitate the dissipation of water and moisture from the [REF:term:bldng:building] .
<bold>F63</bold>        To limit moisture condensation.
<bold>F70</bold>        To provide potable water.
<bold>F71</bold>        To provide facilities for personal hygiene.
<bold>F72</bold>        To provide facilities for the sanitary disposal of human and domestic wastes.
<bold>F73</bold>        To facilitate [REF:term:bc-cc-t-ccbl:access] to and circulation in the [REF:term:bldng:building] and its facilities by [REF:term:bc-prsn-wth-dsblts:persons with disabilities] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part3.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent3:long:Sentence 3.1.1.2.(3)] for application limitation).
<bold>F74</bold>        To facilitate the use of the [REF:term:bldng:building's] facilities by [REF:term:bc-prsn-wth-dsblts:persons with disabilities] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part3.sect1.subsect1.art2.sent3:long:Sentence 3.1.1.2.(3)] for application limitation).
<bold>F75</bold>      To minimize obstacles for future modification to provide [REF:term:bc-cc-t-ccbl:access] .
<bold>F80</bold>        To resist deterioration resulting from expected service conditions.
<bold>F81</bold>        To minimize the risk of malfunction, interference, damage, tampering, lack of use or misuse.
<bold>F82</bold>        To minimize the risk of inadequate performance due to improper maintenance or lack of maintenance.
<bold>F90</bold>        To limit the amount of uncontrolled air leakage through the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope.
<bold>F91</bold>        To limit the amount of uncontrolled air leakage through system components.
<bold>F92</bold>        To limit the amount of uncontrolled thermal transfer through the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope.
<bold>F93</bold>        To limit the amount of uncontrolled thermal transfer through system components.
<bold>F95</bold>        To limit the unnecessary demand and/or consumption of energy for heating and cooling.
<bold>F96</bold>        To limit the unnecessary demand and/or consumption of energy for service water heating.
<bold>F98</bold>        To limit the inefficiency of equipment.
<bold>F99</bold>        To limit the inefficiency of systems.
<bold>F100</bold>      To limit the unnecessary rejection of reusable waste energy.
<bold>F101</bold>    To limit excessive emission of greenhouse gases into the environment.

content.content: The numbered functional statements are grouped according to functions that deal with closely related subjects. For example, the first group deals with fire risks, the second group deals with emergency egress and response, etc. There may be gaps in the numbering sequence for the following reasons:[LIST:bulleted]

items.content: Each group has unused numbers which allows for the possible future creation of additional functional statements within any one group.

There is a master list of functional statements covering the principal Code Documents---the British Columbia Building Code Book I: General, British Columbia Building Code Book II: Plumbing Systems, and the British Columbia Fire Code---but not all functional statements are pertinent to all Codes.

appendix.introduction: These Notes are included for explanatory purposes only and do not form part of the requirements. The number that introduces each Note corresponds to the applicable requirement in this Part.

application_notes.title: Objectives and Functional Statements Attributed to Acceptable Solutions

content.content: The objectives and functional statements attributed to each Code provision are listed in a table following the provisions in each Part.

Many provisions in Division B serve as modifiers of or pointers to other provisions, or serve other clarification or explanatory purposes. In most cases, no objectives and functional statements have been attributed to such provisions, which therefore do not appear in the above-mentioned tables.

For provisions that serve as modifiers of or pointers to other referenced provisions and that do not have any objectives and functional statements attributed to them, the objectives and functional statements that should be used are those attributed to the provisions they reference.

Climatic values for municipalities not listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC:long] can be obtained at [REF:external:https://www.climate.weather.gc.ca:www.climate.weather.gc.ca] or by e-mail from the Engineering Climate Services Unit of Environment and Climate Change Canada at scg-ecs@ec.gc.ca.

The 2.5% values referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent3:long] are the least restrictive temperatures that can be used. A designer may choose to use the 1% values given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC:long] , which are in excess of the Code minimums but are considered acceptable.

content.text: Except as permitted by  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art3:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art5:long] , and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art7:long] , every [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof shall be classified according to its [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] as belonging to one of the Groups or Divisions described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art1.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote3:short] .)

A [REF:term:bldng:building] intended for use by more than one [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] shall be classified according to all [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancies] for which it is used or intended to be used.

content.text: Any [REF:term:bldng:building] is deemed to be occupied by a single [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] , notwithstanding its use for more than one [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] , provided that all [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancies] are classified as belonging to the same Group classification or, where the Group is divided into Divisions, as belonging to the same Division classification described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art1.table1:long]

An arena-type [REF:term:bldng:building] intended for occasional use for trade shows and similar exhibition purposes shall be classified as a Group A, Division 3 [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote4:short] .)

A police station with detention quarters is permitted to be classified as a Group B, Division 2 [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] provided the station is not more than 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] and 600 m^{2} in [REF:term:bldng-r:building area] .

articles.title: Convalescent, Children's Custodial, and Residential Care Homes

content.text: Convalescent homes and children's custodial homes are permitted to be classified as [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancies] within the application of Part 3, provided that occupants are ambulatory and live as a single housekeeping unit in a [REF:term:t:suite] with sleeping accommodation for not more than 10 persons.
A care facility accepted for residential use pursuant to provincial legislation is permitted to be classified as a [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] , provided

clauses.text: occupants live as a single housekeeping unit in a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] with sleeping accommodation for not more than 10 persons,
[REF:term:mk-lrm:smoke alarms] are installed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art4:long] ,
emergency lighting is provided in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect7:long] , and
the [REF:term:bldng:building] is [REF:term:prnklrd:sprinklered] throughout.

articles.title: Group A, Division 2, Low Occupant Load

content.text: A [REF:term:t:suite] of Group A, Division 2 [REF:term:mbl-ccpn:assembly occupancy] , except a child or infant daycare facility, is permitted to be classified as a Group D, [REF:term:bn-nd-pr:business and personal services occupancy] provided

clauses.text: the number of persons in the [REF:term:t:suite] does not exceed 30, and

except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art7.sent2:short] , the [REF:term:t:suite] is separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng:building] by a [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] of not less than 1 h .

content.text: The [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] need not have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] where the [REF:term:t:suite] is located in a [REF:term:bldng:building] that is [REF:term:prnklrd:sprinklered] throughout.

A permanent sign, with lettering not less than 50 mm high with a 12 mm stroke, indicating the lesser of the [REF:term:ccpnt-ld:occupant load] for the [REF:term:t:suite] or 30 persons, shall be posted in a conspicuous location near the [REF:term:t:suite] 's principal entrance.
A daycare facility for children shall be classified as a Group A, Division 2 [REF:term:mbl-ccpn:assembly occupancy] . (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect2.art18:long] .)

revisions.text: A daycare facility for children shall be classified as a Group A, Division 2 [REF:term:mbl-ccpn:assembly occupancy] . (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect2.art17:long] .)
A daycare facility for children shall be classified as a Group A, Division 2 [REF:term:mbl-ccpn:assembly occupancy] . (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect2.art18:long] .)

content.text: Except as permitted by  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent3:short] , [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancies ] shall be separated from adjoining [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancies ] by [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] having [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance ratings] conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect3.art1.table1:long]

In a [REF:term:bldng:building] not more than 3 [REF:term:tr:storeys] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] , if not more than two [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] are contained together with a Group E [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] , the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] of the [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] between the two [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancies] need not be more than 1 h .

In a [REF:term:bldng:building] conforming to the requirements of  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect8.art2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect8.art8:long] , the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] for [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] between [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancies] do not apply at the vertical plane around the perimeter of an opening through the horizontal [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] .

content.text: No [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] of Group F, Division 1 shall be contained within a [REF:term:bldng:building] with any [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] classified as Group A, B or C.

Not more than one [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] shall be contained within a [REF:term:bldng:building] classified as a Group F, Division 2 [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] .

A [REF:term:bldng:building] permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] is permitted to be constructed of [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] materials, with or without [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] components. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote5:short] .)

The [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] on any exposed surface of foamed plastic insulation, and on any surface that would be exposed by cutting through the insulation in any direction, shall be not more than 500.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art2.sent2:short] , foamed plastics that form part of a wall or ceiling assembly in [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] shall be protected from adjacent spaces in the [REF:term:bldng:building] , other than adjacent concealed spaces within [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof spaces] , crawl spaces, and wall and ceiling assemblies,

clauses.text: by one of the interior finishes described in  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect4:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9:long] ,
provided the [REF:term:bldng:building] does not contain a Group A, Group B or Group C [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] , by sheet metal

subclauses.text: mechanically fastened to the supporting assembly independent of the insulation,
not less than 0.38 mm thick, and
with a melting point not below 650°C , or

clauses.text: by any thermal barrier that meets the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art15.sent2:long] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote8:short] ).

content.text: A walk-in cooler or freezer consisting of factory-assembled wall, floor or ceiling panels containing foamed plastics is permitted in a [REF:term:bldng:building] permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] , provided the panels

clauses.text: are protected on both sides by sheet metal not less than 0.38 mm thick having a melting point not less than 650°C,
do not contain an air space, and

when a sample panel with an assembled joint typical of field installation is subjected to the applicable test described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect12:long] , have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] not more than that permitted for the space in which they are located or the space that they bound, as applicable.

content.text: The [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] of doors containing foamed plastics shall comply with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect13.art2.sent1:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect13.art2.sent3:short] .

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art3.sent2:short] , optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables with [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation, jackets or sheathes that are installed in a [REF:term:bldng:building] permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] shall

clauses.text: not convey flame or continue to burn for more than 1 min when tested in conformance with the Vertical Flame Test (FT1 rating) in [REF:standard:csac22.2no.0.3] or
be located in

subclauses.text: totally enclosed [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] raceways (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote10:short] ),
masonry walls,
concrete slabs, or
totally enclosed non-metallic raceways conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art23.sent1.clause2:long] .

content.text: Except as permitted in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art3.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art3.sent4:short] , optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables with [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation, jackets or sheathes that are used for the transmission of voice, sound or data and are installed in a [REF:term:plnm:plenum] in a [REF:term:bldng:building] permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] shall exhibit the following characteristics when tested in conformance with [REF:standard:ulcs102.4] (FT6 rating):

clauses.text: a horizontal flame distance of not more than 1.5 m,
an average optical smoke density of not more than 0.15, and
a peak optical smoke density of not more than 0.5.

content.text: Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art3.sent4:short] , where totally enclosed [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] raceways are used in a [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , exposed components of wiring systems with [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation, jackets or sheathes, including optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables that are used for the transmission of voice, sound or data, that are installed in the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] or that extend not more than 9 m from the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , including drop down to the floor level, are permitted, provided they exhibit a vertical char of not more than 1.5 m when tested in conformance with the Vertical Flame Test – Cables in Cable Trays (FT4 rating) in [REF:standard:csac22.2no.0.3]

Cables or wires within [REF:term:plnm:plenums] that are used for the transmission of signals in fire alarm systems need not comply with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art3.sent2:short] .

Totally enclosed non-metallic raceways used in a [REF:term:plnm:plenum] in a [REF:term:bldng:building] permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] shall meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art23.sent1.clause1:long] .
If [REF:term:fr-rtrdn:fire-retardant-treated wood] is specified in this Part, the wood shall

clauses.text: be pressure impregnated with fire-retardant chemicals in conformance with [REF:standard:csao80series] and
have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] not more than 25.

content.text: If [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] is permitted and is not required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] more than 45 min , [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] is permitted to be used.
If [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] is permitted, it shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art7:long]
Wood elements in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] shall be arranged in heavy solid masses and with essentially smooth flat surfaces to avoid thin sections and sharp projections.

Except as permitted by  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art7.sent3:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art7.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art7.sent12:short] , the minimum dimensions of wood elements in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art7.table1:long]

content.value: Arches supported on the tops of walls or abutments
Arches supported at or near the floor line

content.text: Where splice plates are used at splices of roof arches supported on the tops of walls or abutments, roof trusses, roof beams and roof girders in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] , they shall be not less than 64 mm thick.
Floors in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] shall be of glued-laminated or solid sawn plank not less than

clauses.text: 64 mm thick, splined or tongued and grooved, or
38 mm wide and 89 mm deep set on edge and well spiked together.

content.text: Floors in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] shall be laid

clauses.text: so that no continuous line of end joints will occur except at points of support, and covered with

subclauses.text: tongued and grooved flooring not less than 19 mm thick laid crosswise or diagonally, or
tongued and grooved phenolic-bonded plywood, strandboard or waferboard not less than 12.5 mm thick, and

clauses.text: not closer than 15 mm to the walls to provide for expansion, with the gap covered at the top or bottom.

content.text: Roofs in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] shall be of tongued and grooved phenolic-bonded plywood, strandboard or waferboard not less than 28 mm thick, or glued-laminated or solid sawn plank that is

clauses.text: not less than 38 mm thick, splined or tongued and grooved, or
not less than 38 mm wide and 64 mm deep set on edge and laid so that no continuous line of end joints will occur except at the points of support.

content.text: Wood columns in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] shall be continuous or superimposed throughout all [REF:term:tr:storeys] .
Superimposed wood columns in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] shall be connected by

clauses.text: reinforced concrete or metal caps with brackets,
steel or iron caps with pintles and base plates, or
timber splice plates fastened to the columns by metal connectors housed within the contact faces.

content.text: Where beams and girders in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] enter masonry, wall plates, boxes of the self-releasing type or hangers shall be used.

Wood girders and beams in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] shall be closely fitted to columns, and adjoining ends shall be connected by ties or caps to transfer horizontal loads across the joints.

In [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] , intermediate wood beams used to support a floor shall be supported on top of the girders or on metal hangers into which the ends of the beams are closely fitted.

Roof arches supported on the top of walls or abutments, roof trusses, roof beams and roof girders in [REF:term:hv-tmbr-:heavy timber construction] are permitted to be not less than 64 mm wide provided

clauses.text: where two or more spaced members are used, the intervening spaces are

subclauses.text: blocked solidly throughout, or
tightly closed by a continuous wood cover plate not less than 38 mm thick secured to the underside of the members, or

clauses.text: the underneath of the roof deck or sheathing is [REF:term:prnklrd:sprinklered] .

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art8.sent2:short] , cladding on an exterior wall assembly of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part of a [REF:term:bldng:building] conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art51:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art60:long] shall consist of

clauses.text: [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] cladding, or

except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art8.sent4:short] , a wall assembly that satisfies the criteria of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art5.sent1.clause2:long] .

content.text: For [REF:term:bldng:buildings] described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art8.sent1:short] , [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] cladding representing up to 10% of the cladding on the face of an exterior wall facing a [REF:term:trt:street] or access route shall be permitted, provided all portions of the [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] cladding are located not more than 15 m from a [REF:term:trt:street] or access route conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect5.art6:long] , measured horizontally from the face of the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

A wall assembly conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art8.sent1.clause2:medium] that includes [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] cladding made of [REF:term:fr-rtrdn:fire-retardant-treated wood] shall be tested for fire exposure after the cladding has been subjected to the accelerated weathering test specified in [REF:standard:astmd2898]
Exterior wall assemblies constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:ex000109.7:long] of Appendix D are deemed to comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect4.art8.sent1.clause2:medium] .
Cladding described in this Article must also comply with the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3.art7:long] .

Except as permitted by  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent4:short] and  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art24:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect13.art4:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art16:number] , a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part of a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] shall be constructed with [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] materials. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect13:long] for the requirements regarding the [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] of interior finishes.)

Notwithstanding the definition of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] materials stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect1.art2:long] , a material is permitted to be used in [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] provided that, when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs135] at a heat flux of 50 kW/m^{2} ,

clauses.text: its average total heat release is not more than 3 MJ/m^{2} ,
its average total smoke extinction area is not more than 1.0 m^{2} , and
the test duration is extended beyond the time stipulated in the referenced standard until it is clear that there is no further release of heat or smoke.

content.text: If a material referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] consists of a number of discrete layers and testing reveals that the surface layer or layers protect the underlying layers such that complete combustion of the underlying layers does not occur, the test shall be repeated by removing the outer layers sequentially until all layers have been exposed during testing, or until complete combustion has occurred.

The acceptance criteria for a material tested in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent3:short] shall be based on the cumulative emissions from all layers, which must not exceed the criteria stated in  Clauses [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent2.clause1:medium] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent2.clause2:short] .
The following minor [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] components are permitted in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] :

clauses.text: paint (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect13.art1.sent2.clause2:long] ),

self-adhesive tapes, mastics and caulking materials, including foamed plastic air sealants, applied to provide a seal between the major components of exterior wall construction, (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3:long] for limits on the use of [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] materials in [REF:term:plnm:plenum] spaces),
[REF:term:fr-tp:firestops] and [REF:term:fr-blk:fire blocks] conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9.art1.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect11.art7:long] ,
tubing for pneumatic controls provided it has an outside diameter of not more than 10 mm ,
adhesives, [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barriers] and sheathing papers,
electrical outlet and junction boxes,
wood blocking intended for the attachment of window elements within exterior wall assemblies,
wood blocking within wall assemblies intended for the attachment of handrails, fixtures, and similar items mounted on the surface of the wall, and
similar minor components.

content.text: [REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible ] roof covering that has an A, B, or C classification determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect15:long] is permitted on a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] .

[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible ] roof sheathing and roof sheathing supports installed above a concrete deck are permitted on a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible]  [REF:term:cntrctr:construction] provided

[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible ] duct linings, duct coverings, duct insulation, vibration isolation connectors, duct tape, pipe insulation and pipe coverings are permitted to be used in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] provided they conform to the appropriate requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5:long]

In a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] , [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] ducts need not comply with the requirements of  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] provided the ducts are

clauses.text: part of a duct system conveying only ventilation air, and
contained entirely within a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art2.sent1.clause4:long] and  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art19.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art19.sent3:short] , [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] piping and tubing and associated adhesives are permitted to be used in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] provided that, except when concealed in a wall or concrete floor slab, they

clauses.text: have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] not more than 25, and
if used in a [REF:term:bldng:building] described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6:long] , have a smoke developed classification not more than 50.

content.text: [REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] sprinkler piping is permitted to be used within a [REF:term:prnklrd:sprinklered]  [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] . (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect5.art13:long] )

Polypropylene pipes and fittings are permitted to be used for drain, waste and vent piping for the conveyance of highly corrosive materials and for piping used to distribute distilled or dialyzed water in laboratory and hospital facilities in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] , provided

clauses.text: the [REF:term:bldng:building] is [REF:term:prnklrd:sprinklered] throughout,
the piping is not located in a vertical shaft, and

piping that penetrates a [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] is sealed at the penetration by a [REF:term:fr-tp:firestop] that has an FT rating not less than the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] of the [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] when subjected to the fire test method in [REF:standard:ulcs115] with a pressure differential of 50 Pa between the exposed and unexposed sides, with the higher pressure on the exposed side.

content.text: [REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] plumbing fixtures, including wall and ceiling enclosures that form part of the plumbing fixture, are permitted in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] provided they are constructed of material having a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] and smoke developed classification not more than that permitted for the wall surface of the room or space in which they are installed.

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art22:long] , optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables with [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation, jackets or sheathes are permitted in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] , provided

clauses.text: the wires and cables exhibit a vertical char of not more than 1.5 m when tested in conformance with the Vertical Flame Test – Cables in Cable Trays (FT4 rating) in [REF:standard:csac22.2no.0.3]
the wires and cables are located in

subclauses.text: totally enclosed [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] raceways (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote10:long] ),
masonry walls,
concrete slabs,

a [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng:building] by a [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] having a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] not less than 1 h , or
totally enclosed non-metallic raceways conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art23.sent1.clause2:long] , or

clauses.text: the wires and cables are communication cables used at the service entry to a [REF:term:bldng:building] and are not more than 3 m long.

content.text: Except as permitted in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent4:short] , optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables with [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation, jackets or sheathes that are used for the transmission of voice, sound or data and are not located in totally enclosed [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] raceways are permitted to be installed in a [REF:term:plnm:plenum] in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] , provided the wires and cables exhibit a horizontal flame distance of not more than 1.5 m , an average optical smoke density of not more than 0.15, and a peak optical smoke density of not more than 0.5 when tested in conformance with [REF:standard:ulcs102.4] (FT6 rating).

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent4:short] , where totally enclosed [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] raceways are used in a [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , exposed components of wiring systems with [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation, jackets or sheathes, including optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables that are used for the transmission of voice, sound or data, that are installed in the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] or that extend not more than 9 m from the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] including drop down to the floor level, are permitted provided they exhibit a vertical char of not more than 1.5 m when tested in conformance with the Vertical Flame Test – Cables in Cable Trays (FT4 rating) in [REF:standard:csac22.2no.0.3]

Cables or wires within [REF:term:plnm:plenums] that are used for the transmission of signals in fire alarm systems need not comply with the requirements of  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent3:short] .
[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] travelling cables are permitted on elevating devices in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] .

Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art23.sent2:short] , subject to the limits on the size of elements that penetrate [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations ] when complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9.art2:long] , within a [REF:term:fr-cmprt:fire compartment] of a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] , totally enclosed non-metallic raceways not more than 175 mm in outside diameter, or of an equivalent rectangular area, are permitted to be used to enclose optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables, provided

clauses.text: where the wires and cables in the raceways meet or exceed the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent1.clause1:long] , the non-metallic raceways meet the requirements for at least an FT4 rating in

subclauses.text: [REF:standard:csac22.2no.262] or
[REF:standard:ulcs143] and

clauses.text: where the wires and cables in the raceways do not meet or exceed the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art21.sent1.clause1:long] , the non-metallic raceways exhibit a vertical char of not more than 1.5 m when tested in conformance with the Vertical Flame Test (FT4) – Conduit or Tubing on Cable Tray in [REF:external:csac22.2no.211.0:Clause 6.16 of ] [REF:standard:csac22.2no.211.0]

content.text: Totally enclosed non-metallic raceways used in a [REF:term:plnm:plenum] in a [REF:term:bldng:building] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] shall exhibit a horizontal flame distance of not more than 1.5 m , an average optical smoke density of not more than 0.15, and a peak optical smoke density of not more than 0.5 when tested in conformance with [REF:standard:ulcs102.4] (FT6 rating).

On [REF:term:bldng:buildings] required to be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] , decorative wood cladding is permitted to be used on the exterior fascias and soffits of marquees or canopies on the [REF:term:bldng:building] face of a [REF:term:tr:storey] having direct access to a [REF:term:trt:street] or access route, provided the wood cladding is [REF:term:fr-rtrdn:fire-retardant-treated wood] that has been conditioned in conformance with [REF:standard:astmd2898] before being tested in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs102]
[REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr:Encapsulated mass timber construction] permitted in this Part shall conform to this Subsection.

Except as otherwise provided in this Part and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect4.subsect3.art1.sent1:long] , materials used in a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part of a [REF:term:bldng:building] permitted to be of [REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr:encapsulated mass timber construction] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5:long]

Except as otherwise provided in this Subsection and  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art16:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3.art19:long] , a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part of a [REF:term:bldng:building] permitted to be of [REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr:encapsulated mass timber construction] is permitted to include structural mass timber elements, including beams, columns, arches, and wall, floor and roof assemblies, provided they comply with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent3:short] .
Structural mass timber elements referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text: except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent4:short] , be arranged in heavy solid masses containing no concealed spaces,
have essentially smooth flat surfaces with no thin sections or sharp projections, and
except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art17.sent1:long] , conform to the minimum dimensions stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.table1:long]

content.text: Adhesives used in structural mass timber elements referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent1:short] that are constructed of cross‐laminated timber shall conform to the elevated temperature performance requirements in [REF:standard:apaprg320]

Concealed spaces are permitted within structural mass timber elements referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent2:short] and need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:long] , provided the concealed spaces are

clauses.text: [REF:term:prnklrd:sprinklered] and divided into compartments by [REF:term:fr-blk:fire blocks] in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect11:long] ,
completely filled with rock or slag fibre insulation conforming to [REF:standard:ulcs702] and having a density not less than 32 kg/m^{3} ,

if horizontal, lined with not less than a single layer of 12.7 mm thick Type X gypsum board or [REF:term:cmbtbl:noncombustible] material providing an [REF:term:ncps-rtng:encapsulation rating] of not less than 25 min , or

if vertical, lined with not less than a single layer of 12.7 mm thick Type X gypsum board or [REF:term:cmbtbl:noncombustible] material providing an [REF:term:ncps-rtng:encapsulation rating] of not less than 25 min and vertically divided into compartments by [REF:term:fr-blk:fire blocks] in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect11:long]

gypsum concrete,
[REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] materials,

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent5:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent7:short] , the exposed surfaces of mass timber beams, columns and arches within a [REF:term:t:suite] or [REF:term:fr-cmprt:fire compartment] in a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part of a [REF:term:bldng:building] constructed in conformance with  Article [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art48:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art57:number] or permitted by  Article [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art93:long] to have a 50 min[REF:term:ncps-rtng:encapsulation rating] need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short] , provided

the [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] on any exposed surface is not more than 150. (See  Notes [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote22:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote28:short] .)

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent5:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent7:short] , the exposed surfaces of mass timber walls within a [REF:term:t:suite] in a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part of a [REF:term:bldng:building] constructed in conformance with  Article [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art48:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art57:number] or permitted by  Article [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art93:long] to have a 50 min[REF:term:ncps-rtng:encapsulation rating] need not be protected in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short] , provided

gypsum concrete,
[REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] materials,

One layer of Type X gypsum board conforming to [REF:standard:astmc1396m] , "Standard Specification for Gypsum Board," or [REF:standard:csaa82.27] , "Gypsum Board," not less than 12.7 mm thick, is deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng:encapsulation rating] of 25 min when installed on a mass timber element in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art6.sent6:short] .

Three layers of Type X gypsum board conforming to [REF:standard:astmc1396m] , "Standard Specification for Gypsum Board," or [REF:standard:csaa82.27] , "Gypsum Board," each not less than 12.7 mm thick, are deemed to have an [REF:term:ncps-rtng:encapsulation rating] of 80 min when installed on a mass timber element in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art6.sent6:short] .
