studies of model analogues.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art2:long] , the following categories of loads, specified loads and effects shall be taken into consideration in the design of a [REF:term:bldng:building] and its structural members and connections:[LIST:symbol]where

items.description: [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] – a permanent load due to the weight of [REF:term:bldng:building] components, as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4:long] ,
earthquake load and effects – a rare load due to an earthquake, as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long] ,
a permanent load due to lateral earth pressure, including [REF:term:grndwtr:groundwater] ,

[REF:term:lv-ld:live load] – a variable load due to intended use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] (including loads due to cranes and the pressure of liquids in containers), as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5:long] ,
[REF:term:lv-ld:live load] exclusive of crane loads,
[REF:term:lv-ld:live load] due to cranes including self weight,
self weight of all cranes positioned for maximum effects,
crane bumper impact load,
permanent effects caused by pre-stress,

variable load due to snow, including ice and associated rain, as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2:long] , or due to rain, as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art4:long] ,

effects due to contraction, expansion, or deflection caused by temperature changes, shrinkage, moisture changes, creep, ground settlement, or a combination thereof (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote5:short] ), and
wind load – a variable load due to wind, as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7:long] ,

clauses.text: load means the imposed deformations (i.e. deflections, displacements or motions that induce deformations and forces in the structure), forces and pressures applied to the [REF:term:bldng:building] structure,
permanent load is a load that changes very little once it has been applied to the structure, except during repair,
variable load is a load that frequently changes in magnitude, direction or location, and
rare load is a load that occurs infrequently and for a short time only.

content.text: Minimum specified values of the loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art1.sent1:short] , as set forth in  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:number] , shall be increased to account for dynamic effects where applicable.

For the purpose of determining specified loads S, W or E in  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6:long] ,  [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long] , [REF:term:bldng:buildings] shall be assigned an Importance Category based on intended use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] , in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art1.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote6:short] .)

content.value: A Low Importance Category [REF:term:bldng:building] is a [REF:term:bldng:building] that represents a low direct or indirect hazard to human life in the event of structural failure.

A Normal Importance Category [REF:term:bldng:building] is a [REF:term:bldng:building] that does not meet the criteria for a Low Importance Category [REF:term:bldng:building] , High Importance Category [REF:term:bldng:building] or [REF:term:pt-dtr-b:post-disaster building] .

A High Importance Category [REF:term:bldng:building] is a [REF:term:bldng:building] that provides a greater degree of safety to human life than a Normal Importance Category [REF:term:bldng:building] . Community centres and elementary, middle and secondary schools are High Importance Category [REF:term:bldng:buildings] .

content.text: Where a [REF:term:bldng:building] or structural member can be expected to be subjected to loads, forces or other effects not listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art1:long] , such effects shall be taken into account in the design based on the most appropriate information available. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote8:short] .)
In this Subsection, the term

clauses.text: limit states means those conditions of a [REF:term:bldng:building] structure that result in the [REF:term:bldng:building] ceasing to fulfill the function for which it was designed (those limit states concerning safety are called ultimate limit states (ULS) and include exceeding the load-carrying capacity, overturning, sliding and fracture; those limit states that restrict the intended use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] of the [REF:term:bldng:building] are called serviceability limit states (SLS) and include deflection, vibration, permanent deformation and local structural damage such as cracking; and those limit states that represent failure under repeated loading are called fatigue limit states),
specified loads (C, D, E, H, L, P, S, T and W) means those loads defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art1:long] ,
principal load means the specified variable load or rare load that dominates in a given load combination,
companion load means a specified variable load that accompanies the principal load in a given load combination,
service load means a specified load used for the evaluation of a serviceability limit state,
principal-load factor means a factor applied to the principal load in a load combination to account for the variability of the load and load pattern and the analysis of its effects,

companion-load factor means a factor that, when applied to a companion load in the load combination, gives the probable magnitude of a companion load acting simultaneously with the factored principal load,

importance factor, I, means a factor applied in  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long] to obtain the specified load and take into account the consequences of failure as related to the limit state and the use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] of the [REF:term:bldng:building] ,
factored load means the product of a specified load and its principal-load factor or companion-load factor,
effects refers to forces, moments, deformations or vibrations that occur in the structure,
nominal resistance, R, of a member, connection or structure, is based on the geometry and on the specified properties of the structural materials,

resistance factor, φ, means a factor applied to a specified material property or to the resistance of a member, connection or structure, and that, for the limit state under consideration, takes into account the variability of dimensions and material properties, workmanship, type of failure and uncertainty in the prediction of resistance, and
factored resistance, φR, means the product of nominal resistance and the applicable resistance factor.

content.text: A [REF:term:bldng:building] and its structural components shall be designed to have sufficient strength and stability so that the factored resistance, φR, is greater than or equal to the effect of factored loads, which shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.sent2:short] .

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.sent3:short] , the effect of factored loads for a [REF:term:bldng:building] or structural component shall be determined in accordance with the requirements of this Article and the following load combination cases, the applicable combination being that which results in the most critical effect:

clauses.text: for load cases without crane loads, the load combinations listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long] , and
for load cases with crane loads, the load combinations listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table2:long] .

content.text: Other load combinations that must also be considered are the principal loads acting with the companion loads taken as zero.

Where the effects due to lateral earth pressure, H, restraint effects from pre-stress, P, and imposed deformation, T, affect the structural safety, they shall be taken into account in the calculations, with load factors of 1.5, 1.0 and 1.25 assigned to H, P and T respectively. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote11:short] .)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent2:long] , the counteracting factored [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] —0.9D in load combination cases 2, 3 and 4 and 1.0D in load combination case 5 in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long] , and 0.9D in load combination cases 1 to 5 and 1.0D in load combination case 6 in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table2:long] —shall be used when the [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] acts to resist overturning, uplift, sliding, failure due to stress reversal, and to determine anchorage requirements and the factored resistance of members. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote12:short] .)

The principal-load factor 1.5 for [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] L in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long] and L_{XC} in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table2:long] may be reduced to 1.25 for liquids in tanks.

The companion-load factor for [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] L in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long] and L_{XC} in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table2:long] shall be increased by 0.5 for storage areas, and equipment areas and [REF:term:rvc-rm:service rooms] referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long]

Earthquake load, E, in load combination cases 5 of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table1:long] and 6 of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.table2:long] includes horizontal earth pressure due to earthquake determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art16.sent7:long] .
Provision shall be made to ensure adequate stability of the structure as a whole and adequate lateral, torsional and local stability of all structural parts.
Sway effects produced by vertical loads acting on the structure in its displaced configuration shall be taken into account in the design of [REF:term:bldng:buildings] and their structural members.

A [REF:term:bldng:building] and its structural components, including connections, shall be checked for fatigue failure under the effect of cyclical loads, as required in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote13:short] .)

Where vibration effects, such as resonance and fatigue resulting from machinery and equipment, are likely to be significant, a dynamic analysis shall be carried out. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote14:short] .)

A [REF:term:bldng:building] and its structural components shall be checked for serviceability limit states as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent1.clause1:long] under the effect of service loads for serviceability criteria specified or recommended in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art5:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art6:long] and in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote15:short] .)

The effect of service loads on the serviceability limit states shall be determined in accordance with this Article and the load combinations listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art4.table1:long] , the applicable combination being that which results in the most critical effect.
Other load combinations that must also be considered are the principal loads acting with the companion loads taken as zero.
Deflections calculated for load types P, T and H, if present, with load factors of 1.0 shall be included with the calculated deflections due to principal loads.
The determination of the deflection shall consider the following:

clauses.text: for materials that result in increased deformations over time under sustained loads, the deflection calculation shall consider the portion of [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] , L, that is sustained over time, L_{s}, and the portion that is transitory, L_{t}, and

the calculated deflection due to [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] , D, and sustained [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] , L_{s}, shall be increased by a creep factor as specified in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long] to obtain the additional long-term deflection.

content.text: The determination of the long-term settlement of [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] shall consider the following:

clauses.text: for [REF:term:fndtn:foundation]  [REF:term:l:soil] types that result in increased settlement over time under sustained loads, the additional long-term settlements shall be determined for the portion of [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] , L, that is sustained over time, L_{s}, and the portion that is transitory, L_{t}, and

the additional long-term settlements due to [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] , D, and sustained [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] , L_{s}, shall be calculated from the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation]  [REF:term:l:soil] properties provided by a qualified professional geotechnical engineer.

table_notes.content: The calculated deflection due to [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] , D, is permitted to be excluded where specified in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long]
The companion load factor of 0.35 for [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] , L, shall be increased to 0.5 for storage areas, equipment areas and [REF:term:rvc-rm:service rooms] .
The calculated immediate deflection due to [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] , D, is permitted to be excluded where specified in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long]
L_{s} = sustained portion of the [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] , L.
L_{t} = transitory portion of the [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] , L.

content.value: Deflection for materials not subject to creep
Deflection of the structure or of components of the structure [REF:table-note:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art4.table1.note1]
Deflection for materials subject to creep
Total deflection of the structure or of components of the structure [REF:table-note:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art4.table1.note3]

content.text: In proportioning structural members to limit serviceability problems resulting from deflections, consideration shall be given to

clauses.text: the intended use of the [REF:term:bldng:building] or member,
limiting damage to non-structural members made of materials whose physical properties are known at the time of design,
limiting damage to the structure itself, and
creep, shrinkage, temperature changes and pre-stress.

content.text: The lateral deflection of [REF:term:bldng:buildings] due to service wind and gravity loads shall be checked to ensure that structural elements and non-structural elements whose nature is known at the time the structural design is carried out will not be damaged.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art5.sent4:short] , the total drift per [REF:term:tr:storey] under service wind and gravity loads shall not exceed 1/500 of the [REF:term:tr:storey] height unless other drift limits are specified in the design standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote18:short] .)

The deflection limits required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art5.sent3:short] do not apply to industrial [REF:term:bldng:buildings] or sheds if experience has proven that greater movement will have no significant adverse effects on the strength and function of the [REF:term:bldng:building] .
The [REF:term:bldng:building] structure shall be designed for lateral deflection due to E, in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13:long]

Floor systems susceptible to vibration shall be designed so that vibrations will have no significant adverse effects on the intended [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] of the [REF:term:bldng:building] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote19:short] .)

Where floor vibrations caused by resonance with operating machinery or equipment are anticipated, dynamic analysis of the floor system shall be carried out. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote20:short] .)

Where the fundamental vibration frequency of a structural system supporting an [REF:term:mbl-ccpn:assembly occupancy] used for rhythmic activities, such as dancing, concerts, jumping exercises or gymnastics, is less than 6 Hz , the effects of resonance shall be investigated by means of a dynamic analysis. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote21:short] .)

A [REF:term:bldng:building] susceptible to lateral vibration under wind load shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art1:long] so that the vibrations will have no significant adverse effects on the intended use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] of the [REF:term:bldng:building] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote22:short] .)
The specified [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] for a structural member consists of

clauses.text: the weight of the member itself,
the weight of all materials of construction incorporated into the [REF:term:bldng:building] to be supported permanently by the member,
the weight of [REF:term:prttn:partitions] ,
the weight of permanent equipment, and
the vertical load due to [REF:term:l:soil] , superimposed earth, plants and trees.

content.text: In areas of a [REF:term:bldng:building] for which [REF:term:prttn:partitions] are shown on the drawings, the weight of [REF:term:prttn:partitions] referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent1.clause3:medium] shall be taken as the actual weight of such [REF:term:prttn:partitions] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote23:short] .)

In areas of a [REF:term:bldng:building] for which [REF:term:prttn:partitions] are not shown on the drawings, the weight of [REF:term:prttn:partitions] referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent1.clause3:medium] shall be a [REF:term:prttn:partition] weight allowance determined from the anticipated weight and position of the [REF:term:prttn:partitions] , but shall not be less than 1 kPa over the area of floor being considered. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote24:short] .)

The weights of [REF:term:prttn:partitions ] and [REF:term:prttn:partition ] weight allowances used in the design shall be shown on the drawings as provided in  Clause [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect4.art3.sent1.clause4:long] .

Where the [REF:term:prttn:partition] weight allowance referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent3:short] is counteractive to other loads, it shall not be included in the design calculations.

Except for structures where the [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] of [REF:term:l:soil] is part of the load-resisting system, where the [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] due to [REF:term:l:soil] , superimposed earth, plants and trees is counteractiveto other loads, it shall not be included in the design calculations. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote25:short] .)

articles.title: Loads Due to Use of Floors and Roofs

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] , the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] on an area of floor or roof depends on the intended use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] , and shall not be less than either the uniformly distributed load patterns listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3:long] , the loads due to the intended use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] , or the concentrated loads listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art9:long] , whichever produces the most critical effect. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote26:short] .)

For [REF:term:bldng:buildings] in the Low Importance Category as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art1.table1:long] , a factor of 0.8 may be applied to the [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] .

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art2.sent2:short] , where the use of an area of floor or roof is not provided for in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3:long] , the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] due to the use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] of the area shall be determined from an analysis of the loads resulting from the weight of

clauses.text: the probable assembly of persons,
the probable accumulation of equipment and furnishings, and
the probable storage of materials.

content.text: For [REF:term:bldng:buildings] in the Low Importance Category as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art1.table1:long] , a factor of 0.8 may be applied to the [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] .

The uniformly distributed [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] shall be not less than the value listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] , which may be reduced as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art8:long] , applied uniformly over the entire area or on any portions of the area, whichever produces the most critical effects in the members concerned.

content.text: Exterior areas accessible to vehicular traffic shall be designed for their intended use, including the weight of firefighting equipment, but not for less than the snow and rain loads prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6:long]

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art5.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art5.sent4:short] , roofs shall be designed for either the uniform [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] , the concentrated [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art9.table1:long] , or the snow and rain loads prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6:long] , whichever produces the most critical effect.

content.text: Roof parking decks that are used for the long-term storage of vehicles shall be designed for the appropriate load combination listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2.sent2:long] with a [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] , L, consisting of either a uniformly distributed [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] or a concentrated [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] as listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art9.table1:long] , whichever produces the most critical effect, and a snow load, S, as prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6:long]

The minimum specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] for dining areas may be reduced to 2.4 kPa for areas in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] that are being converted to dining areas, provided that the [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] does not exceed 100 m^{2} and the dining area will not be used for other assembly purposes, including dancing.

Where an area of floor or roof is intended for 2 or more [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancies] at different times, the value to be used from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] shall be the greatest value for any of the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancies] concerned.
One- and two-way floor slabs shall have no reduction for tributary area applied to [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] .

An area used for [REF:term:mbl-ccpn:assembly occupancies] designed for a [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] of less than 4.8 kPa and roofs designed for the minimum loading specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] shall have no reduction for tributary area.

Where a structural member supports a tributary area of a floor or a roof, or a combination thereof, that is greater than 80 m^{2} and either used for [REF:term:mbl-ccpn:assembly occupancies] designed for a [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] of 4.8 kPa or more, or used for storage, manufacturing, retail stores, garages or as a footbridge, the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] due to use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] is the load specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3:long] multiplied by[EQ:display:es007850q1]where A is the tributary area in square metres for this type of use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] .

articles.title: Crane-Supporting Structures and Impact of Machinery and Equipment

content.text: The minimum specified load due to equipment, machinery or other objects that may produce impact shall be the sum of the weight of the equipment or machinery and its maximum lifting capacity, multiplied by an appropriate factor listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art11.table1:long]
Crane-supporting structures shall be designed for the appropriate load combinations listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art2:long]

Crane runway structures shall be designed to resist a horizontal force applied normal to the top of the rails equal to not less than 20% of the sum of the weights of the lifted load and the crane trolley (excluding other parts of the crane).
The force described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art11.sent3:short] shall be equally distributed on each side of the runway and shall be assumed to act in either direction.
Crane runway structures shall be designed to resist a horizontal force applied parallel to the top of the rails equal to not less than 10% of the maximum wheel loads of the crane.

Bleachers shall be checked by the erector after erection to ensure that all structural members, including bracing specified in the design, have been installed.

Individual elements within the [REF:term:guard:guard] , including solid panels and pickets, shall be designed for a horizontal specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] of 0.5 kN applied outward over an area of 100 mm by 100 mm located at any point on the element or elements so as to produce the most critical effect.

The size of the opening between any two adjacent vertical elements within a [REF:term:guard:guard] shall not exceed the limits required by Part 3 when each of these elements is subjected to a horizontal specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] of 0.1 kN applied in opposite directions in the in-plane direction of the [REF:term:guard:guard] so as to produce the most critical effect.

The specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent3:short] need not be considered to act simultaneously with the loads provided for in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent1:short] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent2:short] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent7:short] .

The minimum specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] applied vertically at the top of every required [REF:term:guard:guard] shall be 1.5 kN/m and need not be considered to act simultaneously with the horizontal specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] provided for in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent1:short] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent7:short] .
Handrails and their supports shall be designed and constructed to withstand the following minimum specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] , which need not be considered to act simultaneously:

clauses.text: 0.9 kN applied at any point and in any direction for all handrails, and
0.7 kN/m applied in any direction for handrails not located within [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] .

content.text: Vehicle guardrails shall be designed for a concentrated load of 22 kN applied horizontally outward at any point 500 mm above the floor surface so as to produce the most critical effect. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote32:short] .)

The loads required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art15.sent1:short] need not be considered to act simultaneously with the loads provided for in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art14:long]

articles.title: Loads on Walls Acting As Guards

content.text: Where the floor elevation on one side of a wall, including a wall around a shaft, is more than 600 mm higher than the elevation of the floor or ground on the other side, the wall shall be designed to resist the appropriate outward lateral design loads prescribed elsewhere in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5:long] or 0.5 kPa acting outward, whichever produces the more critical effect.
[REF:term:frwll:Firewalls] shall be designed to resist the maximum effect due to

clauses.text: the appropriate lateral design loads prescribed elsewhere in this Section, or
a factored lateral load of 0.5 kPa under fire conditions, as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art17.sent2:short] .

content.text: Under fire conditions, where the [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating ] of the structure is less than that of the [REF:term:frwll:firewall] ,

clauses.text: lateral support shall be assumed to be provided by the structure on one side only, or
another structural support system capable of resisting the loads imposed by a fire on either side of the [REF:term:frwll:firewall] shall be provided.

subsections.title: Loads Due to Snow and Rain

articles.title: Specified Load Due to Rain or to Snow and Associated Rain

content.text: The specified load on a roof or any other [REF:term:bldng:building] surface subject to snow and associated rain shall be the snow load specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2:long] , or the rain load specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art4:long] , whichever produces the more critical effect. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote34:short] .)

content.text: Except as provided for in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent4:short] , the wind exposure factor, C_{w}, shall be 1.0.

For [REF:term:bldng:buildings] in the Low and Normal Importance Categories as set out in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect2.art1.table1:long] , the wind exposure factor, C_{w}, given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent3:short] may be reduced to 0.75 for rural areas only, or to 0.5 for exposed areas north of the treeline, where

clauses.text: the [REF:term:bldng:building] is exposed on all sides to wind over open terrain as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent5.clause1:long] , and is expected to remain so during its life,

the area of roof under consideration is exposed to the wind on all sides with no significant obstructions on the roof, such as parapet walls, within a distance of at least 10 times the difference between the height of the obstruction and C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ, in m, where γ is the specific weight of snow on roofs as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art13:long] , and
the loading does not involve the accumulation of snow due to drifting from adjacent surfaces.

content.text: Except as provided for in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent7:short] , the slope factor, C_{s}, shall be

clauses.text: 1.0 where the roof slope, α, is equal to or less than 30° ,
(70° − α)/40° where α is greater than 30° but not greater than 70° , and
0 where α exceeds 70° .

content.text: The slope factor, C_{s}, for unobstructed slippery roofs where snow and ice can slide completely off the roof shall be

clauses.text: 1.0 where the roof slope, α, is equal to or less than 15° ,
(60° − α)/45° where α is greater than 15° but not greater than 60° , and
0 where α exceeds 60° .

content.text: Unless otherwise stated in this Subsection, the slope factor, C_{s}, shall be 1.0 when used in conjunction with accumulation factors for increased snow loads.

The accumulation factor, C_{a}, shall be 1.0, which corresponds to the uniform snow load case, except that where appropriate for the shape of the roof, it shall be assigned other values that account for

clauses.text: increased non-uniform snow loads due to snow drifting onto a roof that is at a level lower than other parts of the same [REF:term:bldng:building] or at a level lower than another [REF:term:bldng:building] within 5 m of it horizontally, as prescribed in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art5:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art6:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art8:short] ,

increased non-uniform snow loads on areas adjacent to roof projections, such as penthouses, large [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] and equipment, as prescribed in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art7:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art8:short] ,

non-uniform snow loads on gable, arch or curved roofs and domes, as prescribed in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art9:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art10:short] ,
increased snow or ice loads due to snow sliding as prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art11:long] ,
increased snow loads in roof valleys, as prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art12:long] , and
increased snow or ice loads due to meltwater draining from adjacent [REF:term:bldng:building] elements and roof projections.

content.text: For shapes not addressed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent8:short] , C_{a} corresponding to the non-uniform snow load case shall be established based on applicable field observations, special analyses including local climatic effects, appropriate model tests, or a combination of these methods.

A roof or other [REF:term:bldng:building] surface and its structural members subject to loads due to snow accumulation shall be designed for the specified load given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent1:long] , distributed over the entire loaded area.

In addition to the distribution mentioned in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent1:short] , flat roofs and shed roofs, gable roofs of 15° slope or less, and arch or curved roofs shall be designed for the specified uniform snow load indicated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent1:long] , which shall be calculated using the accumulation factor C_{a} = 1.0, distributed on any one portion of the loaded area and half of this load on the remainder of the loaded area, in such a way as to produce the most critical effects on the member concerned. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote37:short] .)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent4:short] , the specified load, S, due to the accumulation of rainwater on a surface whose position, shape and deflection under load make such an accumulation possible, is that resulting from the one-day rainfall determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long] and applied over the horizontal projection of the surface and all tributary surfaces. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote38:short] .)
The provisions of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:short] apply whether or not the surface is provided with a means of drainage, such as rainwater leaders.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent1:long] , loads due to rain need not be considered to act simultaneously with loads due to snow. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote39:short] .)

Where scuppers are provided as secondary drainage systems and where the position, shape and deflection of the loaded surface make an accumulation of rainwater possible, the loads due to rain shall be the lesser of either the one-day rainfall determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long] or a depth of rainwater equal to 30 mm above the bottom of the scuppers, applied over the horizontal projection of the surface and tributary areas.

content.text: Where the slope, α, of a curved roof at its peak is greater than 10°, C_{a} shall be determined in accordance with the requirements for gable roofs stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art9:long] using a slope equal to the mean slope of the curved roof.
For domes of circular plan form (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art10.figure2:long] ), C_{a} shall

clauses.text: along the central axis parallel to the wind, vary in the same way as for an arch roof with the same rise-to-span ratio, h/b, and
off this axis, vary according to[EQ:display:eg02650a]where[LIST:variable]

= value of C_{a} on the central axis parallel to the wind,

content.text: For all arch roofs, curved roofs and domes, the slope factor, C_{s}, shall be as prescribed in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent5:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent6:short] .
For all arch roofs, curved roofs and domes, the wind exposure factor, C_{w}, shall be as prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art10.table1:long]

graphic.alt_text: Unbalanced snow accumulation factor on a circular dome

notes.content: Refer to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art10.table1:long] for applicable values of C_{w} and  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent5:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent6:short] for applicable values of C_{s}.
Refer to  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art10.sent3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art10.sent4:short] for the calculation of C_{a}(x,0).

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art11.sent2:short] , where an upper roof, or part thereof, slopes downwards with a slope α > 0 towards a lower roof, the snow load, S, on the lower roof, determined in accordance with  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art5:long] , shall be augmented in accordance with  Sentence [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art11.sent3:short] to account for the additional load resulting from sliding snow.
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art11.sent1:short] need not apply where

clauses.text: snow from the upper roof is prevented from sliding by a parapet or other effective means, or
the upper roof is not considered slippery and has a slope of less than 20°.

content.text: The total weight of additional snow resulting from sliding shall be taken as half the total weight of snow resulting from the uniform load case prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2:long] with

clauses.text: the accumulation factor C_{a} = 1.0 for the relevant part of the upper roof,

the slope factor, C_{s}, based on the slope of the lower roof, as prescribed in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent5:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent6:short] , and

the sliding snow distributed on the lower roof such that it is a maximum for x = 0 and decreases linearly to 0 at x = x_{d} , as shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art11.figure1:long] , where x and x_{d} are as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art5:long]

articles.title: Valleys in Curved or Sloped Roofs

content.text: For valleys in curved or sloped roofs with a slope α > 10°, in addition to the full and partial load cases defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art3:long] , the non-uniform load cases II and III presented in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art12.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art12.sent3:short] shall be considered to account for sliding, creeping and movement of meltwater.

content.title: Snow loads in valleys of sloped or curved roofs

notes.content: C_{w} = 1, as per [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent3:long] .
C_{s} = 1, as per [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent7:long] .

content.text: For the purposes of calculating snow loads in drifts, the specific weight of snow, γ, shall be taken as 4.0 kN/m^{3} or 0.43S_{S} + 2.2 kN/m^{3} , whichever is lesser.
Snow removal by mechanical, thermal, manual or other means shall not be used as a rationale to reduce design snow loads.

For lattice structures connected to the [REF:term:bldng:building] , and other [REF:term:bldng:building] components or appurtenances involving small width elements subject to significant ice accretion, the weight of ice accretion and the effective area presented to wind shall be as prescribed in [REF:standard:csas37]

Where solar panels are installed on a roof, the snow loads, S, shall be determined in accordance with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent6:short] or with the requirements for roofs without solar panels, whichever produces the most critical effect.
For the purposes of this Article, solar panels shall be classified as

clauses.text: Parallel Flush, where the panels are installed parallel to the roof surface with their upper surface less than or equal to C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ above the roof surface,
Parallel Raised, where the panels are installed parallel to the roof surface with their upper surface greater than C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ above the roof surface, or
Tilted, where the panels are installed at an angle to the roof surface with their highest edge greater than C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ above the roof surface.

content.text: For sloped roofs with solar panels, the snow loads, S, shall be determined in accordance with the requirements for roofs without solar panels, except that the slope factor, C_{s}, shall be

clauses.text: taken as 1.0 for roof areas extending upslope from the downslope edge of a panel or array of panels at an angle of 45° from each side edge of the panel or array, and
as specified in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent5:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art2.sent7:short] for all other roof areas.

content.text: For sloped roofs with Parallel Flush solar panels, the snow loads, S, shall be determined in accordance with the requirements for roofs without solar panels, except that

clauses.text: C_{s} shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent3:short] ,
where the gap width, w_{g}, between the panels along the roof slope is greater than or equal to the panel width, w_{p}, along the roof slope, the accumulation factor, C_{a}, shall be taken as

subclauses.text: 0.0 for the panels,
2.0 for roof areas within a distance of w_{p} downslope from a downslope panel edge, and
1.0 for all other roof areas

clauses.text: where the gap width, w_{g}, between the panels along the roof slope is less than the panel width, w_{p}, along the roof slope, C_{a} shall be taken as

subclauses.text: 0.0 for panel areas within a distance of w_{g} downslope from an upslope panel edge,
1.0 for other panel areas,
2.0 for roof areas in gaps between the panels, and
1.0 for all other roof areas

content.text: For roofs with Parallel Raised solar panels, the snow loads, S, shall be determined in accordance with the requirements for roofs without solar panels, except that

clauses.text: where the roof is flat, C_{a} shall be taken as

subclauses.text: 1.0 for the panels,
1.0 for roof areas not under the panels,

1.0 for roof areas under the panels within a distance of min(2h_{g},2w_{g}) from a panel edge, where h_{g} is the gap height between the lower surface of the panels and the roof surface, and w_{g} is the gap width between the panels, and
0.0 for other roof areas under the panels

clauses.text: where the roof is sloped, the snow loads, S, derived from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause1:short] shall be used, except that

subclauses.text: C_{s} shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent3:short] ,
S shall be taken as 0.0 on the panels, and

S for all roof areas shall be taken as the sum of S on the panels, as derived from [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause1.subclause1:short] and shifted by a distance of w_{p} downslope onto the roof, where w_{p} is the panel width along the roof slope, and S on the roof areas, as derived from  Subclauses [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause1.subclause2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent5.clause1.subclause4:short]

content.text: For flat roofs with Tilted solar panels, the snow loads, S, shall be determined in accordance with the requirements for roofs without solar panels, except that

clauses.text: C_{a} shall be taken as 0.0 for the panels,

C_{a} shall be taken as 1.0 for roof areas beyond a distance of 5(h – C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ) from the lowest edge of the panels, where h is the height of the highest edge of the panels above the roof surface,

except as provided in  Clauses [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent6.clause4:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent6.clause5:short] , for roof areas within a distance of 5(h – C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ) from the lowest edge of the panels, C_{a} shall be taken as

subclauses.text: 1.25 for (h_{g} – C_{b}C_{w}S_{s}/γ) ≤ 0.3 m , where h_{g} is the gap height between the lowest edge of the panels and the roof surface,

clauses.text: except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent6.clause5:short] , C_{a} shall be taken as 2.0 for roof areas within a distance of w_{ph} beyond the lowest edge of the panels, where w_{ph} is the horizontal projection of the panel width, w_{p}, along the sloped panel edges, and

where the panels, panel supports or back plates obstruct snow from sliding under the panels, the load of the increased volume of snow in the gaps between the panels shall be considered to be uniformly distributed.

content.text: The specified wind loads for a [REF:term:bldng:building] and its components shall be determined using the Static, Dynamic or Wind Tunnel Procedure as stated in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art1.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art1.sent5:short] .

For the design of [REF:term:bldng:buildings] that are not dynamically sensitive, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent1:long] , one of the following procedures shall be used to determine the specified wind loads:

clauses.text: the Static Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3:long] ,
the Dynamic Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art8:long] , or
the Wind Tunnel Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art14:long]

content.text: For the design of [REF:term:bldng:buildings] that are dynamically sensitive, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent2:long] , one of the following procedures shall be used to determine the specified wind loads:

clauses.text: the Dynamic Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art8:long] , or
the Wind Tunnel Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art14:long]

content.text: For the design of [REF:term:bldng:buildings] that may be subject to wake buffeting or channelling effects from nearby [REF:term:bldng:buildings] , or that are very dynamically sensitive, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent3:long] , the Wind Tunnel Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art14:long] , shall be used to determine the specified wind loads.
For the design of cladding and secondary structural members, one of the following procedures shall be used to determine the specified wind loads:

clauses.text: the Static Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3:long] , or
the Wind Tunnel Procedure described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art14:long]

content.text: Computational fluid dynamics shall not be used to determine the specified wind loads for a [REF:term:bldng:building] and its components. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote51:short] .)

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent3:short] , a [REF:term:bldng:building] is permitted to be classified as not dynamically sensitive.
A [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be classified as dynamically sensitive if

clauses.text: its lowest natural frequency is less than 1 Hz and greater than 0.25 Hz ,
its height is greater than 60 m , or

its height is greater than 4 times its minimum effective width, where the effective width, w, of a [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be taken as [EQ:display:eg02684a]where the summations are over the height of the [REF:term:bldng:building] for a given wind direction, h_{i} is the height above [REF:term:grade:grade] to level i, and w_{i} is the width normal to the wind direction at height h_{i}; the minimum effective width is the lowest value of the effective width considering all wind directions.

clauses.text: its lowest natural frequency is less than or equal to 0.25 Hz , or
it contains a human occupancy, and its height is more than 6 times its minimum effective width as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art2.sent2.clause3:medium] .

content.text: The net wind load for the [REF:term:bldng:building] as a whole shall be the algebraic difference of the loads on the windward and leeward surfaces, and in some cases, may be calculated as the sum of the products of the external pressures or suctions and the areas of the surfaces over which they are averaged as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent1:short] .

The net specified pressure due to wind on part or all of a surface of a [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be the algebraic difference, such as to produce the most critical effect, of the external pressure or suction calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent1:short] and the specified internal pressure or suction due to wind calculated as follows:[EQ:display:es007876q1]where [LIST:variable]

content.text: The reference velocity pressure, q, shall be the appropriate value determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long] , based on a probability of being exceeded in any one year of 1 in 50.

The exposure factor, C_{e}, shall be based on the reference height, h, determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent6:short] , for the surface or part of the surface under consideration and shall be

clauses.text: (h/10)^{0.2} but not less than 0.9 for open terrain, where open terrain is level terrain with only scattered [REF:term:bldng:buildings] , trees or other obstructions, open water or shorelines thereof,

0.7(h/12)^{0.3} but not less than 0.7 for rough terrain, where rough terrain is suburban, urban or wooded terrain extending upwind from the [REF:term:bldng:building] uninterrupted for at least 1 km or 20 times the height of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , whichever is greater, or

an intermediate value between the two exposures defined in  Clauses [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent5.clause1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent5.clause2:short] in cases where the site is less than 1 km or 20 times the height of the [REF:term:bldng:building] from a change in terrain conditions, whichever is greater, provided an appropriate interpolation method is used (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote53:short] ).

content.text: The reference height, h, shall be determined as follows:

clauses.text: for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] whose height is less than or equal to 20 m and less than the smaller plan dimension, h shall be the mid-height of the roof above [REF:term:grade:grade] , but not less than 6 m ,
for other [REF:term:bldng:buildings] , h shall be

subclauses.text: the actual height above [REF:term:grade:grade] of the point on the windward wall for which external pressures are being calculated,
the mid-height of the roof for pressures on surfaces parallel to the wind direction, and
the mid-height of the [REF:term:bldng:building] for pressures on the leeward wall, and

clauses.text: for any structural element exposed to wind, h shall be the mid-height of the element above the ground.

content.text: The exposure factor for internal pressures, C_{ei}, shall be determined as follows:

clauses.text: for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] whose height is greater than 20 m and that have a dominant opening, C_{ei} shall be equal to the exposure factor for external pressures, C_{e}, calculated at the mid-height of the dominant opening, and

for other [REF:term:bldng:buildings] , C_{ei} shall be the same as the exposure factor for external pressures, C_{e}, calculated for a reference height, h, equal to the mid-height of the [REF:term:bldng:building] or 6 m , whichever is greater.

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art3.sent9:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.sent1:long] , the gust effect factor, C_{g}, shall be one of the following values:

clauses.text: 2.0 for the [REF:term:bldng:building] as a whole and main structural members, or
2.5 for external pressures and suctions on secondary structural members, including cladding.

content.text: For cases where C_{g} and C_{p} are combined into a single product, C_{g}C_{p}, the values of C_{g} and C_{p} need not be independently specified. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6:long] )

content.text: Applicable values of external pressure coefficients, C_{p}, are provided in

clauses.text: Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent9:short] , and
[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6:long] for certain shapes of low [REF:term:bldng:buildings] .

content.text: For the design of the main structural system, the value of C_{p} shall be established as follows, where H is the height of the [REF:term:bldng:building] and D is the width of the [REF:term:bldng:building] parallel to the wind direction:

clauses.text: on the windward face,[LIST:variable]
on the leeward face,[LIST:variable]
on the walls parallel to the wind, C_{p} = –0.7 .

content.text: For the design of roofs, the value of C_{p} shall be established as follows, where x is the distance from the upwind edge of the roof:

clauses.text: for H/D ≥ 1.0 , C_{p} = –1.0 , and
for H/D < 1.0,[LIST:variable]

items.description: = –1.0 for x ≤ H, and= –0.5 for x > H.

content.text: For the design of the cladding and of secondary structural elements supporting the cladding, the value of C_{p} shall be established as follows, where W and D are the widths of the [REF:term:bldng:building] :

clauses.text: on walls, C_{p} shall be taken as ±0.9 , except that within a distance equal to the larger of 0.1D and 0.1W from a [REF:term:bldng:building] corner, the negative value of C_{p} shall be taken as –1.2 ,

on walls where vertical ribs deeper than 1 m are placed on the facade, C_{p} shall be taken as ±0.9, except that, within a distance equal to the larger of 0.2D and 0.2W from a [REF:term:bldng:building] corner, the negative value of C_{p} shall be taken as –1.4, and
on roofs, C_{p} shall be taken as –1.0 , except that

subclauses.text: within a distance equal to the larger of 0.1D and 0.1W from a roof edge, C_{p} shall be taken as –1.5 ,

in a zone that is within a distance equal to the larger of 0.2W and 0.2D from a roof corner, C_{p} shall be taken as –2.3 but is permitted to be taken as –2.0 for roofs with perimeter parapets that are higher than 1 m , and

on lower levels of flat stepped roofs, positive pressure coefficients established for the walls of the steps apply for a distance b (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.figure4:long] for the definition of b).

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent6:short] , for the design of balcony [REF:term:guard:guards] , the internal pressure coefficient, C_{pi}, shall be taken as zero and the value of C_{p} shall be taken as ±0.9 , except that, within a distance equal to the larger of 0.1W and 0.1D from a [REF:term:bldng:building] corner, C_{p} shall be taken as ±1.2 .

Where the top of the balcony [REF:term:guard:guard] is 2.0 m or less below the roof surface, the values of C_{p} shall be taken as equal to those determined for parapets in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent7:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent8:short] .
To determine the contribution from parapets to the wind loads on the main structural system, the values of C_{p} shall be taken as

clauses.text: on the outer faces, equal to those on the walls below,
on the inner face of the windward parapet, equal to that on the upwind edge of a roof surface at the level of the top of the parapet, and
on the inner faces of the other parapets, zero.

content.text: For the structural design of parapets themselves, the values of C_{p} shall be taken as equal to those specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art5.sent7:short] , except that the value of C_{p} on the inner face of the leeward parapet shall be taken as equal to that on the outer face of the windward parapet.
For the design of cladding on parapets, the values of C_{p} shall be taken as

clauses.text: on the outer vertical surfaces, equal to those on the cladding on the walls below, and
on the inner and top surfaces, equal to those on the cladding of a roof surface at the level of the top of the parapet.

content.text: For the design of [REF:term:bldng:buildings] with a height, H, that is both less than or equal to 20 m and less than the smaller plan dimension, the values of the product of the pressure coefficient and gust factor, C_{g}C_{p}, provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.sent9:short] are permitted to be used.

For the design of the main structural system of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , which is affected by wind pressures on more than one surface as shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.figure1:long] , the values of C_{g}C_{p} are provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.table1:long]

notes.content: The [REF:term:bldng:building] must be designed for all wind directions. Each corner must be considered in turn as the windward corner shown in the sketches. For all roof slopes, Load Case A and Load Case B are required as two separate loading conditions to generate the wind actions, including torsion, to be resisted by the structural system.
For the design of [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] , exclusive of anchorages to the frame, only 70% of the effective load is to be considered.

The reference height, h, for pressures is the mid-height of the roof or 6 m, whichever is greater. The eave height, H, may be substituted for the mid-height of the roof if the roof slope is less than 7°.

End-zone width y should be the greater of 6 m or 2z, where z is the width of the gable-wall end zone defined for Load Case B below. Alternatively, for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] with frames, the end-zone width y may be the distance between the end and the first interior frame.
End-zone width z is the lesser of 10% of the least horizontal dimension and 40% of height, H, but not less than 4% of the least horizontal dimension or 1 m.

For B/H > 5 in Load Case A, the negative coefficients listed for surfaces 2 and 2E in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6.table1:long] should only be applied on an area whose width is 2.5H measured from the windward eave. The pressures on the remainder of the windward roof should be reduced to the pressures for the leeward roof.

content.text: Except where the wind loads are derived from the combined C_{g}C_{p} values determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art6:long] , [REF:term:bldng:buildings] and structural members shall be capable of withstanding the effects of the following loads:

clauses.text: the full wind loads acting along each of the 2 principal horizontal axes considered separately,

75% of the wind loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art9.sent1.clause1:short] but offset from the central geometric axis of the [REF:term:bldng:building] by 15% of its width normal to the direction of the force to produce the worst load effect,
75% of the wind loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art9.sent1.clause1:short] but with both axes considered simultaneously, and

56% of the wind loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect7.art9.sent1.clause1:short] but with both axes considered simultaneously and offset from the central geometric axis of the [REF:term:bldng:building] by 15% of its width normal to the direction of the force.

content.text: In the design of interior walls and [REF:term:prttn:partitions] , due consideration shall be given to differences in air pressure on opposite sides of the wall or [REF:term:prttn:partition] which may result from

clauses.text: pressure differences between the windward and leeward sides of a [REF:term:bldng:building] ,
stack effects due to a difference in air temperature between the exterior and interior of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , and
air pressurization by the mechanical services of the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

content.text: The effects of wind loads on exterior ornamentations, equipment and appendages, including the increase in exposed area as a result of ice buildup as prescribed in [REF:standard:csas37] shall be considered in the structural design of the connections and the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

Where there are a number of similar components, the net increase in force is permitted to be based on the total area for all similar components as opposed to the summation of forces of individual elements.

Positive (C_{g}C_{p})_{net} values denote net forces acting in a downward direction on the canopy, whereas negative (C_{g}C_{p})_{net} values denote net forces acting in an upward direction on the canopy. The canopy must be designed to resist both the positive and negative net forces.

= seismic force resisting system, that part of the structural system that has been considered in the design to provide the required resistance to the earthquake forces and effects defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long] ,
= horizontal force factor for part or portion of a [REF:term:bldng:building] and its anchorage, as given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18.sent1:long] ,
= design spectral acceleration, expressed as a ratio to gravitational acceleration, at period T, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent6:long] ,
= average undrained shear strength, in kPa, in the top 30 m of [REF:term:l:soil] ,
= period, in s,

= fundamental lateral period of vibration of the [REF:term:bldng:building] or structure, in s, in the direction under consideration, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent3:long] ,

= total design displacement of any point in a seismically isolated structure, within or above the isolation system, obtained by calculating the mean + (I_{E} × the standard deviation) of the peak horizontal displacements from all sets of ground motion time histories analyzed, but not less than √I_{E} × the mean, where the peak horizontal displacement is based on the vector sum of the two orthogonal horizontal displacements considered for each time step,

= fundamental lateral period of vibration of the [REF:term:bldng:building] or structure, in s, in the direction under consideration, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1.sent7:long] ,
= floor torque at level x, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent11:long] ,
= specified lateral earthquake force at the base of the structure, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11:long] ,
= specified lateral earthquake force at the base of the structure, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long] ,
= lateral earthquake elastic force at the base of the structure, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long] ,
= adjusted lateral earthquake elastic force at the base of the structure, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art12:long] ,
= specified lateral earthquake force on an element or component, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art18:long] ,

= specified lateral earthquake force at the base of the structure, as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1.sent7:long] , for application in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art1:long] ,
= average shear wave velocity, in m/s, in the top 30 m of [REF:term:l:soil] or [REF:term:rck:rock,]

= specified [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] , as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4.art1:long] , except that the minimum [REF:term:prttn:partition] weight as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect4.art1.sent3:long] need not exceed 0.5 kPa , plus 25% of the specified snow load as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect6:long] , plus 60% of the storage load for areas used for storage, except that [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garages] need not be considered storage areas, and the full contents of any tanks (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote64:short] ),
= portion of W that is located at or is assigned to level i or x respectively,
= weight of a part or portion of a structure, e.g., cladding, [REF:term:prttn:partitions] and appendages,
= site designation, either X_{V} or X_{S},
= site designation in terms of Site Class, where S is the Site Class determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent3:long] ,
= site designation in terms of V_{s30}, where V is the V_{s30} value calculated from in situ measurements of shear wave velocity,
= site designation X_{V} with V_{s30} = 450 m/s ,
= average displacement of the structure at level x, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent10:long] , and
= maximum displacement of the structure at level x, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art11.sent10:long] .

content.text: The [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be designed to meet the requirements of this Subsection and of the design standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long]
Structures shall be designed with a clearly defined load path, or paths, that will transfer the inertial forces generated in an earthquake to the supporting ground.
The structure shall have a clearly defined SFRS, as defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art2:long]
The SFRS shall be designed to resist 100% of the earthquake loads and their effects. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote65:short] .)

All structural framing elements not considered to be part of the SFRS must be investigated and shown to behave elastically or to have sufficient non-linear capacity to support their gravity loads while undergoing earthquake-induced deformations calculated from the deflections determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art13:long]
Stiff elements that are not considered part of the SFRS, such as concrete, masonry, brick or precast walls or panels, shall be

clauses.text: separated from all structural elements of the [REF:term:bldng:building] such that no interaction takes place as the [REF:term:bldng:building] undergoes deflections due to earthquake effects as calculated in this Subsection, or
made part of the SFRS and satisfy the requirements of this Subsection.

content.text: Stiffness imparted to the structure from elements not part of the SFRS, other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent6:short] , shall not be used to resist earthquake deflections but shall be accounted for

clauses.text: in calculating the period of the structure for determining forces if the added stiffness decreases the fundamental lateral period by more than 15%,

in determining the irregularity of the structure, except the additional stiffness shall not be used to make an irregular SFRS regular or to reduce the effects of torsion (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote67:short] ), and
in designing the SFRS if inclusion of the elements not part of the SFRS in the analysis has an adverse effect on the SFRS (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote67:short] ).

content.text: Structural modeling shall be representative of the magnitude and spatial distribution of the mass of the [REF:term:bldng:building] and of the stiffness of all elements of the SFRS, including stiff elements that are not separated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art3.sent6:long] , and shall account for

clauses.text: the effect of cracked sections in reinforced concrete and reinforced masonry elements,
the effect of the finite size of members and joints,
sway effects arising from the interaction of gravity loads with the displaced configuration of the structure, and
other effects that influence the lateral stiffness of the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

content.text: For site designation X, as determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent2:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent3:short] , the peak ground acceleration, PGA(X), the peak ground velocity, PGV(X), and the 5%-damped spectral acceleration values, S_{a}(T,X), at periods T of 0.2 s , 0.5 s , 1.0 s , 2.0 s , 5.0 s and 10.0 s shall

clauses.text: except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent4:short] , be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3:long] , and
except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art23:long] , correspond to a 2% probability of exceedance in 50 years .

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent3:short] , the site designation referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be determined using the average shear wave velocity, V_{s30}, calculated from in situ measurements of shear wave velocity, as follows:

clauses.text: for the ground profiles described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.table1:long] , the site designation shall be determined in accordance with the Table, and
for all other ground profiles, the site designation shall be X_{V}, where V is the value of V_{s30}.

undrained shear strength, s_{u} < 25 kPa

content.text: Where V_{s30} calculated from in situ measurements is not available, the site designation referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be X_{S}, where S is the Site Class determined using the energy-corrected average standard penetration resistance, [EQ:inline:eg02520a]_{60}, or the average undrained shear strength, [EQ:inline:gg00550a], in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8.art4.table2:long] , [EQ:inline:eg02520a]_{60} and [EQ:inline:gg00550a] being calculated based on rational analysis. (See  Notes [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote70:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.appendix.appnote69:short] .)
