articles.title: Crawl Spaces and Attic or Roof Spaces

content.text: Unconditioned and unoccupied crawl spaces and [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof spaces] shall be ventilated by natural or mechanical means as required by Part 5. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote6:short] .)

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent4:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent6:short] , an enclosed [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] for five or more motor vehicles shall have a mechanical ventilation system designed to

clauses.text: limit the concentration of carbon monoxide to not more than 100 parts per million parts of air,
limit the concentration of nitrogen dioxide to not more than 3 parts per million parts of air, where the majority of the vehicles stored are powered by diesel-fuelled engines, or

provide, during operating hours, a continuous supply of outdoor air at a rate of not less than 3.9 L/s for each square metre of [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect3.subsect1.art21:long] ).

content.text: Mechanical ventilation systems provided in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1.clause1:medium] shall be controlled by carbon monoxide monitoring devices, and systems provided in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1.clause2:medium] shall be controlled by nitrogen dioxide or other acceptable monitoring devices. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote8:short] .)

Mechanical ventilation systems provided in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1:short] shall be designed such that the pressure in the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] is less than the pressure in adjoining [REF:term:bldng:buildings ] of other [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] , or in adjacent portions of the same [REF:term:bldng:building] having a different [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] .

In [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garages] subject to the requirements of  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent2:short] , where motor vehicles are parked by mechanical means, the ventilation requirements may be reduced by one half.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent6:short] , ticket and attendant booths of [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garages] shall be pressurized with a supply of uncontaminated air.

The requirements of  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art3.sent5:short] shall not apply to [REF:term:pn-r-tr:open-air storeys] in a [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] .

Heat recovery ventilators with rated capacities of not less than 25 L/s and not more than 200 L/s shall be installed in accordance with  Subsection [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long]
Air contaminants of concern within [REF:term:bldng:buildings] shall

clauses.text: be removed insofar as is possible at their points of origin, and

not be permitted to accumulate in concentrations greater than those permitted by applicable provincial or territorial requirements or, in the absence of such requirements, by good engineering practice such as that described in the publications listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] , measured using the methodology described therein.

content.text: Systems serving spaces that contain sources of contamination and systems serving other occupied parts of the [REF:term:bldng:building] but located in or running through spaces that contain sources of contamination shall be designed in such a manner as to prevent the spread of such contamination to other occupied parts of the [REF:term:bldng:building] .
Heating, ventilating and air-conditioning systems shall be designed to minimize the growth and spread of bio-contaminants.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art5:long] , systems for the ventilation of commercial cooking equipment shall be designed, constructed and installed to conform to [REF:standard:nfpa96]

This Subsection applies to the design, construction and installation of air duct distribution systems serving heating, ventilating and air-conditioning systems other than those in [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] covered by Part 9.
HVAC systems that generate condensate or introduce liquid water into the airstream in the ducts shall be equipped with drain pans that are

clauses.text: designed in accordance with Section 5.10, Drain Pans, of [REF:standard:ashrae62.1]
provided with an outlet that is piped to the outside of the airstream in a location where condensate can be safely disposed of,
installed so that water does not stagnate and drains from the pan, and
designed and installed so as to be accessible for cleaning and maintenance.

content.text: Drain pans and associated piping shall be constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials that do not promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms.

All ducts, duct connectors, associated fittings and [REF:term:plnm:plenums] used in air duct systems shall be constructed of materials as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art1:long]
Ducts that are used in a location where they may be subjected to excessive moisture shall have no appreciable loss of strength when wet and shall be resistant to moisture-induced corrosion.
All ductwork and fittings shall be constructed and installed as recommended in SMACNA Manuals and ASHRAE Standards.

All duct materials shall be suitable for exposure to the temperature and humidity of the air being carried and shall be resistant to corrosion caused by contaminants in the air being conveyed in the duct.
Air duct systems shall have tight-fitting connections throughout.

Coverings, linings and associated adhesives and insulation used in air ducts, [REF:term:plnm:plenums] and other parts of air duct systems shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art4:long]

Duct linings shall be installed so that they will not interfere with the operation of volume or balancing dampers or of [REF:term:fr-dmpr:fire dampers] , [REF:term:fr-tp-fl:fire stop flaps] and other [REF:term:clr:closures] .
The clearance of ducts and [REF:term:plnm:plenums] from [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] materials shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art6:long]

In a [REF:term:ca-cc:care] or [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] , air from one [REF:term:t:suite] shall not be circulated to any other [REF:term:t:suite] or to a [REF:term:pblc-crr:public corridor] .

Except as permitted by  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art7.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent6:long] , air duct systems serving [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garages] shall not be directly interconnected with other parts of the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

[REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent10:long] are permitted to exhaust through an enclosed [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] prior to exhausting to the outdoors, provided

clauses.text: the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] 's exhaust system runs continuously,
the capacity of the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] 's exhaust system is equal to or exceeds the volume of the exhaust entering the garage, and

a leakage rate 1 smoke/ [REF:term:fr-dmpr:fire damper] rated in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs1121] is provided near the duct outlet location in the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] to prevent air from the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] from entering the exhaust ductwork system in the event the [REF:term:bldng:building] 's exhaust fan is shut down.

content.text: In ventilating systems that exhaust air to the outdoors, provision shall be made for the admission of a supply of makeup air in sufficient quantity so that the operation of the exhaust system and other exhaust equipment or combustion equipment is not adversely affected.
Makeup air facilities required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art8.sent1:short] shall be interlocked with the exhaust devices they serve so that both operate together.

Where makeup air facilities are intended to introduce air directly from the outdoors to occupied parts of the [REF:term:bldng:building] in winter, they shall incorporate means of tempering that air to maintain the indoor design temperature.

articles.title: Supply, Return, Intake and Exhaust Air Openings

content.text: Supply, return and exhaust air openings located less than 2 m above the floor in rooms or spaces in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] shall be protected by grilles having openings of a size that will not allow the passage of a 15 mm diam sphere.
Outdoor air intakes shall be located so that

clauses.text: the quality of the air entering the [REF:term:bldng:building] complies with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent3:short] , and
they are separated a minimum distance from sources of contaminants in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art9.table1:long]

content.title: Minimum Distances of Air Intakes from Sources of Contaminants

content.value: Minimum Distance of Outdoor Air Intake, m
Garage entry of a garage for 5 or more motor vehicles, automobile loading area and drive-in queue
Truck loading area or dock, and bus parking
Thoroughfare, arterial road, freeway, and highway
Discharge from evaporative heat rejection systems

content.text: Outdoor air intakes shall be installed not less than 0.3 m above roofs, landscape grades or other surfaces, taking into account anticipated snow accumulation levels.

Exterior openings for outdoor air intakes and exhaust outlets shall be shielded from the entry of snow and rain and shall be fitted with corrosion-resistant screens of mesh having openings not larger than 15 mm , except where experience has shown that climatic conditions require larger openings to prevent the screen openings from icing over.
Screens required in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art9.sent4:short] shall be accessible for maintenance.
[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] grilles, diffusers and other devices covering supply, return, intake and exhaust openings shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art7:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent2:short] , [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] of non-mechanical ventilating systems serving separate rooms or spaces shall not be combined.

[REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] of non-mechanical ventilating systems serving similar [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancies] may be combined immediately below the point of final delivery to the outdoors, such as at the base of a roof ventilator.
[REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] of ventilating systems shall have provision for the removal of condensation where this may be a problem.
Exhaust outlets shall be designed to prevent backdraft under wind conditions.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent6:short] , exhaust systems shall discharge directly to the outdoors. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote12:short] .)
Exhaust systems are permitted to exhaust into a [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] , provided

clauses.text: they serve rooms that are accessible only from that [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] ,
the exhaust contains no contaminants that would adversely affect the air quality in the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote13:short] ), and
they are designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art7.sent3:long] .

content.text: [REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] connected to laundry-drying equipment shall be

clauses.text: independent of other [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] ,
accessible for inspection and cleaning, and
constructed of a smooth corrosion-resistant material.

content.text: Where collective venting of multiple installations of laundry-drying equipment is used, the ventilation system shall

clauses.text: be connected to a common [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] that is vented by one central exhaust fan,
include an interlock to activate the central exhaust fan when laundry-drying equipment is in use, and
be provided with make-up air.

content.text: [REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] or vents connected to laundry-drying equipment shall discharge directly to the outdoors.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent12:short] and except for self-contained systems serving individual [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] serving rooms containing water closets, urinals, basins, showers or slop sinks shall be independent of other [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] .

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent12:short] and except for self-contained systems serving individual [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] serving rooms containing residential cooking equipment shall be independent of other [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] .

Two or more exhaust systems described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent10:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent11:short] may be interconnected or connected with [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] serving other areas of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , provided

clauses.text: the connections are made at the inlet of an exhaust fan, and all interconnected systems are equipped with suitable back pressure devices to prevent the passage of odours from one system to another when the fan is not in operation, or

the [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] discharge to a shaft that is served by an exhaust fan having a capacity that is equal to or greater than the combined capacity of the exhaust fans discharging to the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] multiplied by the operation diversity factor, provided that the exhaust fan serving the shaft operates continuously (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote15:short] ).

content.text: Where [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] containing air from [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned spaces] pass through or are adjacent to unconditioned spaces, the ducts shall be constructed to prevent condensation from forming on the inside or outside of the ducts.
Return-air systems shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art8:long]
Where a ceiling space is used as a return-air [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3:long] shall apply.
A [REF:term:pblc-crr:public corridor] or [REF:term:xt:exit] shall not be used as a return-air [REF:term:plnm:plenum] .
Underground ducts shall

clauses.text: be constructed and installed to provide interior drainage from and access to all low points,
not be connected directly to a sewer, and
be installed and constructed of materials recommended by ASHRAE and SMACNA Standards and HRAI Manuals.

content.text: A clean-out or pump-out connection shall be provided in an underground duct system at every low point of the duct system.
Air filters for air duct systems shall conform to the requirements for Class 2 air filter units as described in [REF:standard:ulcs111]

When electrostatic-type filters are used, they shall be installed so as to ensure that the electric circuit is automatically de-energized when filter access doors are opened or, in [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , when the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] circulation fan is not operating.

Where outdoor air quality conditions do not meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent2:long] , ventilation required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] shall be provided by a ventilation system designed to include devices that reduce particles and gases to the maximum acceptable levels described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent2:long] prior to the introduction of outdoor air to indoor occupied spaces.

Where contaminants of concern are present in the outdoor air of the local area of the [REF:term:bldng:building] site, ventilation required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] shall be provided by a ventilation system designed to include devices that reduce the concentrations of contaminants to those permitted in the ACGIH's [REF:standard:acgih-iv-mrp] prior to the introduction of outdoor air to indoor occupied spaces.
Evaporative heat rejection systems shall

clauses.text: incorporate a drift eliminator or other means to minimize the dispersion of entrained water droplets, and
have a design discharge velocity that does not exceed the maximum discharge velocity recommended by the manufacturer.

content.text: Evaporative heat rejection systems shall be designed so that water continuously circulates through all parts of the system that are normally wetted when the system is operating.

Evaporative heat rejection systems and their components shall be constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials that do not promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms and that are compatible with disinfectants, biocides and other cleaning agents.
Evaporative heat rejection systems shall be installed such that

clauses.text: no discharge air bypasses the drift eliminator or other means referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art15.sent1.clause1:medium] , and
the systems are accessible for cleaning, inspection and maintenance.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art15.sent6:short] , air discharged from evaporative heat rejection systems shall discharge away from the [REF:term:bldng:building] , so as to not re-enter it, to a distance not less than

clauses.text: 2.15 m above sidewalks and driveways,
7.6 m from outdoor air intakes,
3 m horizontally or vertically from exterior doors and operable windows, and
3 m horizontally or vertically from occupiable outdoor spaces, excluding maintenance spaces.

content.text: Air discharged from evaporative heat rejection systems in health care facilities shall discharge away from the [REF:term:bldng:building] in compliance with [REF:standard:csaz317.2] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote16:short] .)
Air intakes of evaporative heat rejection systems shall incorporate protective measures to minimize the entrainment of vegetation and other organic matter.

Make-up water connections shall be equipped with backflow prevention devices that conform to Article 2.6.2.1. of Division B of Book II, (Plumbing Systems), of this code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote17:short] .)
Water treatment systems and equipment for controlling the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms shall

clauses.text: be provided in accordance with [REF:external:ashrae12:Section 7.6.2. of ] [REF:standard:ashrae12] and
include means for drainage, dilution, cleaning, and application of chemicals for the control of scale, corrosion and biological contamination.

content.text: Drains, overflows and blow-downs shall be connected to the [REF:term:bldng:building] 's drainage system in accordance with [REF:external:npc:Clause 2.4.2.1.(1)(e) of Division B of Book II, (Plumbing Systems), of this code]  [REF:standard:nrcc-npc] .
Evaporative heat rejection systems shall be provided with access openings, service platforms, fixed ladders and fall-restraint connections to allow inspection, maintenance and testing.

articles.title: Evaporative Air Coolers, Misters, Atomizers, Air Washers and Humidifiers

content.text: Evaporative air coolers, misters, atomizers, air washers and humidifiers shall be designed in accordance with [REF:external:ashrae12:Sections 8 and 9 of ] [REF:standard:ashrae12]
Systems referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art16.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text: be designed so that water continuously circulates through all parts of the system that are normally wetted when the system is operating, and
incorporate a method of preventing water stagnation within the system itself and the internal plumbing when the system is not operating.

content.text: All components of systems referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art16.sent1:short] , including filters and evaporation media, shall be constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials that do not promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms.
Associated sumps shall

clauses.text: be constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials that do not promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms,
include auxiliary drains to prevent the overflow of water into ductwork, and
be installed so that they can be flushed, drained, cleaned and disinfected.

content.text: Where misters, atomizers or air washers are used in ductwork, the affected duct section shall be

clauses.text: designed to ensure drainage of unevaporated and accumulated water, and
constructed of corrosion-resistant, non-porous materials that do not promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms.

content.text: Make-up water connections shall be equipped with backflow prevention devices that conform to Article 2.6.2.1. of Division B of Book II, (Plumbing Systems), of this code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote19:short] .)
Fans for heating, ventilating and air-conditioning systems shall be located and installed so that their operation

clauses.text: does not adversely affect the draft required for proper operation of fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] , and
does not allow the air in the duct system to be contaminated by air or gases from the [REF:term:blr:boiler] room or [REF:term:frnc:furnace] room.

content.text: Fans and associated air-handling equipment, such as air washers, filters and heating and cooling units, when installed on the roof or elsewhere outside the [REF:term:bldng:building] , shall be of a type designed for outdoor use.
Vibration isolation connectors in air duct systems shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art2:long]
Tape used for sealing joints in air ducts, [REF:term:plnm:plenums] and other parts of air duct systems shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art3:long]

Except as provided in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art3:long] , the products of combustion from oil-, gas- and solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] shall be vented in conformance with the requirements in the applicable [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] installation standard listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art5:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art5:long] , vented products of combustion, other than those referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] , shall be discharged away from the [REF:term:bldng:building] , so as not to re-enter it, to a distance not less than

clauses.text: 2.15 m above sidewalks and driveways,
3 m from outdoor air intakes,
3 m horizontally or vertically from doors and operable windows, and
3 m horizontally or vertically from occupiable outdoor spaces, excluding maintenance spaces.

content.text: Rectangular [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:masonry or concrete chimneys] not more than 12 m in height shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9:long] if they serve

clauses.text: [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] with a combined total rated heat output of 120 kW or less, or
fireplaces.

content.text: [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:Masonry or concrete chimneys] other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art2.sent1:short] shall be designed and installed in conformance with the appropriate requirements in [REF:standard:nfpa211]
Single wall metal smoke stacks shall be designed and installed in conformance with [REF:standard:nfpa211]
Access ladders for [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] , when provided, shall consist of steel or bronze rungs, built into the walls of the [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] .
Rungs for external ladders shall begin at not less than 2.5 m from ground level.

This Subsection applies to laboratories where [REF:term:dngr-gd:dangerous goods] , including [REF:term:flmmbl-l:flammable liquids] and [REF:term:cmbtbl-l:combustible liquids] , are used in normal laboratory operations in quantities or in a manner that creates a fire or explosion hazard.
A laboratory shall be provided with continuous mechanical ventilation designed to ensure that [REF:term:dngr-gd:dangerous goods] vapours and particles

clauses.text: do not accumulate in the laboratory,
are prevented from migrating to other parts of the [REF:term:bldng:building] ,
do not accumulate in the ventilation system,
are exhausted to the outdoors, and
are not returned to the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

content.text: A ventilation system required by this Subsection shall be provided with monitoring devices to

clauses.text: indicate that the ventilation system is in operation, and
sound an alarm if the ventilation system is malfunctioning.

content.text: A ventilation system required by this Subsection shall be maintained in conformance with Article 5.5.4.1. of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code.
The ventilation system for a power-ventilated enclosure required by Sentence 5.5.4.2.(1) of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code shall

clauses.text: conform to [REF:standard:nfpa91]

provide continuous exhaust ventilation at an air velocity sufficient to prevent the accumulation of [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] or reactive deposits in the power-ventilated enclosure and its [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] system,
confine [REF:term:dngr-gd:dangerous goods] vapours and particles to the area where they are generated and exhaust them to the outdoors,
not return the exhausted air to the [REF:term:bldng:building] , and
be provided with well identified control switches that are

subclauses.text: located outside of the power-ventilated enclosure, and
readily accessible in case of an emergency.

content.text: The power-ventilated enclosure required by Sentence 5.5.4.2.(1) of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code and its [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] system shall

clauses.text: except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4.art4.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4.art4.sent3:short] , be constructed of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] materials compatible with and chemically resistant to the [REF:term:dngr-gd:dangerous goods] vapours and particles being exhausted, and
be provided with access doors to permit inspection and maintenance of the fan assembly and [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] system.

content.text: [REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] materials are permitted in systems described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4.art4.sent1.clause1:medium] if

clauses.text: such materials are required by the corrosive or reactive properties of the [REF:term:dngr-gd:dangerous goods] being used, and
their [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] is not more than 25.

content.text: The [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4.art4.sent2:short] is permitted to be greater than 25 if an automatic fire suppression system is provided inside the power-ventilated enclosure and its [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] system.

Except for [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] installed in [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , fuel-fired heating [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] shall be located, enclosed or separated from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng:building ] in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6:long] (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect10:long] )
Fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] installed outside a [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be designed and constructed for outdoor use.

Every [REF:term:nt-htr:unit heater] using either steam or hot water as the heating medium shall be installed such that the clearances between the [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] and adjacent [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect7.subsect1.art2.table1:long]
A [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] lining or backing shall be provided for every steam or hot water radiator and convector

clauses.text: located in a recess or concealed space, or
attached to the face of a wall of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] or [REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr:encapsulated mass timber construction.]

content.text: Every steam or hot water radiator and convector shall be installed so as to conform to the clearance requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect7.subsect1.art2.table1:long]
Insulation and coverings on pipes shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5.art5:long]
Insulation and coverings on pipes shall be composed of material that will withstand deterioration from softening, melting, mildew and mould at the operating temperature of the system.

Exposed piping or equipment subject to human contact shall be insulated so that the temperature of the exposed surface does not exceed 52°C. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote21:short] .)

subsections.title: Refrigerating Systems and Equipment for Air-conditioning

content.text: Where a cooling unit is combined with a fuel-fired [REF:term:frnc:furnace] in the same duct system, the cooling unit shall be installed

clauses.text: in parallel with the heating [REF:term:frnc:furnace] ,
upstream of the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] provided the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] is designed for such application, or
downstream of the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] provided the cooling unit is designed to prevent excessive temperature or pressure in the refrigeration system.

subsections.title: Piping for Heating and Cooling Systems

content.text: Piping shall be made from materials designed to withstand the effects of temperatures and pressures that may occur in the system. (See  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art19:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9.art1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art7:long] for fire safety requirements.)
Every pipe used in a heating or air-conditioning system shall be installed to allow for expansion and contraction due to temperature changes.
Supports and anchors for piping in a heating or air-conditioning system shall be designed and installed to ensure that undue stress is not placed on the supporting structure.
Clearances between [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material and bare pipes carrying steam or hot water shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect7.subsect1.art2.table1:long]

content.title: Clearance Between Steam or Hot Water Pipes and Combustible Material

content.text: The exposed surface temperature of a steam or hot water radiator shall not exceed 70°C unless precautions are taken to prevent human contact. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote21:long] .)

Where a pipe carrying steam or hot water at a temperature above 120°C passes through a [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] floor, ceiling or wall, the construction shall be protected by a sleeve of metal or other [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material not less than 50 mm larger in diameter than the pipe.
Where piping for heating or air-conditioning systems is enclosed in a shaft, the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art1:long] for shafts shall apply.
Service pipes passing through a storage bin for solid fuel shall be protected or so located as to avoid damage to the pipes.
Except for fuel-thawing pipes, every pipe designed to operate at a temperature of 50°C or above shall be located where solid fuel cannot be stored in contact with it.

Any covering of an access opening through which a person could enter shall be openable from the inside without the use of keys where there is a possibility of the opening being accidentally closed while the system or equipment is being serviced.
Air duct systems shall have no openings other than those required for the proper operation and maintenance of the system.
Access openings shall be provided in duct systems to allow the removal of material that may accumulate in [REF:term:plnm:plenums] and ducts.
When odour removal equipment of the adsorption type is used, it shall be

clauses.text: installed to allow access so that adsorption material can be reactivated or renewed, and
protected from dust accumulation by air filters installed on the inlet side.

content.text: Facilities for flushing and drainage shall be provided where filters are designed to be washed in place.
The fire safety characteristics of heating, ventilating and air-conditioning systems shall comply with  Subsection [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5:long]
Characteristics referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] include but are not limited to

clauses.text: use of [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] materials in duct systems,
[REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread ratings] and smoke-developed ratings of duct and pipe materials and coverings,
installation of equipment relative to property lines, and
requirements for [REF:term:fr-dmpr:fire dampers] and [REF:term:fr-tp-fl:fire stop flaps] .

content.text: Except as provided in  Subsection [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect4:long] , systems serving spaces that contain hazardous gases, dusts or liquids shall be designed, constructed and installed to conform to the requirements of the applicable provincial or territorial regulations or municipal bylaws or, in the absence of such regulations or bylaws, to good engineering practice such as that described in the publications of the National Fire Protection Association and in the British Columbia Fire Code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote22:short] .)
When indoor piping for Class I [REF:term:flmmbl-l:flammable liquids] is installed in a trench, the trench shall be

clauses.text: provided with positive ventilation to the outdoors, or
designed to prevent the accumulation of flammable vapours.

content.text: Fire protection systems for commercial cooking equipment referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art6.sent1:long] using vegetable oil or animal fat shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:ul300] or
[REF:standard:ulcc1254.6]

content.text: [REF:term:fr-dmpr:Fire dampers] shall conform to  Article [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art10:long]
Air handling systems shall incorporate [REF:term:mk-dtctr:smoke detectors] where and as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect4.art12:long]
Where an [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] system is used for smoke removal in a high [REF:term:bldng:building] , the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6.art6:long] shall apply.

Where [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] systems from more than one [REF:term:fr-cmprt:fire compartment] are connected to an [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] in a [REF:term:vrtcl-rv:vertical service space] , the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect3.art4:long] shall apply.

Where ducts penetrate [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] separating [REF:term:xt:exits] from the remainder of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , they shall be in accordance with  Article [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect4.subsect4.art4:long]

This Article applies to every [REF:term:bldng:building] that contains an assembly occupancy, a [REF:term:ca-cc:care occupancy] with individual [REF:term:t:suites] or containing sleeping rooms or bed spaces not within a suite, a residential occupancy, a business and personal services occupancy, or a mercantile occupancy, and that

clauses.text: is served by or contains a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] , or
contains a [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] .

content.text: Carbon monoxide (CO) alarms installed in a residential occupancy or a [REF:term:ca-cc:care occupancy] as required by this Article shall

clauses.text: conform to [REF:standard:csa6.19] ,
be equipped with an integral alarm that satisfies the audibility requirements of [REF:standard:csa6.19] ,

have no disconnect switch between the overcurrent device and the CO alarm, where the CO alarm is powered by the electrical system serving the [REF:term:t:suite] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote23:short] ), and
be installed as recommended by the manufacturer.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short] , where a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] is installed in a [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] or in a [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:ca-cc:care occupancy] , a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: inside each sleeping room or bed space, or
outside each sleeping room or bed space, within 5 m of each door serving a sleeping room or bed space, measured following corridors and doorways.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short] , where a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] serves a residential occupancy or a [REF:term:ca-cc:care occupancy] and is installed in a [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] that is not in a [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] nor in a [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:ca-cc:care occupancy] , a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: either inside each sleeping room or bed space, or if outside, within 5 m of each door serving a sleeping room or bed space, measured following corridors and doorways, in every [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] or [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:ca-cc:care occupancy] that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with the [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] , and
in the [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] .

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short] , for each [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] or [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:ca-cc:care occupancy] that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with a [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] or that is adjacent to an attic or crawl space to which the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] is also adjacent, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: inside each sleeping room or bed space, or
outside each sleeping room or bed space, within 5 m of each bedroom door serving a sleeping room or bed space, measured following corridors and doorways.

content.text: CO alarms installed in an assembly occupancy, a business and personal services occupancy, or a mercantile occupancy as required by this Article shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csa6.19] , notwithstanding the scope of that standard,
[REF:standard:ul2034] , notwithstanding the scope of that standard, or
good engineering practice.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short] , where a fuel-burning appliance serves an assembly occupancy, business and personal services occupancy, or mercantile occupancy, a CO alarm shall be,

clauses.text: where the fuel-burning appliance is part of a system that could circulate or distribute CO to a suite of assembly occupancy, business and personal services occupancy or mercantile occupancy, installed

subclauses.text: on each storey of each suite that may be exposed, and
in a suite containing an assembly major occupancy, each classroom and dedicated gathering room or space, and

clauses.text: installed in the room or space in which the fuel-burning appliance is located.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent9:short] , for each suite of assembly occupancy, business and personal services occupancy, or mercantile occupancy that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with either a [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] or a [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] containing a fuel-burning appliance, or that is adjacent to either an attic or crawl space to which the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] or a [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] containing a fuel-burning appliance is also adjacent, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: on each storey of the adjacent suite,
where the adjacent suite contains an assembly major occupancy, each classroom and dedicated room or space, and
in each [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] containing a fuel-burning appliance.

content.text: CO detectors are permitted to be installed in lieu of CO alarms required by this Article provided the CO detectors

clauses.text: sound audible signals within the location they serve, as described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent3:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent5:number] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent7:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent8:number] ,
are installed in conformance with [REF:standard:ulcs524] , and
form part of the fire alarm system.

content.text: Every ash storage bin shall be constructed of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material.
Every opening in an ash storage bin shall be protected by a tight-fitting metal door with metal frame securely fastened to the bin.
Fireplaces shall conform to the requirements of  Section [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22:long]

appendix.introduction: These Notes are included for explanatory purposes only and do not form part of the requirements. The number that introduces each Note corresponds to the applicable requirement in this Part.

content.content: New buildings tend to be considerably more airtight than older ones. Consequently, these buildings may have a reduced pressurization requirement compared to the normal requirement in order to limit drafts and provide a reasonable level of comfort.

The humidification and relative pressurization of buildings and individual spaces in buildings can be significant factors in compromising the ongoing performance of the building envelope and other environmental separators.

In new construction, HVAC designers should take this issue into consideration and confer with those responsible for the design of the environmental separators so as to limit unintended effects on the environmental separators. In existing buildings, the ability of the environmental separators to resist or accommodate increases in pressure differential or moisture loading should be considered before changes are made to the HVAC system.

HVAC designers should either develop a water management plan or complete a formal risk and hazard assessment to determine what measures are required for the control of legionella. The risk and hazard assessment should include inspections of the building and its surroundings to locate potential sources of legionella and to identify equipment or systems that could promote the growth and spread of legionella. The assessment should also evaluate the risk to building occupants that is associated with any identified equipment or systems, taking into account their design, location and operating conditions.
Further information on minimizing the growth and spread of legionella can be found in the following publications:[LIST:bulleted]

“Legionella and the Prevention of Legionellosis” (World Health Organization, 2007),

“Legionnaires' Disease: Technical Guidance: Part 1: The Control of Legionella Bacteria in Evaporative Cooling Systems, and Part 3: The Control of Legionella Bacteria in Other Risk Systems” (U.K. Health and Safety Executive, 2013), and
“Recognition, Evaluation and Control of Legionella in Building Water Systems” (American Industrial Hygiene Association, 2015).

content.content: In the past, the practice of ventilating buildings with outdoor air assumed that the outdoor air was of better quality than the indoor air. It has become evident that the outdoor air in some areas of Canada may not be of an acceptable quality for ventilating buildings unless certain particles and gases are first removed or reduced. In order to manage the air quality of a building's indoor environment, thus reducing the potential for adverse effects on occupants' health, the quality of outdoor air for building ventilation purposes must be addressed.

In the past, the practice of ventilating buildings with outdoor air assumed that the outdoor air was of better quality than the indoor air. It has become evident that the outdoor air in some areas of Canada may not be of an acceptable quality for ventilating buildings unless certain particles and gases are first removed or reduced. For particulate matter, the maximum acceptable level is the 98th percentile of the average 24 hour values; for ozone, the maximum acceptable level is the average of the average 8 hour values. A recent estimate suggests that many Canadians are exposed to contaminated outdoor air via buildings' ventilation systems, which may lead to health problems such as cardiovascular and cerebral vascular diseases, respiratory irritation and illnesses, asthma, allergies, cancer, mucus membrane disorders and possibly death.

In order to manage the air quality of a building's indoor environment, thus reducing the potential for adverse effects on occupants' health, the quality of outdoor air for building ventilation purposes must be addressed. The air pollutants for which standards have been developed are particulate matter and ground-level ozone. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art2.sent2:long] sets limits on the maximum acceptable levels of these particles and gas that a building's ventilation system should introduce directly to the indoor environment. These limits form part of the Canada-wide Standards for Particulate Matter (PM) and Ozone, which were established pursuant to the 1998 Canada-wide Accord on Environmental Harmonization of the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment (CCME) and its Canada-wide Environmental Standards Sub-Agreement. Information on related regulations is available from Environment and Climate Change Canada and the provincial/territorial ministries of the environment. A database of particle measurements for certain Canadian locations is available from the National Air Pollution Surveillance Network (NAPS), which is run by Environment and Climate Change Canada in conjunction with the provinces and territories.

The outdoor air at the local area of the building site, including its immediate surroundings, should be assessed to identify the levels of contaminants that may be of concern if allowed to enter the building. Examples of contaminants of concern include the following:[LIST:bulleted]Factors that can influence the infiltration of contaminants, such as the building's geometry and prevailing winds and seasonal activity in the local area, should also be considered. Features can be incorporated in the design of the building to mitigate the effects of the identified contaminants of concern to the building occupants.

items.content: irritants from restaurant and dumpster emissions
visible plumes from cooling towers and incinerators
combustion exhaust from vehicles on loading docks and highways
other visible sources of contaminants on site and from adjoining properties (e.g. manufacturing plants)

content.content: This Article is intended to remind designers and installers of mechanical systems of one aspect of the “good engineering practice” referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1:long]
In determining how to accommodate structural movement, there are two important principles to bear in mind:[LIST:bulleted]

items.content: The prime concern of the British Columbia Building Code is the safety of people in and around the building, as opposed to protection of the mechanical systems and equipment.

The nature of the accommodation will vary with the type of movement being considered, taking into account particularly how often the movement is likely to be encountered over the life of the building.

content.content: For example, a gas line supported on columns that also support a crane must be installed in such a way that the movement of the columns, which occurs many times daily, does not cause the lines to break, thus creating a hazard. Even if the gas line installation could somehow be designed to break in a non-hazardous manner, it would hardly be recognized as good engineering practice if movement that occurs so frequently could disrupt the operation of the mechanical system.

On the other hand, earthquakes occur far less frequently and it would not be surprising to have a non-critical mechanical system fail as a result of an earthquake. However, even in this situation, the failure must occur in a manner that does not create a hazard to building occupants. For example, heavy mechanical equipment should be properly anchored so that it does not topple on building occupants during an earthquake. The design of the anchors should take into account accelerations consistent with the seismic data given in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC:long] for the location of the building. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long] provides guidance on the calculation of the loads such equipment would exert on the building structure during an earthquake; these same loads can be used in designing the anchors.

Some mechanical equipment can be an important component of post-disaster life safety systems. In these cases, the measures needed to accommodate the movements caused by an earthquake become even more critical since failure of the equipment would not be acceptable.
Clearly, complying with this requirement will, in most cases, necessitate close coordination between the mechanical designer and the structural designer.

For additional information on the types of structural movement that may be encountered, see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art5:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect3.art3.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect8:long]
Ducts or pipes without dampers or valves are generally not considered to constitute “equipment” and are therefore not subject to this requirement.
The indirect supply of required outdoor ventilation air to normally occupied spaces through corridor pressurization or other indirect systems is not permitted.

application_notes.title: Ventilation and Venting of Crawl Spaces and Attic or Roof Spaces

content.content: The cross-reference to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5:long] pertains to unconditioned and unoccupied crawl spaces, and attic or roof spaces, which are effectively within the building envelope. That is, unconditioned and unoccupied attic or roof spaces are located between the roof deck and roofing above, and the insulation, air barrier system and vapour barrier below. Unconditioned and unoccupied crawl spaces are located between the ground cover below and the insulation, air barrier system and vapour barrier above. Venting of these spaces has implications for the performance of the building envelope rather than having direct effects on indoor conditions. The ventilation of conditioned or occupied crawl spaces and attic or roof spaces must comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6:long] .

The requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5:long] are stated in terms of loads that must be resisted rather than in terms of building elements. Thus, the Code user will not find explicit references in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5:long] to crawl spaces, or attic or roof spaces. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5:long] makes reference to the need for venting environmental separators, i.e., the dissipation of heat or moisture.

[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect1.art2.sent1:long] requires that crawl spaces be ventilated either by natural (above-grade only) or mechanical means. High moisture levels within the crawl space can lead to problems such as the formation of mould, lifting of flooring or long-term damage to structural components.

Crawl space ventilation cannot be expected to correct moisture-related problems caused by other factors like inadequate surface drainage from the foundation walls or improper protection against moisture from the ground. These conditions must be properly addressed so that crawl space ventilation can meet its intended objectives.

Several factors favour the use of mechanical ventilation rather than reliance on natural drafts. Local conditions, such as areas with high water tables, may dictate the need for mechanical ventilation to remove excessive moisture.

Crawl spaces should be maintained at a negative pressure relative to the conditioned area above to prevent the migration of moisture into occupied areas. This can be achieved through the use of an exhaust fan and relying on air transfer through floor penetrations, such as pipes.
Areas where motor vehicles are parked with the engine off for extended periods of time, such as car dealership showrooms, are not considered as storage garages.

Storage garages are ventilated to protect occupants from exposure to carbon monoxide and other vehicular exhaust fumes. In certain cases, such as small two- or three-bay storage garages that are used for occasional vehicle storage, and where occupants are not present, carbon monoxide or nitrogen dioxide monitoring devices may be omitted if the ventilation system is interlocked with a local light switch or other controls to ensure continuous system operation whenever the area is occupied. In any event, the ventilation system capacity must be designed to limit the concentrations of carbon monoxide or nitrogen dioxide at or below the prescribed values.

Indoor air can contain complex mixtures of contaminants of concern such as formaldehyde, legionella, mould and emissions from building materials. While some contaminants may be knowingly introduced—as in the case of processing and manufacturing environments—others may be unintentionally released into indoor environments. [REF:standard:acgih-iv-mrp] published by the ACGIH, and the [REF:standard:hc46-2.90-156e] published by Health Canada, are useful references on the control of contaminants in industrial workplace environments and residential settings, respectively. These and other guidelines and manuals should be interpreted while keeping in mind the settings and purposes for which they were developed compared to those to which they will be applied. Note that such documents do not necessarily consider the interactions between various contaminants.

content.title: Minimizing the Growth and Spread of Bio-contaminants

content.content: Bio-contaminants, such as bacteria, mould, mildew, fungi, viruses, and pollen, can thrive in or be spread by sources like drain pans, spray-water air-washers, contaminated filters, poorly maintained cooling coils, water incursion into ductwork, high humidity and stagnant water, potentially causing a wide range of adverse health effects including respiratory allergic reactions, asthma, and diseases ranging from influenza to legionellosis.
Some of the control measures are as follows: [LIST:alphabetic]

items.content: Air-handling equipment should be accessible for the maintenance of filters, cooling coils and condensate drain pans located below the cooling coils. Access doors should be large and easy to open to facilitate thorough and regular maintenance.

If moisture is added to building ventilation air to maintain humidity levels in a designated range, humidifiers that inject steam or water vapour into central air-handling units or main supply ducts are normally used. Injection nozzles should not be located in air-handling unit plenums or ductwork that is insulated with internal fibrous lining. If the lining becomes wet, conditions conducive to the growth and spread of bio-contaminants will result.

HVAC systems that generate condensate or introduce liquid water into the airstream in the ducts require adequate drainage of excess water and, in some cases, a means of capturing air-entrained water droplets. These measures reduce the potential for bio-contaminants, including legionella, to proliferate in stagnant water and for water droplets containing bio-contaminants to be introduced into the airstream and contaminate the indoor environment. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art2:long] )

content.content: The above only addresses built-in features of an HVAC system that can help to minimize the growth and spread of bio-contaminants. Even more important than the built-in features is a program of regular maintenance and cleaning of those portions of the system where such growth is likely to occur.
It is important to eliminate stagnant water as it can promote the proliferation of disease-causing micro-organisms, such as legionella.
Of particular concern is the potential for legionella bacteria in water to become airborne in water droplets or mist that can be inhaled by humans or can contaminate other water sources or systems.

The TIAC [REF:standard:tiac_bp] is a comprehensive source of information on the selection, installation and proper use of thermal insulation materials. (Note that [REF:external:tiac_bp:Section 4 of this Guide] is not included in the scope of this Note as it contains information on proprietary products, which are not within the mandate of the Code.)

A frequent practice in the design of ventilation systems serving buildings which have associated parking garages is to discharge exhaust air from the building to the garage in order to reduce the cost of heating the garage or reduce the length of the exhaust ducts. However, this practice entails a certain amount of risk since, when the exhaust system is not running, stack effect may turn the exhaust outlets into intakes and exhaust fumes (including carbon monoxide) can be drawn from the garage into the building. Incorporating a backdraft damper at the exhaust outlet provides some additional protection but backdraft dampers are generally not regarded as being very reliable. Therefore this practice is only permitted in very limited circumstances.

For the purpose of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art10.sent6.clause2:long] , washroom exhaust air is not considered to contain contaminants that would adversely affect the air quality in the storage garage.

application_notes.title: Exhaust Ducts Connected to Laundry-Drying Equipment

content.content: Clothes dryers are a major cause of fires in buildings often due to a build-up of lint in the system, which then ignites or obstructs the venting or ventilation. Proper cleaning and regular maintenance of lint traps is directly proportional to the ease of access to the lint traps. It is therefore important to ensure that lint traps in multiple installations of laundry-drying equipment are installed in such a way as to allow easy access for inspection, maintenance, repair and cleaning.

The operation diversity factor has to be assessed for each specific application. Good engineering practice (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1:long] ) design guidelines can provide information on the subject. [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.appendix.appnote15.figure1:long] , which originates from ASHRAE handbooks, provides an example of factors that can be used for general applications.

Ensuring adequate distance between the air discharge locations of evaporative heat rejection systems and certain outdoor spaces and building components minimizes the potential for contamination of the air of occupiable spaces. For example, if a building's ventilation air intake were located too close to an air discharge location of an evaporative heat rejection system, warm discharge air and associated drift, which could contain biological contaminants, could be introduced to the indoor environment through the air intake.

The minimum distances stated in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art15.sent5:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art15.sent6:short] may need to be increased where warranted by local conditions such as prevailing winds, adjacent structures, or special processes being carried out, any of which would make further analysis necessary. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art1.sent2:long] .)

application_notes.title: Assessment of System and Make-Up Water

content.content: The chemical characteristics of the water in the evaporative heat rejection system and of the make-up water should be assessed to select a suitable water treatment system.
Common strategies to prevent water stagnation include flushing, providing an inactivity drain, and periodic activation, even with no load.

The chemical characteristics of the make-up water should be assessed to ensure that any chemicals added to a system referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect2.art16.sent1:long] for precipitation control, disinfection or another purpose will not adversely affect the system.

[REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art1.sent2:long] requires that vented products of combustion from appliances be discharged a minimum distance away from certain outdoor spaces and building components in cases where the vented products could contaminate the air of occupiable spaces. These minimum distances may need to be increased due to local conditions such as prevailing winds, adjacent structures, special processes being carried out, specific contaminants or effluent discharges, all of which would require further analysis.

“Occupiable outdoor spaces” refers to areas that could be occupied for a duration of more than fifteen minutes at any time, but does not include maintenance spaces. Occupiable outdoor spaces are located adjacent to an indoor space and are considered to be an extension of this indoor space: e.g. main entries, balconies, patios, decks, green roofs and other public assembly areas. Although sidewalks and driveways are mentioned in the provision, these areas are not considered as occupiable outdoor spaces since they are used as transport routes to and from the building, and people are not expected to remain there for extended periods of time.

The requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3.subsect3.art1.sent2:long] are not meant to override similar requirements found in the installation standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art5:long] that address identical situations.

Piping carrying steam, high-temperature hot water, or another heat transfer fluid at high temperature is usually insulated to reduce heat losses as an economy measure. Above a temperature of approximately 52°C , however, a bare pipe can cause a burn to human skin coming in contact with the pipe. According to [REF:standard:astmc1055] skin can be in contact with a surface at a temperature of 52°C for up to 60 s without experiencing irreversible damage. If pipes above this temperature are normally out of reach of all persons other than maintenance personnel or are properly guarded, it would be expected that no insulation would be needed for public safety.

content.content: Battery-powered carbon monoxide alarms are acceptable provided that they are installed as recommended by the manufacturer.

Although the scope of [REF:standard:csa6.19] and [REF:standard:ul2034] is limited to carbon monoxide alarms for residential applications, their use may be appropriate in some other locations where they are not subject to excessive contaminants or risk of damage, such as in classrooms and meeting spaces. The designer is also given the option to follow good engineering practice. For example, some carbon monoxide devices used in storage garages may be suitable for use in other applications.

application_notes.title: Spaces Served by a Fuel-Burning Appliance

content.content: Where a fuel-burning appliance such as a furnace circulates or distributes air to a space there is the potential for leakage of combustion products into the duct system which could then circulate combustion products including carbon monoxide (CO) to that space, so a CO alarm is required to protect occupants of that space. Fuel-burning appliances such as a boiler do not have the same potential of the system circulating or distributing CO to the spaces served via the piping system. In both examples of a fuel-burning furnace and a fuel-burning boiler, a CO alarm is required in the service room containing the appliances.

Suites that share a common attic or crawl space with a storage garage or service room, as well as suites that share a common wall or floor/ceiling assembly with a storage garage or service room are considered adjacent for the application of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect9.subsect3.art1.sent8:short] .

content.text: The scope of this Part shall be as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3:long] .
This Part applies to the design, construction, extension, [REF:term:ltrtn:alteration] , renewal or repair of [REF:term:plmbng-t:plumbing systems] .

content.text: Compliance with the British Columbia Building Code Book II (Plumbing Systems) may be achieved using alternative solutions as described in Clause 1.2.1.1.(1)(b) of Division A of this Code, using the objectives and functional statements attributed to the applicable acceptable solutions in Division B of the British Columbia Building Code Book II (Plumbing Systems).

parts.title: Safety Measures at Construction and Demolition Sites

content.text: The scope of this Part shall be as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect3.subsect3:long] .

This Part applies to fire safety and the protection of the public during the construction, [REF:term:ltrtn:alteration] or demolition of every [REF:term:bldng:building] , including any incompleted or abandoned [REF:term:bldng:building] .
Fire safety at construction and demolition sites shall conform to Section 5.6. of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code.
Words that appear in italics are defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect4.subsect1.art2:long] .
Measures shall be taken during demolition to protect the public in conformance with Section 5.6. of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code.

Where a [REF:term:bldng:building] is undergoing construction, [REF:term:ltrtn:alteration ] or demolition, measures shall be taken at the [REF:term:bldng:building] site in conformance with this Code. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.appendix.appnote1:short] .)
Precautions shall be taken to ensure that no person is exposed to undue risk.

Where the construction may constitute a hazard to the public, work shall not commence on the construction, [REF:term:ltrtn:alteration] or repair of a [REF:term:bldng:building] until a covered way has been provided as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect1.art2:long] to protect the public, except where

clauses.text: the work is done within a solid enclosure,
the [REF:term:bldng:building] is at a distance of 2 m or more from a [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] used by pedestrians, or
site conditions warrant a distance greater than provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:short] .

content.text: A covered way shall

clauses.text: have a clear height of not less than 2.5 m ,
have a clear width of not less than 1.5 m or the width of the [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] , whichever is the lesser,
be designed and constructed to support safely all loads that may be reasonably expected to be applied to it, but in no case less than 2.4 kPa on the roof,
have a weathertight roof sloped towards the site or, if flat, be equipped with a splash board not less than 300 mm high on the [REF:term:trt:street] side,
be totally enclosed on the site side with a structure having a reasonably smooth surface facing the [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] ,
have a railing 1 070 mm high on the [REF:term:trt:street] side where the covered way is supported by posts on the [REF:term:trt:street] side, and
be adequately lighted when the [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] is lighted.

content.text: When a construction or demolition activity may constitute a hazard to the public and is located 2 m or more from a [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] , a strongly constructed fence, boarding or barricade not less than 1.8 m high shall be erected between the site and the [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] or open sides of a construction site.
Barricades shall have a reasonably smooth surface facing the [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] and shall be without openings, except those required for access.
Access openings through barricades shall be equipped with gates that shall be

clauses.text: kept closed and locked when the site is unattended, and
maintained in place until completion of the construction or demolition activity.

content.text: Where any special hazard exists from which it is not possible to protect the public by other means, persons shall be employed to prevent the public from entering the danger zone at any time of the day or night.
When work on a construction site is suspended or ceases so that it will not be occupied during normal working hours, the hazardous part of the construction site shall be protected by

clauses.text: covering all windows, doors and other openings located within 3 m of the ground which may give access to the [REF:term:bldng:building] with a securely fastened barricade, or
a fence or barricade constructed according to the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect1.art3:long]

content.text: [REF:term:xcvtn:Excavations] shall be kept reasonably clear of water.
If the stability of adjoining [REF:term:bldng:buildings] may be endangered by the work of excavating, adequate underpinning, shoring and bracing shall be provided to prevent

clauses.text: damage to, or movement of, any part of the adjoining [REF:term:bldng:building] , and
the creation of a hazard to the public.

subsections.title: Use of Streets or Public Property

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect3.art2:long] , provisions shall be made at all times for the safe passage of pedestrian and vehicular traffic past the site.
Material or equipment shall not be placed on any [REF:term:trt:street] or other public property except as authorized.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect3.art1.sent4:short] , where a sidewalk exists adjacent to the site it shall be kept clear of obstructions at all times.
Where construction operations necessitate the obstruction of a sidewalk, a temporary sidewalk shall be provided and it shall be kept clear of obstruction at all times.

Operations such as the hoisting of major components onto a tall [REF:term:bldng:building] or other overhead activities that constitute a hazard to pedestrians below from which the public cannot be protected by barricades, covered ways or similar means shall not be carried out until the [REF:term:trt:street] or other [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] is closed.
[REF:term:xcvtn:Excavations] in [REF:term:trt:streets] or public property shall

clauses.text: be adequately barricaded, and
have warning signs or lights installed on each section of the barricades referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect3.art3.sent1.clause1:short] .

content.text: All sidewalks, [REF:term:trt:streets] or other public property that have been damaged shall be restored to a safe condition.
All obstructions on sidewalks, [REF:term:trt:streets] or other public property shall be removed when the need for such obstructions is ended.
Warning lights shall be placed and shall be in operation during the hours of darkness at all obstructions on [REF:term:trt:streets] or other [REF:term:pblc-w:public ways] .
Where a hazard to vehicular traffic on a [REF:term:pblc-w:public way] is created by work on a construction site, the following shall be provided to direct the traffic:

clauses.text: one or more workers,
warning signs,
barriers,
lane control devices, or
flashing lights or flares located at a suitable distance from the hazard.

content.text: A flag used to direct traffic shall be

clauses.text: red,
not less than 450 mm by 500 mm ,
mounted on a staff not less than 1 m long, with the long side of the flag attached securely to the staff along its entire length, and
maintained in a clean and untorn condition when being used.

content.text: A sign used to direct traffic shall be

clauses.text: diamond-shaped and of material not less rigid than 6 mm thick plywood,
not less than 450 mm by 450 mm in size and mounted at one corner on a substantial pole not less than 1.2 m long,

red on one side with black corner areas so that the red area is a regular 8-sided figure, and with the word “STOP” or “ARRÊT” in clearly distinguishable white letters not less than 150 mm high located centrally on the sign,

yellow on the other side with the word “SLOW” or “LENTEMENT” in clearly distinguishable black letters not less than 150 mm high located centrally on the sign, or symbols recognized by the International Traffic Code, and
maintained in a clean condition when being used.

content.text: A worker who is directing traffic shall

clauses.text: be equipped as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect4.art5:long] ,
be instructed in the signals to be used in controlling traffic,
be provided with a copy of written instructions on the correct methods for traffic direction, and
direct traffic by using either a flag or sign.

content.text: A worker while directing traffic shall wear the following clothing which shall be fluorescent and coloured either blaze orange or red:

clauses.text: a vest, or
sleeves that extend from above the elbow to the wrist.

content.text: Waste material or other material shall not be permitted to fall freely from one [REF:term:tr:storey] to another.
Waste material shall be removed as quickly as possible by means of

clauses.text: appropriate containers,
an enclosed shaft or chute conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect5.art4.sent1:long] , or
a hoisting apparatus if large pieces or objects are involved.

content.text: Waste material cleared as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect5.art2.sent1:long] shall be deposited in an enclosure

clauses.text: so arranged as to prevent waste material from being projected beyond the confines of the enclosure, and
not accessible to the public.

content.text: The chute described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect2.subsect5.art2.sent1.clause2:long] shall be closed if it is inclined more than 45° to the horizontal.

For the purpose of compliance with this Code as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect2.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] , the objectives and functional statements attributed to the acceptable solutions in this Part shall be the objectives and functional statements listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part8.sect3.subsect1.art1.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.appendix.appnote1:long] .)

content.text: For the purpose of this Subsection, the term "total energy use intensity" (TEUI) shall mean a metric of the energy used over a year by the [REF:term:bldng:building] , estimated by using an energy model in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art4:long] , normalized per square metre of floor area of [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] and expressed in kWh/m^{2}/year, for all of the following combined:

clauses.text: space-heating equipment,
space-cooling equipment,
fans,
interior and exterior lighting devices,
service water heating equipment,
pumps,
auxiliary HVAC equipment,
receptacle loads and miscellaneous equipment,
appliances, and
elevators and escalators.

content.text: For the purpose of this Subsection, the term "thermal energy demand intensity" (TEDI) shall mean a metric of the annual heating required by the [REF:term:bldng:building] for space conditioning and for conditioning of ventilation air, estimated by using an energy model in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect2.subsect3.art4:long] , normalized per square metre of floor area of [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] and expressed in kWh/m^{2}/year, taking into account all of the following:

clauses.text: thermal transmittance of above-ground walls and roof-ceiling assemblies,
thermal transmittance of floors and walls in contact with the ground, or space that is not [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] ,
thermal transmittance and solar heat gain of windows, doors and skylights,
air leakage through the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] ,
internal heat gains from occupants and equipment, and
heat recovery from exhaust ventilation.

content.text: Modeling of greenhouse gas emissions shall conform to the City of Vancouver Energy Modeling Guidelines.
For the purposes of this Section, the term "greenhouse gas", expressed with the abbreviation "GHG", shall have the same meaning as defined in the Climate Change Accountability Act.

For the purposes of this Section, the term "greenhouse gas intensity", expressed with the abbreviation "GHGI", shall mean the total greenhouse gas emissions, expressed as kgCO_{2e} per square metre of floor area of [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] per year, associated with the energy used by the [REF:term:bldng:building's] systems.

For the purposes of this Section, the symbol "CO_{2e}" shall mean carbon dioxide or carbon dioxide equivalent, with carbon dioxide equivalent meaning one or more greenhouse gases with a global warming potential equivalent to carbon dioxide.
For the purposes of this Section, the term "Emissions Level" shall mean an Emissions Level referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part10.sect3.subsect1.art3.table1:long] .

For the purposes of this Section, the term "measure only" shall mean that the GHGI and the total greenhouse gases are calculated, as applicable, and the values reported in accordance with Subsection 2.2.8. of Division C.
