content.text: Where a [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] is insulated in a manner that will reduce heat flow to the [REF:term:l:soil] beneath the footings, the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] depth shall conform to that required for [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] containing no heated space. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote85:short] .)

The minimum depth of [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] for exterior concrete steps with more than 2 risers shall conform to  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect2.art2.sent2:short]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect2.art2.sent5:short] .
Concrete steps with 1 and 2 risers are permitted to be laid on ground level.

The [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] depths required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] are permitted to be decreased where experience with local [REF:term:l:soil] conditions shows that lesser depths are satisfactory, or where the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] is designed for lesser depths.
The [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] depths required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] do not apply to [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] for

clauses.text: [REF:term:bldng:buildings]

subclauses.text: that are not of masonry or masonry veneer construction, and
whose superstructure conforms to the requirements of the deformation resistance test in [REF:standard:csaz240.2.1] or

clauses.text: accessory [REF:term:bldng:buildings]

subclauses.text: that are not of masonry or masonry veneer construction,
not more than 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] in height,
not more than 55 m^{2} in [REF:term:bldng-r:building area] , and
where the distance from finished ground to the underside of the floor joists is not more than 600 mm .

content.text: The [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] depths required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] do not apply to [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] for decks and other accessible exterior platforms

clauses.text: of not more than 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] ,
not more than 55 m^{2} in area,
where the distance from finished ground to the underside of the joists is not more than 600 mm ,
not supporting a roof, and
not attached to another structure, unless it can be demonstrated that differential movement will not adversely affect the performance of that structure.

content.text: Where decks or other accessible exterior platforms are supported on surface [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] supported on other than coarse-grained [REF:term:l:soil] with good drainage or [REF:term:rck:rock] , access to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] positions to permit re-levelling of the platform shall be provided

clauses.text: by passageways with a clear height under the platform of not less than 600 mm and a width of not less than 600 mm , or
by installing the decking in a manner that allows easy removal.

content.text: Backfill shall be placed to avoid damaging the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall, the drainage tile, externally applied thermal insulation and waterproofing or dampproofing of the wall.
Backfill shall be graded to prevent drainage towards the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] after settling.

Backfill that is within 600 mm of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] shall be free of deleterious debris and boulders larger than 250 mm diam. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote86:short] .)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect3.art3.sent3:short] , backfill shall not contain pyritic material or material that is susceptible to ice lensing in concentrations that will damage the [REF:term:bldng:building] to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote14:long] .)
Backfill with material of any concentration that is susceptible to ice lensing is permitted where [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls are

clauses.text: cast-in-place concrete,
concrete block insulated on the exterior, or
concrete block protected from the backfill by a material that serves as a slip plane.

content.text: The [REF:term:l:soil] in trenches beneath footings for sewers and watermains shall be compacted by tamping up to the level of the footing base, or shall be filled with concrete having a strength not less than 10 MPa to support the footing.

sections.title: Dampproofing, Waterproofing and Soil Gas Control

content.text: This Section presents measures to control the ingress of water, moisture and [REF:term:l:soil] gas.

[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2:long] applies to below-ground walls and floors-on-ground where drainage is provided in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14:long] over and along the entire below-ground portion of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall.
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3:long] applies to below-ground walls, floors-on-ground and roofs of underground structures that are subject to hydrostatic pressure.
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4:long] applies to walls, roofs and floors that are in contact with the ground.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3.art1:long] , where the exterior finished ground level is at a higher elevation than the ground level inside the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls, exterior surfaces of [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls below ground level shall be dampproofed.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art1.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3.art1:long] , floors-on-ground shall be dampproofed.
Dampproofing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art1.sent2:short] need not be provided for

clauses.text: floors in garages,
floors in unenclosed portions of [REF:term:bldng:buildings] , or
floors installed over not less than 100 mm of coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve.

content.text: Materials installed to provide required dampproofing shall be

clauses.text: capable of protecting assemblies against moisture transfer from the ground,
compatible with adjoining materials, and
resistant to mechanisms of deterioration that may reasonably be expected, given the nature, function and exposure of the materials.

content.text: Except as otherwise specified in this Section, materials used for exterior dampproofing shall

clauses.text: conform to one of the following standards:

subclauses.text: [REF:standard:astmd1227] Type III, Class I,
[REF:standard:astmd4479m] Type III,
[REF:standard:cgsb-51.34] or
[REF:standard:csaa123.4] or

clauses.text: have a water vapour permeance of not more than 43 ng/(Pa×s×m^{2}) when tested in accordance with Procedure A (wet cup) of [REF:standard:astme96m] and consist of one of the following material types:

subclauses.text: a vapour-resistant coating,
a cold-fluid-applied or hot-rubberized bituminous dampproofing membrane,
a liquid-applied or spray-applied asphalt-based emulsion dampproofing, or
a type III hot-applied asphalt.

content.text: The area in which dampproofing is to be carried out shall be kept free of water during the application and curing of the dampproofing system.
The surface to be dampproofed shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions of the dampproofing material manufacturer.
Where the dampproofing material is to be applied on insulating concrete form (ICF) walls, the instructions of the ICF wall manufacturer shall be followed.

Unit masonry walls to be dampproofed shall be parged on the exterior face below ground level with not less than 6 mm of mortar conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long] coved over the footing.

Concrete walls to be dampproofed shall have holes and recesses sealed with cement mortar or a mastic or sealant that is suitable for vertical applications and compatible with the dampproofing material.

The surface required to be dampproofed shall be clean and dry and free of ice, snow, frost, dust, dirt, oil, grease, cracks, projections and depressions, loose particles and debris that could be detrimental to the performance of the material to be applied.
Exterior dampproofing shall be applied from finished ground level to the top of the exterior of the footing.
Unless otherwise stated in this Subsection, dampproofing shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions with regard to

clauses.text: surface priming,
conditions during application,
application quantity and rate, and
curing times.

content.text: Joints, cracks and penetrations shall be sealed to maintain the continuity of the dampproofing, where the dampproofing material is not capable of bridging such discontinuities.

The interior surface of [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls below ground level shall be protected by means that minimize the ingress of moisture from the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall into interior spaces, where

clauses.text: a separate interior finish is applied to a concrete or unit masonry wall that is in contact with the [REF:term:l:soil] , or
wood members are placed in contact with such walls for the installation of insulation or finish.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art5.sent3:short] , where the protection of interior finishes required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art5.sent1:short] consists of membranes or coatings,

clauses.text: the membrane or coating shall extend from the [REF:term:bmnt:basement] floor surface up to the highest extent of the interior insulation or finish, but not higher than the exterior finished ground level, and

no membrane or coating with a permeance less than 170 ng/(Pa×s×m^{2}) shall be applied to the interior surface of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall above ground level between the insulation and the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall.

content.text: Where insulation functions as both moisture protection for interior finishes and as a [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4:long] , it shall be applied over the entire interior surface of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall.
Where dampproofing is installed below the floor, it shall consist of

clauses.text: polyethylene not less than 0.15 mm thick with joints lapped not less than 100 mm ,
type S roll roofing with joints lapped not less than 100 mm , or
rigid extruded/expanded polystyrene with sealed or ship-lapped joints that has

subclauses.text: sufficient compressive strength to support the floor assembly, and
a water vapour permeance complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art2.sent2.clause1:long] .

content.text: Where dampproofing is installed between a floor-on-ground and a finished floor, it shall consist of

clauses.text: rigid extruded/expanded polystyrene with sealed or ship-lapped joints that has

subclauses.text: sufficient compressive strength to support the floor assembly, and
a water vapour permeance complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect2.art2.sent2.clause2:long] , or

clauses.text: polyethylene not less than 0.05 mm thick with joints lapped not less than 100 mm .

content.text: Where hydrostatic pressure occurs, waterproofing is required for assemblies separating interior space from the ground to prevent the ingress of water into [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies and interior spaces.
Waterproofing is required for roofs of underground structures to prevent the ingress of water into [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies and interior spaces.
Materials installed to provide required waterproofing shall be

clauses.text: compatible with adjoining materials, and
resistant to mechanisms of deterioration that may reasonably be expected, given the nature, function and exposure of the materials.

content.text: Materials used for exterior waterproofing shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmd1227] in which case, they shall be installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3.art3.sent3:long] ,
[REF:standard:astmd3019] where non-fibered and non-asbestos-fibered (Types I and III) asphalt roll roofing are permitted,
[REF:standard:astmd4479m] in which case, they shall be installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect3.art3.sent3:long] and with reinforcing material,
[REF:standard:astmd4637m]
[REF:standard:astmd4811m]
[REF:standard:astmd6878m]
[REF:standard:cgsb37-gp-9ma] where a primer is required,
[REF:standard:cgsb-37.50]
[REF:standard:cgsb-37.54]
[REF:standard:cgsb37-gp-56m]
[REF:standard:cgsb-37.58]
[REF:standard:csaa123.2]
[REF:standard:csaa123.4] in which case, they shall be installed with reinforcing material, or
[REF:standard:csaa123.17]

content.text: Surfaces to be waterproofed shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions of the waterproofing material manufacturer.
Where the waterproofing material is to be applied on ICF walls, the instructions of the ICF wall manufacturer shall be followed.

Unit masonry walls that are to be waterproofed shall be parged on exterior surfaces below ground level with not less than 6 mm of mortar conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long] coved over the footing.
Concrete walls that are to be waterproofed shall have all holes and recesses sealed with mortar or waterproofing material.

Surfaces required to be waterproofed shall be clean and dry and free of ice, snow, frost, dust, dirt, oil, grease, cracks, projections and depressions, loose particles and debris that could be detrimental to the performance of the waterproofing material.
Unless otherwise stated in this Subsection, waterproofing shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions with regard to

clauses.text: surface priming,
conditions during application,
the required number of layers of reinforcing fabric on [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] , footings, floors, walls and structural slabs,
application quantity and rate, and
curing times.

content.text: Waterproofing shall be continuous across joints and at junctions between different [REF:term:bldng:building] elements.
The waterproofed surface shall be protected with a suitable material to minimize mechanical damage during backfilling.
The area in which the waterproofing is to be carried out shall be kept free of water during the application and curing of the waterproofing system.

[REF:term:bmnt:Basement] floors-on-ground to be waterproofed shall have a system of membrane waterproofing provided between 2 layers of concrete, each of which shall be not less than 75 mm thick, with the floor membrane made continuous with the wall membrane to form a complete seal.
This Subsection applies to

clauses.text: a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] that has a wall, roof or floor assembly, or part thereof, that is in contact with the ground, and
the protection of the [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] described in Clause (a).

content.text: This Subsection addresses the leakage of [REF:term:l:soil] gas from the ground into the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

All wall, roof and floor assemblies separating [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from the ground shall be protected by an [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long]

Unless the space between the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] and the ground is designed to be accessible for the future installation of a subfloor depressurization system, [REF:term:bldng:buildings] shall

clauses.text: be provided with the rough-in for a subfloor depressurization system conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3:long] , or

conform to Parts 5 and 6 for the protection from radon ingress and the means to address high radon concentrations in the future (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part5.sect4.subsect1.art1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1:long] ).

articles.title: Rough-in for a Subfloor Depressurization System

content.text: Floors-on-ground shall accommodate the future installation of a subfloor depressurization system by installing a radon vent pipe, and a contiguous gas-permeable layer between the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] and the ground consisting of

clauses.text: a material or materials that allow effective depressurization of that space (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect2.art1.sent1:long] ), or
not less than 100 mm of coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that would pass a 4 mm sieve.

content.text: The radon vent pipe required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text: be sealed to maintain the integrity of the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] , with no perforations along the pipe above the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] ,
have one or more inlets that allow for the effective depressurization of the gas-permeable layer (see Note A-9.13.4.3.(2)(b) and (3)(b)), and
permit connection to depressurization equipment,
where it passes through [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] , be completely surrounded by [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] ,
consist of pipe and fittings in accordance with 7.1.3 of CAN/CGSB-149.11, "Radon control options for new construction in low-rise residential buildings,"
terminate outside the [REF:term:bldng:building] in a manner that does not constitute a hazard,
be installed to prevent the accumulation of moisture and away from locations where snow and ice accumulate, and
be clearly labeled every 1.8 m and at every change in direction to indicate that it is intended only for the future removal of radon from below the floor-on-ground.

content.text: A radon vent pipe shall be deemed to comply with

clauses.text: [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent2.clause2:medium] where its inlet or inlets below the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] are located at or near the centre of the floor-on-ground with gas-permeable material extending not less than 100 mm beyond any inlet, and

[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4.art3.sent2.clause6:medium] where it terminates outside the [REF:term:bldng:building] , not less than 1.8 m from a property line, and located in accordance with either 7.2.4.6 or 7.3.4 of CAN/CGSB-149.11, "Radon control options for new construction in low-rise residential buildings," with the opening of the pipe fitted with a corrosion-resistant screen or grille with a mesh opening size of 10 mm to 12.5 mm or a product of equivalent air flow performance.

revisions.change_summary: Struck out "Providing for the" from title

content.text: This Section applies to subsurface drainage and to surface drainage.
Drainage for crawl spaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18:long]
Drainage requirements beneath floors-on-ground shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16:long]

Unless it can be shown to be unnecessary, the bottom of every exterior [REF:term:fndtn:foundation ] wall shall be drained by drainage tile or pipe laid around the exterior of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect3:long] or by a layer of gravel or crushed [REF:term:rck:rock] in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect4:long]
Where mineral fibre insulation or crushed [REF:term:rck:rock] backfill is provided adjacent to the exterior surface of a [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall,

clauses.text: the insulation or backfill shall extend to the footing level to facilitate the drainage of ground water to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] 's drainage system (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote92:short] ), and

any pyritic material in the crushed [REF:term:rck:rock] shall be limited to a concentration that will not damage the [REF:term:bldng:building] to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12.subsect3.art3.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote14:long] ).

content.text: Drain tile and drain pipe for [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] drainage shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc4]
[REF:standard:astmc412m]
[REF:standard:astmc444m]
[REF:standard:astmc700]
[REF:standard:bnq3624-115]
[REF:standard:csab182.1] or
[REF:standard:csag401]

content.text: Drain tile or pipe used for [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] drainage shall be not less than 100 mm in diam.
Drain tile or pipe shall be laid on undisturbed or well-compacted [REF:term:l:soil] so that the top of the tile or pipe is below the bottom of the floor slab or the ground cover of the crawl space.
Drain tile or pipe with butt joints shall be laid with 6 mm to 10 mm open joints.

The top half of joints referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect3.art3.sent2:short] shall be covered with sheathing paper, 0.10 mm polyethylene or No. 15 asphalt or tar-saturated felt.

The top and sides of drain pipe or tile shall be covered with not less than 150 mm of crushed stone or other coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve.
Granular material used to drain the bottom of a [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] shall consist of a continuous layer of crushed stone or other coarse clean granular material containing

clauses.text: not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve, and

no pyritic material in a concentration that will damage the [REF:term:bldng:building] to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote14:long] ).

content.text: Granular material described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect4.art1:long] shall be laid on undisturbed or compacted [REF:term:l:soil] to a minimum depth of not less than 125 mm beneath the footing of the [REF:term:bldng:building] and extend not less than 300 mm beyond the outside edge of the footings.

The bottom of an [REF:term:xcvtn:excavation] drained by a granular layer shall be graded so that the entire area described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect4.art2:long] is drained to a sump conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect5.art2:long]

Where because of wet site conditions [REF:term:l:soil] becomes mixed with the granular drainage material, sufficient additional granular material shall be provided so that the top 125 mm are kept free of [REF:term:l:soil] .
[REF:term:fndtn:Foundation] drains shall drain to a sewer, drainage ditch or dry well.
Where a sump pit is provided it shall be

clauses.text: not less than 750 mm deep,
not less than 0.25 m^{2} in area, and
provided with a cover.

content.text: Covers for sump pits shall be designed

clauses.text: to resist removal by children, and
to be airtight in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art3.sent7:long] .

content.text: Where gravity drainage is not practical, an automatic sump pump shall be provided to discharge the water from the sump pit described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect5.art2.sent1:short] into a sewer, drainage ditch or dry well.
Dry wells may be used only when located in areas where the natural [REF:term:grndwtr-:groundwater level] is below the bottom of the dry well.
Dry wells shall be not less than 5 m from the [REF:term:bldng:building]  [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] and located so that drainage is away from the [REF:term:bldng:building] .
The [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be located or the [REF:term:bldng:building] site graded so that water will not accumulate at or near the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

articles.title: Drainage away from Wells or Septic Disposal Beds

content.text: Surface drainage shall be directed away from the location of a water supply well or septic tank disposal bed.
Every window well shall be drained to the footing level or other suitable location.
Where runoff water from a driveway is likely to accumulate or enter a garage, a catch basin shall be installed to provide adequate drainage.
Downspouts shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect18.art2:long]
Except as provided in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect1.art2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect1.art3:long] , this Section applies to

clauses.text: concrete or unit masonry [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls and concrete footings not subject to surcharge

subclauses.text: on stable [REF:term:l:soils] with an allowable bearing pressure of 75 kPa or greater, and
for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of wood-frame or masonry construction,

clauses.text: wood-frame [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls and wood or concrete footings not subject to surcharge

subclauses.text: on stable [REF:term:l:soils] with an allowable bearing pressure of 75 kPa or greater, and
for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of wood-frame construction, and

clauses.text: flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls and concrete footings not subject to surcharge (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote94:short] )

subclauses.text: on stable [REF:term:l:soils] with an allowable bearing pressure of 75 kPa or greater, and

for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of light-frame or flat insulating concrete form construction that are not more than 2 [REF:term:tr:storeys] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] , with a maximum floor-to-floor height of 3 m .

content.text: [REF:term:fndtn:Foundations ] for applications other than as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4:long]

[REF:term:bldng:Buildings ] erected on permafrost shall have [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] designed by a [REF:term:dgnr:designer] competent in this field in accordance with the appropriate requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long] .

Where the superstructure of a detached [REF:term:bldng:building] conforms to the requirements of the deformation resistance test in [REF:standard:csaz240.2.1] the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] shall be constructed in conformance with

clauses.text: the remainder of this Section, or
[REF:standard:csaz240.10.1]

content.text: Concrete shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3:long]
Concrete block shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa165.1] and shall have a compressive strength over the average net cross-sectional area of the block of not less than 15 MPa .
Mortar, grout, mortar joints, corbelling and protection for unit masonry shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long]
For concrete block [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls required to be reinforced,

clauses.text: mortar shall be Type S, conforming to [REF:standard:csaa179]
grout shall be coarse, conforming to [REF:standard:csaa179] and
placement of grout shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa371]

content.text: Where pier-type [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] are used, the piers shall be designed to support the applied loads from the superstructure.

Where piers are used as a [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] system in a [REF:term:bldng:building] of 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] , the piers shall be installed to support the principal framing members and shall be spaced not more than 3.5 m apart along the framing, unless the piers and their footings are designed for larger spacings.
The height of piers described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect2.art3.sent2:short] shall not exceed 3 times their least dimension at the base of the pier.

Where concrete block is used for piers described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect2.art3.sent2:short] , they shall be laid with cores placed vertically, and where the width of the [REF:term:bldng:building] is 4.3 m or less, placed with their longest dimension at right angles to the longest dimension of the [REF:term:bldng:building] .
[REF:term:fndtn:Foundations] of wood-frame construction shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csas406] or
Part 4.

content.text: Footings shall be provided under walls, pilasters, columns, piers, fireplaces and [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] that bear on [REF:term:l:soil] or [REF:term:rck:rock] , except that footings may be omitted under piers or monolithic concrete walls if the safe [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] capacity of the [REF:term:l:soil] or [REF:term:rck:rock] is not exceeded.
Footings shall rest on undisturbed [REF:term:l:soil] , [REF:term:rck:rock] or compacted granular [REF:term:fll:fill] .

Granular [REF:term:fll:fill] shall not contain pyritic material in a concentration that will damage the [REF:term:bldng:building] to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect4.art4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote14:long] .)

articles.title: Application of Footing Width and Area Requirements

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect3.art4.sent2:long] , the minimum footing width or area requirements provided in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect3.art4:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect3.art7:long] shall apply to footings, where

clauses.text: the footings support

subclauses.text: [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls of masonry, concrete, or flat insulating concrete form walls,
above-ground walls of masonry, flat insulating concrete form walls or light wood-frame construction, and
floors and roofs of light wood-frame construction,

clauses.text: the span of supported joists does not exceed 4.9 m , and
the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] on any floor supported by the footing does not exceed 2.4 kPa (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] ).

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect3.art4.sent2:long] , where the span of the supported joists exceeds 4.9 m , footings shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2:long]
Where the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] exceeds 2.4 kPa , footings shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect2:long]

articles.title: Adjustments to Footing Widths for Exterior Walls

content.text: The strip footing widths for exterior walls shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect3.art4.table1:long] shall be increased by

clauses.text: 65 mm for each [REF:term:tr:storey] of masonry veneer over wood-frame construction supported by the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall,
130 mm for each [REF:term:tr:storey] of masonry construction supported by the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall, and
150 mm for each [REF:term:tr:storey] of flat insulating concrete form wall construction supported by the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall.

articles.title: Adjustments to Footing Widths for Interior Walls

content.text: The minimum strip footing widths for interior [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] masonry walls shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect3.art4.table1:long] shall be increased by 100 mm for each [REF:term:tr:storey] of masonry construction supported by the footing.

Footings for interior non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] masonry walls shall be not less than 200 mm wide for walls up to 5.5 m high and the width shall be increased by 100 mm for each additional 2.7 m of height.

articles.title: Adjustments to Footing Area for Columns

content.text: The footing area for column spacings other than shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect3.art4.table1:long] shall be adjusted in proportion to the distance between columns.
Footing thickness shall be not less than the greater of

clauses.text: 100 mm , or
the width of the projection of the footing beyond the supported element.

content.text: Where step footings are used,

clauses.text: the vertical rise between horizontal portions shall not exceed 600 mm , and
the horizontal distance between risers shall not be less than 600 mm .

content.text: Flat wall insulating concrete form units shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs717.1]

content.text: Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art2.sent2:short] , the thickness of [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls made of unreinforced concrete block, concrete core in flat wall insulating concrete forms or solid concrete and subject to lateral earth pressure shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art2.table1:long] for walls not exceeding 3.0 m in unsupported height.
The concrete core in flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall be not less than the greater of

clauses.text: the walls are laterally supported at the top,
average stable [REF:term:l:soils] are encountered, and
wind loads on the exposed portion of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] are no greater than 0.70 kPa .

content.text: For concrete block walls required to be reinforced, continuous vertical reinforcement shall

clauses.text: be provided at wall corners, wall ends, wall intersections, at changes in wall height, at the jambs of all openings and at movement joints,
extend from the top of the footing to the top of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall, and
where [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls are laterally supported at the top, have not less than 50 mm embedment into the footing, if the floor slab does not provide lateral support at the wall base.

content.text: For concrete block walls required to be reinforced, a continuous horizontal bond beam containing not less than one 15M bar shall be installed

clauses.text: along the top of the wall,
at the sill and head of all openings greater than 1.20 m in width, and
at structurally connected floors.

content.text: In concrete block walls required to be reinforced, all vertical bar reinforcement shall be installed along the centre line of the wall.

In concrete block walls required to be reinforced, ladder- or truss-type lateral reinforcement not less than 3.8 mm in diameter (no. 9 ASWG) shall be installed in the bed joint of every second masonry course.

articles.title: Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Top

content.text: Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art3.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art3.sent4:short] pertain to lateral support for walls described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art2.sent1:long] .
[REF:term:fndtn:Foundation] walls shall be considered to be laterally supported at the top if

clauses.text: such walls support a [REF:term:sld-m:solid masonry] superstructure or flat insulating concrete form wall,
the floor joists are embedded in the top of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls,

the floor system is anchored to the top of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls with anchor bolts, in which case the joists may run either parallel or perpendicular to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls, or

they extend from the footing to no more than 300 mm above the finished ground level and are backfilled on both sides such that the difference in elevation between the finished ground levels on either side of the wall is no more than 150 mm .

content.text: Unless the wall around an opening is reinforced to withstand earth pressure, the portion of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall beneath an opening shall be considered laterally unsupported if

clauses.text: the opening is more than 1.2 m wide, or
the total width of the openings in the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall constitutes more than 25% of the length of the wall.

content.text: For the purposes of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art3.sent3:short] , the combined width of the openings shall be considered as a single opening if the average width is greater than the width of solid wall between them.

Flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall be considered to be laterally supported at the top if the floor joists are installed according to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art5:long]

articles.title: Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Bottom

content.text: Flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall be considered to be laterally supported at the bottom where the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall

clauses.text: supports backfill not more than 1.2 m in height,
is supported at the footing by a shear key and at the top by the ground floor framing, or
is doweled to the footing with not less than

subclauses.text: 15M bars spaced not more than 1.2 m o.c. , or
10M bars spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.

articles.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Foundation Walls

content.text: Horizontal reinforcement in flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall

clauses.text: consist of

subclauses.text: one 10M bar placed not more than 300 mm from the top of the wall, and
10M bars at 600 mm o.c., and

clauses.text: be located

subclauses.text: in the inside half of the wall section, and
with a minimum cover of 30 mm from the inside face of the concrete.

content.text: Vertical reinforcement in flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall be

clauses.text: provided in accordance with

subclauses.text: [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art5.table1:long] for 150 mm walls,
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art5.table2:long] for 190 mm walls, and
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art5.table3:long] for 240 mm walls,

clauses.text: located in the inside half of the wall section with a minimum cover of 30 mm from the inside face of the concrete wall, and
where interrupted by wall openings, placed not more than 600 mm from each side of the openings.

content.text: Cold joints in flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall be reinforced with no less than one 15M bar spaced at not more than 600 mm o.c. and embedded 300 mm on both sides of the joint.

Reinforcing around openings in flat insulating concrete form [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art3:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art4:long]

content.text: Exterior [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall extend not less than 150 mm above finished ground level.

Where the top of a [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall is reduced in thickness to permit the installation of floor joists, the reduced section shall be not more than 350 mm high and not less than 90 mm thick.
Where the top of a [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall is reduced in thickness to permit the installation of a masonry exterior facing, the reduced section shall be

clauses.text: not less than 90 mm thick, and
tied to the facing material with metal ties conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent3:long] spaced not more than

subclauses.text: 200 mm o.c. vertically, and
900 mm o.c. horizontally.

content.text: The space between wall and facing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art7.sent2:short] shall be filled with mortar.
Corbelling of masonry [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls supporting [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect12.art2:long]
Crack control joints shall be provided in [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls more than 25 m long at intervals of not more than 15 m .

Joints required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect4.art9.sent1:short] shall be designed to resist moisture penetration and shall be keyed to prevent relative displacement of the wall portions adjacent to the joint.
Interior masonry [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls not subject to lateral earth pressure shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long]

subsections.title: Support of Joists and Beams on Masonry Foundation Walls

content.text: Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] , [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls of hollow masonry units supporting floor joists shall be capped with

clauses.text: not less than 50 mm of concrete,
[REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] that are 100% solid and not less than 50 mm high, or
semi-solid or hollow [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] that have the top course completely filled with mortar, grout or concrete.

content.text: Capping required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art1.sent1:short] need not be provided

clauses.text: in localities where termites are not known to occur,
when the joists are supported on a wood plate not less than 38 mm by 89 mm , and
when the siding overlaps the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall not less than 12 mm .

content.text: Not less than 190 mm depth of [REF:term:sld-m:solid masonry] shall be provided beneath beams supported on masonry.

Where the beam referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art2.sent1:short] is supported below the top of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls, the ends of such beams shall be protected from the weather.
Pilasters shall be provided under beams that frame into unit masonry [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls 140 mm or less in thickness.
Pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art3.sent1:short] shall be not less than 90 mm by 290 mm and shall be bonded or tied into the wall.

The top 200 mm of pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect5.art3.sent1:short] shall be [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry] with the cells of hollow or semi-solid units filled with mortar, grout or concrete.

subsections.title: Parging and Finishing of Masonry Foundation Walls

content.text: Concrete block [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall be parged on the exterior face below ground level as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13:long]
Exterior surfaces of concrete block [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls above ground level shall have tooled joints, or shall be parged or otherwise suitably finished.
All form ties shall be removed at least flush with the concrete surface.
This Section applies to floors supported on ground or on granular [REF:term:fll:fill] that do not provide structural support for the superstructure.
Floors-on-ground that support loads from the superstructure shall be designed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long] .
All spaces within [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , except crawl spaces, shall be provided with a floor-on-ground, where

clauses.text: access is provided to the space, and
a floor supported by the structure is not provided.

content.text: Dampproofing and waterproofing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect2.art1.sent2:short] , not less than 100 mm of coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve shall be placed beneath floors-on-ground. (See Note A-9.16.2.1.(1) and see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect13.subsect4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote88:long] )
Granular material need not be installed under

clauses.text: slabs in garages, carports or accessory [REF:term:bldng:buildings] , or

[REF:term:bldng:buildings] of [REF:term:ndtrl-cc:industrial occupancy] where the nature of the process contained therein permits or requires the use of large openings in the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope even during the winter.

content.text: Material that is susceptible to changes in volume due to variations in moisture content or chemical-microbiological oxidation shall not be used as [REF:term:fll:fill] beneath floors-on-ground in a concentration that will damage the [REF:term:bldng:building] to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect4.art4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote14:long] .)

Material that is susceptible to changes in volume due to freezing shall not be used as [REF:term:fll:fill] beneath floors-on-ground that will be subjected to freezing temperatures. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect4.art4:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote14:long] .)
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect2.art2.sent4:short] , [REF:term:fll:fill] beneath floors-on-ground shall be compacted.
[REF:term:fll:Fill] beneath floors-on-ground need not be compacted where the material is clean coarse aggregate containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect3.art2:long] or where it can be shown to be unnecessary, ingress of water underneath a floor-on-ground shall be prevented by grading or drainage.
Where [REF:term:grndwtr-:groundwater levels] may cause hydrostatic pressure beneath a floor-on-ground, the floor-on-ground shall be

clauses.text: a poured concrete slab, and
designed to resist such pressures.

content.text: When floor drains are required (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect31:long] ), the floor surface shall be sloped so that no water can accumulate.
The finished surface of concrete floor slabs shall be trowelled smooth and even.
Dry cement shall not be added to the floor surfaces to absorb surplus water.

When a topping course is provided for a concrete floor slab, it shall consist of 1 part cement to 2.5 parts clean, well graded sand by volume, with a water/cement ratio approximately equal to that of the base slab.
When concrete topping is provided, it shall not be less than 20 mm thick.
Concrete slabs shall not be less than 75 mm thick exclusive of concrete topping.
A bond-breaking material shall be placed between the slab and footings or [REF:term:rck:rock] .
Floors-on-ground constructed of wood shall conform to [REF:standard:csas406]
This Section applies to columns used to support

clauses.text: beams carrying loads from not more than 2 wood-frame floors where

subclauses.text: the supported length of joists bearing on such beams does not exceed 5 m , and
the [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] on any floor does not exceed 2.4 kPa (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect1.subsect5.art3.table1:long] ),

clauses.text: beams or header joists carrying loads from not more than 2 levels of wood-frame balconies, decks or other accessible exterior platforms, or 1 level plus the roof, where

subclauses.text: the supported length of joists bearing on such beams or joists does not exceed 5 m ,

the sum of the specified snow and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] loads does not exceed 4.8 kP a (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect2.art3.sent1:long] for the determination of load on platform-type constructions), and
the platform serves only a single [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] , or

clauses.text: carport roofs (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect35:long] ).

content.text: Columns for applications other than as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long] .
Columns shall be centrally located on a footing conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long]

Columns shall be securely fastened to the supported member to reduce the likelihood of lateral differential movement between the column and the supported member. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect6.art2:long] )
Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect2.art2.sent3:short] , columns shall be laterally supported to resist racking

clauses.text: directly, or
by connection to the supported members.

content.text: Columns need not be provided with lateral support as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] , where

clauses.text: the distance from finished ground to the underside of the joists is not more than 600 mm , and
the columns support a deck with no superstructure.

content.text: Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art1.sent2:short] , steel pipe columns shall have an outside diameter of not less than 73 mm and a wall thickness of not less than 4.76 mm .

Columns of sizes other than as specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] are permitted to be used where the [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] capacities are shown to be adequate.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art2.sent2:short] , steel columns shall be fitted with not less than 100 mm by 100 mm by 6.35 mm thick steel plates at each end, and where the column supports a wooden beam, the top plate shall extend across the full width of the beam.

The top plate required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art2.sent1:short] need not be provided where a column supports a steel beam and provision is made for the attachment of the column to the beam.
Exterior steel columns shall be treated on the outside surface with at least one coat of rust-inhibitive paint.
Where the imposed load does not exceed 36 kN , adjustable steel columns shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-7.2]
Steel columns other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] shall be designed in accordance with Part 4.
The width or diameter of a wood column shall be not less than the width of the supported member.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect35.subsect4.art2:long] , columns shall be not less than 184 mm for round columns and 140 mm by 140 mm for rectangular columns, unless calculations are provided to show that lesser sizes are adequate.
Wood columns shall be either solid, glued-laminated or built-up.
Built-up columns shall consist of not less than 38 mm thick full-length members

clauses.text: bolted together with not less than 9.52 mm diam bolts spaced not more than 450 mm o.c., or
nailed together with not less than 76 mm nails spaced not more than 300 mm o.c.

content.text: Glued-laminated columns shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3:long]
Wood columns shall be separated from concrete in contact with the ground by 0.05 mm polyethylene film or Type S roll roofing.
Unit masonry columns shall be built of masonry units

clauses.text: conforming to [REF:standard:csaa165.1] and
having a compressive strength over the net area of the block of not less than 15 MPa .

content.text: Unit masonry columns shall be not less than 290 mm by 290 mm or 240 mm by 380 mm in size.
Concrete shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3:long]
Concrete columns shall be not less than 200 mm by 200 mm for rectangular columns and 230 mm diam for circular columns.
This Section applies to crawl spaces whose exterior walls have less than 25% of their total area above exterior ground level open to the outdoors.
[REF:term:fndtn:Foundations ] enclosing crawl spaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long]
Crawl spaces shall be considered to be heated where the space

clauses.text: is used as a hot air [REF:term:plnm:plenum] ,
contains heating ducts that are not sealed and insulated to minimize heat loss to the space, or
is not separated from heated space in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25:long]

content.text: Heating of heated crawl spaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long]

Insulation, an [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] and a [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] shall be installed in the walls of heated crawl spaces in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25:long]

An access opening of not less than 500 mm by 700 mm shall be provided to each crawl space where the crawl space serves a single [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , and not less than 550 mm by 900 mm for other crawl spaces.
Access openings shall be fitted with a door or hatch, except when the crawl space is heated and the access opening into the crawl space is from an adjacent heated space.
Unheated crawl spaces shall be ventilated by natural or mechanical means.

Where an unheated crawl space is ventilated by natural means, ventilation shall be provided to the outside air by not less than 0.1 m^{2} of unobstructed vent area for every 50 m^{2} of [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] .
Vents shall be

clauses.text: uniformly distributed on opposite sides of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , and
designed to prevent the entry of snow, rain and insects.

content.text: Heated crawl spaces shall be ventilated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long]

Where equipment requiring service such as plumbing cleanouts, traps and burners is located in crawl spaces, an access way with a height and width of not less than 600 mm shall be provided from the access door to the equipment and for a distance of 900 mm on the side or sides of the equipment to be serviced.
Except where it can be shown to be unnecessary, the ingress of water into a crawl space shall be controlled by grading or drainage.
Drainage of [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14.subsect2.art1:long]
Drainage of the ground cover or floor-on-ground in the crawl space shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect16.subsect3:long]
Drains shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14:long]

articles.title: Ground Cover in Unheated Crawl Spaces

content.text: Where a crawl space is unheated, a ground cover shall be provided consisting of not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm of asphalt,
100 mm of 15 MPa Portland cement concrete,
Type S roll roofing, or
0.10 mm polyethylene.

content.text: Joints in sheet-type ground cover required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art1.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 100 mm and weighted down.

articles.title: Ground Cover in Heated Crawl Spaces

content.text: Where a crawl space is heated, a ground cover consisting of not less than 0.15 mm polyethylene sheet conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-51.34] shall be installed as part of an [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long]
The ground cover required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall have its joints lapped not less than 300 mm , and

clauses.text: be sealed and evenly weighted down, or
be covered with concrete not less than 50 mm thick.

content.text: The perimeter of the ground cover required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall be sealed to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall. (See  Notes [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote88:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote145:long] ,  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote146:long] .)

All penetrations of the ground cover required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall be sealed against air leakage. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] )

articles.title: Crawl Spaces as Warm Air Plenums

content.text: Only crawl spaces under 1- [REF:term:tr:storey] portions of [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] shall be used as warm-air [REF:term:plnm:plenums] .

Enclosing material in crawl spaces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect7.art1.sent1:short] , including insulation, shall have a surface [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating ] not greater than 150.

[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] ground cover in crawl spaces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect7.art1.sent1:short] shall be protected beneath each register opening with [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material.
The [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] register protection described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect7.art1.sent3:short] shall

clauses.text: extend not less than 300 mm beyond the projection of the register opening, and
have up-turned edges.

content.text: Except where it can be shown to be unnecessary, where insulation is installed between a ceiling and the underside of the roof sheathing, a space shall be provided between the insulation and the sheathing, and vents shall be installed to permit the transfer of moisture from the space to the exterior. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote101:short] .)
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art2.sent2:short] , the unobstructed vent area shall be not less than 1/300 of the insulated ceiling area.
Where the roof slope is less than 1 in 6 or in roofs that are constructed with roof joists, the unobstructed vent area shall be not less than 1/150 of the insulated ceiling area.
Required vents may be roof type, eave type, gable-end type or any combination thereof, and shall be distributed

clauses.text: uniformly on opposite sides of the [REF:term:bldng:building] ,
with not less than 25% of the required openings located at the top of the space, and
with not less than 25% of the required openings located at the bottom of the space.

content.text: Except where each joist space is separately vented, roof joist spaces shall be interconnected by installing purlins not less than 38 mm by 38 mm on the top of the roof joists.
Vents shall comply with [REF:standard:csaa93]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art3.sent2:short] , not less than 63 mm of space shall be provided between the top of the insulation and the underside of the roof sheathing.
At the junction of sloped roofs and exterior walls, where preformed baffles are used to contain the insulation, the baffles shall

clauses.text: provide an unobstructed air space, between the insulation and the underside of the roof sheathing, that is

subclauses.text: not less than 25 mm in dimension, and
of sufficient cross area to meet the [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof space] venting requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art2:long] , and

clauses.text: extend vertically not less than 50 mm above the top of the insulation.

content.text: Ceiling insulation shall be installed in a manner that will not restrict the free flow of air through roof vents or through any portion of the [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof space] .
The lower portion of a mansard or gambrel style roof need not be ventilated.

The upper portion of roofs described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art4.sent1:short] shall be ventilated in conformance with  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art1:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art3:long]
Every [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof space] shall be provided with an access hatch where the open space in the [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof space ] measures

clauses.text: 3 m^{2} or more in area,
1 m or more in length or width, and

600 mm or more in height over at least the area described in  Clauses [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect2.art1.sent1.clause1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect2.art1.sent1.clause2:short] .

content.text: The hatch required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect2.art1.sent1:short] shall be not less than 550 mm by 900 mm except that, where the hatch serves not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , the hatch may be reduced to 0.32 m^{2} in area with no dimension less than 500 mm .
Hatchways to [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof spaces] shall be fitted with doors or covers.

sections.title: Masonry and Insulating Concrete Form Walls Not In Contact with the Ground

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect1.art2:long] , this Section applies to

clauses.text: unreinforced masonry and masonry veneer walls not in contact with the ground, where

subclauses.text: the height of the walls constructed on the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls does not exceed 11 m , and
the roof or floor assembly above the [REF:term:frt-tr:first storey] is not of concrete construction, and

clauses.text: flat insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the ground that (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote94:short] )

subclauses.text: have a maximum floor-to-floor height of 3 m ,
are erected in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] not more than 2 [REF:term:tr:storeys] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] , and
are erected in locations where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is not greater than 0.27 (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect2.art5:long] ).

content.text: For walls other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] , or where the masonry walls or insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the ground are designed for specified loads on the basis of ultimate and serviceability limit states, [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long] shall apply.

In locations where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than 0.37, [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] elements of masonry [REF:term:bldng:buildings] more than 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] shall be reinforced with not less than the minimum amount of reinforcement required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect15:long]

In locations where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than 0.23 but not greater than 0.37, [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] elements of masonry [REF:term:bldng:buildings] 3 [REF:term:tr:storeys ] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] shall be reinforced with not less than the minimum amount of reinforcement required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect15:long]
Masonry units shall comply with

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc73]
[REF:standard:astmc126]
[REF:standard:astmc212]
[REF:standard:csaa82]
[REF:standard:csaa165.1]
[REF:standard:csaa165.2] or
[REF:standard:csaa165.3]

content.text: Used bricks shall be free of old mortar, soot or other surface coating and shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect2.art1:long]
Glass blocks shall not be used as [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] units or in the construction of fireplaces or [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] .
Masonry made with cellular concrete shall not be used in contact with the [REF:term:l:soil] or exposed to the weather.
Stone shall be sound and durable.

articles.title: Concrete Blocks Exposed to the Weather

content.text: Concrete blocks exposed to the weather shall have density and water absorption characteristics conforming to concrete types A, B, C, or D described in [REF:standard:csaa165.1]
The compressive strength of concrete blocks shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect2.art7.table1:long]

content.value: Minimum Compressive Strength Over Net Area, MPa

content.text: Cementitious materials and aggregates for mortar and grout shall comply with [REF:standard:csaa179]
Water and aggregate shall be clean and free of significant amounts of deleterious materials.
Lime used in mortar shall be hydrated.
If lime putty is used in mortar, it shall be made by slaking quicklime in water for not less than 24 h or soaking hydrated lime in water for not less than 12 h .
Mortar types shall be in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect3.art2.table1:long] .
Mortar for glass block masonry shall be

clauses.text: Type S Portland cement-lime where exposed to the exterior, or
Type S or N where protected from the exterior.

content.text: Mortar shall be mixed within the proportion limits provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect3.art2.table2:long] , with sufficient water to bring the mixture to a consistency adequate for laying masonry units.

Grout shall be mixed within the proportion limits provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect3.art2.table3:long] , with sufficient water to provide a suitable flow to fill all voids completely, without excessive segregation or bleeding.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect3.art2.sent6:short] , mortar shall be used and placed in final position

clauses.text: within 1.5 h after mixing when the air temperature is 25°C or higher, or
within 2.5 h after mixing when the air temperature is less than 25°C.

content.text: Mortar and grout containing a set-control admixture shall be manufactured off-site in a batching plant and shall be used and placed in final position within a time not exceeding the useful life stipulated by the manufacturer.
Grout used for reinforced masonry shall be placed in accordance with the requirements of [REF:standard:csaa371]

content.value: 2¼ to 3 times the sum of the cement and lime volumes
1 to 2 times the sum of the cement and lime volumes

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect4.art1.sent2:short] , mortar joint thickness for burned clay brick and concrete masonry units shall be 10 mm .
Permitted tolerances in head and bed joints shall be not more than ± 5 mm .
Hollow masonry units shall be laid with mortar applied to head and bed joints of both inner and outer face shells.
Vertically aligned webs of hollow masonry units shall be laid in a full bed of mortar

clauses.text: under the starting course,
in all courses of columns, and
where adjacent to cells or cavities that are to be filled with grout.

content.text: Except for head joints left open for weep holes and ventilation, [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] shall be laid with full head and bed joints.

All masonry shall be supported on masonry, concrete or steel, except that masonry veneer walls may be supported on [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] of wood frame constructed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect2.art4.sent1:long] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote104:short] .)
Every masonry wall shall be at least as thick as the wall it supports, except as otherwise permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect12.art2:long]
Masonry over openings shall be supported by steel, masonry or reinforced concrete lintels, or masonry arches.
Steel angle lintels supporting masonry veneer above openings shall

clauses.text: conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect5.art2.table1:long] , and
have a bearing length not less than 90 mm .

content.title: Maximum Allowable Spans for Steel Lintels Supporting Masonry Veneer

content.text: Steel angle lintels supporting masonry other than veneer, masonry and reinforced concrete lintels, and masonry arches shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long] to support the imposed load.
Steel angle lintels supporting masonry shall be prime painted or otherwise protected from corrosion.

Masonry exterior walls, other than [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] , in 1- [REF:term:tr:storey]  [REF:term:bldng:buildings] and the top [REF:term:tr:storeys] of 2- and 3- [REF:term:tr:storey]  [REF:term:bldng:buildings] shall be not less than 140 mm thick, provided the walls are not more than 2.8 m high at the eaves and 4.6 m high at the peaks of gable ends.

The exterior walls of the bottom [REF:term:tr:storeys] of 2- [REF:term:tr:storey]  [REF:term:bldng:buildings] , and exterior walls of the bottom 2 [REF:term:tr:storeys] of 3- [REF:term:tr:storey]  [REF:term:bldng:buildings] shall be not less than 190 mm thick.
In exterior walls composed of more than one wythe, each wythe shall be not less than 90 mm thick.
[REF:term:cvt-wll:Cavity walls] shall be made with not less than 90 mm wide units if the joints are raked and not less than 75 mm wide units if the joints are not raked.
The width of a cavity in a [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity wall ] shall be not less than 50 mm and not greater than 150 mm .

The minimum thickness of [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls ] above the supporting base shall be 230 mm for the top 7.6 m and 330 mm for the remaining portion, except that where 75 mm wide units are used, the wall height above the top of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall shall not exceed 6 m .

The thickness of [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] interior walls shall be determined on the basis of the maximum lateral support spacing as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent3:short] .
The thickness of interior non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls shall be

clauses.text: determined on the basis of the maximum lateral support spacing as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent3:short] , and
in any case, not less than 65 mm .

content.text: Except for masonry veneer where each masonry unit is supported individually by the structural backing, masonry veneer shall consist of [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] not less than 75 mm thick.
Veneer described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect6.art4.sent1:short] over wood-frame walls shall have not less than a 25 mm air space behind the veneer.
Masonry veneer less than 90 mm thick shall have unraked joints.
Masonry veneer shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long] , where the masonry units are required to be individually supported by the structural backing.
The height of parapet walls above the adjacent roof surface shall be not more than 3 times the parapet wall thickness.
Parapet walls shall be [REF:term:sld-m:solid masonry]

clauses.text: with the cells of hollow or semi-solid units filled with mortar, grout, or concrete, and
that extends from the top of the parapet to not less than 300 mm below the adjacent roof level.

content.text: Slab and panel facings of precast concrete and natural or artificial stone shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long]

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art2.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art4:long] , the depth of any chase or recess shall not exceed one third the thickness of the wall, and the width of the chase or recess shall not exceed 500 mm .

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art2.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art4:long] , no chase or recess shall be constructed in any wall 190 mm or less in thickness.
Recesses may be constructed in 190 mm walls provided they do not exceed 100 mm in depth, 750 mm in height and 500 mm in width.
Chases and recesses shall be not less than

clauses.text: 4 times the wall thickness apart, and
600 mm away from any pilaster, cross wall, buttress or other vertical element providing required lateral support for the wall.

content.text: Chases or recesses that do not conform to the limits specified in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art1:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect7.art3:long] shall be considered as openings, and any masonry supported above such a chase or recess shall be supported by a lintel or arch as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect5.art2:long]

articles.title: Chases or Recesses Cut into Walls

content.text: Chases and recesses shall not be cut into walls made with hollow units after the masonry units are in place.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art1.sent2:short] , [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls of hollow masonry units supporting roof or floor framing members shall be capped with not less than 50 mm of [REF:term:sld-m:solid masonry] or have the top course filled with concrete.
Capping required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art1.sent1:short] may be omitted where the roof framing is supported on a wood plate not less than 38 mm by 89 mm .
Floor joists supported on [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls ] shall be supported on [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] not less than 57 mm high.
Floor joists described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art2.sent1:short] shall not project into the cavity.
Roof and ceiling framing members bearing on [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] shall be supported on

clauses.text: [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] not less than 57 mm high that bridge the full thickness of the wall, or
a wood plate not less than 38 mm thick, bearing not less than 50 mm on each wythe.

content.text: The bearing area under beams and joists shall be sufficient to carry the supported load.
In no case shall the minimum length of end bearing of beams supported on masonry be less than 90 mm .
The length of end bearing of floor, roof or ceiling joists supported on masonry shall be not less than 40 mm .
Beams and columns supported on masonry walls shall be supported on pilasters where the thickness of the masonry wall or wythe is less than 190 mm .
Not less than 190 mm depth of [REF:term:sld-m:solid masonry] or concrete shall be provided under the beam or column referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] .
Pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be bonded or tied to masonry walls.
Concrete pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be not less than 50 mm by 300 mm .
Unit masonry pilasters required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be not less than 100 mm by 290 mm .

articles.title: Projection of Masonry Veneer Beyond Supporting Members

content.text: Masonry veneer of [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] resting on a bearing support shall not project more than one third of the thickness of the veneer. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote105:short] .)
Where the masonry veneer described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect8.art5.sent1:short] is rough stone masonry,

clauses.text: the projection shall be measured as the average projection of the units, and
the thickness of the veneer shall be measured as the average thickness of the veneer.

articles.title: Joints to be Offset or Reinforced

content.text: Vertical joints in adjacent masonry courses shall be offset unless each wythe of masonry is reinforced with the equivalent of not less than 2 corrosion-resistant steel bars of 3.76 mm diam placed in the horizontal joints at vertical intervals not exceeding 460 mm .
Where joints in the reinforcing referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art1.sent1:short] occur, the bars shall be lapped not less than 150 mm .

articles.title: Bonding or Tying of Other than Masonry Veneer

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art5:long] regarding masonry veneer, masonry walls that consist of 2 or more wythes shall have the wythes bonded or tied together with masonry bonding units as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art3:long] or with metal ties as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4:long]
Where wythes are bonded together with masonry units, the bonding units shall comprise not less than 4% of the wall surface area.

Bonding units described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art3.sent1:short] shall be spaced not more than 600 mm vertically and horizontally in the case of brick masonry and 900 mm o.c. in the case of block or tile.
Units described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art3.sent1:short] shall extend not less than 90 mm into adjacent wythes.

Where 2 or more wythes are tied together with metal ties of the individual rod type, the ties shall conform to the requirements in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent3:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent6:short] .
Other ties may be used where it can be shown that such ties provide walls that are at least as strong and as durable as those made with the individual rod type.
Metal ties of the individual rod type shall

clauses.text: be corrosion-resistant,
have a minimum cross-sectional area of not less than 17.8 mm^{2} , and
have not less than a 50 mm portion bent at right angles at each end.

content.text: Metal ties of the individual rod type shall

clauses.text: extend from within 25 mm of the outer face of the wall to within 25 mm of the inner face of the wall,
be completely embedded in mortar except for the portion exposed in [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] , and
be staggered from course to course.

content.text: Where 2 or more wythes in walls other than [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls are tied together with metal ties of the individual rod type, the space between wythes shall be completely filled with mortar.
Ties described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent5:short] shall be

clauses.text: located within 300 mm of openings and spaced not more than 900 mm apart around openings, and
spaced not more than 900 mm apart horizontally and 460 mm apart vertically at other locations.

content.text: Except as required in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent8:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent9:short] , where the inner and outer wythes of [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] are tied with individual wire ties, the ties shall be spaced not more than 900 mm apart horizontally and 400 mm apart vertically.

Within 100 mm of the bottom of each floor or roof assembly where the cavity extends below the assemblies, the ties described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent7:short] shall be spaced not more than 600 mm apart horizontally.
Within 300 mm of any openings, the ties described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art4.sent7:short] shall be spaced not more than 900 mm apart.
Masonry veneer 75 mm or more in thickness and resting on a bearing support shall be tied to masonry backing or to wood framing members with straps that are

clauses.text: corrosion-resistant,
not less than 0.76 mm thick ,
not less than 22 mm wide ,
shaped to provide a key with the mortar,
pre-bent during manufacture to a right angle within 6 mm of the fastener hole,
fastened with

subclauses.text: corrosion-resistant wood screws conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art1.sent3:long] that have a minimum diameter of 4.16 mm(No. 8) and a wood penetration of not less than 38 mm , or

corrosion-resistant common spiral nails conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art1.sent1:long] that are not less than 76 mm long and have a wood penetration of not less than 63 mm , and

clauses.text: spaced in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art5.table1:long]

content.text: Where hot-dipped, zinc-coated straps are used to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art5.sent1:short] , they shall be pre-bent and pre-drilled or pre-punched prior to hot-dip, zinc-coated galvanizing.
Masonry veneer individually supported by masonry or wood-frame backing shall be secured to the backing in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long]
Glass block shall have horizontal joint reinforcement of 2 corrosion-resistant bars of not less than 3.76 mm diam or expanded metal strips not less than 75 mm wide

clauses.text: spaced at vertical intervals of not more than 600 mm for units 200 mm or less in height, and
installed in every horizontal joint for units higher than 200 mm .
