content.text: Reinforcement required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect9.art6.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 150 mm .
Masonry walls shall be laterally supported by floor or roof construction or by intersecting masonry walls or buttresses.
The spacing of supports required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent1:short] shall be not more than

clauses.text: 20 times the wall thickness for all [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing ] walls and exterior non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls, and
36 times the wall thickness for interior non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing ] walls.

content.text: In applying [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent2:short] , the thickness of [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] shall be taken as the greater of

clauses.text: two-thirds of the sum of the thicknesses of the wythes, or
the thickness of the thicker wythe.

content.text: Floor and roof constructions providing lateral support for walls as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10.art1.sent1:short] shall be constructed to transfer lateral loads to walls or buttresses approximately at right angles to the laterally supported walls.

subsections.title: Anchorage of Roofs, Floors and Intersecting Walls

articles.title: Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require Lateral Support

content.text: Where required to receive lateral support (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect10:long] ), masonry walls shall be anchored to each floor or roof assembly at maximum intervals of 2 m , except that anchorage to floor joists not more than 1 m above [REF:term:grade:grade] may be omitted.
Anchors required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art1.sent1:short] shall be corrosion-resistant and be not less than the equivalent of 40 mm by 4.76 mm thick steel straps.

Anchors required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art1.sent1:short] shall be shaped to provide a mechanical key with the masonry and shall be securely fastened to the horizontal support to develop the full strength of the anchor.
When joists are parallel to the wall, anchors required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art1.sent1:short] shall extend across not less than 3 joists.

articles.title: Bonding and Tying Intersecting Masonry Walls where Walls Require Lateral Support

content.text: Where required to provide lateral support, intersecting walls shall be bonded or tied together.

Where bonding is used to satisfy the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art2.sent1:short] , 50% of the adjacent masonry units in the intersecting wall, distributed uniformly over the height of the intersection, shall be embedded in the laterally supported wall.
Where tying is used to satisfy the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art2.sent1:short] , the ties shall be

clauses.text: corrosion-resistant metal,
equivalent to not less than 4.76 mm by 40 mm steel strapping,
spaced not more than 800 mm o.c. vertically, and
shaped at both ends to provide sufficient mechanical key to develop the strength of the ties.

articles.title: Anchoring Intersecting Wood-Frame Walls to Masonry Walls

content.text: Wood-frame walls shall be anchored to masonry walls that they intersect with not less than 4.76 mm diam corrosion-resistant steel rods spaced not more than 900 mm o.c. vertically.

Anchors required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art3.sent1:short] shall be fastened to the wood framing at one end and shaped to provide a mechanical key at the other end to develop the strength of the anchor.

articles.title: Anchoring Wood-Frame Roof Systems to Masonry Walls

content.text: Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art4.sent2:short] , roof systems of wood-frame construction shall be anchored to exterior masonry walls by not less than 12.7 mm diam anchor bolts,

clauses.text: spaced not more than 2.4 m apart,
embedded not less than 90 mm into the masonry, and
fastened to a rafter plate of not less than 38 mm thick lumber.

content.text: The roof system described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect11.art4.sent1:short] is permitted to be anchored by nailing the wall furring strips to the side of the rafter plate.

articles.title: Anchoring Masonry Cornices, Sills and Trim to Masonry Walls

content.text: Cornices, sills or other trim of masonry material which project beyond the wall face shall have not less than 65% of their mass, but not less than 90 mm , within the wall or shall be adequately anchored to the wall with corrosion-resistant anchors.

Where anchor bolts are to be placed in the top of a masonry pier, the pier shall conform to the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15.subsect2.art3.sent4:long] and shall be capped with concrete or reinforced masonry not less than 200 mm thick.
All corbelling shall consist of [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] .

The units referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect12.art1.sent1:short] shall be corbelled so that the horizontal projection of any unit does not exceed 25 mm and the total projection does not exceed one third of the total wall thickness.

[REF:term:cvt-wll:Cavity walls] of greater thickness than the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall on which they rest shall not be corbelled but may project 25 mm over the outer face of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall disregarding parging.

Where the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect12.art2.sent1:short] is unit masonry, it is permitted to be corbelled to meet flush with the inner face of a [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity wall] provided

clauses.text: the projection of each course does not exceed half the height or one third the thickness of the corbelled unit, and
the total corbel does not exceed one third of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall thickness.

content.text: Masonry veneer resting on a bearing support shall not project more than 25 mm beyond the supporting base where the veneer is not less than 90 mm thick, and 12 mm beyond the supporting base where the veneer is less than 90 mm thick.
In the case of rough stone veneer, the projection, measured as the average projection of the stone units, shall not exceed one-third the bed width beyond the supporting base.
Materials used for flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art1.table1:long]

content.value: Copper or aluminum laminated to felt or kraft paper

content.text: Aluminum flashing in contact with masonry or concrete shall be effectively coated or separated from the masonry or concrete by an impervious membrane.
Fastening devices for flashing shall be corrosion-resistant and, where metal flashing is used, shall be compatible with the flashing with respect to galvanic action.
Flashing shall be installed in masonry and masonry veneer walls

clauses.text: beneath jointed masonry window sills,
over the back and top of parapet walls,
over the heads of glass block panels,
beneath weep holes, and

over the heads of window or door openings in exterior walls when the vertical distance between the top of a window or door frame and the bottom edge of the eave exceeds one-quarter of the horizontal eave overhang.

content.text: When installed beneath jointed masonry window sills or over the heads of openings, flashing shall extend from the front edge of the masonry up behind the sill or lintel.

articles.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry/Masonry Walls

content.text: Flashing beneath weep holes in [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls shall

clauses.text: be bedded not less than 25 mm in the inside wythe,
extend to not less than 5 mm beyond the outer face of the [REF:term:bldng:building] element below the flashing, and
be installed with a nominally horizontal slope toward the outside wythe.

articles.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry Veneer

content.text: Flashing beneath weep holes in masonry veneer over masonry backing walls shall conform to the flashing requirements for [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls in  Article [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art5:long]

Flashing beneath weep holes in masonry veneer over wood-frame walls shall be installed so that it extends from a point not less than 5 mm beyond the outer face of the [REF:term:bldng:building] element below the flashing to a point 150 mm up the wood-frame wall.

Where the frame wall is sheathed with a sheathing membrane, a non-wood-based rigid exterior insulating sheathing or a semi-rigid insulating sheathing with an integral sheathing membrane, the flashing shall be installed behind the sheathing membrane or insulating sheathing.

Flashing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art6.sent2:short] is permitted to conform to the requirements for concealed flashing in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art1.table1:long]
Joints in flashing shall be made watertight.
Weep holes spaced not more than 800 mm apart shall be provided at the bottom of

clauses.text: cavities in [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] , and
cavities or air spaces in masonry veneer walls.

content.text: The cavities or air spaces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art8.sent1:short] shall include those above lintels over window and door openings required to be flashed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art3:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art9.sent3:short] , where the interior finish of the exterior walls of a [REF:term:bldng:building] is a type that may be damaged by moisture, exterior masonry walls, other than [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] or walls that are protected for their full height by a roof of a carport or porch, shall be covered on the interior surface with sheathing membrane conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-51.32] lapped not less than 100 mm at the joints.
In situations described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art9.sent1:short] , flashing shall be provided where water will accumulate, to lead it to the exterior.

Where insulation that effectively limits the passage of water is applied by a waterproof adhesive or mortar directly to parged masonry, the requirements for sheathing membrane in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art9.sent1:short] do not apply. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote107:short] .)
[REF:term:cvt-wll:Cavity walls] shall be constructed so that mortar droppings are prevented from forming a bridge to allow the passage of rain water across the cavity.

articles.title: Caulking at Door and Window Frames

content.text: The junction of door and window frames with masonry shall be caulked in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long]
Where no flashing is installed beneath window sills, such sills shall be provided with a drip not less than 25 mm from the wall surface.

articles.title: Laying Temperature of Mortar and Masonry

content.text: Mortar and masonry shall be maintained at a temperature not below 5°C during installation and for not less than 48 h after installation.
No frozen material shall be used in mortar mix.
The top surface of uncompleted masonry exposed to the weather shall be completely covered with a waterproofing material when construction is not in progress.

Where reinforcement is required in this Section, masonry walls shall be reinforced horizontally and vertically with steel having a total cross-sectional area of not less than 0.002 times the horizontal cross-sectional area of the wall, so that not less than one-third of the required steel area is installed either horizontally or vertically and the remainder in the other direction.
Where reinforcement for masonry is required in this Section, it shall be installed in conformance with the requirements for reinforced masonry as contained in [REF:standard:csaa371]
Carbon steel connectors required to be corrosion-resistant shall be galvanized to at least the minimum standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect16.art1.table1:long]

table_notes.content: [REF:standard:astma123m] does not apply to metal less than 0.76 mm thick . Galvanizing coatings may be interpolated for thicknesses between 3.18 mm and 0.76 mm .

content.value: Wire ties and continuous reinforcing (hot-dipped galvanizing)
Strip, plate, bars and rolled sections (not less than 3.18 mm thick )

subsections.title: Above-Ground Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

articles.title: Thickness of Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text: The thickness of the concrete in flat insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the ground shall be

clauses.text: not less than 140 mm , and
constant for the entire height of the wall.

articles.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text: Horizontal reinforcement in above-grade flat insulating concrete form walls shall

clauses.text: consist of

subclauses.text: one 10M bar placed not more than 300 mm from the top of the wall, and
10M bars at 600 mm o.c., and

clauses.text: be placed in the middle third of the wall section.

content.text: Vertical reinforcement in above-grade flat insulating concrete form walls shall

clauses.text: consist of 10M bars at 400 mm o.c., and
be placed in the middle third of the wall section.

content.text: Vertical reinforcement required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art2.sent2:short] and interrupted by wall openings shall be placed not more than 600 mm from each side of the opening.

articles.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text: No openings shall occur within 1 200 mm of interior and exterior corners of exterior non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] flat insulating concrete form walls.

Portions of walls above openings in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] flat insulating concrete form walls shall have a minimum depth of concrete of no less than 200 mm across the width of the opening.

Openings that are more than 600 mm but not more than 3 000 mm in width in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] flat insulating concrete form walls shall be reinforced at the top and bottom with one 10M bar.
Openings more than 3 000 mm in width in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] flat insulating concrete form walls shall be reinforced on all four sides with two 10M bars.

Reinforcing bars described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art3.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art3.sent4:short] shall extend 600 mm beyond the edges of the opening.
The cumulative width of openings in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] flat insulating concrete form walls shall not make up more than 70% of the length of any wall.

articles.title: Openings in Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text: No openings shall occur within 1 200 mm of interior and exterior corners of exterior [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] flat insulating concrete form walls.
In [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] flat insulating concrete form walls, lintels shall be provided over all openings wider than 900 mm .

Lintels described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art4.sent2:short] shall be constructed in accordance with  Span Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table2:number] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table3:number] .

Lintels described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art4.sent2:short] over openings wider than 1 200 mm shall be reinforced for shear with 10M stirrups at a maximum spacing of half the distance from the bottom reinforcing bar to the top of the lintel.

articles.title: Framing Supported on Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text: Floor joists supported on the side of flat insulating concrete form walls shall be supported with joist hangers secured to wood ledger boards.
The ledger boards referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art5.sent1:short] shall be not less than

clauses.text: 38 mm thick, and
the depth of the floor joists.

content.text: Anchor bolts shall be used to secure ledger boards to flat insulating concrete form walls and shall be

clauses.text: embedded in the wall to a depth not less than 100 mm , and
spaced in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art5.table1:long]

content.text: Floor joists and [REF:term:bldng:building] frames supported on the top of flat insulating concrete form walls shall be anchored in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect6.art1:long]

content.title: Maximum Anchor Bolt Spacing for the Connection of Floor Ledgers to Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

articles.title: Anchoring of Roof Framing to the Top of Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls

content.text: Roof framing supported on the top of flat insulating concrete form walls shall be fixed to the top plates, which shall be anchored to the wall with anchor bolts

clauses.text: not less than 12.7 mm in diameter, and
spaced at not more than 1 200 mm o.c.

content.text: The anchor bolts described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect17.art6.sent1:short] shall be placed in the centre of the flat insulating concrete form wall and shall be embedded no less than 100 mm into the concrete.
Attachment of roof framing to wood top plates shall be in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]
Above-ground flat insulating concrete form walls shall be protected from precipitation and damage in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27:long]

sections.title: Masonry and Concrete Chimneys and Flues

content.text: This Section applies to

clauses.text: rectangular [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:masonry or concrete chimneys] not more than 12 m in height serving fireplaces or serving [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] having a combined total rated heat output of 120 kW or less, and
[REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipes] connected to such [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] .

content.text: [REF:term:chmn:Chimneys] , other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] , [REF:term:g-vnt:gas vents] and [REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipes] serving gas-, oil- or solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] and their associated equipment, including [REF:term:tv:stoves] , [REF:term:cktp:cooktops] , ovens and [REF:term:pc-htr:space heaters] , covered by the standards referenced in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art3.sent1:long] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect10:long]

[REF:term:chmn:Chimneys] and [REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipes] other than those described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect1.art1.sent2:short] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect3:long]
The walls of any [REF:term:chmn:chimney] or [REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipe] shall be constructed so as to be smoke- and flame-tight.
A [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] that serves a fireplace or incinerator shall not serve any other [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] .
A [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] that serves a solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] shall not be connected to a natural-gas- or propane-fired [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] .

A [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] that serves a solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] shall not be connected to an oil-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] unless the solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] is certified for such installation and the installation of both [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] meets the requirements of the relevant standards referenced in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2:long]

articles.title: Connections of More Than One Appliance

content.text: Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art1:long] , where two or more fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] are connected to the same [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] , the connections shall be made as described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art2.sent4:short] and an adequate draft shall be provided for the connected [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] in conformance with the requirements of applicable provincial or territorial regulations or municipal bylaws or, in the absence of such regulations or bylaws, with the requirements of the relevant standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect10:long]

Where 2 or more fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] are connected to the same [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] , the [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] shall be located on the same [REF:term:tr:storey] .

The connection referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] for a solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] shall be made below connections for [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] burning other fuels.

The connection referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] for a liquid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] shall be made below any connections for [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] burning natural gas or propane.
[REF:term:chmn:Chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flues] shall not be inclined more than 45° to the vertical.

Except for [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] serving fireplaces, the size of a [REF:term:chmn:chimney ] [REF:term:fl:flue] shall conform to the requirements of the [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] installation standards referenced in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art3.sent1:long] .

Where a [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] serves only one [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] , the [REF:term:fl:flue] area shall be at least equal to that of the [REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipe] connected to it.

The size of a [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] serving a masonry fireplace shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art5.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect2.art5.table2:long] .

content.title: Diameter of Round Flues for Fireplace Chimneys
Rectangular Flue Sizes for Fireplace Chimneys

content.text: The width of an oval [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] shall be not less than two-thirds its breadth.
Every [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:masonry or concrete chimney] shall have a lining of clay, concrete, firebrick or metal.

Joints of [REF:term:chmn-lnr:chimney liners] shall be sealed to provide a barrier to the passage of [REF:term:fl:flue] gases and condensate into the cavity between the liner and the surrounding masonry.
Joints of clay, concrete or firebrick [REF:term:chmn-lnr:chimney liners] shall be struck flush to provide a straight, smooth, aligned [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] .
Clay liners shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa324]

Liners referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect3.art3.sent1:short] shall be not less than 15.9 mm thick and shall be capable of resisting, without softening or cracking, a temperature of 1 100°C .
Firebrick liners shall conform to [REF:standard:astmc27]
Firebrick liners shall be laid with high temperature cement mortar conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-10.3]
Concrete [REF:term:fl:flue] liners shall conform to [REF:external:csaa405:Clause 4.2.6.4 of ] [REF:standard:csaa405]
Metal liners shall be constructed of not less than 0.3 mm thick stainless steel.

Metal liners referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] shall only be used in [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] serving gas- or oil-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote108:short] .)
[REF:term:chmn-lnr:Chimney liners] shall be installed when the surrounding masonry or concrete is placed.

articles.title: Spaces between Liners and Surrounding Masonry

content.text: A space not less than 10 mm wide shall be left between a [REF:term:chmn-lnr:chimney liner] and surrounding masonry.
The space required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect3.art8.sent1:short] shall not be filled with mortar.
[REF:term:chmn-lnr:Chimney liners] used in [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] for solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] shall be laid in a full bed of

clauses.text: high temperature cement mortar conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-10.3] or
mortar consisting of 1 part Portland cement to 3 parts sand by volume.

content.text: [REF:term:chmn-lnr:Chimney liners] used in [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] for oil- or gas-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] shall be laid in a full bed of mortar consisting of 1 part Portland cement to 3 parts sand by volume.

[REF:term:chmn-lnr:Chimney liners] shall extend from a point not less than 200 mm below the lowest [REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipe] connection to a point not less than 50 mm or more than 100 mm above the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] cap.
Unit masonry shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long]
Concrete shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3:long]
Footings for [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:masonry chimneys] and [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:concrete chimneys] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long]
A [REF:term:chmn:chimney ] [REF:term:fl:flue] shall extend not less than

clauses.text: 900 mm above the highest point at which the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] comes in contact with the roof, and
600 mm above the highest roof surface or structure within 3 m of the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] .

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect4.art5.sent2:short] , [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] shall be braced in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect2:long] to provide lateral stability under wind loads.
A [REF:term:chmn:chimney] need not be laterally braced provided

clauses.text: no horizontal outside dimension is less than 400 mm , and
the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] extends not more than 3.6 m above a roof or the masonry wall of which it forms a part.

content.text: The top of a [REF:term:chmn:chimney] shall have a waterproof cap of reinforced concrete, masonry or metal.
The cap required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect4.art6.sent1:short] shall slope from the lining and be provided with a drip not less than 25 mm from the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] wall.
Cast-in-place concrete caps shall be separated from the [REF:term:chmn-lnr:chimney liner] by a bond break and be sealed at that location.
Jointed precast concrete or masonry [REF:term:chmn:chimney] caps shall have flashing installed beneath the cap extending from the liner to the drip edge.
A cleanout opening with a metal frame and a tight-fitting metal door shall be installed near the base of the [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] .
The walls of a masonry [REF:term:chmn:chimney] shall be built of [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] not less than 75 mm thick.

[REF:term:fl:Flue] liners in the same [REF:term:chmn:chimney] shall be separated by not less than 75 mm of masonry or concrete exclusive of liners where clay liners are used, or 90 mm of firebrick where firebrick liners are used.
[REF:term:fl:Flue] liners referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21.subsect4.art9.sent1:short] shall be installed to prevent significant lateral movement.
Junctions with adjacent materials shall be adequately flashed to shed water.
The clearance between [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:masonry or concrete chimneys] and [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] framing shall be not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm for interior [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] , and
12 mm for exterior [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] .

content.text: A clearance of not less than 150 mm shall be provided between a cleanout opening and [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material.
[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] flooring and subflooring shall have not less than a 12 mm clearance from [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:masonry or concrete chimneys] .
All spaces between [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:masonry or concrete chimneys] and [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] framing shall be sealed top or bottom with [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material.

Joists or beams may be supported on masonry walls which enclose [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flues] provided the [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] members are separated from the [REF:term:fl:flue] by not less than 290 mm of [REF:term:sld-m:solid masonry] .
Except when otherwise specifically stated herein, this Section applies to masonry fireplaces constructed on-site.
Except as otherwise stated in this Section, unit masonry shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long] and concrete to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3:long]
Masonry above openings shall be supported by steel lintels conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect5.art2.sent2:long] , reinforced concrete or a masonry arch.
Footings for masonry and concrete fireplaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long]

Where a supply of combustion air is provided directly to the fire chamber of a fireplace, including a factory-built fireplace, the installation shall comply with the “Outdoor Air Supply” requirements provided in [REF:standard:csaa405]
Except where a fireplace is equipped with a steel liner, every fireplace shall have a firebrick liner.
Firebrick liners shall be not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm thick for the sides and back, and
25 mm thick for the floor.

content.text: Firebrick liners shall be laid with high temperature cement mortar conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-10.3]
Joints between a firebrick liner and the adjacent backing masonry shall be offset.
Steel liners for fireplaces shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs639] and shall be installed in accordance with the installation instructions in that standard.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22.subsect3.art1.sent2:short] , the thickness of the back and sides of a fireplace, including the thickness of any firebrick liner, shall be not less than 190 mm where a metal liner or a firebrick liner less than 51 mm thick is used.
When a steel fireplace liner is used with an air circulating chamber surrounding the firebox, the back and sides of the fireplace shall consist of

clauses.text: [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] not less than 90 mm thick, or
hollow masonry units not less than 190 mm thick.

content.text: The distance from the back of the fire chamber to the plane of the fireplace opening shall be not less than 300 mm .

Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] , fireplaces shall have a [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] hearth extending not less than 400 mm in front of the fireplace opening and not less than 200 mm beyond each side of the fireplace opening.

Where the fire chamber floor is elevated more than 150 mm above the hearth, the dimension of the hearth measured perpendicular to the plane of the fireplace opening shall be increased by not less than

clauses.text: 50 mm for an elevation above 150 mm and not more than 300 mm , and
an additional 25 mm for every 50 mm in elevation above 300 mm .

content.text: Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22.subsect5.art2.sent2:short] , the fire chamber floor and hearth shall be supported on a reinforced concrete slab not less than 100 mm thick at its supports and, if cantilevered, not less than 50 mm thick at its unsupported edge.

A hearth for a fireplace with an opening raised not less than 200 mm from a [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] floor is permitted to be supported on that floor provided the requirements of [REF:external:csaa405:Clauses 5.3.6.5. to 5.3.6.7. of ] [REF:standard:csaa405] are followed.
The throat of every fireplace shall be equipped with a metal damper sufficiently large to cover the full area of the throat opening.
The sides of the smoke chamber connecting a fireplace throat with a [REF:term:fl:flue] shall not be sloped at an angle greater than 45° to the vertical.

The thickness of masonry walls surrounding the smoke chamber shall be not less than 190 mm at the sides, front and back, except that the portions of the back exposed to the outside may be 140 mm thick.
Factory-built fireplaces and their installation shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs610]

[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] material shall not be placed on or near the face of a fireplace within 150 mm of the fireplace opening, except that where the [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material projects more than 38 mm out from the face of the fireplace above the opening, such material shall be not less than 300 mm above the top of the opening.

Metal exposed to the interior of a fireplace such as the damper control mechanism shall have not less than a 50 mm clearance from any [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material on the face of the fireplace where such metal penetrates through the face of the fireplace.

Not less than a 100 mm clearance shall be provided between the back and sides of a fireplace and [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] framing, except that a 50 mm clearance is permitted where the fireplace is located in an exterior wall.

Not less than a 50 mm clearance shall be provided between the back and sides of the smoke chamber of a fireplace and [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] framing, except that a 25 mm clearance is permitted where the fireplace is located in an exterior wall.
The clearance of [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material above heat-circulating duct outlets from those outlets shall be not less than

clauses.text: 300 mm where the [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material projects not less than 38 mm from the face, and
150 mm where the projection is less than 38 mm .

content.text: Fireplace inserts and hearth-mounted [REF:term:tv:stoves] vented through the throat of a fireplace shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs628]
The installation of fireplace inserts and hearth-mounted [REF:term:tv:stoves] vented through the throat of a fireplace shall conform to [REF:standard:csab365]

Subject to the application limitations defined elsewhere in this Part, this Section applies to constructions where wall, floor and roof planes are generally comprised of lumber frames of small repetitive structural members, or engineered components, and where

clauses.text: roof and wall planes are clad, sheathed or braced on at least one side,
the small repetitive structural members are spaced not more than 600 mm o.c. ,
the constructions do not serve as [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] ,
the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live load] on supported subfloors and floor framing does not exceed 2.4 kPa , and
the span of any structural member does not exceed 12.20 m .

content.text: Where the conditions in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] are exceeded for wood constructions, the design of the framing and fastening shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4.sect3.subsect1:long]
All members shall be so framed, anchored, fastened, tied and braced to provide the necessary strength and rigidity.

Ends of wood joists, beams and other members framing into masonry or concrete shall be treated to prevent decay where the bottom of the member is at or below ground level, or a 12 mm air space shall be provided at the end and sides of the member.
Air spaces required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] shall not be blocked by insulation, [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barriers] or airtight materials.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art3.sent2:short] , wood framing members that are not pressure-treated with a wood preservative and that are supported on concrete in contact with the ground or [REF:term:fll:fill] shall be separated from the concrete by not less than 0.05 mm polyethylene film or Type S roll roofing.
Dampproofing material referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art3.sent1:short] is not required where the wood member is at least 150 mm above the ground.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art4.sent3:short] , connectors in contact with preservative-treated wood shall be made of

clauses.text: hot-dipped, zinc-coated galvanized steel with a coating weight not less than Z550 conforming to [REF:standard:astma653m] , "Standard Specification for Steel Sheet, Zinc-Coated (Galvanized) or Zinc-Iron Alloy-Coated (Galvannealed) by the Hot-Dip Process,"
a material that provides an equivalent level of corrosion protection to that provided by the material described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art4.sent1.clause1:short] , or
stainless steel.

content.text: Fasteners used to attach the connectors referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect2.art4.sent1:short] shall be made of

clauses.text: galvanized steel coated with zinc in accordance with [REF:standard:astma153m] , "Standard Specification for Zinc Coating (Hot-Dip) on Iron and Steel Hardware," or
a material that provides an equivalent level of performance and is compatible with the connector.

content.text: Connectors and fasteners that are in contact with wood that has been treated with a disodium octaborate tetrahydrate (SBX (DOT)) or zinc borate preservative and is installed in a dry interior environment are permitted to be made of uncoated carbon steel. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote114:short] .)
Lumber shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect3.subsect2:long]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art1.sent2:short] and unless otherwise indicated, nails specified in this Section shall be common steel wire nails or common spiral nails conforming to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmf1667] , "Standard Specification for Driven Fasteners: Nails, Spikes, and Staples," or
[REF:standard:csab111] , "Wire Nails, Spikes and Staples."

content.text: Nails used to comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long] and 9.23.3.5.-A to 9.23.3.5.-C shall have a diameter not less than that stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art1.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote115:short] .)
Wood screws specified in this Section shall conform to [REF:standard:asmeb18.6.1] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote116:short] .)
All nails shall be long enough so that not less than half their required length penetrates into the second member.

Splitting of wood members shall be minimized by staggering the nails in the direction of the grain and by keeping nails well in from the edges. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote117:short] .)
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.sent2:short] , nailing of framing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]

Where the bottom wall plate or sole plate of an exterior wall is not nailed to floor joists, [REF:term:rm-jst:rim joists] or blocking in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long] , the exterior wall is permitted to be fastened to the floor framing by

clauses.text: having plywood, OSB or waferboard sheathing extend down over floor framing and fastened to the floor framing by nails or staples conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art5:long] , or
tying the wall framing to the floor framing by galvanized-metal strips

subclauses.text: 50 mm wide,
not less than 0.41 mm thick,
spaced not more than 1.2 m apart, and
fastened at each end with at least two 63 mm nails.

table_notes.content: See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote115:short]
See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4:long] for requirements on the nailing of top plates splices in [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] .
See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.sent2:short] .
See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.sent3:short] .
Where heavyweight construction is used in the roof of the space, at least 8 nails are required (see Note A-9.23.13.2.(3)).

content.text: Holes drilled in roof, floor or ceiling framing members shall be not larger than one-quarter the depth of the member and shall be located not less than 50 mm from the edges, unless the depth of the member is increased by the size of the hole.

Exterior steel beams shall be shop primed.
Where a beam is made up of individual pieces of lumber that are nailed together, the individual members shall be 38 mm or greater in thickness and installed on edge.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect8.art3.sent3:short] , where individual members of a built-up beam are butted together to form a joint, the joint shall occur over a support.

Where a beam is continuous over more than one span, individual members are permitted to be butted together to form a joint at or within 150 mm of the end quarter points of the clear spans, provided the quarter points are not those closest to the ends of the beam.
Members joined at quarter points shall be continuous over adjacent supports.

Joints in individual members of a beam that are located at or near the end quarter points shall not occur in adjacent members at the same quarter point and shall not reduce the effective beam width by more than half.
Not more than one butt joint shall occur in any individual member of a built-up beam within any one span.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect8.art3.sent8:short] , where 38 mm members are laid on edge to form a built-up beam, individual members shall be nailed together with a double row of nails not less than 89 mm in length, spaced not more than 450 mm apart in each row with the end nails located 100 mm to 150 mm from the end of each piece.

Where 38 mm members in built-up wood beams are not nailed together as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect8.art3.sent7:short] , they shall be bolted together with not less than 12.7 mm diam bolts equipped with washers and spaced not more than 1.2 m o.c., with the end bolts located not more than 600 mm from the ends of the members.
Except when supported on ribbon boards, floor joists shall have not less than 38 mm length of end bearing.
Ribbon boards referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art1.sent1:short] shall be not less than 19 mm by 89 mm lumber let into the studs.
Floor joists may be supported on the tops of beams or may be framed into the sides of beams.
When framed into the side of a wood beam, joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art2.sent1:short] shall be supported on

clauses.text: joist hangers or other acceptable mechanical connectors, or

not less than 38 mm by 64 mm ledger strips nailed to the side of the beam, except that 38 mm by 38 mm ledger strips may be used provided each joist is nailed to the beam by not less than four 89 mm nails, in addition to the nailing for the ledger strip required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]

content.text: When framed into the side of a steel beam, joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art2.sent1:short] shall be supported on the bottom flange of the beam or on not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber bolted to the web with not less than 6.3 mm diam bolts spaced not more than 600 mm apart.

Joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art2.sent3:short] shall be spliced above the beam with not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber at least 600 mm long to support the flooring.
Not less than a 12 mm space shall be provided between the splice required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art2.sent4:short] and the beam to allow for shrinkage of the wood joists.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent1:long] , bottoms of floor joists shall be restrained from twisting at each end by toe-nailing to the supports, end-nailing to the header joists or by providing continuous strapping, blocking between the joists or cross-bridging near the supports.

articles.title: Strapping, Bridging, Furring and Ceilings in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A and -B

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent5:short] , where strapping is specified in  Span Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table4:long] , it shall be

clauses.text: not less than 19 mm by 64 mm , nailed to the underside of floor joists,
located not more than 2 100 mm from each support or other rows of strapping, and
fastened at each end to a sill or header.

content.text: Where bridging is specified in  Span Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table4:long] , it shall consist of not less than 19 mm by 64 mm or 38 mm by 38 mm cross bridging located not more than 2 100 mm from each support or other rows of bridging.
Where bridging and strapping are specified in  Span Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table4:long] ,

clauses.text: bridging shall

subclauses.text: comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent2:short] , or
consist of 38 mm solid blocking located not more than 2 100 mm from each support or other rows of bridging and securely fastened between the joists, and

clauses.text: except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent5:short] , strapping shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent1:short] and be installed under the bridging.

content.text: Bridging specified in  Span Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table5:long] shall consist of

clauses.text: bridging as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent2:short] , or
38 mm solid blocking located not more than 2 100 mm from each support or other rows of bridging and securely fastened between the joists.

content.text: Strapping described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art4.sent3.clause2:medium] is not required where

clauses.text: furring strips complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect3.art1.table1:long] are fastened directly to the joists, or

a panel-type ceiling finish complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6:number] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect7:number] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect8:number] , or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9:number] is attached directly to the joists.

content.text: Where a ceiling attached to wood furring is specified in  Span Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table5:long] ,

clauses.text: the ceiling finish shall consist of gypsum board, plywood or OSB not less than 12.7 mm thick, and
the furring shall be

subclauses.text: 19 mm by 89 mm wood furring spaced at not more than 600 mm o.c., or
19 mm by 64 mm wood furring spaced at not more than 400 mm o.c.

content.text: Header joists around floor openings shall be doubled when they exceed 1.2 m in length.
The size of header joists exceeding 3.2 m in length shall be determined by calculations.
Trimmer joists around floor openings shall be doubled when the length of the header joist exceeds 800 mm .
When the header joist exceeds 2 m in length the size of the trimmer joists shall be determined by calculations.

articles.title: Support of Tail and Header Joists

content.text: When tail joists and header joists are supported by the floor framing, they shall be supported by suitable joist hangers or nailing in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]
Non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls parallel to the floor joists shall be supported by joists beneath the wall or on blocking between the joists.
Blocking referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art8.sent1:short] for the support of non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls shall be

clauses.text: not less than 38 mm by 89 mm lumber, and
except as required for the fastening of walls constructed with required [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] , spaced not more than 1.2 m apart.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art8.sent6:short] , non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] interior walls at right angles to the floor joists are not restricted as to location.

[REF:term:ldbrng:Loadbearing] interior walls parallel to floor joists shall be supported by beams or walls of sufficient strength to safely transfer the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] to the vertical supports.
Unless the joist size is designed to support such loads, [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] interior walls at right angles to floor joists shall be located

clauses.text: not more than 900 mm from the joist support where the wall does not support a floor, and
not more than 600 mm from the joist support where the wall supports one or more floors.

content.text: [REF:term:ldbrng:Loadbearing] and non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls constructed with required [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] shall be continuously supported by floor joists, blocking or [REF:term:rm-jst:rim joists] to allow for the required fastening (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long] ).

Floor joists supporting roof loads shall not be cantilevered more than 400 mm beyond their supports where 38 mm by 184 mm joists are used and not more than 600 mm beyond their supports where 38 mm by 235 mm or larger joists are used.

The cantilevered portions referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art9.sent1:short] shall not support floor loads from other [REF:term:tr:storeys] unless calculations are provided to show that the design resistances of the cantilevered joists are not exceeded.

Where cantilevered floor joists described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art9.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art9.sent2:short] are at right angles to the main floor joists, the tail joists in the cantilevered portion shall extend inward away from the cantilever support a distance equal to not less than 6 times the length of the cantilever, and shall be end nailed to an interior doubled header joist in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]
The size and spacing of studs shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art1.table1:long]

table_notes.content: See  Article [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art3:long]

content.text: Where [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] interior walls are not finished in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29:long] , blocking or strapping shall be fastened to the studs at mid-height to prevent sideways buckling.

Except as permitted in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art3.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art3.sent3:short] , all studs shall be placed at right angles to the wall face.

Studs on the flat are permitted to be used in gable ends of roofs that contain only unfinished space or in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] interior walls within the limits described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art1:long]

Wall studs that support only a load from an attic not accessible by a stairway are permitted to be placed on the flat within the limits permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art1:long] provided

clauses.text: the studs are clad on not less than one side with plywood, OSB or waferboard sheathing fastened to the face of the studs with a structural adhesive, and
the portion of the roof supported by the studs does not exceed 2.1 m in width.

content.text: Wall studs shall be continuous for the full [REF:term:tr:storey] height except at openings and shall not be spliced except by fingerjoining with a structural adhesive. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote125:short] .)

articles.title: Support for Cladding, Sheathing and Finishing Materials

content.text: Corners and intersections shall be designed to provide adequate support for the vertical edges of interior finishes, sheathing and cladding materials, and in no instance shall exterior corners be framed with less than the equivalent of 2 studs.

Where the vertical edges of interior finishes at wall intersections are supported at vertical intervals by blocking or furring, the vertical distance between such supports shall not exceed the maximum distance between supports specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29:long]
Where the lintel spanning the opening is more than 3 m long, studs shall be tripled on each side of the opening so that

clauses.text: the two inner studs on each side extend from the bottom of the supported lintel to the top of the bottom wall plate, and
the outer stud on each side extends from the bottom of the top wall plate to the bottom wall plate.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect10.art6.sent3:short] , where the lintel spanning the opening is not more than 3 m long, studs shall be doubled on each side of the opening so that

clauses.text: the inner studs on each side extend from the bottom of the supported lintel to the top of the bottom wall plate, and
the outer stud on each side extends from the bottom of the top wall plate to the bottom wall plate.

content.text: Single studs are permitted to be used on either side of openings

clauses.text: in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] interior walls not required to have [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance ratings] , provided the studs extend from the top wall plate to the bottom wall plate, or
in [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] or non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] interior or exterior walls, provided

subclauses.text: the opening is less than and within the required stud spacing, and
no 2 such openings of full stud-space width are located in adjacent stud spaces.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art1.sent2:short] , wall plates shall be

clauses.text: not less than 38 mm thick, and
not less than the required width of the wall studs.

content.text: In non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls and in [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls where the studs are located directly over framing members, the bottom wall plate is permitted to be 19 mm thick.
A bottom wall plate shall be provided in all cases.
The bottom plate in exterior walls shall not project more than one-third the plate width over the support.

Except as permitted in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art3.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art3.sent4:short] , at least 2 top plates shall be provided in [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls.
A single top plate is permitted to be used in a section of a [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] wall containing a lintel provided the top plate forms a tie across the lintel.

A single top plate is permitted to be used in [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls where the concentrated loads from ceilings, floors and roofs are not more than 50 mm to one side of the supporting studs and in all non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls.
The top plates need not be provided in a section of [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] wall containing a lintel provided the lintel is tied to the adjacent wall section with not less than

clauses.text: 75 mm by 150 mm by 0.91 mm thick galvanized steel, or
19 mm by 89 mm by 300 mm wood splice nailed to each wall section with at least three 63 mm nails.

content.text: Joints in the top plates of [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls shall be staggered not less than

clauses.text: one stud spacing where the number of nails required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short] is not more than 16,
two stud spacings where the number of nails required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short] is greater than 16 and not more than 32, and
three stud spacings where the number of nails required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short] is greater than 32.

content.text: The top plates in [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls shall be lapped or otherwise tied at corners and intersecting walls in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent4:short] .
Joints in single top plates used with [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls shall be tied in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent4:short] .

Ties referred to in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent3:short] shall be the equivalent of not less than 75 mm by 150 mm by 0.91 mm thick galvanized steel nailed to each wall with at least three 63 mm nails.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent7:short] , doubled top plates in [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] shall be fastened on each side of a splice with not less than 76 mm long common steel wire nails or spiral nails in accordance with the minimum number of nails required by Table 9.23.11.4.-B or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.table2:long] , whichever is greater, where

clauses.text: S_{max} is not greater than 2.6, or
the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 1.2 kPa .

revisions.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent7:short] , doubled top plates in [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] shall be fastened on each side of a splice with not less than 76 mm long common steel wire nails or spiral nails in accordance with the minimum number of nails required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.table2:long] , whichever is greater, where

clauses.text: the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than 0.47 and S_{max} is not greater than 2.6, or
the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is equal to or greater than 0.6 kPa but not greater than 1.2 kPa .

revisions.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent7:short] , doubled top plates in [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] shall be fastened on each side of a splice with not less than 76 mm long common steel wire nails or spiral nails in accordance with the minimum number of nails required by Table 9.23.11.4.-B or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.table2:long] , whichever is greater, where

clauses.text: S_{max} is not greater than 2.6, or
the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 1.2 kPa .

revisions.change_summary: Struck out '9.23.11.4.-C' and substituted '9.23.11.4.-B', removed text from clause (a), and removed text from clause (b)

content.text: Nails referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short] shall be spaced not less than 75 mm o.c. along the top plate in rows spaced not less than 35 mm apart.
Doubled top plates in [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] shall be designed according to Part 4 where

clauses.text: the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is greater than 1.2 kPa ,
the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is greater than 2.6, or
the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is greater than 0.47 for Site Class C for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of 3 [REF:term:tr:storeys] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] and

subclauses.text: of heavy weight construction,
clad with masonry veneer, or
clad with stone veneer.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect12.art1.sent2:short] , openings in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls shall be framed with not less than 38 mm material the same width as the studs, securely nailed to adjacent studs.

Openings for doors in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls required to be [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] with a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] shall be framed with the equivalent of at least two 38 mm thick members that are the same width as the wall plates.

Openings in [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls greater than the required stud spacing shall be framed with lintels designed to carry the superimposed loads to adjacent studs. (See Note A-9.23.10.6.(3).)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect12.art3.sent2:long] , where 2 or more members are used in lintels, they shall be fastened together with not less than 82 mm nails in a double row, with nails not more than 450 mm apart in each row.
Lintel members are permitted to be separated by filler pieces.

Spans and sizes of wood lintels shall conform to the spans shown in  Span Tables [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table15:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table16:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table19:long]

clauses.text: for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] ,
where the wall studs exceed 38 mm by 64 mm in size,
where the spans of supported joists do not exceed 4.9 m , and
where the spans of trusses do not exceed 9.8 m .

content.text: In [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] exterior and interior walls of 38 mm by 64 mm framing members, lintels shall consist of

clauses.text: 64 mm thick members on edge, or
38 mm thick and 19 mm thick members fastened together with a double row of nails not less than 63 mm long and spaced not more than 450 mm apart.

content.text: Lintels referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect12.art3.sent2:short]

clauses.text: shall be not less than 50 mm greater in depth than those shown in  Span Tables [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table15:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table16:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table19:long] for the maximum spans shown, and
shall not exceed 2.24 m in length.

subsections.title: Bracing to Resist Lateral Loads Due to Wind and Earthquake

articles.title: Requirements for Low to Moderate Wind and Seismic Forces

content.text: This Article applies where

clauses.text: the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C, is not more than 0.47,
the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 0.60 kPa ,
the unsupported height of the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] in the [REF:term:bldng:building] is not greater than 3.1 m , and
the lowest exterior frame wall supports a roof and not more than 2 floors.

content.text: Bracing to resist lateral loads shall be designed and constructed in accordance with

clauses.text: the simplified approach outlined in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art11:long] , where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is not greater than 0.47 and the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 0.60 kPa ,
Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art4:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art10:long] ,
Part 4, or
good engineering practice such as that provided in [REF:standard:cwc-egwfc] .

articles.title: Requirements for High Wind and Seismic Forces

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art1:long] , this Article applies where

clauses.text: the unsupported height of the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] in the [REF:term:bldng:building] is not greater than 3.1 m ,
1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 1.2 kPa ,
the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is not greater than 2.6, and
the lowest exterior frame wall supports a roof and not more than

subclauses.text: 2 floors in a [REF:term:bldng:building] of normal-weight construction, or
1 floor in a [REF:term:bldng:building] of heavyweight construction or clad at full height with masonry veneer or stone veneer.

content.text: Bracing to resist lateral loads shall be designed and constructed in accordance with

clauses.text: Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art4:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art10:long] ,
Part 4, or
good engineering practice such as that provided in [REF:standard:cwc-egwfc] .

content.text: For the purposes of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art2.sent1:short] and this Part,

clauses.text: in a [REF:term:bldng:building] of normal-weight construction, the average dead weight per [REF:term:tr:storey] shall not exceed

subclauses.text: 0.5 kPa for floors and 0.5 kPa for [REF:term:prttn:partitions] and interior walls,
0.5 kPa for the roof, and
0.4 kPa for exterior walls,

clauses.text: in a [REF:term:bldng:building] of heavyweight construction, the average dead weight per [REF:term:tr:storey] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art2.sent3.clause1:short] , except that the average dead weight per [REF:term:tr:storey] shall not exceed

subclauses.text: 1.5 kPa for floors and 0.5 kPa for [REF:term:prttn:partitions] and interior walls,
1.0 kPa for the roof, or
1.2 kPa for exterior walls,

clauses.text: in a [REF:term:bldng:building] clad with masonry veneer, the average dead weight of the masonry veneer shall not exceed 1.9 kPa , and
in a [REF:term:bldng:building] clad with stone veneer, the average dead weight of the stone veneer shall not exceed 3.2 kPa . (See Note A-9.23.13.2.(3).)

content.text: Except as provided in Tables 9.23.13.7.-B and 9.23.13.7.-D, all adjustment factors required for the calculation of the minimum total length of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] in accordance with this Article shall be taken as 1.

The minimum total length of all [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] in a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] shall be taken as the greater of L_{w} determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent3:short] for the appropriate 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) and L_{s} as determined in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent4:short] for the appropriate seismic design parameter, S_{max}, where

clauses.text: HWP is not greater than 1.2 kPa , and
S_{max} for Site Class C, is not greater than 2.6.

content.text:
For resistance to wind pressure, the minimum total length of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] in each [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] , L_{w}, shall be determined by applying the adjustment factors provided in Table 9.23.13.7.-B to the unadjusted minimum total [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panel] length L_{uw} provided in Table 9.23.13.7.-A using the following equation:
L_{w} = L_{uw}K_{exp}K_{roof}K_{Wspacing}K_{Wnumber}K_{gyp}K_{sheath} ≥ BWP_{min}
where
K_{exp} = wind exposure adjustment factor, and
= 1 for rough terrain (suburban, urban or wooded terrain extending upwind from the [REF:term:bldng:building] uninterrupted for at least 1 km),
K_{roof} = roof eave-to-ridge height adjustment factor, and
= 1 for a roof eave-to-ridge height of 3 m
K_{Wspacing} = [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] spacing adjustment factor for wind (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent5:short] ),per [REF:term:bldng:building] plan direction, and
= 1 for a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] spacing of 7.6 m
K_{Wnumber} = number of parallel [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] adjustment factor for wind, per [REF:term:bldng:building] plan direction, and
= 1 for two exterior walls and no intermediate [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] ,
K_{gyp} = interior gypsum board adjustment factor, and
= 1 for [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] with gypsum board installed on the interior side,
K_{sheath} = intermittent [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] adjustment factor, and
= 1 for continuously sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] , and
BWP_{min} = Minimum length of individual [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] as per [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.table1:long] .
(See Note A-9.23.13.7.(3) for an alternative procedure to calculate L_{w}, directly and Note A-9.23.13.7.(4).)

content.text:
For resistance to seismic forces, the minimum total length of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] in each [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] , L_{s}, shall be determined by applying the adjustment factors provided in Table 9.23.13.7.-D to the unadjusted minimum total [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panel] length, L_{us}, provided in Table 9.23.13.7.-C using the following equation:
L_{s} = L_{us}K_{weight}K_{snow}K_{Sspacing}K_{Snumber}K_{gyp}K_{sheath} ≥ BWP_{min}
Where:
K_{weight} = weight of construction and cladding adjustment factor, and
= 1 for normal-weight construction (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art2.sent3:short] ),
K_{snow} = roof snow load adjustment factor, and
= 1 for a specified roof snow load of 2 kPa or less, as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect2.art2:long] ,
K_{Sspacing} = [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] spacing adjustment factor for seismic forces (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent5:short] ), per [REF:term:bldng:building] plan direction, and
= 1 for a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] spacing of 7.6 m ,
K_{Snumber} = number of parallel [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] adjustment factor for seismic forces, per [REF:term:bldng:building] plan direction, and
= 1 for two exterior walls and no intermediate [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] ,
K_{gyp} = interior gypsum board adjustment factor, and
= 1 for [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] with gypsum board installed on the interior side,
K_{sheath} = intermittent [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] adjustment factor, and
= 1 for continuously sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] , and
BWP_{min} = minimum length of individual [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] , per [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.table1:long] . (See Note A-9.23.13.7.(4) for an alternative procedure to calculate L_{s} directly and Note A-9.23.13.7.(3) and (4).)

of the same construction as the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] of the [REF:term:tr:storey] above but sheathed with wood sheathing regardless of the construction, where the length of the cripple wall bracing is equal to the length of the [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] multiplied by an adjustment factor of 1.2, in addition to any adjustments required by  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent2:short] , and

clauses.text: do not support heavyweight construction, masonry or stone veneer.

content.text: Where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is greater than 0.60, [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] cripple walls need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent1:short] , provided they

clauses.text: comply with  Clauses [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2.clause3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2.clause4:short] ,
are not more than 350 mm in height, and
are not more than 5 m length,

content.text: Where interior finish, such as gypsum board, is omitted from the interior side of the cripple wall referred to in  Sentence [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent3:short] , the interior gypsum board adjustment factor described in  Sentence [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent3:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art7.sent4:short] shall be applied to the length of the cripple wall bracing.

Cripple walls in stepped [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] need not be braced in accordance with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8.sent4:short] , provided

clauses.text: the lowest floor framing rests directly on a sill plate anchored to a [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] not less than 2.4 m in length within a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] not more than 7.6 m in length,
the top plate of the cripple wall extends not less than 1.2 m along the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] , and
anchor bolts are located not more than 300 mm and 900 mm from the step in the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] .

content.text: This Article applies where

clauses.text: the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, is not greater than 1.2, and
the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is not greater than 1.2 kPa .

content.text: Walls in detached garages and in accessory [REF:term:bldng:buildings] serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , and the front wall of attached garages serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.sent1:short] where these walls do not support a floor.

[REF:term:br-wl-pnl:Braced wall panels] in the [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] at the front of an attached garage serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art5.sent1:short] , provided

clauses.text: the maximum spacing between the front of the garage and the back wall of the garage does not exceed 7.6 m ,
there is not more than one floor above the garage,
not less than 50% of the length of the back wall of the garage is constructed of wood-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] , and
not less than 25% of the length of the side walls is constructed of wood-sheathed [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] .

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art10.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art10.sent7:short] , one exterior wall of the uppermost [REF:term:tr:storey] in each orthogonal direction may be set back from the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr:storey] below, provided the adjacent interior [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] of the [REF:term:tr:storey] below the setback

clauses.text: is spaced not more than 10.6 m from the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr:storey] below the setback wall,
consists of [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] that are constructed of a wood-based material in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art6.sent1:short] ,

content.text: The [REF:term:flr-r:floor] system shall be anchored to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] at intervals not exceeding 3 m along the length of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall, except that where the [REF:term:flr-r:floor] is anchored to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] at adjacent [REF:term:brng-rfc:bearing walls] or [REF:term:bm:beams] , the maximum spacing shall be 6 m .

revisions.text: Where the exterior wall of the uppermost [REF:term:tr:storey] is set back from the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr:storey] below, the roof and floor space supporting the setback wall shall be sheathed with a wood-based material between the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr:storey] below the setback and the adjacent interior [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall bands] of the [REF:term:tr:storey] below the setback.

The [REF:term:flr-r:floor] system shall be anchored to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] at intervals not exceeding 3 m along the length of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall, except that where the [REF:term:flr-r:floor] is anchored to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] at adjacent [REF:term:brng-rfc:bearing walls] or [REF:term:bm:beams] , the maximum spacing shall be 6 m .

content.text: Where the exterior wall of the uppermost [REF:term:tr:storey] is set back from the exterior wall of the [REF:term:tr:storey] below, the exterior walls perpendicular to the setback wall shall

clauses.text: have their top plate connected with nails that are spaced at no greater than half the spacing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long] , and

have their top plate splices fastened with twice the number of nails specified in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent5:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect11.art4.sent6:short] .

content.text: The maximum distance between adjacent required [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] in a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] , measured from the edge of the panels, may be increased to 7.3 m provided that, throughout the height of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , the length of any [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panel] within the [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] is not less than 1.2 m .

content.text: Wall portions clad with masonry veneer that are located both perpendicular to a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] and within a [REF:term:br-wl-bnd:braced wall band] are permitted to be considered as normal-weight construction.

Bracing to resist lateral loads shall be designed and constructed in accordance with  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art4:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art6:long] and  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art8:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect13.art10:long] .
Roof rafters and joists and ceiling joists shall be continuous or shall be spliced over vertical supports that extend to suitable bearing.
Roof and ceiling framing members shall be doubled on each side of openings greater than 2 rafter or joist spacings wide.
The length of end bearing of joists and rafters shall be not less than 38 mm .
Rafters shall be located directly opposite each other and tied together at the peak, or may be offset by their own thickness if nailed to a ridge board not less than 17.5 mm thick.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art4.sent3:short] , framing members shall be connected by gusset plates or nailing at the peak in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art4.table1:long]

Where the roof framing on opposite sides of the peak is assembled separately, such as in the case of factory-built houses, the roof framing on opposite sides is permitted to be fastened together with galvanized-steel strips not less than 200 mm by 75 mm by 0.41 mm thick spaced not more than 1.2 m apart and nailed at each end to the framing by at least two 63 mm nails.
Rafters shall be shaped at supports to provide even bearing surfaces and supported directly above the exterior walls.
Hip and valley rafters shall be not less than 50 mm greater in depth than the common rafters and not less than 38 mm thick, actual dimension.

articles.title: Intermediate Support for Rafters and Joists

content.text: Ceiling joists and collar ties of not less than 38 mm by 89 mm lumber are permitted to be assumed to provide intermediate support to reduce the span for rafters and joists where the roof slope is 1 in 3 or greater.

Collar ties referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art7.sent1:short] more than 2.4 m long shall be laterally supported near their centres by not less than 19 mm by 89 mm continuous members at right angles to the collar ties.
