Dwarf walls and struts are permitted to be used to provide intermediate support to reduce the span for rafters and joists.

When struts are used to provide intermediate support they shall be not less than 38 mm by 89 mm material extending from each rafter to a [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] wall at an angle of not less than 45° to the horizontal.

When dwarf walls are used for rafter support, they shall be framed in the same manner as [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls and securely fastened top and bottom to the roof and ceiling framing to prevent over-all movement.
Solid blocking shall be installed between floor joists beneath dwarf walls referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art7.sent5:short] that enclose finished rooms.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent4:short] , roof rafters and joists shall be supported at the ridge of the roof by

clauses.text: a [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] wall extending from the ridge to suitable bearing, or
a ridge beam supported by not less than 89 mm length of bearing.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent3:short] , the ridge beam referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent1:short] shall conform to the sizes and spans shown in  Span Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table15:long] , provided

clauses.text: the supported rafter or joist length does not exceed 4.9 m , and
the roof does not support any concentrated loads.

content.text: The ridge beam referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent1:short] need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent2:short] where

clauses.text: the beam is of not less than 38 mm by 140 mm material, and
the beam is supported at intervals not exceeding 1.2 m by not less than 38 mm by 89 mm members extending vertically from the ridge to suitable bearing.

content.text: Where the roof slope is 1 in 3 or steeper, ridge support need not be provided when the lower ends of the rafters are adequately tied to prevent outward movement.

Ties required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent4:short] are permitted to consist of tie rods or ceiling joists forming a continuous tie for opposing rafters and nailed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.table1:long]

table_notes.content: Nails with a diameter less than 3.66 mm are permitted to be used, provided the minimum number of nails stated in the Table is modified as follows:Where more than 10 nails are required, the connections between the rafters and the ceiling joists shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause3:short] .[LIST:bulleted]

items.content: For a nail diameter greater than or equal to 2.86 mm and less than 3.25 mm , add 3 nails to the minimum number of nails, up to a maximum of 10 nails .
For a nail diameter greater than or equal to 3.25 mm and less than 3.66 mm , add 2 nails to the minimum number of nails, up to a maximum of 10 nails .

table_notes.content: The minimum number of nails stated in the Table is applicable to Spruce-Pine-Fir, Douglas Fir-Larch and Hem-Fir members. For Northern Species members, add 2 nails to the minimum number of nails, up to a maximum of 10 nails. Where more than 10 nails are required, the connections between the rafters and the ceiling joists shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause3:short] .

To accommodate nail spacing, not less than 38 mm × 140 mm joists shall be used where 6 or more nails are required, and not less than 38 mm × 184 mm joists shall be used where 8 or more nails are required.
The minimum number of nails in the Table is applicable for a maximum roof [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] of 0.5 kPa .

The connections between the rafters and the ceiling joists shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause3:short] .

content.value: Minimum Number of Nails Not Less Than 76 mm Long and 3.66 mm in Diameter [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.table1.note1]  [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.table1.note2]  [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.table1.note3]  [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.table1.note4]

content.text: Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent7:short] , ceiling joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent5:short] shall be tied to the base of every rafter.

Where ceiling joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent5:short] are raised above the base of the rafters, the connections between the rafters and the ceiling joists shall be designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause2:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect4.subsect1.art1.sent1.clause3:short] .

Ceiling joists referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent5:short] that are spliced to make a continuous joist shall be fastened together at each splice with at least one more nail than required for the rafter-to-joist connection shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.table1:long]

Members referred to in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent6:short]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art8.sent8:short] are permitted to be fastened together either directly or through a gusset plate.

Roof joists supporting a finished ceiling, other than plywood, OSB or waferboard, shall be restrained from twisting along the bottom edges by means of furring, blocking, cross bridging or strapping conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect9.art3:long]

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art10.sent2:short] , ceiling joists supporting part of the roof load from the rafters shall be not less than 25 mm greater in depth than required for ceiling joists not supporting part of the roof load.

When the roof slope is 1 in 4 or less, the ceiling joist sizes referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art10.sent1:short] shall be determined from  Span Tables [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table6:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table9:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables2.table15:long] for roof joists.

Wood roof trusses shall be designed in accordance with good engineering practice such as that described in TPIC 2019, "Truss Design Procedures and Specifications for Light Metal Plate Connected Wood Trusses."

The joint connections used in trusses described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect14.art11.sent1:short] shall be designed in conformance with the requirements in Subsection 4.3.1. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote135:short] .)

All member bracing shall be installed as per the truss design drawings, and continuous lateral bracing shall be adequately anchored to the roof and ceiling diaphragms at intervals no greater than 6.10 m o.c.
Subflooring shall be provided beneath finish flooring where the finish flooring does not have adequate strength to support the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] (see Subsection 9.30.3.).
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art2.sent2:short] , wood-based panels for subfloors shall conform to

clauses.text: CSA O121, "Douglas fir plywood,"
CSA O151, "Canadian softwood plywood,"
CSA O153, "Poplar plywood,"
CSA O325, "Construction sheathing," or
CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard."

content.text: Particleboard subflooring may be used only where a [REF:term:bldng:building] is constructed in a factory so that the subfloor will not be exposed to the weather.
Subflooring described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art2.sent2:short] shall conform to grade D-2 or D-3 in ANSI A208.1, "Particleboard."

Subflooring described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art2.sent2:short] shall have its upper surface and all edges treated to restrict water absorption, where the subfloor is used in bathrooms, kitchens, laundry rooms or other areas subject to periodic wetting. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote136:short] .)

Where the edges of panel-type subflooring are required to be supported (see Sentence 9.30.2.1.(2)), such support shall consist of tongue-and-groove panel edges or not less than 38 mm by 38 mm blocking securely nailed between framing members.
Plywood subflooring shall be installed with the surface grain at right angles to the joists and with joints parallel to floor joists staggered.

OSB subflooring conforming to CSA O325, "Construction sheathing," or to O-1 and O-2 grades in CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard," and waferboard subflooring conforming to R-1 grade in CSA O437.0 shall be installed so that the direction of face orientation is at right angles to the joists and the joints parallel to the floor joists are staggered. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote137:short] .)

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.sent3:short] , subfloors shall conform to either [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table2:long] .

content.value: OSB, O-1 Grade, and Waferboard, R-1 Grade

content.title: Rating for Subfloor when Applying CSA O325

content.text: Where the finished flooring consists of not less than 19 mm matched wood strip flooring laid at right angles to joists spaced not more than 600 mm o.c. , subflooring shall be permitted to consist of not less than

clauses.text: 12.5 mm thick plywood,
12.5 mm thick OSB conforming to O-2 grade,
12.7 mm thick OSB conforming to O-1 grade,
12.7 mm thick waferboard conforming to R-1 grade, or
OSB conforming to 2R32/2F16 grade.

content.text: Except where the flooring consists of ceramic tiles applied with adhesive, where a separate panel-type underlay or concrete topping is applied to a subfloor on joists spaced not more than 400 mm o.c., the subfloor is permitted to consist of not less than

clauses.text: 12.5 mm thick plywood,
12.5 mm thick OSB conforming to O-2 grade,
12.7 mm thick OSB conforming to O-1 grade,
12.7 mm thick waferboard conforming to R-1 grade, or
OSB conforming to 2R32/2F16 grade.

content.text: When resilient flooring is applied directly to an OSB, waferboard, particleboard or plywood subfloor, the subfloor shall be fastened to the supports with annular grooved nails.
Lumber subflooring shall be laid at an angle of not less than 45° to the joists.
Lumber subflooring shall be fully supported at the ends on solid bearing.
Lumber for subflooring shall be of uniform thickness and not more than 184 mm wide.

Except where the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is less than 0.8 kPa and the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C, is less than or equal to 0.47, continuous lumber or panel-type roof sheathing shall be installed to support the roofing.
Wood-based panels used for roof sheathing shall conform to the requirements of

clauses.text: CSA O121, "Douglas fir plywood,"
CSA O151, "Canadian softwood plywood,"
CSA O153, "Poplar plywood,"
CSA O325, "Construction sheathing," or
CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard."

content.text: Plywood roof sheathing shall be installed with the surface grain at right angles to the roof framing.

OSB roof sheathing conforming to CSA O325, "Construction sheathing," or to O-1 and O-2 grades as specified in CSA O437.0, "OSB and Waferboard," shall be installed with the direction of face orientation at right angles to the roof framing members. (See Note A-9.23.15.4.(2).)
Panel-type sheathing board shall be applied so that joints perpendicular to the roof ridge are staggered where

clauses.text: the sheathing is applied with the surface grain parallel to the roof ridge, and
the thickness of the sheathing is such that the edges are required to be supported.

content.text: A gap of not less than 2 mm shall be left between sheets of plywood, OSB or waferboard.
Lumber roof sheathing shall not be more than 286 mm wide and shall be applied so that all ends are supported with end joints staggered.
Lumber roof sheathing shall be installed diagonally, where

clauses.text: the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than 0.47 but not greater than 0.8, or
the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is equal to or greater than 0.80 kPa but less than 1.20 kPa .

content.text: Lumber roof sheathing shall be designed according to Part 4, where

clauses.text: the seismic spectral acceleration, S_{a}(0.2), is greater than 1.2, or
the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is equal to or greater than 1.20 kPa .

content.text: Where panel-type roof sheathing requires edge support, the support shall consist of metal H clips or not less than 38 mm by 38 mm blocking securely nailed between framing members.

The thickness or rating of roof sheathing on a flat roof used as a walking deck shall conform to either [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art5.table2:long] for subfloors.

The thickness or rating of roof sheathing on a roof not used as a walking deck shall conform to either [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art7.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art7.table2:long] .

Asphalt-coated or asphalt-impregnated fibreboard not less than 11.1 mm thick conforming to CAN/ULC-S706.1, "Standard for Wood Fibre Insulating Boards for Buildings," is permitted to be used as a roof sheathing over supports spaced not more than 400 mm o.c. provided the roofing consists of

clauses.text: a continuous sheet of galvanized steel not less than 0.33 mm in thickness, or
a continuous sheet of aluminum not less than 0.61 mm in thickness.

content.text: All edges of sheathing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art7.sent3:short] shall be supported by blocking or framing.

content.value: OSB, O-1 Grade, and Waferboard, R-1 Grade

content.title: Rating for Roof Sheathing When Applying CSA O325

content.text: Exterior walls and gable ends shall be sheathed when the exterior cladding requires intermediate fastening between supports or if the exterior cladding requires solid backing.

Where wall sheathing is required for the purpose of complying with this Section, it shall conform to either [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17.art2.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17.art2.table2:short] . (See also Article 9.25.5.1.)

table_notes.content: See also Sentences 9.27.5.1.(2) to (4).

The [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] of gypsum board shall be determined in accordance with CAN/ULC-S102, "Standard Method of Test for Surface Burning Characteristics of Building Materials and Assemblies."

content.value: OSB, O-1 Grade, and Waferboard, R-1 Grade
CSA O121 CSA O151 CSA O153
Polyurethane and Polyisocyanurate Types 2 and 3, faced

content.title: Rating for Wall Sheathing when Applying CSA O325

content.text: Gypsum sheathing, rigid insulation and fibreboard shall not be used for the attachment of cladding materials.
Lumber wall sheathing shall be applied so that all ends are supported.
Where lumber wall sheathing is required to provide bracing according to Article 9.23.10.2., it shall be applied with end joints staggered.
A gap of not less than 2 mm shall be left between sheets of plywood, OSB, waferboard or fibreboard.

Where the bottom portions of mansard style roofs are vented, the vertical framing members behind the sloping portions shall be considered on the same basis as exterior wall studs and shall conform to Articles 9.27.3.2. to 9.27.3.6.
This Section applies to sheet steel studs for use in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] exterior and interior walls.
Where [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] steel studs are used, they shall be designed in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part4:long] .
Steel studs and runners shall conform to [REF:standard:aisis201]
Metal thickness specified in this Section shall be the minimum base steel thickness exclusive of coatings.
Screws for the application of cladding, sheathing or interior finish materials to steel studs, runners and furring channels shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc954] or
[REF:standard:astmc1002]

articles.title: Cladding, Sheathing and Interior Finish Required

content.text: Cladding or sheathing, and interior finish shall be installed on steel stud framing and shall be fastened with screws

clauses.text: spaced at the appropriate spacing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29:long] , and
penetrating not less than 10 mm through the metal.

articles.title: Size and Spacing of Studs in Interior Walls

content.text: Except as required in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art4:long] , the size and spacing of steel studs for non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing ] interior walls shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Steel Studs for Non-Loadbearing Interior Walls

table_notes.content: The values in the Table are based on a single layer of 12.7 mm gypsum panel sheathing installed on each side of the studs. Where one side is not accessible, gypsum panels on only one side will suffice. The values are also based on attaching gypsum panel sheathing using screws not smaller than No. 6 spaced at a maximum of 300 mm at edges and at intermediate supports.

content.text: Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art4:long] , steel studs in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] interior walls shall have a metal thickness of not less than 0.46 mm .
Runners for interior and exterior non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] walls shall have a thickness not less than the thickness of the corresponding studs and shall have not less than 30 mm flanges.
Where openings for doors in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing]  [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] do not exceed 1 200 mm in width,

clauses.text: the width of steel studs shall be not less than 63 mm , and
the metal thickness shall be not less than 0.46 mm .

content.text: Where openings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art4.sent1:short] exceed 1 200 mm in width,

clauses.text: the width of steel studs shall be not less than 91 mm , and
the metal thickness shall be not less than 0.85 mm .

content.text: The distance to the first stud beyond the jamb of any door opening in a [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] shall not exceed 400 mm .

Where the distance between the framing over the opening referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art4.sent3:short] and the top runner exceeds 400 mm in such walls, intermediate support shall be installed at intervals of not more than 400 mm above the opening.

articles.title: Size and Spacing of Studs in Exterior Walls

content.text: The size and spacing of non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] steel studs for exterior walls shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect2.art5.table1:long]

content.title: Size and Spacing of Steel Studs for Non-Loadbearing Exterior Walls

content.text: Runners shall be provided at the tops and bottoms of walls.

Runners required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] shall be securely attached to the [REF:term:bldng:building] at approximately 50 mm from the ends, and at intervals of not more than 600 mm o.c. for interior walls and 300 mm o.c. for exterior walls.
Fasteners used for attachment described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art1.sent2:short] shall consist of the equivalent of 63 mm nails or 25 mm screws.
Studs at openings and which are not full wall height shall be supported by a runner at the ends of the studs, securely fastened to the full length studs at the sides of the opening.

Steel studs used in walls required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] shall be installed so that there is not less than a 12 mm clearance between the top of the stud and the top of the runner to allow for expansion in the event of fire.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art6:long] , studs in walls referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art2.sent1:short] shall not be attached to the runners in a manner that will prevent such expansion.

Framing above doors with steel door frames in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing]  [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] shall consist of 2 runners on the flat fastened back to back. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote138:short] .)
The upper runner required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art2.sent3:short] shall be bent at each end to extend upwards not less than 150 mm and fastened to the adjacent studs.

A gypsum board filler piece, the width and length of the runner, shall be provided between the door frame referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art2.sent3:short] and the adjacent runner.
Steel studs shall be installed with webs at right angles to the wall face and, except at openings, shall be continuous for the full wall height.
Corners and intersections of walls shall be constructed to provide support for the cladding materials.
Studs shall be doubled on each side of every opening where such openings involve more than one stud space, and shall be tripled where the openings in exterior walls exceed 2.4 m in width.

Studs described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art5.sent1:short] shall be fastened together by screws, crimping or welding to act as a single structural unit in resisting transverse loads.
Studs shall be attached to runners by screws, crimping or welding around wall openings and elsewhere where necessary to keep the studs in alignment during construction.

Where clearance for expansion is required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art2:long] , attachment required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] shall be applied between studs and bottom runners only.

Openings for [REF:term:fr-dmpr:fire dampers] in non- [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing]  [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] shall be framed with double studs on each side of the opening.

The sill and header for openings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art7.sent1:short] shall consist of a runner track with right angle bends made on each end so as to extend 300 mm above the header or below the sill and fastened to the studs.
The openings described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect24.subsect3.art7.sent1:short] shall be lined with a layer of gypsum board not less than 12.7 mm thick fastened to stud and runner webs.

sections.title: Heat Transfer, Air Leakage and Condensation Control

content.text: This Section is concerned with heat, air and water vapour transfer and measures to control condensation.
All walls, ceilings and floors separating [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from unconditioned space, the exterior air or the ground shall be

clauses.text: provided with

subclauses.text: thermal insulation conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long] ,
an air barrier conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long] , and
a [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4:long] , and

clauses.text: constructed in such a way that the properties and relative position of all materials conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5:long]

content.text: Insulation and sealing of heating and ventilating ducts shall conform to  Sections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long]

All walls, ceilings and floors separating heated space from unheated space, the exterior air or the exterior [REF:term:l:soil] shall be provided with sufficient thermal insulation to prevent moisture condensation on their room side during the winter and to ensure comfortable conditions for the occupants. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote1:long] .)
Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] , thermal insulation shall conform to the requirements of

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc726]
[REF:standard:cgsb-51.25]
[REF:standard:cgsb51-gp-27m]
[REF:standard:ulcs701]
[REF:standard:ulcs702]
[REF:standard:ulcs703]
[REF:standard:ulcs704]
[REF:standard:ulcs705.1] or
[REF:standard:ulcs706]

content.text: The [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread ratings] requirements contained in the standards listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] shall not apply. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote140:short] .)
Insulation in contact with the ground shall be inert to the action of [REF:term:l:soil] and water and shall be such that its insulative properties are not significantly reduced by moisture.
Insulation shall be installed so that there is a reasonably uniform insulating value over the entire face of the insulated area.
Insulation shall be applied to the full width and length of the space between furring or framing.

Except where the insulation provides the principal resistance to air leakage, thermal insulation shall be installed so that at least one face is in full and continuous contact with an element with low air permeance. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote141:short] .)

Insulation shall be installed over the full height of [REF:term:fndtn-nt:foundation] walls enclosing a [REF:term:bmnt:basement] or heated crawl space. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote229:long] .)

Insulation around concrete slabs-on-ground shall be located so that heat from the [REF:term:bldng:building] is not restricted from reaching the ground beneath the perimeter, where exterior walls are not supported by footings extending below frost level.
Where insulation is exposed to the weather and subject to mechanical damage, it shall be protected with not less than

clauses.text: 6 mm preservative-treated plywood, or
12 mm cement parging on wire lath applied to the exposed face and edge.

content.text: Insulation located in areas where it may be subject to mechanical damage shall be protected by a covering such as gypsum board, plywood, particleboard, OSB, waferboard or hardboard.
Insulation in factory-built [REF:term:bldng:buildings] shall be installed so that it will not become dislodged during transportation.

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art4.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art4.sent6:short] , loose-fill insulation shall be used on horizontal surfaces only.
Where loose-fill insulation is installed in an unconfined sloped space, such as an attic space over a sloped ceiling, the supporting slope shall not be more than

clauses.text: 4.5 in 12 for mineral fibre or cellulose fibre insulation, and
2.5 in 12 for other types of insulation.

content.text: Loose-fill insulation is permitted to be used in wood-frame walls of existing [REF:term:bldng:buildings] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote142:short] .)
Where blown-in insulation is installed in above-ground or below-ground wood-frame walls of new [REF:term:bldng:buildings] ,

clauses.text: the density of the installed insulation shall be sufficient to preclude settlement,
the insulation shall be installed behind a membrane that will permit visual inspection prior to the installation of the interior finish,
the insulation shall be installed in a manner that will not interfere with the installation of the interior finish, and
no water shall be added to the insulation, unless it can be shown that the added water will not adversely affect other materials in the assembly.

content.text: Water repellent loose-fill insulation is permitted to be used between the outer and inner wythes of masonry [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity walls] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote143:short] .)
Where soffit venting is used, measures shall be taken

clauses.text: to prevent loose-fill insulation from blocking the soffit vents and to maintain an open path for circulation of air from the vents into the [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof space] , and
to minimize airflow into the insulation near the soffit vents to maintain the thermal performance of the material. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect19.subsect1.art3:long] )

content.text: Spray-applied polyurethane insulation shall be installed in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs705.2]

Wall, ceiling and floor assemblies separating [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from unconditioned space or from the ground shall be constructed so as to include an [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] that will provide a continuous barrier to air leakage

clauses.text: from the interior of the [REF:term:bldng:building] into wall, floor, [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof spaces] , sufficient to prevent excessive moisture condensation in such spaces during the winter, and
from the exterior or the ground inward sufficient to

subclauses.text: prevent moisture condensation on the room side during winter,
ensure comfortable conditions for the occupants, and
minimize the ingress of [REF:term:l:soil] gas.

content.text: [REF:term:r-brrr:Air barrier systems] shall possess the characteristics necessary to provide an effective barrier to air infiltration and exfiltration under differential air pressure due to stack effect, mechanical systems or wind.
Where polyethylene sheet is used to provide airtightness in the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] , it shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-51.34]

articles.title: Continuity of the Air Barrier System

content.text: Where the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] consists of an air-impermeable panel-type material, all joints shall be sealed to prevent air leakage.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art6.sent3:long] , where the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] consists of flexible sheet material, all joints shall be

clauses.text: sealed, or
lapped not less than 100 mm and clamped, such as between framing members, furring or blocking, and rigid panels.

content.text: Where an interior wall meets an exterior wall, ceiling, floor or roof required to be provided with air barrier protection, the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] shall extend across the intersection.

Where an interior wall projects through a ceiling or extends to become an exterior wall, spaces in the wall shall be blocked to provide continuity across those spaces with the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] in the abutting walls or ceiling.

Where an interior floor projects through an exterior wall or extends to become an exterior floor, continuity of the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] shall be maintained from the abutting walls across the floor assembly.

Penetrations of the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] , such as those created by the installation of doors, windows, electrical wiring, electrical boxes, piping or ductwork, shall be sealed to maintain the integrity of the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] over the entire surface.

Where access hatches and sump pit covers are installed through assemblies constructed with an [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] , they shall be weatherstripped around their perimeters to prevent air leakage.

Clearances between [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] or [REF:term:g-vnt:gas vents] and the surrounding construction that would permit air leakage from within the [REF:term:bldng:building] into a wall or [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof space] shall be sealed by [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material to prevent such leakage.

articles.title: Air Leakage Control in Masonry Walls

content.text: Masonry walls required to provide a barrier to the ingress of air from the ground shall

clauses.text: include a course of masonry units without voids, or
be sealed with flashing material extending across the full width of the masonry.

content.text: The masonry course or flashing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text: be located at the level of the adjoining floor and be sealed to it in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art6:long] , or
in the absence of a floor, be located at the level of the ground cover required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect18.subsect6.art1:long] and be sealed to it.

articles.title: Air Leakage Control in Underground Roofs

content.text: Waterproofing systems for roofs of underground structures shall be sealed to the air barrier in the walls.
Materials used to provide a barrier to the ingress of air through floors-on-ground shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-51.34]
Where the floor-on-ground is a concrete slab, the air barrier shall be

clauses.text: installed below the slab, or
applied to the top of the slab, provided a separate floor is installed over the slab.

content.text: Where the air barrier installed below a floor-on-ground is flexible sheet material, joints in the barrier shall be lapped not less than 300 mm . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote146:short] .)

Where installed in conjunction with a framed floor-on-ground or above a floor-on-ground, the air barrier shall be installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3.art3:long]
A floor-on-ground shall be sealed around its perimeter to the inner surfaces of adjacent walls using flexible sealant.

All penetrations of a floor-on-ground that are required to drain water from the floor surface shall be sealed in a manner that prevents the upward flow of air without preventing the downward flow of liquid water.

Thermally insulated wall, ceiling and floor assemblies shall be constructed with a [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] so as to provide a barrier to diffusion of water vapour from the interior into wall spaces, floor spaces or [REF:term:ttc-r-rf:attic or roof spaces] .

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4.art2.sent2:short] , [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barriers] shall have a permeance not greater than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m^{2}) measured in accordance with [REF:standard:astme96m] using the desiccant method (dry cup).

Thermally insulated [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall assemblies are permitted to be constructed with variable-permeance [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barriers] having a permeance not greater than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m^{2}) using the desiccant method (dry cup) and greater than 300 ng/(Pa×s×m^{2}) using the water method (wet cup) measured in accordance with [REF:standard:astme96m] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote147:short] .)

Where the intended use of the interior space will result in high moisture generation, the assembly shall be designed according to Part 5. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote148:short] .)

Where polyethylene is installed to serve only as the [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] , it shall comply with [REF:external:cgsb-51.34:Clause 4.4, Thermal Stability, and Clause 5.7, Oxidative Induction Time, of ] [REF:standard:cgsb-51.34]
Membrane-type [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barriers] other than polyethylene shall conform to the requirements of [REF:standard:cgsb-51.33]
Membrane-type [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barriers] other than polyethylene that are susceptible to deterioration under prolonged exposure to direct ultraviolet radiation shall

clauses.text: be covered, or
only be installed in locations that are not exposed to direct ultraviolet radiation after the completion of construction.

content.text: Where a coating is applied to gypsum board to function as the [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] , the permeance of the coating shall be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:cgsb-1.501]

Where foamed plastic insulation functions as the [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] , it shall be sufficiently thick so as to meet the requirement of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4.art2.sent1:short] .
Products installed to function as the [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] shall protect the warm side of wall, ceiling and floor assemblies.

Where different products are used for the [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] and the insulation, the [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] shall be installed sufficiently close to the warm side of the insulation to prevent condensation at design conditions. (See  Notes [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote150:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote152:long] .)

Where the same product is used for the [REF:term:vpr-brrr:vapour barrier] and the insulation, the product shall be installed sufficiently close to the warm side of the assembly to prevent condensation at design conditions. (See  Notes [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote150:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote152:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote155:number] )

subsections.title: Properties and Position of Materials in the Building Envelope

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1.sent4:short] , sheet and panel-type materials incorporated into assemblies described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect1.art1:long] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art2:long] , where

clauses.text: the material has

subclauses.text: an air leakage characteristic less than 0.1 L/(s×m^{2}) at 75 Pa , and

a water vapour permeance less than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m^{2}) when measured in accordance with [REF:standard:astme96m] using the desiccant method (dry cup) (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote153:short] ), and

clauses.text: the intended use of the interior space where the materials are installed will not result in high moisture generation.

content.text: Where the intended use of the interior space will result in high moisture generation, the assembly shall be designed according to Part 5.

Wood-based sheathing materials not more than 12.5 mm thick and complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17.art2:long] need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1.sent1:short] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote154:short] .)

Where a material has a water vapour permeance not less than 30 ng/(Pa×s×m^{2}) and a thermal resistance not less than 0.7 (m^{2}×K)/W and the heating degree-days of the [REF:term:bldng:building] location are less than 6000 , the assembly need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1.sent1:short] .
Sheet and panel-type materials described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art1:short] shall be installed

clauses.text: on the warm face of the assembly (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4.art2:long] ),

at a location where the ratio between the total thermal resistance of all materials outboard of its innermost impermeable surface and the total thermal resistance of all materials inboard of that surface is not less than that required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art2.table1:long] , or
outboard of an air space that is vented to the outdoors.

content.text: For walls, the air space described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art2.sent1.clause3:medium] shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause1:long] .

content.title: Ratio of Outboard to Inboard Thermal Resistance

table_notes.content: See  Sentence [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent1:long] .

content.value: Heating Degree-Days of [REF:term:bldng:Building] Location [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5.art2.table1.note1] , Celsius degree-days
Minimum Ratio of Total Thermal Resistance Outboard of Material's Inner Surface to Total Thermal Resistance Inboard of Material's Inner Surface

content.text: For the purpose of this Section, the term “roof” shall mean sloped or near-horizontal assemblies that protect the spaces beneath them, including platforms that effectively serve as roofs with respect to the accumulation or drainage of precipitation. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote156:short] .)
For the purpose of this Section, the term “roofing” shall mean the primary covering for roofs.
Roofs shall be protected with roofing, including flashing, installed so as to

clauses.text: effectively shed water,
prevent the ingress of water and moisture into [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies and occupied space, and
minimize the ingress of water due to ice damming into [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies.

content.text: Compliance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect1.art2.sent1:short] shall be demonstrated by conforming to

clauses.text: the remainder of this Section, or
Part 5.

content.text: Methods described in [REF:standard:csaa123.51] are permitted to be used for the installation of asphalt shingles in lieu of the methods described in this Section.
Materials used for the preparation of the substrate for roofing shall conform to the requirements of the applicable standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect2.art1.table1:long] .

content.title: Materials for Preparation of the Substrate for Roofing

content.text: Roofing materials shall conform to the requirements of the applicable standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect2.art1.table2:long] .

table_notes.content: For the purpose of this Subsection, [REF:standard:astmd3019] shall only apply to the non-fibered and non-asbestos-fibered types (I and III) of asphalt roll roofing.

content.text: Materials listed in  Tables [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect2.art1.table1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect2.art1.table2:long] shall be installed in conformance with the manufacturer's written instructions. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect5.subsect1.art2.sent1:long] .)
Nails used for roofing shall be corrosion-resistant roofing or shingle nails conforming to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmf1667] or
[REF:standard:csab111]

content.text: Nails shall have sufficient length to penetrate through, or 12 mm into, roof sheathing.
Nails used with asphalt roofing shall have a head diameter of not less than 9.5 mm and a shank thickness of not less than 2.95 mm .

Nails used with wood shingles or shakes shall have a head diameter of not less than 4.8 mm and a shank thickness of not less than 2.0 mm and shall be stainless steel, aluminum or hot-dipped galvanized. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote157:short] .)
Staples used to apply asphalt or wood shingles shall be corrosion-resistant and shall be driven with the crown parallel to the eaves.

Staples used with asphalt shingles shall be not less than 19 mm long, 1.6 mm diam or thickness, with not less than a 25 mm crown, except that an 11 mm crown may be used as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent2:long] .

Staples used with wood shingles shall be not less than 29 mm long, 1.6 mm diam or thickness, with not less than a 9.5 mm crown and shall be stainless steel or aluminum. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote157:long] .)

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent3:short] , the slopes on which roof coverings may be applied shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.table1:long]

Asphalt and gravel or coal tar and gravel roofs may be constructed with lower slopes than required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] when effective drainage is provided by roof drains located at the lowest points on the roofs.

Profiled metal roof cladding systems specifically designed for low-slope applications are permitted to be installed with lower slopes than required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] , provided they are installed in conformance with the manufacturer's written recommendations.

Except where back-slope will not adversely affect adjacent supported or supporting constructions due to water ingress, roofs and constructions that effectively serve as roofs shall be constructed with sufficient slope away from

clauses.text: exterior walls, and
[REF:term:guard:guards] that are connected to the roof, or to a construction that effectively serves as a roof, by more than pickets or posts.

content.text: The slope required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent4:short] shall be sufficient to maintain a positive slope

clauses.text: after expected shrinkage of the [REF:term:bldng:building] frame, where these surfaces are supported by exterior walls and exterior columns (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote170:long] ), and
once design loading is taken into consideration, where these surfaces are cantilevered from exterior walls.

table_notes.content: See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect3.art1.sent3:long] .

content.value: Glass Fibre Reinforced Polyester Roofing Panels

content.text: Except where the omission of flashing will not adversely affect adjacent supported or supporting constructions, flashing shall be installed at junctions between roofs and

clauses.text: walls that rise above the roof, and
[REF:term:guard:guards] that are connected to the roof by more than pickets or posts.

content.text: For the purpose of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art1.sent1:short] , roofs shall include platforms that effectively serve as roofs with respect to the accumulation or drainage of precipitation.
Sheet metal flashing shall consist of not less than

clauses.text: 1.73 mm thick sheet lead,
0.33 mm thick galvanized steel,
0.33 mm thick copper,
0.35 mm thick zinc, or
0.48 mm thick aluminum.

content.text: Where sloping surfaces of shingled roofs intersect to form a valley, the valley shall be flashed.
Valley flashing shall be installed over continuous sheathing.
Closed valleys shall not be used with rigid shingles on slopes of less than 1 in 1.2.
Open valleys shall be flashed with at least

clauses.text: one layer of sheet metal not less than 600 mm wide, or
2 layers of roll roofing.

content.text: The bottom layer of roofing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art3.sent4:short] shall consist of at least Type S smooth roll roofing or Type M mineral surface roll roofing (mineral surface down) not less than 457 mm wide, centred in the valley and fastened with nails spaced not more than 450 mm o.c. located 25 mm away from the edges.

The top layer of roofing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art3.sent4:short] shall consist of at least Type M mineral surface roll roofing (mineral surface up), 914 mm wide, centred in the valley, applied over a 100 mm wide strip of cement along each edge of the bottom layer, and fastened with a sufficient number of nails to hold it in place until the shingles are applied.

articles.title: Intersection of Shingle Roofs and Masonry

content.text: The intersection of shingle roofs and masonry walls or [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] shall be protected with flashing.

Counter flashing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4.sent1:short] shall be embedded not less than 25 mm in the masonry and shall extend not less than 150 mm down the masonry and lap the lower flashing not less than 100 mm .

Flashing along the slopes of a roof described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4.sent1:short] shall be stepped so that there is not less than a 75 mm head lap in both the lower flashing and counter flashing.

Where the roof described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4.sent1:short] slopes upwards from the masonry, the flashing shall extend up the roof slope to a point equal in height to the flashing on the masonry, but not less than 1.5 times the shingle exposure.

articles.title: Intersection of Shingle Roofs and Walls other than Masonry

content.text: The intersection of shingle roofs and walls clad with other than masonry shall be protected with flashing.

Flashing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art5.sent1:short] shall be installed so that it extends up the wall not less than 75 mm behind the sheathing paper, and extends not less than 75 mm horizontally.
Along the slope of the roof, the flashing required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art5.sent1:short] shall be stepped with not less than a 75 mm head lap.

articles.title: Intersection of Built-Up Roofs and Masonry

content.text: The intersection of built-up roofs with masonry walls or [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] shall have a cant strip at the intersection, and a roofing membrane shall be mopped over the cant strip and not less than 150 mm up the wall.

Counter flashing installed over the intersection referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art6.sent1:short] shall be embedded not less than 25 mm in the masonry, and shall be of sufficient length to extend down not less than 150 mm , lapping the membrane on the masonry not less than 100 mm .

articles.title: Intersection of Built-Up Roofs and Walls other than Masonry

content.text: The intersection of built-up roofs with walls clad with other than masonry shall have a cant strip at the intersection.
The roofing membrane shall be mopped over the cant strip referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art7.sent1:short] .
Flashing plies shall extend not less than 150 mm up the wall referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art7.sent1:short] behind the sheathing paper.

Except as otherwise permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art8.sent5:short] , [REF:term:chmn:chimney] saddles shall be installed where the upper side of a [REF:term:chmn:chimney] on a sloping roof is more than 750 mm wide.
[REF:term:chmn:Chimney] saddles shall be covered with sheet metal or roofing material of weight and quality equivalent to the roofing.
Saddles shall be flashed where they intersect the roof.
The intersection of the saddle and the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] shall be flashed and counterflashed as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4:long]

A [REF:term:chmn:chimney] saddle need not be installed if the intersection between the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] and roof is protected by sheet metal flashing that extends up the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] to a height equal to at least one sixth the width of the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] , but not less than 150 mm , and up the roof slope to a point equal in height to the flashing on the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] , but not less than 1.5 times the shingle exposure.

Flashing described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art8.sent5:short] at the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] shall be counterflashed as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4.art4:long]

subsections.title: Eave Protection for Shingles and Shakes

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] , eave protection shall be provided on shingle, shake or tile roofs, extending from the edge of the roof a minimum of 900 mm up the roof slope to a line not less than 300 mm inside the inner face of the exterior wall.
Eave protection is not required

clauses.text: over unheated garages, carports and porches,
where the roof overhang exceeds 900 mm measured along the roof slope from the edge of the roof to the inner face of the exterior wall,
on roofs of asphalt shingles installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect8:long] ,
on roofs with slopes of 1 in 1.5 or greater, or
in regions with 3 500 or fewer degree-days.

content.text: Eave protection shall be laid beneath the starter strip and shall consist of

clauses.text: No. 15 asphalt-saturated felt laid in two plies lapped 480 mm and cemented together with lap cement,
Type M or S roll roofing laid with not less than 100 mm head and end laps cemented together with lap cement,
glass fibre or polyester fibre coated base sheets, or
self-sealing composite membranes consisting of modified bituminous coated material.

content.text: Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect6.art1.sent2:short] , when underlay is used beneath shingles, it shall be

clauses.text: asphalt-saturated sheathing paper weighing not less than 0.195 kg/m^{2} , or
No. 15 plain or perforated asphalt-saturated felt.

content.text: Underlay used beneath wood shingles shall be breather type.
When used with shingles, underlay shall be installed parallel to the eaves with head and end lap of not less than 50 mm .

The top edge of each strip of underlay referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall be fastened with sufficient roofing nails to hold it in place until the shingles are applied.

The underlay referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] shall overlap the eave protection by not less than 100 mm . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect10.art2:long] for underlay beneath wood shakes.)

subsections.title: Asphalt Shingles on Slopes of 1 in 3 or Greater

content.text: Coverage shall be not less than 2 thicknesses of shingle over the entire roof, disregarding cutouts.

A starter strip shall be installed along the lower edge of the roof so that it extends approximately 12 mm beyond the eaves and rake of the roof and fastened along the bottom edge with nails spaced not more than 300 mm o.c.
Starter strips shall be

clauses.text: at least Type M mineral-surfaced roll roofing not less than 300 mm wide,
shingles of the same weight and quality as those used as a roof covering with tabs facing up the roof slope, or
pre-manufactured starter strips installed with sealant at the eaves.

content.text: Starter strips need not be provided where eave protection of not less than Type M mineral-surfaced roll roofing is provided.
Shingles shall have a head lap of not less than 50 mm .

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent2:short] , shingles shall be fastened with at least 4 nails or staples for 1 m wide shingles so that no nails or staples are exposed.
Where staples with an 11 mm crown are used, shingles shall be fastened with at least 6 staples.
Fasteners may be reduced for narrower shingles in proportion to the width of the shingle or when shingles incorporating interlocking devices are used.

Fasteners referred to in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent2:short] shall be located 25 mm to 40 mm from each end of each strip shingle with other fasteners equally spaced between them.

Fasteners referred to in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4.sent2:short] shall be located not less than 12 mm above the tops of the cutouts.
Shingle tabs shall be secured by a spot of plastic cement not exceeding 25 mm diam under the centre of each tab or by interlocking devices or self-sealing strips.
Shingles on hips and ridges shall be applied so they extend not less than 100 mm on either side of the hip or ridge, and shall be lapped not less than 150 mm .

Shingles referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art6.sent1:short] shall be fastened with nails or staples on each side located not more than 25 mm from the edge and 25 mm above the butt of the overlying shingle.
Eave protection shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect5:long]
Flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]

subsections.title: Asphalt Shingles on Slopes of less than 1 in 3

content.text: Except for the first 2 courses, coverage shall be not less than 3 thicknesses of shingle over the entire roof, disregarding cutouts.
A starter strip shall be installed as in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art2:long]
Starter strips required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect8.art2.sent1:short] shall be laid in a continuous band of cement not less than 200 mm wide.

Shingle tabs shall be secured with cold application cement applied at the rate of not less than 0.5 L/m^{2} of cemented area, or hot application asphalt applied at the rate of 1 kg/m^{2} of cemented area.
The first course of shingles shall be secured by a continuous band of cement along the eaves applied so that the width of the band equals the shingle exposure plus 100 mm .
The succeeding courses of shingles shall be secured by a continuous band of cement applied so that the width of the band equals the shingle exposure plus 50 mm .
The band required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect8.art4.sent2:short] shall be located not more than 50 mm above the butt of the overlying course of shingles.
Shingles on hips and ridges shall be not less than 300 mm wide applied to provide triple coverage.

Shingles referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect8.art5.sent1:short] shall be cemented to the roof shingles and to each other with a coat of cement and fastened with nails or staples located 40 mm above the butt of the overlying shingle and 50 mm from each edge.
Flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]
Shingles shall be fastened in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7.art4:long]
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art1.sent1:long] , decking for wood shingled roofs may be continuous or spaced.
Western cedar shingles shall be not less than No. 2 grade.
Eastern white cedar shingles shall be not less than B (clear) grade.
Wood shingles shall be not less than 400 mm long and not less than 75 mm or more than 350 mm wide.
Shingles shall be spaced approximately 6 mm apart and offset at the joints in adjacent courses not less than 40 mm so that joints in alternate courses are staggered.
Shingles shall be fastened with 2 nails or staples located approximately 20 mm from the sides of the shingle and 40 mm above the exposure line.
The exposure of wood roof shingles shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect9.art6.table1:long]

content.value: No.1 or A Grade Length of Shingle, mm
No. 2 or B Grade Length of Shingle, mm

content.text: Flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]
Eave protection shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect5:long]
Shakes shall be not less than 450 mm long and not less than 100 mm nor more than 350 mm wide with a butt thickness of not more than 32 mm and not less than 9 mm .

Where eave protection is not provided, an underlay conforming to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect6.art1:long] for wood shingles shall be laid as a strip not less than 900 mm wide along the eaves.

A strip of material similar to that described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect10.art2.sent1:short] not less than 450 mm wide shall be interlaid between each course of shakes with the bottom edge of the strip positioned above the butt line at a distance equal to double the exposure of the shakes.

Interlaid strips referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect10.art2.sent2:short] shall be lapped not less than 150 mm at hips and ridges in a manner that will prevent water from reaching the roof sheathing.
Shakes shall be spaced 6 mm to 9 mm apart and the joints in any one course shall be separated not less than 40 mm from joints in adjacent courses.
Shakes shall be fastened with nails located approximately 20 mm from the sides of the shakes and 40 mm above the exposure line.
The exposure of wood shakes shall not exceed

clauses.text: 190 mm for shakes not less than 450 mm long, and
250 mm for shakes not less than 600 mm long.

content.text: Flashing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]
Eave protection shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect5:long]
Shakes shall be not less than No. 1 or Handsplit grade.
The quantities of bituminous materials used on built-up roofs shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art1.table1:long]

content.title: Quantities of Bitumen for Built-up Roofs

content.value: Amount of Bitumen per Square Metre of Roof Surface

content.text: Coal-tar products and asphalt products shall not be used together in built-up roof construction.
Bitumen roofing felts shall be at least No. 15 felt.

Aggregate used for surfacing built-up roofs shall be clean, dry and durable and shall consist of particles of gravel, crushed stone or air-cooled blast [REF:term:frnc:furnace] slag having a size of from 6 mm to 15 mm .
The minimum amount of aggregate surfacing per square metre of roof surface shall be 15 kg gravel or crushed stone or 10 kg crushed slag.
Flashing for built-up roofs shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect4:long]
Built-up roofing shall consist of not less than 3 mopped-down layers of roofing felt flood coated with bitumen.
In hot process applications each layer of bitumen-saturated felt shall be laid while the bitumen is hot, with each layer overlapping the previous one.
The full width under each lap referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art7.sent1:short] shall be coated with bitumen so that in no place does felt touch felt.
Felt shall be laid free of wrinkles and shall be rolled directly into the hot bitumen and broomed forward and outward from the centre to ensure complete adhesion.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art8.sent2:short] , built-up roofing applied over wood, plywood, OSB or waferboard roof sheathing shall be laid over an additional base layer of felt laid dry over the entire roof deck with not less than a 50 mm headlap and a 50 mm sidelap between each sheet.

Where plywood, OSB or waferboard roof sheathing is used, the dry layer of felt required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art8.sent1:short] may be omitted when the joints are taped and the sheathing is primed with asphalt.

Roofing shall be securely attached to the decking or where insulation is applied above the deck, the insulation shall be securely attached to the deck before the first layer of felt is fastened to the insulation.
Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art10.sent4:short] , a cant strip shall be provided at the edges of roofs.
At least 2 plies of the roofing membrane shall be carried over the top of the cant strip.
Flashing shall extend over the top of the cant strip and be shaped to form a drip.
The cant strip required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art10.sent1:short] need not be provided where a gravel stop is installed at the edge of roofs.

The roofing membranes shall be carried over the edge of the roof before the gravel stop referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art10.sent4:short] is fastened and 2 plies of roofing membrane mopped to the top surface of the gravel stop before the flood coat is applied.

The gravel stop referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect11.art10.sent4:short] shall extend over the edge of the roof to form a drip or shall be flashed so that the flashing extends over the edge to form a drip.
Wide selvage asphalt roofing shall provide double coverage over the entire roof surface.
Plies of selvage roofing shall be cemented together to ensure a watertight joint.
Sheet metal roofing shall be not less than

clauses.text: 0.33 mm thick galvanized steel,
0.46 mm thick copper,
0.46 mm thick zinc, or
0.48 mm thick aluminum.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art1.sent1:long] , where sheet metal roofing is not supported by roof decking but spans between spaced supports, the panels shall be designed to support the specified [REF:term:lv-ld:live loads] for roofs.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art1.sent1:long] , where glass-reinforced polyester roofing panels are not supported by roof decking but span between spaced supports, the panels shall be designed to support the specified live roof loads.
Hot applied rubberized asphalt roofing shall be installed in accordance with [REF:standard:cgsb-37.51]
Polyvinyl chloride sheet applied roofing membrane shall be installed in accordance with [REF:standard:cgsb37-gp-55m]

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect16.art1.sent1:long] , concrete roof tiles shall be installed according to [REF:standard:csaa220s] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote159:short] .)
When roof drains are provided they shall conform to Part 7.

Where downspouts are provided and are not connected to a sewer, extensions shall be provided to carry rainwater away from the [REF:term:bldng:building] in a manner which will prevent [REF:term:l:soil] erosion.

Where lumber, wood shingles, shakes, fibre-cement shingles, planks and sheets, plywood, OSB, waferboard, hardboard, vinyl, insulated vinyl, polypropylene, aluminum or steel, including trim and soffits, are installed as cladding on wood-frame walls or above-ground flat insulating concrete form walls exposed to precipitation, the cladding assembly shall comply with

clauses.text: Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect13:long] , or
Part 5.

content.text: Where stucco is installed as cladding on wood-frame walls, above-ground flat insulating concrete form walls or masonry walls exposed to precipitation, the cladding assembly shall comply with

clauses.text: Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5:long] , and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28:long] , or
Part 5.

content.text: Where masonry serves as cladding on wood-frame walls, above-ground flat insulating concrete form walls or masonry walls exposed to precipitation, the cladding assembly shall comply with

clauses.text: Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long] , and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long] , except for masonry veneer, which shall be attached to above-ground flat insulating concrete form walls in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art4.sent2:long] , or
Part 5.

content.text: Where asphalt shingles are installed as cladding on wood-frame walls exposed to precipitation, the cladding assembly shall comply with

clauses.text: Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect26.subsect7:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long] , or
Part 5.

content.text: Where an exterior insulation finish system is installed as cladding on wood-frame, masonry, cold-formed steel stud, above-ground flat insulating concrete form or cast-in-place concrete walls exposed to precipitation, the cladding assembly shall comply with(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote160:short] .)

clauses.text: Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long] , and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14:long] , or
Part 5.

content.text: Where cladding materials other than those described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect1.art1.sent5:short] are installed, or where the cladding materials described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect1.art1.sent5:short] are installed on substrates other than those identified in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect1.art1.sent5:short] , the materials and installation shall comply with Part 5.

articles.title: Minimizing and Preventing Ingress and Damage

content.text: Except where exterior walls are protected from precipitation or where it can be shown that precipitation ingress will not adversely affect occupant health or safety, exterior walls shall be designed and constructed to

clauses.text: minimize the ingress of precipitation into the assembly, and
prevent the ingress of precipitation into interior space.

content.text: Except where exterior walls are protected from specific mechanisms of deterioration, such as mechanical impact and ultraviolet radiation, exterior walls shall be designed and constructed to minimize the likelihood of their required performance being reduced to an unacceptable level as a result of those mechanisms.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] , a cladding assembly is deemed to have a capillary break between the cladding and the backing assembly, where

clauses.text: there is a drained and vented air space not less than 9.5 mm deep behind the cladding, over the full height and width of the wall (see also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art3:long] ),

an open drainage material, not less than 10 mm thick and with a cross-sectional area that is not less than 80% open, is installed between the cladding and the backing, over the full height and width of the wall,
the cladding is loosely fastened to the backing and behind each cladding component there is a clear air space that is

subclauses.text: continuous for the full width of the component,
reserved,

revisions.text: not less than 10 mm deep at the bottom of the component, and
reserved,
revisions.change_summary: Struck out 'Reserved.' and substituted 'reserved,'

subclauses.text: reserved.

revisions.text: not less than 6 mm deep over not less than 90 mm for every 230 mm of exposed height of the component,
reserved.
revisions.change_summary: Struck out 'Reserved.' and substituted 'reserved.'

clauses.text: the wall is a masonry [REF:term:cvt-wll:cavity wall] or the cladding is masonry veneer constructed according to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20:long] , or
the cladding conforms to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14:long]

content.text: The drained and vented air space, and drainage material described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art1.sent1:short] may be interrupted by

clauses.text: penetrations for windows, doors and services,
flashing, and
furring, provided the furring does not make up more than 20% of the furred area.

content.text: Where a construction projects over the top of the drained and vented air space described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause1:medium] or over the drainage material described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause2:medium] , the air space or drainage material shall not be contiguous with concealed spaces in the projecting construction.

Exterior walls exposed to precipitation shall be protected against precipitation ingress by an exterior cladding assembly consisting of a first plane of protection and a second plane of protection, where such walls enclose spaces of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] or spaces that directly serve spaces of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] .

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent6:short] , exterior walls exposed to precipitation shall be protected against precipitation ingress by an exterior cladding assembly consisting of a first plane of protection and a second plane of protection incorporating a capillary break, where

clauses.text: the number of degree-days is less than 3400 and the moisture index is greater than 0.90, or
the number of degree-days is 3400 or more, and the moisture index is greater than 1.00.

see_also.content: (See [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3.art1.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC:short] for information on the moisture index.)

content.text: In exterior walls described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent5:short] , the first and second planes of protection need not incorporate a capillary break, where

clauses.text: it can be shown that omitting the capillary break will not adversely affect the performance of the [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies,
the [REF:term:bldng:building] is an accessory [REF:term:bldng:building] , or
the wall

subclauses.text: is constructed of non-moisture-sensitive materials, and intersecting or supported floors are also constructed of non-moisture-sensitive materials, or
is constructed as a mass wall of sufficient thickness to minimize the transfer of moisture to the interior.

articles.title: First and Second Planes of Protection

content.text: Where walls required to provide protection from precipitation comprise cladding assemblies with first and second planes of protection,

clauses.text: the first plane of protection shall

subclauses.text: consist of cladding with appropriate trim, accessory pieces and fasteners, and

be designed and constructed to minimize the passage of rain and snow into the wall by minimizing holes and managing precipitation ingress caused by the kinetic energy of raindrops, surface tension, capillarity, gravity, and air pressure differences (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long] ),

clauses.text: the second plane of protection shall be designed and constructed to (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3:long] )

subclauses.text: intercept all rain and snow that gets past the first plane of protection, and
effectively dissipate any rain or snow to the exterior, and

clauses.text: the protection provided by the first and second planes of protection shall be maintained

subclauses.text: at wall penetrations created by the installation of components and services such as windows, doors, ventilation ducts, piping, wiring and electrical outlets, and
at the interface with other wall assemblies.

content.text: A clearance of not less than 200 mm shall be provided between finished ground and cladding that is adversely affected by moisture, such as untreated wood, plywood, OSB, waferboard and hardboard.
A clearance of not less than 50 mm shall be provided between a roof surface and cladding that is adversely affected by moisture, such as untreated wood, plywood, OSB, waferboard and hardboard.

articles.title: Elements of the Second Plane of Protection

content.text: The second plane of protection shall consist of a drainage plane having an appropriate inner boundary and flashing to dissipate rainwater to the exterior.

Except for cladding systems conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14:long] , the inner boundary of the drainage plane shall comply with  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art6:long]
The protection provided by the second plane of protection shall be maintained

clauses.text: at wall penetrations created by the installation of components and services such as windows, doors, ventilation ducts, piping, wiring and electrical outlets, and
at the interface with other wall assemblies.

content.text: Flashing material and its installation shall comply with  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art7:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art8:long]
Sheathing membranes shall conform to the performance requirements of [REF:standard:cgsb-51.32]

Except as provided in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art4:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art6:long] , at least one layer of sheathing membrane shall be applied beneath cladding.
Sheathing membrane required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art3.sent1:short] shall be applied so that joints are lapped not less than 100 mm .
Where sheathing membrane required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art3.sent1:short] is applied horizontally, the upper sheets shall overlap the lower sheets.

articles.title: Insulating Sheathing in lieu of Sheathing Membrane

content.text: Where non-wood-based rigid exterior insulating sheathing, or exterior insulating sheathing with an integral sheathing membrane is installed, a separate sheathing membrane is not required.
Where insulating sheathing is installed as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] ,

clauses.text: sheathing panels subject to moisture deterioration shall be sealed at all joints, and
the joints of sheathing panels not subject to moisture deterioration shall be

subclauses.text: sealed at all joints, or
lapped or tongue and groove, and detailed to ensure drainage of water to the exterior.

articles.title: Sheathing Membranes in lieu of Sheathing

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art6:long] , where no sheathing is used, at least 2 layers of sheathing membrane shall be applied beneath the cladding. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17.art1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote166:short] .)

All joints in the sheathing membrane required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art5.sent1:short] shall occur over framing, and the membrane shall be fastened to the framing with roofing nails or staples spaced not more than 150 mm along the edges of the outer layer of sheathing membrane.

Wall sheathing is permitted to be used in lieu of one layer of sheathing membrane required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art5.sent1:short] , and its thickness need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17.art2.table1:long] .

Sheathing membrane is permitted to be omitted beneath cladding when the joints in the cladding are formed to effectively prevent the passage of wind and rain in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art6.sent2:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art6.sent3:short] , as applicable.
