Cladding consisting of sheets of plywood, hardboard, OSB, waferboard or fibre cement is considered to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] , provided the cladding is applied so that

clauses.text: all edges are directly supported by framing,
the vertical joints between adjacent sheets are sealed and

subclauses.text: covered with battens,
shiplapped, or
otherwise matched to provide weathertight joints, and

clauses.text: the horizontal joints between adjacent sheets are sealed and

subclauses.text: shiplapped, or
otherwise matched to provide weathertight joints.

content.text: Metal siding consisting of sheets of metal is considered to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] where the joints between sheets are of the locked-seam type.
Flashing shall consist of not less than

clauses.text: 1.73 mm thick sheet lead,
0.33 mm thick galvanized steel,
0.46 mm thick copper,
0.46 mm thick zinc,
0.48 mm thick aluminum, or
1.02 mm thick vinyl.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art8.sent2:short] , flashing shall be installed at

clauses.text: every horizontal junction between cladding elements,
every horizontal offset in the cladding, and
every horizontal line where the cladding substrates change and where

subclauses.text: the substrates differ sufficiently for stresses to be concentrated along that line, or
the installation of the cladding on the lower substrate may compromise the drainage of moisture from behind the cladding above.

content.text: Flashing need not be installed as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art8.sent1:short]

clauses.text: where the upper cladding elements overlap the lower cladding elements by not less than 25 mm ,
where

subclauses.text: the cladding above and below the joint is installed outboard of a drained and vented air space (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause1:long] ), and
the horizontal detail is constructed so as to minimize the ingress of precipitation into the air space, or

clauses.text: at horizontal construction joints in stucco, where

subclauses.text: the joint is finished with an expansion-contraction strip, and
the cladding is installed outboard of a drained and vented air space (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect2.art2.sent1.clause1:long] ).

content.text: Flashing shall be installed over exterior wall openings where the vertical distance from the bottom of the eave to the top of the trim is more than one-quarter of the horizontal overhang of the eave. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote169:short] .)
Flashing described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art8.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art8.sent3:short] shall

clauses.text: extend not less than 50 mm upward inboard of the sheathing membrane or sheathing installed in lieu of the sheathing membrane (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art4:long] ),
have a slope of not less than 6% toward the exterior after the expected shrinkage of the [REF:term:bldng:building] frame,
terminate at each end with an end-dam

subclauses.text: with a height in millimetres not less than 25 mm or 1/10 the value of the 1-in-5 driving rain wind pressure in Pa, and
at the height defined in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3.art8.sent4.clause3.subclause1:short] , extending to the face of the adjacent cladding,

clauses.text: lap not less than 10 mm vertically over the [REF:term:bldng:building] element below, and
terminate in a drip offset not less than 5 mm outward from the outer face of the [REF:term:bldng:building] element below.

content.text: Where the sills of windows and doors installed in exterior walls are not self-flashing, flashing shall be installed between the underside of the window or door and the wall construction below. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote171:short] .)
Sealant shall be provided where required to prevent the entry of water into the structure.
Sealant shall be provided between masonry, siding or stucco and the adjacent door and window frames or trim, including sills, unless such locations are completely protected from the entry of rain.

Sealant shall be provided at vertical joints between different cladding materials unless the joint is suitably lapped or flashed to prevent the entry of rain. (See  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect7.subsect6.art2:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect13.art12:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect1.art5:long] )
Sealants shall be

clauses.text: a non-hardening type suitable for exterior use,
selected for their ability to resist the effects of weathering, and
compatible with and adhere to the substrate to which they are applied.

content.text: Sealants shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc834]
[REF:standard:astmc920]
[REF:standard:astmc1184] or
[REF:standard:astmc1311]

content.text: Backer rod shall conform to [REF:standard:astmc1330] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote172:long] .)

Except as permitted by  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art1.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art1.sent5:short] , cladding shall be fastened to the framing members or furring members, or to blocking between the framing members.

Vertical lumber, stucco lath or reinforcing, vertically applied vinyl siding, vertically applied insulated vinyl siding, and polypropylene siding are permitted to be attached to sheathing only where the sheathing consists of not less than

clauses.text: 14.3 mm lumber,
12.5 mm plywood or waferboard, or
11 mm OSB.

content.text: Vertically applied metal siding and wood shingles and shakes are permitted to be attached to the sheathing only where the sheathing consists of not less than

clauses.text: 14.3 mm lumber,
7.5 mm plywood, or
7.5 mm OSB or waferboard.

content.text: Where wood shingles or shakes are applied to sheathing which is not suitable for attaching the shingles or shakes, the shingles or shakes are permitted to be attached to a wood lath not less than 38 mm by 9.5 mm thick securely nailed to the framing and applied as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5:long]

Cladding, trim and furring members are permitted to be attached to the web fastening strips of flat wall insulating concrete form units using screws in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art4.sent2:long] .
Blocking for the attachment of cladding shall be not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber securely nailed to the framing and spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art1.sent4:long] , furring for the attachment of cladding shall be not less than 19 mm by 38 mm lumber when applied over sheathing.
When applied without sheathing, furring referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art3.sent1:short] shall be not less than

clauses.text: 19 mm by 64 mm lumber on supports spaced not more than 400 mm o.c., or
19 mm by 89 mm lumber on supports spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.

content.text: Furring referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art3.sent1:short] shall be

clauses.text: securely fastened to the framing, and
spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.

content.text: Nail or staple size and spacing for the attachment of cladding and trim to wood framing, furring members or blocking shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art4.table1:long] .

content.title: Attachment of Cladding to Wood Framing, Furring Members or Blocking

table_notes.content: The minimum fastener length need not exceed the minimum fastener penetration depth required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art7:long]

The maximum spacing of 400 mm o.c. applies to nails and staples used to attach horizontally applied vinyl, insulated vinyl and polypropylene siding, unless a greater spacing is permitted in an evaluation report prepared by an accredited certification organization.

content.value: Minimum Nail or Staple Length, mm [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art4.table1.note1]
Minimum Number of Nails or Staples
Maximum Nail or Staple Spacing, mm o.c.
Lumber siding or horizontal siding made from sheet material

content.text: Screw size and spacing for the attachment of cladding, trim and furring members to the web fastening strips of flat wall insulating concrete form (ICF) units shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art4.table2:long] where the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure (HWP) is less than or equal to 0.60 kPa . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote173:short] .)

content.title: Attachment of Cladding to Flat Wall ICF Units where the 1-in-50 HWP ≤ 0.60 kPa

table_notes.content: Wood shakes and wood shingles are permitted to be attached to horizontal wood furring members in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art4.table1:long] . The wood furring members shall be attached to the web fastening strips of flat wall ICF units with screws not less than 4.2 mm in diameter spaced horizontally not more than 400 or 450 mm o.c. (two horizontal spacing options are given to accommodate the 150 and 200 mm o.c. horizontal spacing options for web fastening strips).

Two horizontal spacing options are given to accommodate the 150 mm o.c. and 200 mm o.c. horizontal spacing options for web fastening strips. The maximum vertical spacing of screws or masonry ties, as applicable, shall be 400 mm .
Screws must be long enough to penetrate through the web fastening strips by a minimum of 6 mm .
See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect20.subsect5:long] for requirements on the support of masonry veneer.

content.value: Maximum Horizontal Spacing of Screws, mm o.c. [REF:table-note:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art4.table2.note2]
Lumber siding or horizontal siding made from sheet material
400 or 450 (masonry tie screwed to web fastening strip)

content.text: Nails or staples for the attachment of cladding and wood trim shall be corrosion-resistant and shall be compatible with the cladding material.
Fasteners for metal cladding shall be positioned to permit expansion and contraction of the cladding.
Fasteners for vinyl siding, insulated vinyl siding and polypropylene siding shall be installed in the centre of the slots of the nail hem.
Fasteners for shakes and shingles shall penetrate through the nail-holding base or not less than 19 mm into the framing.
Fasteners for vinyl cladding, insulated vinyl cladding and polypropylene cladding shall penetrate through the nail-holding base or not less than 32 mm into the framing.

Fasteners for cladding other than that described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art7.sent1:short]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art7.sent2:short] shall penetrate through the nail-holding base or not less than 25 mm into the framing.
Lumber siding shall be sound, free of knot holes, loose knots, through checks or splits.
Drop, rustic, novelty, lapped board and vertical wood siding shall be not less than 14.3 mm thick and not more than 286 mm wide.
Bevel siding shall be

clauses.text: not less than 5 mm thick at the top, and
not less than

subclauses.text: 12 mm thick at the butt for siding 184 mm or less in width, and
14.3 mm thick at the butt for siding wider than 184 mm .

content.text: Bevel siding shall be not more than 286 mm wide.
Lumber siding shall prevent water from entering at the joints by the use of lapped or matched joints or by vertical wood battens.
Siding shall overlap not less than 1 mm per 16 mm width of lumber, but not less than

clauses.text: 9.5 mm for matched siding,
25 mm for lapped bevel siding, or
12 mm for vertical battens.

content.text: Shingles and shakes shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csao118.1] or
[REF:standard:csao118.2]

content.text: Western cedar shakes shall be not less than No. 1 or Handsplit grade, and western cedar shingles not less than No. 2 grade, except that No. 3 grade may be used for undercoursing.
Eastern white cedar shingles shall be at least B (clear) grade, except that C grade may be used for the lower course of double course applications.
Shingles and shakes shall be not less than 65 mm or more than 350 mm wide.

Shingles or shakes shall be fastened with nails or staples located approximately 20 mm from each edge and not less than 25 mm above the exposure line for single-course applications, or approximately 50 mm above the butt for double-course applications.
In single-course application, joints in succeeding courses shall be offset not less than 40 mm so that joints in any 2 of 3 consecutive courses are staggered.

In double-course application, joints in the outer course shall be offset from joints in the under-course by not less than 40 mm , and joints in succeeding courses shall be offset not less than 40 mm .

When lath is used with double-course application [see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5.art1.sent4:long] ], it shall be spaced according to the exposure and securely fastened to the framing.
The butts of the under-course of the application referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5.sent1:short] shall rest on the top edge of the lath.

The outer course of the application referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5.sent1:short] shall be fastened to the lath with nails of sufficient length to penetrate through the lath.

The butts of the shingles or shakes shall be so located that they project not less than 12 mm below the bottom edge of the lath referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5.sent1:short] .

If wood lath is not used, the butts of the under-course shingles or shakes of the application referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art5.sent1:short] shall be located 12 mm above the butts of the outer course.
The exposure and butt thickness of shingles and shakes shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect7.art6.table1:long]

content.title: Exposure and Thickness of Wood Shingles and Shakes

content.text: Plywood cladding shall be exterior type conforming to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:hpvahp1]
[REF:standard:csao121]
[REF:standard:csao151] or
[REF:standard:csao153]

content.text: Plywood cladding shall be not less than 6 mm thick when applied directly to sheathing.
When applied directly to framing or over furring strips, plywood cladding thickness shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art2.table1:long]

content.value: Face Grain Right Angles to Supports

content.text: The thickness of grooved or textured plywood cladding shall be measured at the point of least thickness.
The edges of plywood cladding shall be treated with a suitable paint or sealer.
Plywood applied in panels shall have all edges supported.
Not less than a 2 mm gap shall be provided between panels referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] .
Vertical joints in cladding referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be protected with batten strips or sealant when the plywood joints are not matched.
Horizontal joints in cladding referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art4.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 25 mm or shall be suitably flashed.
Plywood applied in horizontal lapped strips shall have not less than a 2 mm gap provided at the butted ends, which shall be caulked.
The horizontal joints of siding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art5.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 25 mm .
Wedges shall be inserted under all vertical butt joints and at all corners when horizontal lapped plywood is applied without sheathing.
Hardboard cladding shall conform to [REF:standard:ansia135.6]
Hardboard cladding shall be not less than

clauses.text: 9.5 mm thick when applied over sheathing that provides continuous support or over furring or framing members not more than 400 mm o.c. , or
11.1 mm thick when applied over furring or framing members not more than 600 mm o.c.

content.text: Where hardboard cladding is grooved, the grooves shall not extend more than 1.5 mm into the minimum required thickness. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote175:short] .)
Hardboard cladding applied in panels shall have all edges supported with not less than a 5 mm gap provided between sheets.
Vertical joints in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect9.art3.sent1:short] shall be protected with batten strips or sealant when the joints are not matched.
Horizontal joints in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect9.art3.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 25 mm or shall be suitably flashed.
Hardboard applied in horizontal lapped strips shall have not less than a 5 mm gap provided at the butted ends, which shall be sealed or otherwise protected with suitable mouldings.

The horizontal joints of siding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect9.art4.sent1:short] shall overlap not less than 1 mm per 16 mm width of siding board but not less than 9.5 mm for matched joint siding or 25 mm for lapped siding.
Not less than 3 mm clearance shall be provided between hardboard cladding and door or window frames.
OSB and waferboard cladding shall conform to [REF:standard:csao437.0]
OSB conforming to O-2 grade shall be not less than 6.0 mm thick where applied directly to sheathing.

OSB conforming to O-2 grade applied directly to framing or over furring strips shall conform to the thickness shown for plywood in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect8.art2.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote176:short] .)
OSB conforming to O-1 grade and waferboard conforming to R-1 grade shall be not less than 7.9 mm thick where applied directly to sheathing.
Where applied directly to framing or over furring strips, OSB conforming to O-1 grade and waferboard conforming to R-1 grade shall be not less than

clauses.text: 9.5 mm thick on supports spaced not more than 400 mm o.c., and
12.7 mm thick on supports spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.

content.text: OSB and waferboard applied in panels shall have all edges supported and treated with a primer or sealer.
Not less than a 3 mm gap shall be provided between sheets in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect10.art3.sent1:short] .

Vertical joints in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect10.art3.sent1:short] shall be protected with batten strips or sealant when the OSB and waferboard joints are not matched.
Horizontal joints in cladding described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect10.art3.sent1:short] shall be lapped not less than 25 mm or shall be suitably flashed.
Not less than a 3 mm clearance shall be provided between OSB and waferboard cladding and door or window frames.
Steel sheet cladding, including horizontal and vertical strip steel siding, flashing and trim accessories, shall

clauses.text: have a minimum thickness of 0.33 mm , and
conform to [REF:standard:cssbi23m]

content.text: Horizontal and vertical strip aluminum siding, including flashing and trim accessories, shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-93.2] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote178:short] .)

Aluminum sheet cladding shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-93.1] and shall have a thickness of not less than 0.58 mm , except that siding supported by backing or sheathing shall have a thickness of not less than 0.46 mm . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote178:short] .)

subsections.title: Vinyl Siding, Insulated Vinyl Siding and Vinyl Soffits

content.text: Vinyl siding shall conform to [REF:standard:astmd3679]
Insulated vinyl siding shall conform to [REF:standard:astmd7793]
Rigid vinyl soffits shall conform to [REF:standard:astmd4477]

Where vinyl siding, insulated vinyl siding or rigid vinyl soffits are required to have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] , the rating shall be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs102.2]
The attachment of vinyl siding and insulated vinyl siding shall conform to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5:long]
Polypropylene siding shall conform to [REF:standard:astmd7254]
Where polypropylene siding is required to have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] , the rating shall be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs102.2]
The attachment of polypropylene siding shall conform to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5:long]
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14.art1.sent2:short] , this Subsection applies to exterior insulation finish systems (EIFS) that

clauses.text: are covered in the scope of [REF:standard:ulcs716.1] and
have a geometrically defined drainage cavity with a minimum cavity depth of 9.5 mm and an open area equal to not less than 13% of the area of a full-size EIFS panel.

content.text: EIFS that are not covered by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14.art1.sent1:short] shall comply with Part 5.
The materials used in EIFS shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs716.1]
The substrate on which the EIFS is installed shall

clauses.text: be compatible with that particular system (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote180:short] ), and
comply with the structural requirements for sheathing materials stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23:long]

content.text: The design and installation of EIFS on the substrate described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect14.art2.sent2:long] shall comply with

clauses.text: [REF:standard:ulcs716.2] and
[REF:standard:ulcs716.3]

content.text: Sheathing shall be provided beneath stucco applied over wood-frame walls except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect4.art2:long]
Where applied beneath stucco, sheathing shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect17:long]
Stucco lath or reinforcing shall be used to attach stucco to any substrate other than masonry.
Stucco lath or reinforcing shall be used to attach stucco to masonry where

clauses.text: the masonry is soft-burned tile or brick of less strength than the stucco, or
the masonry surface is not sound, clean and sufficiently rough to provide a good key.

content.text: Stucco applied over masonry [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] shall be reinforced.
Stucco finish shall not be applied over concrete masonry units less than one month old unless the units have been cured by the autoclave process.
Stucco shall be not less than 200 mm above finished ground level except when it is applied over concrete or masonry.

Flashing and caulking used with stucco shall conform to  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:number] , except that if aluminum flashing is used, it shall be separated from the stucco by an impervious membrane or coating. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect7.subsect6.art2:long] for caulking around window frames.)
Portland cement shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa3001]
Aggregate shall be clean, well-graded natural sand or sand manufactured from crushed stone, gravel or air-cooled blast furnace slag and shall contain no significant amounts of deleterious material.
Aggregate grading shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect2.art2.table1:long]
Water shall be clean and free of significant amounts of deleterious material.
Fasteners for stucco lath or reinforcing shall be corrosion-resistant and of a material other than aluminum.
Nails for stucco lath or reinforcing shall be not less than 3.2 mm diam with a head diameter of not less than 11.1 mm .
Staples for stucco lath or reinforcing shall be not less than 1.98 mm diam or thickness.

Staples and nails for attaching stucco lath or reinforcing to vertical surfaces shall be of sufficient length to penetrate 25 mm into framing members or to the full depth of the sheathing where the sheathing is used for attachment.
On horizontal surfaces nails for stucco lath or reinforcing shall be not less than 38 mm long.
Rib lath or expanded metal stucco mesh shall be

clauses.text: copper-alloy steel coated with rust-inhibitive paint after fabrication, or
galvanized.

content.text: Woven or welded wire mesh shall be galvanized.

Sheathing need not be provided beneath stucco where not less than 1.19 mm diam galvanized wire is applied horizontally to the framing at vertical intervals of not more than 150 mm , or where paper-backed welded wire metal lath is used.
Stucco lath shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect4.art3.table1:long]
Stucco lath shall be held not less than 6 mm away from the backing by means of suitable self-furring devices.
Stucco lath shall be applied with the long dimension horizontal.
Horizontal and vertical joints in stucco lath shall be lapped not less than 50 mm .
End joints of stucco lath shall be staggered and shall occur over framing members.

External corners of stucco lath shall be reinforced with a vertical strip of lath or reinforcing extending not less than 150 mm on both sides of the corner, or the lath or reinforcing shall extend around corners not less than 150 mm .
Stucco lath shall be fastened in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect5:long]
Fasteners on vertical surfaces shall be spaced not more than

clauses.text: 150 mm o.c. vertically and 400 mm o.c. horizontally, or
100 mm o.c. vertically and 600 mm o.c. horizontally.

content.text: Nailing patterns other than those required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect4.art6.sent2:short] are permitted to be used provided there are at least 20 fasteners per square metre of wall surface.
Fasteners on horizontal surfaces shall be spaced not more than

clauses.text: 150 mm o.c. along the framing members when members are spaced not more than 400 mm o.c., and
100 mm o.c. along members when members are spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.

content.text: Stucco mixes shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect28.subsect5.art1.table1:long]

content.value: 3.25 to 4 parts per part of cementitious material

content.text: Pigment if used shall consist of pure mineral oxides inert to the action of sun, lime and cement.
Pigment shall not exceed 6% of the Portland cement by weight.
Materials shall be thoroughly mixed before and after water is added.
Stucco shall be applied not later than 3 h after the initial mixing.
The base for stucco shall be maintained above freezing.
Stucco shall be maintained at a temperature of not less than 10°C during application, and for not less than 48 h afterwards.

articles.title: Number of Coats and Total Thickness

content.text: Stucco shall be applied with at least 2 base coats and one finish coat, providing a total thickness of not less than 15 mm , measured from the face of the lath or the face of the masonry where no lath is used.
The first coat shall be not less than 6 mm thick, measured from the face of the lath or masonry, fully embedding the lath.
The surface of the first coat shall be scored to provide a key with the second coat.
The second coat shall be not less than 6 mm thick.
The surface of the second coat shall be lightly roughened to provide a key with the finish coat if the finish coat is other than stone dash.
When the finish coat is other than stone dash, the base shall be dampened but not saturated before the finish coat is applied.
The thickness of the finish coat shall be not less than 3 mm .
When a stone dash finish is used, the stone shall be partially embedded in the second coat before the second coat starts to set or stiffen.

A wall or ceiling finish shall also conform to the appropriate requirements in  Sections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect11:number] , in addition to the requirements in this Section.
Waterproof finish shall be provided to a height of not less than

clauses.text: 1.8 m above the floor in shower stalls,
1.2 m above the rims of bathtubs equipped with showers, and
400 mm above the rims of bathtubs not equipped with showers.

content.text: Waterproof finish shall consist of ceramic, plastic or metal tile, sheet vinyl, tempered hardboard, laminated thermosetting decorative sheets or linoleum.
Wood furring for the attachment of wall and ceiling finishes shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect3.art1.table1:long]
Furring shall be fastened to the framing or to wood blocks with not less than 51 mm nails.
Application of plaster wall and ceiling finishes, including installation of metal or gypsum lath, shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa82.30]
The requirements for application of gypsum board in this Subsection apply to the single layer application of gypsum board to wood furring or framing using nails or screws.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art1.sent3:short] , gypsum board applications not described in this Subsection shall conform to [REF:standard:csaa82.31]
The application of gypsum board to flat insulating concrete form (ICF) walls shall conform to [REF:standard:astmc840] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote182:short] .)
Gypsum products shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc1178m] or
[REF:standard:astmc1396m] except that the [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] of gypsum board shall be determined in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs102]

content.text: Maximum spacing of supports for gypsum board applied as a single layer shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art3.table1:long]

content.title: Spacing of Supports for Gypsum Board

content.value: Maximum Spacing of Supports, mm o.c.
Gypsum board conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art2.sent1:long] (except [REF:external:astmc1396m:Sections 9 and 12 of ] [REF:standard:astmc1396m] )
Gypsum ceiling board conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art2.sent1.clause2:long] (only [REF:external:astmc1396m:Section 12 of ] [REF:standard:astmc1396m] )

content.text: Gypsum board supporting insulation shall be not less than 12.7 mm thick.

The length of fasteners for gypsum board shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art5.table1:long] , except that lesser depths of penetration are permitted for assemblies required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] provided it can be shown, on the basis of fire tests, that such depths are adequate for the required rating.
Nails for fastening gypsum board to wood supports shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmf1667] or
[REF:standard:csab111]

content.text: Screws for fastening gypsum board to wood supports shall conform to [REF:standard:astmc1002]
For single-layer application on a ceiling, nails shall be spaced

clauses.text: not more than 180 mm o.c. on ceiling supports, or
every 300 mm o.c. along ceiling supports, in pairs about 50 mm apart.

content.text: Where the ceiling sheets are supported by the wall sheets around the perimeter of the ceiling, this support may be considered as equivalent to nailing at this location.
Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art8.sent4:short] , for single-layer application on walls, nails shall be spaced

clauses.text: not more than 200 mm o.c. on vertical wall supports, or
every 300 mm o.c. along vertical wall supports, in pairs about 50 mm apart.

content.text: For single-layer application on walls, where gypsum board provides required bracing in [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] , lateral support for studs, or fire protection, nails shall be spaced not more than 200 mm o.c. on

clauses.text: vertical wall supports, and
top and bottom plates.

content.text: The uppermost nails on vertical wall supports shall be not more than 200 mm below the ceiling.
Nails shall be located not less than 10 mm from the side or edge of the board.
Nails shall be driven so that the heads do not puncture the paper.
For single-layer application on a ceiling, screws shall be spaced not more than 300 mm o.c. on ceiling supports.
Where the ceiling sheets are supported by the wall sheets around the perimeter of the ceiling, this support may be considered as equivalent to screwing at this location.
Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art9.sent4:short] , for single-layer application on walls, screws shall be spaced

clauses.text: not more than 300 mm o.c. on vertical wall supports where the supports are more than 400 mm o.c. , or
not more than 400 mm o.c. on vertical wall supports where the supports are not more than 400 mm o.c.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art9.sent5:short] , for single-layer application on walls, where gypsum board provides required bracing in [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] , lateral support for studs, or fire protection, screws shall be spaced not more than 300 mm o.c. on

clauses.text: vertical wall supports, and
top and bottom plates.

content.text: Where a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] is determined based on [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.spectables1.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect5.art9.sent4:short] need not apply for the purpose of fire protection.
Screws shall be located not less than 10 mm from the edge of the board.
Screws shall be driven so that the heads do not puncture the paper.
In cold weather, heat shall be provided to maintain a temperature not below 10°C for 48 h prior to taping and finishing and maintained for not less than 48 h thereafter.

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.sent3:short] , the minimum thickness of plywood interior finish shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long]

content.value: Maximum Spacing of Supports, mm o.c.
On Supports with no Horizontal Blocking
On Supports with Blocking at Vertical Intervals not Exceeding 1.2 m

content.text: A manufacturing tolerance of −0.4 mm may be applied to the thicknesses listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long]
No minimum thickness is required where plywood is applied over continuous backing.

Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art2.sent2:short] , where plywood for interior finish is grooved, the grooves shall not extend through the face ply and into the plies below the face ply unless the groove is supported by framing or furring.

If the grain of the face ply is at right angles to the supporting members, the groove is permitted to extend into plies below the face ply provided the thickness of the plywood exceeds the value shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long] by an amount equal to not less than the depth of penetration of the grooves into the plies below the face ply.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art3.sent2:short] , nails for attaching plywood finishes shall not be less than 38 mm casing or finishing nails spaced not more than 150 mm o.c. along edge supports and 300 mm o.c. along intermediate supports, except that staples providing equivalent lateral resistance may also be used.

Where plywood finish provides required bracing in [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] , the plywood shall be fastened in accordance with the fastening requirements for sheathing stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art5.sent2:long] .
All plywood edges shall be supported by furring, blocking or framing.
Hardboard shall conform to [REF:standard:cgsb-11.3]
Hardboard shall be not less than

clauses.text: 3 mm thick where applied over continuous backing,
6 mm thick when applied over supports spaced not more than 400 mm o.c., and
9 mm thick when applied over supports spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.

content.text: Nails for fastening hardboard shall be casing or finishing nails not less than 38 mm long, spaced not more than 150 mm o.c. along edge supports and 300 mm o.c. along intermediate supports.
All hardboard edges shall be supported by furring, blocking or framing where the backing is not continuous.
Insulating fibreboard shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs706]
Insulating fibreboard sheets shall be not less than 11.1 mm thick on supports not more than 400 mm o.c.
Insulating fibreboard tile shall be not less than 12.7 mm thick on supports spaced not more than 400 mm o.c.
Nails for fastening fibreboard sheets shall be not less than 2.6 mm shank diameter casing or finishing nails of sufficient length to penetrate not less than 20 mm into the supports.
Nails shall be spaced not more than 100 mm o.c. along edge supports and 200 mm o.c. along intermediate supports.
All fibreboard edges shall be supported by blocking, furring or framing.
Particleboard finish shall conform to [REF:standard:ansia208.1]
OSB or waferboard finish shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csao325] or
[REF:standard:csao437.0]

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9.art2.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9.art2.sent3:short] , the minimum thickness of O-2 grade OSB used as an interior finish shall conform to that shown for plywood in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long]
Thicknesses listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect6.art1.table1:long] shall permit a manufacturing tolerance of −0.4 mm .
No minimum thickness is required where O-2 grade OSB is applied over continuous backing.
OSB conforming to O-1 grade, waferboard conforming to R-1 grade and particleboard shall be

clauses.text: not less than 6.35 mm thick on supports not more than 400 mm o.c. ,
not less than 9.5 mm thick on supports not more than 600 mm o.c. , and
not less than 6.35 mm thick on supports not more than 600 mm o.c. in walls where blocking is provided at midwall height.

content.text: OSB conforming to [REF:standard:csao325] shall meet the minimum panel mark of

clauses.text: W16, on supports not more than 400 mm o.c.,
W24, on supports not more than 600 mm o.c., and
W16, on supports not more than 600 mm o.c. where blocking is provided at mid-wall height.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect9.art3.sent2:short] , nails for fastening particleboard, OSB or waferboard shall be not less than 38 mm casing or finishing nails spaced not more than 150 mm o.c. along edge supports and 300 mm o.c. along intermediate supports.

Where OSB or waferboard provides required bracing in [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] , the OSB or waferboard shall be fastened in accordance with the fastening requirements for sheathing stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect3.art5.sent2:long] .
All particleboard, OSB or waferboard edges shall be supported by furring, blocking or framing.
Ceramic tile shall be set in a mortar base or applied with an adhesive.
Plastic tile shall be applied with an adhesive.
When ceramic tile is applied to a mortar base the cementitious material shall consist of one part Portland cement to not more than one-quarter part lime by volume.

The cementitious material described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect29.subsect10.art2.sent1:short] shall be mixed with not less than 3 nor more than 5 parts of aggregate per part of cementitious material by volume.
Mortar shall be applied over metal lath or masonry.
Ceramic tile applied to a mortar base shall be thoroughly soaked and pressed into place forcing the mortar into the joints while the tile is wet.

Adhesives to attach ceramic and plastic tile shall be applied to the finish coat or brown coat of plaster that has been steel-trowelled to an even surface or to gypsum board or to masonry provided the masonry has an even surface.
Ceramic and plastic tile installed on walls around bathtubs or showers shall be applied over moisture-resistant backing.
The joints between wall tiles and a bathtub shall be suitably caulked with material conforming to [REF:standard:cgsb-19.22]
Finished flooring shall be provided in all [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancies] .

Where water permeable finished flooring in bathrooms, kitchens, public entrance halls and laundry areas is supported by a subfloor of a type that would be damaged by water, such flooring shall be installed over a membrane with a water permeance not exceeding 18 ng/(Pa×s×m^{2}) when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:astme96m] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote183:short] .)
Wood sleepers supporting finished flooring over a concrete base supported on the ground shall be not less than 19 mm by 38 mm and shall be treated with a wood preservative.
Finished flooring shall have a surface that is smooth, even and free from roughness or open defects.

A panel-type underlay shall be provided under resilient flooring, parquet flooring, ceramic tile, felted-synthetic-fibre floor coverings or carpeting laid over lumber subflooring. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect30.subsect3.art2.sent1:long] .)

Panel-type underlay shall be provided under resilient flooring, parquet flooring, felted-synthetic-fibre floor coverings or carpeting on panel-type subflooring whose edges are unsupported. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art3:long] )
Panel-type underlay shall be provided under ceramic tile applied with adhesive.
Panel-type underlay shall be not less than 6 mm thick and shall conform to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:ansia208.1]
[REF:standard:cgsb-11.3]
[REF:standard:hpvahp1]
[REF:standard:csao121]
[REF:standard:csao151]
[REF:standard:csao153] or
[REF:standard:csao437.0]

content.text: Panel-type underlay under ceramic tile applied with adhesive shall be not less than

clauses.text: 6 mm thick where the supports are spaced up to 300 mm o.c., and
11 mm thick where the supports are spaced wider than 300 mm o.c.

content.text: Panel-type underlay shall be fastened to the subfloor with staples, annular grooved flooring nails or spiral nails, spaced not more than 150 mm o.c. along the edges and 200 mm o.c. both ways at other locations.
Nails for panel-type underlay shall be not less than 19 mm long for 6 mm thick underlay and 22 mm long for 7.9 mm thick underlay.
Staples for panel-type underlay shall

clauses.text: have not less than a 1.2 mm shank diameter or thickness with a 4.7 mm crown, and
be not less than

subclauses.text: 22 mm long for 6 mm underlay, and
28 mm long for 7.9 mm and 9.5 mm underlay.

content.text: Where panel-type underlay is required to be installed over plywood, OSB or waferboard, the joints in the underlay shall be offset not less than 200 mm from the joints in the underlying subfloor.
Underlay beneath resilient or ceramic floors applied with an adhesive shall have all holes or open defects on the surface patched so that the defects will not be transmitted to the finished surface.
The thickness of wood strip flooring shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect30.subsect3.art1.table1:long]
Wood strip flooring shall not be laid parallel to lumber subflooring unless a separate underlay is provided.
If wood strip flooring is applied without a subfloor, it shall be laid at right angles to the joists so that the end joints are staggered and occur over supports or are end matched.
If the flooring is end matched, it shall be laid so that no 2 adjoining strips break joints in the same space between supports and each strip bears on no fewer than 2 supports.

When nails are used, wood strip flooring shall be toe nailed or face nailed with not less than one nail per strip at the spacings shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect30.subsect3.art3.table1:long] , except that face nailed strips more than 25 mm in width shall have at least 2 nails per strip.

content.value: Minimum Length of Flooring Nails, mm
Maximum Spacing of Flooring Nails, mm

content.text: Face nails shall be countersunk.

Staples are permitted to be used to fasten wood strip flooring not more than 7.9 mm in thickness provided the staples are not less than 29 mm long with a shank diameter of 1.19 mm and with 4.7 mm crowns.
Adhesive used to attach parquet block flooring shall be suitable for bonding wood to the applicable subfloor material.
Resilient flooring used on concrete slabs supported on ground shall consist of asphalt, rubber, unbacked vinyl or vinyl with an inorganic type backing.
Flooring described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect30.subsect5.art1.sent1:short] shall be attached to the base with a suitable waterproof and alkali-resistant adhesive.
Ceramic tile shall be set in a mortar bed or applied to a sound smooth base with a suitable adhesive.
Panel-type subfloor to which ceramic tile is to be applied with adhesive shall have its edges supported according to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect15.art3:long]
This Section applies to the plumbing facilities and [REF:term:plmbng-t:plumbing systems] within [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] .

In [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancies] other than [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , plumbing facilities, grab bars, floor drains, and floor and wall finishes around urinals shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect2:long] (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8:long] regarding [REF:term:brrr-fr:accessible] plumbing facilities.)
Medical gas piping systems shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect7.subsect3:long]
Systems used for service water heating shall conform to the energy efficiency requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long]
The construction, extension, [REF:term:ltrtn:alteration] , renewal or repair of [REF:term:plmbng-t:plumbing systems] and sewage disposal systems shall conform to Part 7.
Metal pipes in contact with cinders or other corrosive material shall be protected by a heavy coating of bitumen or other corrosion protection.
When provided, grab bars shall be capable of resisting a load of not less than 1.3 kN applied vertically or horizontally.
Every [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] shall be supplied with potable water.
Where a piped water supply is available, piping for hot and cold water shall be connected to every kitchen sink, lavatory, bathtub, shower, slop sink and laundry area.
Piping for cold water shall be run to every water closet.
A kitchen sink, lavatory, bathtub or shower, and water closet shall be provided for every [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] where a piped water supply is available.
Where a piped water supply is available a hot water supply shall be provided in every [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .
Where gravity drainage to a sewer, drainage ditch or dry well is possible, a floor drain shall be installed in a [REF:term:bmnt:basement] forming part of a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .
A floor drain shall be provided in a garbage room, incinerator room or [REF:term:blr:boiler] room serving more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .
Wastes from every plumbing fixture shall be piped to the [REF:term:bldng:building] sewer.
[REF:term:bldng:Building] sewers shall discharge into a public sewage system where such system is available.
Where a public sewage system is not available, the [REF:term:bldng:building] sewer shall discharge into a [REF:term:prvt-wg-:private sewage disposal system] .
Where hot water is required to be supplied in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect31.subsect4.art2:long] , equipment shall

clauses.text: provide an adequate supply of hot water, and
be installed in conformance with Part 7.

content.text: [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:Service water heaters] shall conform to appropriate provincial or territorial requirements or, in the absence of such requirements, to Book II (Plumbing Systems) of this Code.

revisions.text: [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:Service water heaters] shall conform to appropriate provincial or territorial requirements or, in the absence of such requirements, to the [REF:standard:nrcc-npc] .
[REF:term:rvc-wtr-:Service water heaters] shall conform to appropriate provincial or territorial requirements or, in the absence of such requirements, to Book II (Plumbing Systems) of this Code.
revisions.change_summary: Struck out 'the NPC' and substituted 'Book II (Plumbing Systems) of this Code'

content.text: The installation of [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:service water heaters] , including provisions for mounting, clearances and air supply, shall conform to

clauses.text: the Safety Standards Act and pursuant regulations,
[REF:standard:csab139] Series,
reserved,
[REF:standard:csab365] , or
a combination thereof.

content.text: Where the [REF:term:bldng:building] is in a location where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than 0.37, [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:service water heaters] shall be secured to the structure to prevent overturning. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote184:short] .)
Where storage tanks for [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:service water heaters] are of steel, they shall be coated with zinc, vitreous enamel (glass lined), hydraulic cement or other corrosion-resistant material.
Fuel-burning [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:service water heaters] shall be connected to a [REF:term:chmn:chimney ] [REF:term:fl:flue] conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21:long]

Heating coils of [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:service water heaters] shall not be installed in a [REF:term:fl:flue] or in the combustion chamber of a [REF:term:blr:boiler] or [REF:term:frnc:furnace] heating a [REF:term:bldng:building] .

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art2:long] , this Section applies to the ventilation of rooms and spaces in [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancies] by natural ventilation and to self-contained mechanical ventilation systems serving only

clauses.text: one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , or
a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces.

content.text: Mechanical ventilation systems other than self-contained systems serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] or a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces shall conform to Part 6.
A [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] for more than 5 motor vehicles shall be ventilated in accordance with Part 6.
Systems used for ventilation shall conform to the energy efficiency requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long]
Every [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] shall incorporate

clauses.text: provisions for non-heating-season ventilation in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect2:long] , and

except as required by  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art2.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art2.sent3:short] , if supplied with electrical power, provisions for heating-season ventilation in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long] .

content.text: A self-contained heating-season ventilation system serving a single [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] or a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces shall comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote194:short] .)
In houses that contain a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces, heating-season ventilation need not be provided for

clauses.text: [REF:term:xt:exits] ,
[REF:term:pblc-crr:public corridors] , and
ancillary spaces that are not within a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art2.sent4:short] .

content.text: Where ancillary spaces described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art2.sent3.clause3:medium] contain exhaust devices, these spaces shall be provided with make-up air in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art1:long]
[REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] or vents connected to laundry-drying equipment shall discharge directly to the outdoors.
[REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] connected to laundry-drying equipment shall be

clauses.text: independent of other [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] ,
accessible for cleaning, and
constructed of a smooth corrosion-resistant material.

content.text: Where collective venting of multiple installations of laundry-drying equipment is used, the ventilation system shall

clauses.text: be connected to a common [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] that is vented by one central exhaust fan,
include an interlock to activate the central exhaust fan when laundry-drying equipment is in use, and
where required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art8:long] , be provided with make-up air.

content.text: Rooms or spaces in [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] shall be ventilated during the non-heating season by

clauses.text: natural ventilation in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect2.art2:long] , or
conforming to Subsection 9.32.3.

revisions.text: a mechanical ventilation system in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long]
conforming to Subsection 9.32.3.
revisions.change_summary: Struck out 'in accordance with Article' and substituted 'conforming to Subsection'

content.text: Where a habitable room or space is not provided with natural ventilation as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect2.art1.sent1.clause1:medium] , mechanical ventilation shall be provided to exhaust inside air from, or to introduce outside air to, that room or space at the rate of

clauses.text: one-half air change per hour if the room or space is mechanically cooled during the non-heating season, or
one air change per hour if the room or space is not mechanically cooled during the non-heating season.

content.text: The unobstructed openable ventilation area to the outdoors for rooms and spaces in residential [REF:term:bldng:buildings] ventilated by natural means shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect2.art2.table1:long]

content.value: Dining rooms, living rooms, bedrooms, kitchens, combined rooms, dens, recreation rooms and all other finished rooms
0.28 m^{2} per room or combination of rooms
Corridors, storage rooms and other similar public rooms or spaces
Unfinished [REF:term:bmnt:basement] space not used on a shared basis

content.text: Where a vestibule opens directly off a living or dining room within a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , ventilation to the outdoors for such rooms may be through the vestibule.
Openings for natural ventilation other than windows shall provide protection from the weather and insects.
Screening shall be of corrosion-resistant material.
Every [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] that is supplied with electrical power shall be provided by a mechanical ventilation system that conforms to

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csaf326] , "Residential Mechanical Ventilation Systems,"
this Subsection, or

for ducted mechanical ventilation systems serving more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces, the mechanical ventilation system shall comply with this Subsection or Part 6.

content.text: Aspects of mechanical ventilation systems not specifically described in this Subsection shall be designed, constructed and installed in accordance with good practice such as that described in the ASHRAE Handbooks and Standards, the [REF:standard:hraisar-g1] the HRAI Residential Mechanical Ventilation Manual, the Hydronics Institute Manuals and the SMACNA Manuals.
Exhaust fans and supply fans shall be installed in accordance with this Subsection and the manufacturer's instructions.
The mechanical components of a mechanical ventilation system shall be installed so as to be accessible for inspection, maintenance, repair, and cleaning.

In a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces, where a heating or ventilation system serves more than a single [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , the system shall be designed and installed to prevent the circulation of smoke upon a signal from a duct-type [REF:term:mk-dtctr:smoke detector] . (See Note A-9.32.3.2.(4).)

Where [REF:term:bldng:buildings] are sprinklered in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art1.sent1:medium] , the sprinkler system shall be designed, constructed, installed and tested in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect5.art12.sent1:long] , except that the maximum distance between sprinklers shall be in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art9.sent6:medium] .

revisions.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art6:medium] , ducts penetrating [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] shall be equipped with [REF:term:fr-dmpr:fire dampers] in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect8.art10:long] .

Where [REF:term:bldng:buildings] are sprinklered in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art1.sent1:medium] , the sprinkler system shall be designed, constructed, installed and tested in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect5.art12.sent1:long] , except that the maximum distance between sprinklers shall be in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art9.sent6:medium] .
revisions.change_summary: Struck out 'Sentence 9.10.9.6.(14)' and substituted 'Sentence 9.10.9.9.(6)'

content.text: A mechanical ventilation system shall include:

clauses.text: a principal ventilation fan system that

subclauses.text: provides supply air in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4:long] , and
includes an exhaust fan that conforms with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5:long] ,

clauses.text: the kitchen and bathroom exhaust fans that are required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art6:long] , and
if the [REF:term:bldng:building] includes a heated crawl space, the components that are required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7:long] .

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent6:short] , a principal ventilation system shall mechanically provide supply air in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2:short] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent3:short] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent4:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent5:short] .
Where the principal ventilation system is a ducted forced-air heating system, the ducted forced-air heating system shall

clauses.text: provide supply air through the ducting to

subclauses.text: each bedroom,
each floor level without a bedroom, and

ancillary spaces that contain an exhaust device, where the space is not within a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] and where the house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] contains a fuel-fired [REF:term:pc-htng-:space-heating appliance] or fuel-fired water-heating [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] of other than [REF:term:drct-vnt:direct-vented] or [REF:term:mchnl-vnt:mechanically vented] types,

clauses.text: draw supply air from an outdoor inlet that is connected to the cabinet containing the furnace air circulating fan required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause4:medium] by ducting that measures, from that cabinet to the point at which the ducting intersects the return air plenum,

subclauses.text: between 3 m and 4.5 m in length, or
if a flow control device is used, not more than 4.5 m in length,

clauses.text: draw supply air through ducting that is

subclauses.text: rigid ducting with an equivalent diameter of at least 100 mm, or
flexible ducting with an equivalent diameter of at least 125 mm, and

clauses.text: have a furnace air circulating fan set to run continuously.

content.text: Where the principal ventilation system is a ducted forced-air heating system used in combination with a heat-recovery ventilator,

clauses.text: the ducted forced-air heating system shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause1:medium] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause3:medium] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause4:medium] ,
the heat-recovery ventilator shall draw supply air from an outdoor inlet into the return air plenum of the ducted forced-air heating system, and
the heat-recovery ventilator shall draw exhaust air, through dedicated ducting,

subclauses.text: from one or more indoor inlets, at least one of which is located at least 2 m above the floor of the uppermost floor level, and
at the capacity rating of the heat-recovery ventilator, which shall be no less than the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.table1:long] .

content.text: Where the principal ventilation system is a ducted central-recirculation ventilation system, the ducted central-recirculation ventilation system shall

clauses.text: draw supply air from an outdoor inlet connected upstream of the fan,
draw air from

subclauses.text: each bedroom and deliver it to a common area, or
a common area and deliver it to each bedroom, and

clauses.text: deliver air to each ancillary space described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause1.subclause3:medium] .

content.text: A principal ventilation system need not conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] if the principal ventilation system

clauses.text: services a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] that

subclauses.text: is located where the January design temperature, on a 2.5% basis determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divA.sect1.subsect1.art3.sent1:long:Article 1.1.3.1.] , is greater than −20°C,
has only 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] and a [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] of less than 168 m^{2} within the [REF:term:bldng-r:building envelope] (see Note A-9.32.3.4.(6)(a)(ii)),
does not have a ducted forced-air heating system, and

except for a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] , is not located in a [REF:term:bldng:building] conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect6:long:Subsection 9.36.6.] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part2.sect2.subsect3:long:10.2.3.] , and

clauses.text: provides supply air passively from outdoors through dedicated inlets that

subclauses.text: are located in each bedroom, at least one common area and each ancillary space described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2.clause1.subclause3:medium:Subclause (2)(a)(iii)] ,
are located at least 1 800 mm above the floor, and
have an unobstructed vent area of not less than 25 cm^{2} .

content.text: A principal ventilation system exhaust fan shall

clauses.text: run continuously, and
provide at least the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.table1:long] .

content.title: Principal Ventilation System Exhaust Fan Minimum Air-flow Rate

content.text: For the purposes of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.sent1:short] , the capacity rating of the principal ventilation system exhaust fan shall be determined, based on air-flow performance at 50 pa of external static pressure, in accordance with

clauses.text: HVI Publication 916, "Airflow Test Procedure," or
CAN/CSA-C260-M, "Rating the Performance of Residential Mechanical Ventilating Equipment."

content.text: The principal ventilation system exhaust fan shall be

clauses.text: designed to run continuously, and
controlled by a dedicated switch that

subclauses.text: has 2 settings, on and off,
is located where it will be accessible for the purposes of servicing the exhaust fan but not likely to be turned off inadvertently, and
is clearly marked "PRINCIPAL VENTILATION EXHAUST FAN."

content.text: If the principal ventilation system exhaust fan is designed to run at multiple air-flow rates,

clauses.text: the air-flow rate of the fan shall be controlled by a switch other than the switch described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.sent3.clause2:medium] , and
the lowest air-flow rate shall not be less than the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.table1:long] .

content.text: The sound rating of the principal ventilation system exhaust fan shall not exceed 1.0 sone when running continuously at the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5.table1:long] as determined in accordance with

clauses.text: HVI Publication 915, "Loudness Testing and Rating Procedure," or
CAN/CSA-C260-M, "Rating the Performance of Residential Mechanical Ventilating Equipment."

content.text: An exhaust fan that provides at least the air-flow rate specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art6.table1:long] shall be installed in

clauses.text: every kitchen, and

every bathroom or water-closet room, unless the bathroom or water-closet room is served by the principal ventilation system exhaust fan that complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art5:long] .

content.text: For the purposes of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] , the capacity rating of the exhaust fan shall be determined, based on air-flow performance at 50 pa of external static pressure, in accordance with

clauses.text: HVI Publication 916, "Airflow Test Procedure," or
CAN/CSA-C260-M, "Rating the Performance of Residential Mechanical Ventilating Equipment."

content.title: Kitchen/Bathroom Exhaust Fan Minimum Air-flow Rate

content.value: Minimum Exhaust Fan Air-flow Rate, L/s

content.text: Where a crawl space is heated by a ducted forced-air heating system that does not draw air from the crawl space to the furnace through the return air plenum, the crawl space shall be connected to the floor space above the crawl space by at least one air-transfer grille.
Where a crawl space is heated other than by a ducted forced-air heating system, the crawl space shall

clauses.text: be connected to

subclauses.text: the floor space above the crawl space by at least one air-transfer grille, and
the principal ventilation system by a supply air outlet or an exhaust air inlet,

clauses.text: be connected to the floor space above the crawl space by at least 2 air-transfer grilles for every 30 m^{2} of crawl space area, or
be connected to

subclauses.text: the floor space above the crawl space by at least one air-transfer grille, and
the outdoors by a dedicated exhaust fan that complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent4:short] .

content.text: An air-transfer grille required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent1:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent2:short] shall have an unobstructed vent area of the greater of

clauses.text: 25 cm^{2} , and
0.83 cm^{2} for every m^{2} of crawl space area.

content.text: Where a dedicated exhaust fan is installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent2.clause3.subclause2:medium] , the dedicated exhaust fan shall

clauses.text: provide an air-flow rate of at least 23 L/s, and
be controlled by

subclauses.text: a humidity control device, or
an adjustable time control device that is capable of providing not less than 8 total hours of ventilation per 24 hour period.

content.text: Where a crawl space is divided into 2 or more compartments, each heated compartment shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent1:short] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art7.sent2:short] .

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art8.sent3:short] , this Article applies to air ducts other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect1.art3:long] .
[REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] shall discharge to the outdoors.
[REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] that are downstream of an exhaust fan shall have no connections to other fans or ducts.
[REF:term:xht-dct:Exhaust ducts] , and [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply ducts] that conduct heated or cooled air, shall

clauses.text: be sized in accordance with the requirements of the manufacturer of the fans to which they are connected, and
have an equivalent diameter not less than that specified by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art8.table1:long] .

table_notes.content: The equivalent length of a duct is the length of the duct plus 10 m for the exterior hood and 3 m for each 90° elbow.
