content.text: Where an [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust duct] passes through or is located adjacent to a space that is not [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] , the duct shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2:long] , except that in no case shall such a duct be insulated to less than RSI 0.75.
Where a principal ventilation system [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply duct] passes through or is located adjacent to a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] , the duct shall be

clauses.text: insulated to not less than RSI 0.75, and
provided with an effective vapour barrier.

content.text: Where a kitchen exhaust fan grille is installed within 1.2 m horizontally of a [REF:term:cktp:cooktop] , the exhaust fan duct shall

clauses.text: be constructed of a material that is noncombustible, corrosion-resistant, and cleanable, and
be equipped with a grease filter at the intake end.

content.text: Except for a supply air system described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent2:medium] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art4.sent3:medium] , all joints in [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] , and in [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply ducts] that conduct conditioned air, shall be sealed against air leakage with

clauses.text: sealants or gaskets made from liquids, mastics or heat-applied materials,
mastic with embedded fabric,
foil-faced butyl tape, or
aluminum foil tape.

content.text: [REF:term:ppl-dct:Supply ducts] for a mechanical ventilation system shall not be used to provide combustion or dilution air to fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] .
Outdoor air inlets and exhaust outlets shall be shielded from the weather, birds and rodents by using hoods incorporating a screen of corrosion-resistant material with openings of 6 to 12 mm.

Interior doors shall be undercut by a minimum of 12 mm above the finished floor or the rooms shall be provided with an air-transfer grille with an unobstructed vent area that is not less than 100 cm^{2} .

Additional make-up air for the actual [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] exhaust rate shall be provided for any [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] that discharges air to the exterior at an installed rate exceeding 0.5 air changes per hour when it is located within a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] or house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] that contains a vented [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] that is subject to back drafting (Naturally Aspirating Fuel Fired Vented Appliance). (See Note A-9.32.4.1.)

Where additional make-up air is required for [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art1.sent1:short] , it shall be provided by a supply fan rated to deliver outdoor air at the rate of the installed exhaust [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] .
The supply fan as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art1.sent2:short] shall be interconnected with the exhaust fan for which make-up air is required.
The outdoor air required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect4.art1.sent3:short] shall be

clauses.text: tempered to at least 1°C before being introduced to a normally unoccupied area of the [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] or house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces, or
tempered to at least 12°C before being introduced to occupied areas either by passive transfer grille or directly from outside.

content.text: This Article applies to every [REF:term:bldng:building] that contains a [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] , a business and personal services occupancy, or a mercantile occupancy and that

clauses.text: is served by or contains a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] , or
contains a [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] .

content.text: Carbon monoxide (CO) alarms installed in a residential occupancy required by this Article shall

clauses.text: conform to [REF:standard:csa6.19] ,
be equipped with an integral alarm that satisfies the audibility requirements of [REF:standard:csa6.19] ,
have no disconnect switch between the overcurrent device and the CO alarm, where the CO alarm is powered by the [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] 's electrical system, and
be installed as recommended by the manufacturer.

content.text: Where a room in a residential occupancy contains a solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] , a CO alarm conforming to [REF:standard:csa6.19] shall be

clauses.text: installed as recommended by the manufacturer where these instructions specifically mention solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] , or
in the absence of specific instructions related to solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] , on or near the ceiling.

content.text: Where a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] is installed in a [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] , a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: inside each bedroom, or
outside each bedroom, within 5 m of each bedroom door, measured following corridors and doorways.

content.text: Where a fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] serves a residential occupancy and is installed in a [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] that is not in a [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] , a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: either inside each bedroom, or if outside, within 5 m of each bedroom door, measured following corridors and doorways, in every [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with the [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] , and
in the [REF:term:rvc-rm:service room] .

content.text: For each [REF:term:t:suite] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with a [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] or that is adjacent to an attic or crawl space to which the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] is also adjacent, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: inside each bedroom, or
outside each bedroom, within 5 m of each bedroom door, measured following corridors and doorways.

content.text: Where CO alarms are installed in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces, the CO alarms shall be interconnected so that the actuation of any one CO alarm causes all CO alarms within the house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces to sound.
CO alarms installed in a business and personal services occupancy, or a mercantile occupancy as required by this Article shall conform to

clauses.text: CAN/CSA-6.19, "Residential carbon monoxide alarming devices," notwithstanding the scope of that standard,
UL 2034, "Standard for Single and Multiple Station Carbon Monoxide Alarms," notwithstanding the scope of that standard, or
good engineering practice.

content.text: Where a fuel-burning appliance serves a business and personal services occupancy, or mercantile occupancy, a CO alarm shall be,

clauses.text: where the fuel-burning appliance is part of a system that could circulate or distribute CO to a suite of business and personal services occupancy or mercantile occupancy, installed on each storey of each suite that may be exposed, and
installed in the room or space in which the fuel-burning appliance is located.

content.text: For each suite of business and personal services occupancy or mercantile occupancy that shares a wall or floor/ceiling assembly with either a storage garage, or a service room containing a fuel-burning appliance, or that is adjacent to an attic or crawl space to which either a storage garage, or a service room containing a fuel-burning appliance is also adjacent, a CO alarm shall be installed

clauses.text: on each storey of the adjacent suite, and
in each service room containing a fuel-burning appliance.

content.text: This Section applies to the design and installation of

clauses.text: heating systems, including requirements for combustion air, and air-conditioning systems serving only one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] or houses with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces, and
reserved.

content.text: The design and installation of heating systems, including requirements for combustion air, and air-conditioning systems other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect1.art1.sent1:short] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6:long:Part 6] . (See [REF:internal:en000354:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect10:long:Subsection 9.10.10.] )

Unless the air duct distribution systems serving one of the [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] are designed and installed to prevent the circulation of smoke in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art2.sent4:long] and equipped with fire dampers in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art2.sent5:long] , the air duct distribution system shall not be directly interconnected with other parts of the house.
Systems used for heating and air-conditioning shall conform to the energy efficiency requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36:long]
Residential [REF:term:bldng:buildings] intended for use in the winter months on a continuing basis shall be equipped with heating facilities conforming to this Section.

Except where determination according to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art1:long] or good engineering practice according to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6.sect2.subsect1.art1:long] can show it to be unnecessary, [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] intended for use in the summer months on a continuing basis shall be equipped with cooling facilities conforming to this Section. (See [REF:internal:en001271:short] )
At the outside winter design temperature, required heating facilities shall be capable of maintaining an indoor air temperature of not less than

clauses.text: 22°C in all living spaces,
18°C in unfinished [REF:term:bmnt:basements] ,
18°C in common [REF:term:rvc-rm:service rooms] , ancillary spaces and [REF:term:xt:exits] in houses with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] , and
15°C in heated crawl spaces.

content.text: At the outside summer design temperature, required cooling facilities shall be capable of maintaining an indoor air temperature of not more than 26°C in at least one living space in each [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .
The outdoor conditions to be used in designing heating and air-conditioning systems shall be determined in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.sect1.subsect3.art1:long]

subsections.title: General Requirements for Heating and Air-conditioning Systems

articles.title: Design of Heating and Air-conditioning Systems

content.text: Aspects of heating and air-conditioning systems not specifically addressed in this Subsection, including ducting, and mechanical heating and refrigeration equipment, shall be designed, constructed and installed in accordance with good practice such as that described in the ASHRAE Handbooks and Standards, the [REF:standard:hraisar-g1] the CHC Handbook on Hydronic Heating Systems, the Hydronics Institute Manuals, the SMACNA Manuals and the TECA Quality First Manuals. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3:long] for the design of systems that also provide ventilation.)
The installation of a hydronic heating system shall conform to [REF:standard:csab214] .

Where a single heating system serves a house with a [REF:term:scnd-t:secondary suite] , individual temperature controls shall be provided in each [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] served by the system. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote204:short] .)

Equipment forming part of a heating or air-conditioning system, with the exception of embedded pipes or ducts, shall be installed with provision for access for inspection, maintenance, repair and cleaning.

Where a heating or air-conditioning system serves more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] in a house with a [REF:term:bc-scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces, access required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect4.art4.sent1:short] from more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , common space or ancillary space is not required.
Equipment forming part of a heating or air-conditioning system that may be adversely affected by freezing temperatures and that is located in an unheated area shall be protected from freezing.

Heating and cooling systems shall be designed to allow for expansion and contraction of the heat transfer fluid and to maintain the system pressure within the rated working pressure limits of all components of the system.
Mechanical systems and equipment shall be designed and installed to accommodate the maximum amount of structural movement provided for in the construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] .

Where the [REF:term:bldng:building] is in a location where the seismic design parameter, S_{max}, for Site Class C is greater than 0.37, heating and air-conditioning equipment with fuel or power connections shall be secured to the structure to resist overturning and displacement. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote184:long] .)
Asbestos shall not be used in air distribution systems or equipment.

Systems serving garages, and systems serving other occupied parts of a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] but located in or running through a garage, shall be designed and constructed in a manner such that means are not provided for the transfer of contaminants from the garage into other spaces in the [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .

content.text: Fireplaces shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect22:long]
The design, construction and installation of air duct distribution systems serving heating systems in which the rated heat input does not exceed 120 kW shall conform to this Subsection.
Air duct distribution systems in which the rated heat input exceeds 120 kW shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part6:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect5:long]

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent6:short] and in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3:long] , all ducts, duct connectors, associated fittings and [REF:term:plnm:plenums] used in air duct systems shall be constructed of steel, aluminum alloy, copper, clay or similar [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material.
Ducts, associated fittings and [REF:term:plnm:plenums] are permitted to contain [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material provided they

clauses.text: conform to the appropriate requirements for Class 1 duct materials in [REF:standard:ulcs110]
conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art18:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9:long] ,
are not used in vertical runs serving more than 2 [REF:term:tr:storeys] , and
are not used in air duct systems in which the air temperature may exceed 120°C .

content.text: Duct sealants shall have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] of not more than 25 and a smoke developed classification of not more than 50.
Duct connectors that contain [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] materials and that are used between ducts and air outlet units shall

clauses.text: conform to the appropriate requirements for Class 1 air duct materials in [REF:standard:ulcs110]
be limited to 4 m in length,
be used only in horizontal runs, and
not penetrate required [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] .

content.text: [REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] ducts that are part of a duct system carrying only ventilation air and that are contained entirely within a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] need not comply with the requirements of  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent4:short] .

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art13.sent2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art13.sent3:short] , ducts that are part of a return-air duct system and that are contained entirely within a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] need not comply with the requirements of  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent4:short] .

Materials referred to in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art2.sent6:short] , when used in a location where they may be subjected to excessive moisture, shall

clauses.text: have no appreciable loss of strength when wet, and

content.text: Tape used for sealing duct joints in air ducts, [REF:term:plnm:plenums] and other parts of air duct systems shall meet the flame-resistance requirements for fabric in [REF:standard:ulcs109] , "Standard Method for Flame Tests of Flame-Resistant Fabrics and Films."

Coverings, linings and associated adhesives and insulation of air ducts, [REF:term:plnm:plenums] and other parts of air duct systems shall be of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material when exposed to heated air or radiation from heat sources that would result in the exposed surface exceeding a temperature of 120°C .

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent3:short] , when [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] coverings and linings, including associated adhesives and insulation, are used, they shall have

clauses.text: a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] of not more than 25 on any exposed surface, or any surface that would be exposed by cutting through the material in any direction, and
a smoke developed classification of not more than 50.

content.text: The outer covering of ducts, [REF:term:plnm:plenums] and other parts of air duct systems used within an assembly of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] are permitted to have

clauses.text: an exposed surface [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] of not more than 75, and
a smoke developed classification greater than 50.

content.text: [REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible ] coverings, linings and foamed plastic insulation described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent2:short] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent6:short] shall not flame, glow, smoulder or smoke when tested in accordance with the method of test in [REF:standard:astmc411] , "Standard Specification for Hot-Surface Performance of High-Temperature Thermal Insulation," at the maximum temperature to which they are to be exposed in service.

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art4.sent7:short] , foamed plastic insulation shall not be used as part of an air duct.

clauses.text: the foamed plastic insulation applied to supply ductwork is not less than 3 m from the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] bonnet,
the temperature within the ductwork where the insulation is installed is not greater than 50°C ,

content.text: Foamed plastic insulation is permitted to be used in a ceiling space that acts as a return air [REF:term:plnm:plenum] provided the foamed plastic insulation is protected from exposure to the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art14.sent4:long] .
[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] coverings and linings of ducts, including associated adhesives and insulation, shall be interrupted

clauses.text: at the immediate area of operation of heat sources in a duct system, such as electric resistance heaters or fuel-burning heaters or [REF:term:frnc:furnaces] , and
where the duct penetrates a [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] .

content.text: Linings of ducts shall be installed so that they will not interfere with the operation of volume or balancing dampers or of [REF:term:fr-dmpr:fire dampers] , [REF:term:fr-tp-fl:fire stop flaps] and other closures.

articles.title: Galvanized Steel or Aluminum Supply Ducts

content.text: Galvanized steel or aluminum [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply ducts] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art5.table1:long]

The design of fittings for ducts shall conform to [REF:standard:smacna006] , "HVAC Duct Construction Standards -- Metal and Flexible," except that metal thicknesses shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art5.table1:long]

content.value: Rectangular, not enclosed, for single [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , with required clearance up to 12 mm
Rectangular, not enclosed, with required clearance of more than 12 mm

content.text: Where the installation of heating [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply ducts] in walls and floors creates a space between the duct and construction material, the space shall be firestopped with [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material at each end.
Ducts shall be securely supported by metal hangers, straps, lugs or brackets, except that, where zero clearance is permitted, wooden brackets are permitted to be used.
All round duct joints shall be tight-fitting and lapped not less than 25 mm .
Rectangular duct connections shall be made with S and drive cleats or equivalent mechanical connections.
Duct systems shall have no openings other than those required for the proper operation and maintenance of the system.
Air duct systems serving garages shall not be interconnected with other parts of the [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .
Trunk [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply ducts] shall not be nailed directly to wood members.
Branch ducts shall be supported at suitable spacings to maintain alignment and prevent sagging.
Ducts passing through unheated spaces shall have all joints taped or otherwise sealed to ensure that the ducts are airtight throughout their length.

[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] ducts in concrete slabs-on-ground that are connected to a [REF:term:frnc:furnace] supply [REF:term:plnm:plenum] shall be located not closer than 600 mm to that [REF:term:plnm:plenum] and not less than 600 mm from its connection to a riser or register.
Ducts in or beneath concrete slabs-on-ground shall be watertight and corrosion-, decay-, and mildew-resistant.
Underground ducts shall

clauses.text: be constructed to provide interior drainage from and access to all low points, and
not be connected directly to a sewer.

content.text: The clearance of [REF:term:frnc:furnace]  [REF:term:plnm:plenums] from [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material shall conform to the appropriate standards in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2.sent1:long] .

Where the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] clearance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent1:short] is 75 mm or less, the clearance between a [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply duct] and [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material shall

clauses.text: be equal to the required [REF:term:plnm:plenum] clearance within 450 mm of the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , and

be not less than 12 mm at a distance of 450 mm or more from the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , except that this clearance may be reduced to zero beyond a bend or offset in the duct sufficiently large to shield the remainder of the [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply duct] from direct radiation from the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] heat exchanger. (See Note A-3.6.5.6.(2).)

content.text: Where the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] clearance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent1:short] is more than 75 mm but not more than 150 mm , the clearance between a [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply duct] and [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material shall be

clauses.text: equal to the required [REF:term:plnm:plenum] clearance within a horizontal distance of 1.8 m of the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , and

not less than 12 mm at a horizontal distance of 1.8 m or more from the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , except that this distance may be reduced to zero beyond a bend or offset in the duct sufficiently large to shield the remainder of the duct from direct radiation from the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] heat exchanger. (See Note A-3.6.5.6.(3).)

content.text: Where the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] clearance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent1:short] is more than 150 mm , the clearance between a [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply duct] and [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material shall be

clauses.text: equal to the required [REF:term:plnm:plenum] clearance within a horizontal distance of 1 m of the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] ,
not less than 150 mm within a horizontal distance between 1 m and 1.8 m from the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , and

not less than 25 mm at a horizontal distance of 1.8 m or more from the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , except that this distance may be reduced to 8 mm beyond a bend or offset in the duct sufficiently large to shield the remainder of the [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply duct] from direct radiation from the [REF:term:frnc:furnace ] heat exchanger. (See Note A-3.6.5.6.(4).)

content.text: Where a register is installed in a floor directly over a pipeless [REF:term:frnc:furnace] , a double-walled register box with not less than 100 mm between walls, or a register box with the warm-air passage completely surrounded by the cold-air passage, shall be permitted in lieu of the clearances listed in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art8.sent4:short] .

All branch [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply ducts] that are not fitted with diffusers with adjustable balance stops shall be supplied with adjustable dampers and fitted with devices to indicate the positions of the dampers.

articles.title: Warm-Air Supply Outlets and Return Inlets --- General

content.text: Supply outlets and return openings in the [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , when located less than 2 m above the floor, shall be protected by grilles having openings of a size that will not allow the passage of a 15 mm diam sphere.
[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible] grilles, diffusers and other devices for the supply and return air openings installed in walls and ceilings shall have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] of

clauses.text: not more than 200 in bathrooms, and
not more than 150 in rooms or spaces other than bathrooms.

content.text: In a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , a warm-air supply outlet shall be provided in each finished room that is located adjacent to unheated space.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art11.sent3:short] , when a room described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect6.art11.sent1:short] is located adjacent to exterior walls, such outlet shall be located so as to bathe at least one exterior wall or window with warm air, except in bathrooms, utility rooms or kitchens, where this may not be practical.

Where the heating system is also designed to provide ventilation air, ceiling outlets or outlets located high on interior walls are permitted to be installed, provided the outlets are designed for this purpose and are installed with diffusers.

At least one warm-air supply outlet shall be provided for each 40 m^{2} of floor surface area in unfinished [REF:term:bmnt:basements] serving [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , and it shall be located so as to provide adequate distribution of warm air throughout the [REF:term:bmnt:basement] .

At least one warm-air supply outlet shall be provided for each 80 m^{2} of floor surface area in heated crawl spaces serving [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , and it shall be located so as to provide adequate distribution of warm air throughout the crawl space.

Except for pipeless [REF:term:frnc:furnaces] , the capacity of warm-air supply outlets serving [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] shall be not less than the design heat loss from the area served and shall not exceed 3 kW per outlet.

In [REF:term:bmnt:basements] and heated crawl spaces, the calculated heat gain from the [REF:term:ppl-dct:supply ducts] and [REF:term:plnm:plenum] surfaces is permitted to be considered in calculating the design heat loss.
The temperature of supply air at warm-air supply outlets shall not exceed 70°C .
Warm-air supply outlets located in finished areas shall be provided with diffusers and adjustable openings and shall not be located on a [REF:term:frnc:furnace]  [REF:term:plnm:plenum] .
Return-air inlets shall not be installed in an enclosed room or crawl space that provides combustion air to a [REF:term:frnc:furnace] .

Except for unfinished areas and floor levels which are less than 900 mm above or below an adjacent floor level which is provided with a return-air inlet, at least one return-air inlet shall be provided in each floor level in a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .
Provision shall be made for the return of air from all rooms by leaving gaps beneath doors, using louvred doors or installing [REF:term:rtrn-dct:return duct] inlets.
The return-air system shall be designed to handle the entire air supply.

Where any part of a [REF:term:rtrn-dct:return duct] will be exposed to radiation from the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] heat exchanger or other radiating part within the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] , such part of a [REF:term:rtrn-dct:return duct] directly above or within 600 mm of the outside [REF:term:frnc:furnace] casing shall be [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] .
[REF:term:rtrn-dct:Return ducts] serving solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:frnc:furnaces] shall be constructed of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material.
[REF:term:cmbtbl:Combustible]  [REF:term:rtrn-dct:return ducts] shall be lined with [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material

clauses.text: below floor registers,
at the bottom of vertical ducts, and
under [REF:term:frnc:furnaces] having a bottom return.

content.text: Spaces between studs or joists used as [REF:term:rtrn-dct:return ducts] shall be separated from the unused portions of such spaces by tight-fitting metal stops or wood blocking.
A vertical [REF:term:rtrn-dct:return duct] shall have openings to return air on not more than one floor.
The return-air system shall be designed so that the negative pressure from the circulating fan cannot

clauses.text: affect the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] combustion air supply, nor
draw combustion products from joints or openings in the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] or [REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipe] .

content.text: Air filters for air duct systems shall conform to the requirements for Class 2 air filter units as described in [REF:standard:ulcs111]

When electrostatic-type filters are used, they shall be installed so as to ensure that the electric circuit is automatically de-energized when filter access doors are opened or, in [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , when the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] circulation fan is not operating.
When odour removal equipment of the adsorption type is used it shall be

clauses.text: installed to provide access so that adsorption material can be reactivated or renewed, and
protected from dust accumulation by air filters installed on the inlet side.

content.text: Every steam or hot water radiator and convector located in a recess or concealed space or attached to the face of a wall of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] shall be provided with a [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] lining or backing.
The exposed surface temperature of a steam or hot water radiator shall not exceed 70°C unless precautions are taken to prevent human contact.

subsections.title: Piping for Heating and Cooling Systems

content.text: Piping shall be made from materials designed to withstand the effects of temperatures and pressures that may occur in the system. (See  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art19:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect9.art1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art7:long] , and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect10.subsect9.art9.sent3:long] for fire safety requirements.)
Every pipe used in a heating or air-conditioning system shall be installed to allow for expansion and contraction due to temperature changes.
Supports and anchors for piping in a heating or air-conditioning system shall be designed and installed to ensure that undue stress is not placed on the supporting structure.
Insulation and coverings on pipes shall be composed of material suitable for the operating temperature of the system to withstand deterioration from softening, melting, mildew and mould.
Insulation and coverings on pipes in which the temperature of the fluid exceeds 120°C

clauses.text: shall be made of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material, or

shall not flame, glow, smoulder or smoke when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:astmc411] , "Standard Specification for Hot-Surface Performance of High-Temperature Thermal Insulation," at the maximum temperature to which such insulation or covering is to be exposed in service.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8.art2.sent6:short] , where [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation is used on piping in a horizontal or [REF:term:vrtcl-rv:vertical service space] , the insulation and coverings on such pipes shall have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] throughout the material of not more than

clauses.text: 25 in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible construction] , and
75 in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] .

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8.art2.sent6:short] , insulation and coverings on piping located in rooms and spaces other than the [REF:term:rvc-pc:service spaces] described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8.art2.sent3:short] shall have a [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] not more than that required for the interior finish for the ceiling of the room or space.
Pipes that are exposed to human contact shall be insulated so that the exposed surface does not exceed 70°C . (See Note A-6.5.1.1.(3).)

No [REF:term:flm-prd-:flame-spread rating] or smoke developed classification limitations are required where [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation and coverings are used on piping when such piping is

clauses.text: located within a concealed space in a wall,
located in a floor slab, or
enclosed in a [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] raceway or conduit.

content.text: Clearances between [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] material and bare pipes carrying steam or hot water shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8.art3.table1:long]

content.title: Clearance between Steam or Hot Water Pipes and Combustible Material

content.text: Where a pipe carrying steam or hot water at a temperature above 120°C passes through a [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] floor, ceiling or wall, the construction shall be protected by a sleeve of metal or other [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] material not less than 50 mm larger in diameter than the pipe.

Unprotected steam or hot water pipes that pass through a storage space shall be covered with not less than 25 mm thickness of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] insulation to prevent direct contact with the material stored.

subsections.title: Refrigerating Systems and Equipment for Air-conditioning

content.text: Where a cooling unit is combined with a fuel-fired [REF:term:frnc:furnace] in the same duct system, the cooling unit shall be installed

clauses.text: in parallel with the heating [REF:term:frnc:furnace] ,
upstream of the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] , provided the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] is designed for such application, or
downstream of the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] , provided the cooling unit is designed to prevent excessive temperature or pressure in the refrigeration system.

content.text: Except as provided in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect10.art2:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect10.art3:long] , the products of combustion from oil-, gas- and solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] , including [REF:term:tv:stoves] , [REF:term:cktp:cooktops] , ovens and [REF:term:pc-htr:space heaters] , shall be vented in conformance with the applicable [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] installation standard listed in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art2.sent1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art3.sent1:long] .

[REF:term:fctr-blt:Factory-built chimneys] serving solid-fuel-burning [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] , and their installation, shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs629] , "Standard for 650°C Factory-Built Chimneys." (See Note A-9.33.10.2.(1).)
[REF:term:mnr-r-cn:Masonry or concrete chimneys] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect21:long]

Electrical installations, including the service capacity of the installation and the number and distribution of circuits and receptacles, shall meet the requirements of the appropriate provincial, territorial or municipal legislation or, in the absence of such legislation, shall conform to the Safety Standards Act and pursuant regulations
Where electrical services are available, electrical facilities shall be provided for every [REF:term:bldng:building] in conformance with this Section.

articles.title: Location of Equipment in Public Areas

content.text: Entrance switches, meters, panel boxes, splitter boxes, time clocks and other similar equipment shall not be located in any public area unless adequate precautions are taken to prevent interference with the equipment.
Recessed lighting fixtures shall not be located in insulated ceilings unless the fixtures are designed for such installations.

Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect1.art5.sent2:short] , optical fibre cables and electrical wires and cables installed in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] permitted to be of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] shall

clauses.text: not convey flame or continue to burn for more than 1 min when tested in conformance with the Vertical Flame Test (FT1 rating) in [REF:standard:csac22.2no.0.3] or
be located in

subclauses.text: totally enclosed [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] raceways (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote10:long] ),
masonry walls,
concrete slabs, or
totally enclosed non-metallic raceways conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect5.art23.sent1.clause2:long] .

content.text: Except as permitted in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect1.art5.sent3:short] , where a concealed space in a floor or ceiling assembly is used as a [REF:term:plnm:plenum] , electrical wires and cables with [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] insulation, jackets or sheathes that are used for the transmission of voice, sound or data and optical fibre cables installed within the [REF:term:plnm:plenum] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect6.subsect4.art3.sent1.clause1:long] .

Wires or cables within [REF:term:plnm:plenum] spaces that are used for the transmission of signals in fire alarm, security, radio, and television broadcasting, closed circuit television or community television systems need not meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect1.art5.sent2:short] .

An exterior lighting outlet with fixture controlled by a wall switch located within the [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be provided at every entrance to [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] .

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art2.sent2:short] , a lighting outlet with fixture controlled by a wall switch shall be provided in kitchens, bedrooms, living rooms, utility rooms, laundry rooms, dining rooms, bathrooms, water-closet rooms, vestibules and hallways in [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] .

Where a receptacle controlled by a wall switch is provided in bedrooms or living rooms, such rooms need not conform to the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] .
Every stairway shall be lighted.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art3.sent3:short] , 3-way wall switches located at the head and foot of every stairway shall be provided to control at least one lighting outlet with fixture for stairways with 4 or more risers in [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] and houses with a [REF:term:scnd-t:secondary suite] including their common spaces.

The stairway lighting for [REF:term:bmnt:basements] that do not contain finished space or lead to an outside entrance or built-in garage and which serve not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] is permitted to be controlled by a single switch located at the head of the stairs.
A lighting outlet with fixture shall be provided for each 30 m^{2} or fraction thereof of [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] in unfinished [REF:term:bmnt:basements] .
The outlet required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art4.sent1:short] nearest the stairs shall be controlled by a wall switch located at the head of the stairs.
A lighting outlet with fixture shall be provided in storage rooms.
A lighting outlet with fixture shall be provided for an attached, built-in or detached garage or carport.

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art6.sent3:short] , outlets required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art6.sent1:short] shall be controlled by a wall switch near the doorway.

Where the outlet and fixture required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art6.sent1:short] are ceiling mounted above an area not normally occupied by a parked car, or are wall mounted, a fixture with a built-in switch accessible to an adult of average height is permitted to be used.
Where a carport is lighted by a light at the entrance to a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , additional carport lighting is not required.
Every public or service area in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] shall be provided with lighting outlets with fixtures controlled by a wall switch or panel to illuminate every portion of such areas.

When provided by incandescent lighting, illumination required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect12.art2:long] for lighting in [REF:term:mn-f-gr:means of egress] .)
When other types of lighting are used, illumination equivalent to that shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.table1:long] shall be provided.

Notwithstanding [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect34.subsect2.art7.sent3:short] , rooms and spaces used by the public shall be equipped to provide illumination as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect7.art1.sent4:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect7.art1.sent7:short] .

content.value: Minimum Lighting Power Density, W/m^{2} of [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] (incandescent lighting)
Rooms for storage of combustible refuse

content.text: Emergency lighting shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect9.subsect12:long]
This Section applies to garages and carports serving not more than one [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] .
The construction of a garage or carport shall conform to the requirements for other [REF:term:bldng:buildings] in this Part except as provided in this Section.
Where a roofed enclosure used for the storage or parking of motor vehicles has more than 60% of the total perimeter enclosed by walls, doors or windows, the enclosure shall be considered a garage.

Where an attached or built-in garage is provided and where adjacent spaces in the [REF:term:bldng:building] are less than 50 mm above the garage floor,
(See Note A-9.35.2.2.(1).)

clauses.text: the garage floor shall be sloped to the outdoors, or

where the garage can accommodate not more than 3 vehicles , an airtight curb or [REF:term:prttn:partition] not less than 50 mm high shall be installed at the edges of the garage floor adjacent to interior space.

content.text: Except as permitted in this Subsection, [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] conforming to  Sections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect15:long] shall be provided for the support of carport and garage super-structures, including that portion beneath garage doors.

Detached garages of less than 55 m^{2}[REF:term:flr-r:floor area] and not more than 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] in height that are not of masonry or masonry veneer construction are permitted to be supported on

clauses.text: wood mud sills, or
a 100 mm thick concrete floor slab.

articles.title: Protection from Damage due to Soil Movement

content.text: In clay-type [REF:term:l:soils] subject to significant movement with a change in [REF:term:l:soil] moisture content, the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] depth of carports or garages connected to a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] directly or by a breezeway shall be approximately the same depth as the main [REF:term:bldng:building]  [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] .
Where slab-on-ground construction is used, a construction joint shall be provided between the main [REF:term:bldng:building] slab and a slab serving an attached garage, breezeway or carport.
Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect12:long] , [REF:term:fndtn:foundations] for attached unheated garages or carports shall be below frost level.

Detached garages of less than 55 m^{2}[REF:term:flr-r:floor area] and not more than 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] in height that are not of masonry or masonry veneer construction need not conform with the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] drainage requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect14:long] , where the finished ground level is at or near the elevation of the garage's floor and where the ground slopes away from the [REF:term:bldng:building] .
Piers for the support of carport columns shall extend not less than 150 mm above ground level.

Piers referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect35.subsect3.art4.sent1:short] shall project not less than 25 mm beyond the base of the column but in no case be less than 190 mm by 190 mm in size.
Interior finish need not be applied to garage and carport walls.
Columns for garages and carports shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect17:long] , except that 89 mm by 89 mm wood columns may be used.

Garage or carport walls and columns shall be anchored to the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] to resist wind uplift in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect23.subsect6:long] , except that where a garage is supported on the surface of the ground, ground anchors shall be provided to resist wind uplift.
This Section is concerned with the energy used by [REF:term:bldng:buildings] as a result of

clauses.text: the design and construction of the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope, and
the design and construction or specification of systems and equipment for

subclauses.text: heating, ventilating or air-conditioning, and
service water heating.

content.text: For the purpose of this Section, the term “common space” shall mean all spaces required to be [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned spaces] in accordance with the requirements of the Code that are not within a [REF:term:t:suite] but shall not include crawl spaces and [REF:term:vrtcl-rv:vertical service spaces] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote216:long] .)

For the purpose of this Section, the term “overall thermal transmittance,” or U-value, shall mean the rate, in W/(m^{2}×K) , at which heat is transferred through a [REF:term:bldng:building] assembly that is subject to temperature differences. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote211:short] .)

For the purpose of this Section, the term “effective thermal resistance,” or RSI value, shall mean the inverse of the overall thermal transmittance of an assembly, in (m^{2}×K)/W . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote212:short] .)

For the purpose of this Section, the term “fenestration” shall mean all [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assemblies, including their frames, that transfer visible light, such as windows, clerestories, skylights, translucent wall panels, glass block assemblies, transoms, sidelights, sliding, overhead or swinging glass doors, and glazed inserts in doors, etc. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote213:short] .)

For the purpose of this Section, the term "annual energy consumption" shall mean the annual sum of service water heating and space-conditioning energy consumption of the proposed house design, calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect6.art5:medium] , as applicable. Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art1.sent2:short] , this Subsection is concerned with the loss of energy due to heat transfer and air leakage through materials, components and assemblies, including their interfaces, forming part of the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope where it separates [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from unconditioned space, the exterior air or the ground.

The requirements of this Subsection also apply to components of a [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assembly that separate a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from an adjoining [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] , even if the [REF:term:trg-grg:storage garage] is intended to be heated. articles.title: Determination of Thermal Characteristics of Materials, Components and Assemblies

content.text: The thermal characteristics of materials shall be determined by calculation or by testing in accordance with the applicable product standards listed in the Code or, in the absence of such standards or where such standards do not address the determination of thermal resistance, in accordance with

clauses.text: [REF:standard:astmc177] or
[REF:standard:astmc518]

see_also.content: (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote223.div3.table3:long] for the thermal characteristics of commonly used materials.)

content.text: Calculations and tests performed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art2.sent1:short] shall be carried out at an average temperature of 24±2°C and under a temperature differential of 22±2°C .
The thermal characteristics of windows, doors and skylights shall be determined by calculation or testing in accordance with

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csaa440.2a440.3] for the reference sizes listed therein, or
[REF:standard:nfrc100] and [REF:standard:nfrc200] for the reference sizes listed therein.

content.text: The effective thermal resistance of opaque [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies shall be determined from

clauses.text: calculations conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art4:long] , or
laboratory tests performed in accordance with [REF:standard:astmc1363] using an indoor air temperature of 21±1°C and an outdoor air temperature of –18±1°C .

content.text: The thermal characteristics of log walls shall be determined by calculation in accordance with [REF:external:icc400:Section 305 of ] [REF:standard:icc400] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote220:short] .)

articles.title: Calculation of Ceiling, Wall, Fenestration and Door Areas

content.text: The gross ceiling or roof area shall be calculated as the sum of the interior surface areas of insulated ceiling and/or roof assemblies and of skylight openings.

Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent3:short] , the gross wall area shall be calculated as the sum of the interior surface areas of all exterior [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assemblies above the finished ground level that are inclined 60° or more from the horizontal, including

clauses.text: [REF:term:rm-jst:rim joists] ,
fenestration and opaque portions of doors,
insulated walls extending from finished ground level to the interior side of the insulated ceiling and/or roof assembly, and
the exposed areas of below-ground [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assemblies, where fenestration or doors are located below the plane of the adjacent finished ground.

content.text: Where a [REF:term:bldng:building] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] contains more than two [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , the gross wall area enclosing [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] shall be permitted to include the interior surface areas of walls that enclose a [REF:term:t:suite] , measured from the top surface of the lowest floor to the underside of the highest ceiling in the [REF:term:t:suite] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote221:short] .)
Fenestration and door areas shall be the actual sizes of windows, doors and skylights including all related frame and sash members.

The fenestration area made of flat panes that are not all in the same plane or curved panes shall be measured along the surface of the glass. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote222:short] .)

articles.title: Calculation of Effective Thermal Resistance of Assemblies

content.text: In calculating the thermal resistance of assemblies for the purpose of comparison with the requirements of  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8:long] , the thermal bridging effect of closely spaced, repetitive structural members, such as studs and joists, and of ancillary members, such as lintels, sills and plates, shall be accounted for. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote223:short] .)

Minor penetrations through assemblies, such as pipes, ducts, equipment with through-the-wall venting, packaged terminal air conditioners or heat pumps, shelf angles, anchors and ties and associated fasteners, and minor structural members that must partially or completely penetrate the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope to perform their intended function need not be taken into account in the calculation of the effective thermal resistance of that assembly.

Major structural penetrations, such as balcony and canopy slabs, beams, columns and ornamentation or appendages that must completely penetrate the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope to perform their intended function, need not be taken into account in the calculation of the effective thermal resistance of the penetrated assembly, provided

clauses.text: the insulation is installed tight against the outline of the penetration, and

the sum of the areas of all such major structural penetrations is limited to a maximum of 2% of the gross wall area calculated as described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent2:long] .

content.text: Where a component of the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope is protected by an enclosed unconditioned space, such as a sun porch, enclosed veranda, vestibule or attached garage, the required effective thermal resistance of the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope component between the [REF:term:bldng:building] and the unconditioned enclosure is permitted to be reduced by 0.16 (m^{2}×K)/W . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote225:short] .)

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent2:short]  to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent10:short] and in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art4.sent3:long] regarding balcony and canopy slabs, and except for clearances around components required for fire safety reasons, interior [REF:term:bldng:building] components that meet [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope components and major structural members that partly penetrate the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope shall not break the continuity of the insulation and shall not decrease the effective thermal resistance at their projected area to less than that required in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote226:short] .)

Where an interior wall, [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall, [REF:term:frwll:firewall] , [REF:term:prt-wll:party wall] or structural element penetrates an exterior wall or insulated roof or ceiling and breaks the continuity of the plane of insulation, the penetrating element shall be insulated

clauses.text: on both of its sides, inward or outward from the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope, for a distance equal to 4 times its uninsulated thickness to an effective thermal resistance not less than that required for exterior walls as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:short] ,
within the plane of insulation of the penetrated element to an effective thermal resistance not less than 60% of that required for the penetrated element, or
within itself to an effective thermal resistance not less than that required for the penetrated element.

content.text: Where a masonry fireplace or flue penetrates an exterior wall and breaks the continuity of the plane of insulation, it shall be insulated within the plane of insulation of the wall or within itself to an effective thermal resistance not less than 55% of that required for the exterior wall as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:short] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote228:short] .)
Where an ornamentation or appendage penetrates an exterior wall and breaks the continuity of the plane of insulation, the penetrating element shall be insulated

clauses.text: on both of its sides, inward or outward from the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope, for a distance equal to 4 times the insulated thickness of the exterior wall to an effective thermal resistance not less than that required for the wall as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:short] ,
within the plane of insulation of the wall to an effective thermal resistance not less than 55% of that required for the exterior wall, or
within the penetrating element to an effective thermal resistance not less than that required for the exterior wall.

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent9:short]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent10:short] , where two planes of insulation are separated by a [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assembly and cannot be physically joined, one of the planes of insulation shall be extended for a distance equal to at least 4 times the thickness of the assembly separating the two planes. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote229:short] .)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent7:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11:long] , where mechanical, plumbing or electrical system components, such as pipes, ducts, conduits, cabinets, chases, panels or recessed heaters, are placed within and parallel to a wall assembly required to be insulated, the effective thermal resistance of that wall at the projected area of the system component shall be not less than that required by  Tables [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote230:short] .)

The effective thermal resistance of a wall at the projected areas of plumbing and electrical system components, such as plumbing vent pipes, conduits, and electrical outlet and switch boxes, need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent6:short] , provided

clauses.text: the effective thermal resistance at the projected area of the system component is not less than 60% of that required in  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8:long] , and
the insulation is continuous on the cold side behind the system component.

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11:long] , where mechanical ducts, plumbing pipes, conduits for electrical services or communication cables are placed within the insulated portion of a floor or ceiling assembly, the effective thermal resistance of the assembly at the projected area of the ducts, pipes, conduits or cables shall be not less than 2.78 (m^{2}×K)/W.

Joints and junctions between walls and other [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope components shall be insulated in a manner that provides an effective thermal resistance that is no less than the lower of the minimum values required for the respective adjoining components. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote231:short] .)
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art5.sent1:short] does not apply where the continuity of the insulation is interrupted

clauses.text: between the insulation in the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall and that of the floor slab,

by an integral perimeter footing of a slab-on-grade (see  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect2.art3.sent5:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent8:long] ), or
at the horizontal portion of a [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall that supports masonry veneer and is insulated on the exterior.

A reduction in the effective thermal resistance of ceiling assemblies in attics under sloped roofs is permitted for a length no greater than 1 200 mm but only to the extent imposed by the roof slope and minimum venting clearance, provided the nominal thermal resistance of the insulation directly above the exterior wall is not less than 3.52 (m^{2}×K)/W . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote233:short] .)

Except for tubular daylighting devices, the minimum effective thermal resistance values for walls stated in  Tables [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:long] shall also apply to shafts for skylights.

content.text: Glass block assemblies separating [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from unconditioned space or the exterior shall have

clauses.text: an overall thermal transmittance of not more than 2.9 W/(m^{2}×K), and
a total aggregate area of not more than 1.85 m^{2}.

content.text: One door separating a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from an unconditioned space or the exterior is permitted to have an overall thermal transmittance up to 2.6 W/(m^{2}×K).
Storm windows and doors need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] .
Vehicular access doors separating a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from an unconditioned space or the exterior shall have a nominal thermal resistance of not less than 1.1 (m^{2}×K)/W.
Access hatches separating a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from an unconditioned space shall be insulated to a nominal thermal resistance of not less than 2.6 (m^{2}×K)/W.
A door separating a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from an unconditional space or the exterior is not required to conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent1:short] if,

clauses.text: in the case of a [REF:term:bldng:building] in a location with a heating degree-day value of less than or equal to 3999, the door is one of not more than three nonconforming doors, each of which has an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.10 W/m^{2}·K,

in the case of a [REF:term:bldng:building] in a location with a heating degree-day value of at least 4000 and not greater than 5999, the door is one of not more than two nonconforming doors, each of which has an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.10 W/m^{2}·K,

in the case of a [REF:term:bldng:building] in a location with a heating degree-day value of greater than or equal to 6000, the door is one of not more than two nonconforming doors, each of which has an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.00 W/m^{2}·K, or
in any case, the door is the only nonconforming door and has an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.60 W/m^{2}·K.

content.text: A [REF:term:bldng:building] described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent9.clause1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent9.clause2:short] is permitted to have an additional nonconforming door with an overall thermal transmittance not greater than 2.10 W/m^{2}·K if the effective thermal resistance of the ceilings of the [REF:term:bldng:building] is at least 0.88 m^{2}·K/W greater than the relevant value shown in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table2:long] , as applicable.
