content.text: Where an entire floor assembly falls into two of the categories listed in  Tables [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] , the more stringent value shall apply. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote239:short] .)

Where the top of a section of [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall is on average less than 600 mm above the adjoining ground level, the above-ground portion of that section of wall shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in  Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] .

Unheated floors-on-ground that are above the frost line and have no embedded heating pipes, cables or ducts shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]

clauses.text: on the exterior of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall down to the footing, or
on the interior of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall and, as applicable,

subclauses.text: beneath the slab for a distance not less than 1.2 m horizontally or vertically down from its perimeter with a thermal break along the edge of the slab that meets at least 50% of the required thermal resistance,
on top of the slab for a distance not less than 1.2 m horizontally from its perimeter, or
within the wooden sleepers below the floor for a distance not less than 1.2 m horizontally from its perimeter.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent6:short] , floors-on-ground with embedded heating ducts, cables or pipes shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in  Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] under their full bottom surface including the edges.

Where only a portion of a floor-on-ground has embedded heating ducts, cables or pipes, that heated portion shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in  Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] under its full bottom surface to 1.2 m beyond its perimeter including exterior edges if applicable.

In addition to the requirements stated in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent5:short]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent6:short] , heated floors-on-ground shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in  Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] vertically

clauses.text: around their perimeter, or
on the outside of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall, extending down to the level of the bottom of the floor.

content.text: Floors on permafrost shall be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in  Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] under the entire slab and around all edges, and under the integral perimeter footing.
Slabs-on-grade with an integral perimeter footing shall

clauses.text: be insulated to the effective thermal resistance required in  Table [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table2:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long] under the entire slab and around all edges, but not under the integral perimeter footing, and
be constructed with skirt insulation having the same effective thermal resistance as the insulation installed under the slab.

content.text: Junctions between below- [REF:term:grade:grade] assemblies shall be protected from the ingress of [REF:term:l:soil] gas in conformance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long]
The leakage of air into and out of [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned spaces] shall be controlled by constructing

clauses.text: a continuous [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] in accordance with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent6:short] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art10:long] ,

a continuous [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] in accordance with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and a [REF:term:bldng:building] assembly having an air leakage rate not greater than 0.20 L/(s×m^{2}) (Type A4) when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:ulcs742] at a pressure differential of 75 Pa , or

a continuous [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] in accordance with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent6:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and a [REF:term:bldng:building] assembly having an air leakage rate not greater than 0.20 L/(s·m^{2}) when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:astme2357] where

subclauses.text: the [REF:term:bldng:building] will not be subjected to sustained wind loads calculated based on a 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure that exceed 0.65 kPa , and
the air barrier assembly is installed on the warm side of the thermal insulation of the opaque [REF:term:bldng:building] assembly.

content.text: An [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] installed to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9.sent1:short] shall be continuous

clauses.text: across construction, control and expansion joints,
across junctions between different [REF:term:bldng:building] materials and assemblies, and
around penetrations through all [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies.

content.text: Windows, doors and skylights and their components shall comply with the minimum air leakage requirements stated in

clauses.text: [REF:standard:csa101a440] (Harmonized Standard), and
[REF:standard:csaa440S1]

content.text: Vehicular access doors that separate heated garages from unconditioned spaces or the exterior shall be weatherstripped around their perimeter to prevent air leakage.

Fireplaces shall be equipped with doors, enclosures or devices to restrict air movement through the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] when the fireplace is not in use. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote243:short] .)

Where the airtight material used in the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] is installed toward the exterior of the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope, its location and properties shall conform to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect5:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote244:short] .)
Materials intended to provide the principal resistance to air leakage shall conform to [REF:standard:ulcs741]

see_also.content: (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote152:long] for air leakage characteristics and water vapour permeance values for a number of common materials.)

content.text: Materials referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art10.sent1:short] shall be

clauses.text: compatible with adjoining materials, and
free of holes and cracks.

content.text: Where the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] consists of rigid panel-type material, all joints shall be sealed. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote245:long] .)

Where the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] consists of timber logs, all joints shall be sealed to resist airflow through gaps between logs that have shifted due to in-service conditions such as shrinkage and settling.
Where the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] consists of flexible sheet material, all joints shall be

clauses.text: lapped not less than 50 mm ,
sealed (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote245:short] ), and
structurally supported.

content.text: Sealant material used for the purpose of creating a continuous [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] shall

clauses.text: be a non-hardening type, or
conform to

subclauses.text: [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect27.subsect4:long] ,
[REF:standard:ulcs710.1] or
[REF:standard:ulcs711.1]

content.text: Penetrations by electrical wiring, outlets, switches or recessed light fixtures through the plane of airtightness shall be constructed airtight

clauses.text: where the component is designed to provide a seal against air leakage, by sealing the component to the air barrier material (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote246:short] ), or
where the component is not designed to provide a seal against air leakage, by covering the component with an air barrier material and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material.

content.text: The joints between the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] wall and the sill plate, between the sill plate and [REF:term:rm-jst:rim joist] , between the [REF:term:rm-jst:rim joist] and the subfloor material, and between the subfloor material and the bottom plate of the wall above shall be constructed airtight by

clauses.text: sealing all joints and junctions between the structural components, or
covering the structural components with an air barrier material and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material.

content.text: The interfaces between windows, doors and skylights and wall/ceiling assemblies shall be constructed airtight by sealing all joints and junctions between the air barrier material in the wall and the window, door or skylight frame. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote247:short] .) (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect7.subsect6:long] )
Cantilevered floors and floors over unheated spaces or over the exterior shall be constructed airtight by one of the following methods or a combination thereof:

clauses.text: sealing all joints and junctions between the structural components, or
covering the structural components with an air barrier material and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material.

content.text: Interior walls that meet exterior walls or ceilings whose plane of airtightness is on the interior of the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope and knee walls that separate [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from unconditioned space shall be constructed airtight by

clauses.text: sealing all junctions between the structural components,
covering the structural components with an air barrier material and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material, or
maintaining the continuity of the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] above or through the interior wall or below or through the knee wall, as applicable.

content.text: Steel-lined [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] that penetrate the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope shall be constructed airtight by blocking the void between required clearances for metal [REF:term:chmn:chimneys] and surrounding construction with sheet metal and sealant capable of withstanding high temperatures.

[REF:term:mnr-r-cn:Masonry or concrete chimneys] that penetrate the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope shall be constructed airtight by mechanically fastening a metal flange or steel stud that extends not less than 75 mm out from the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] and sealing the air barrier material to it with a sealant capable of withstanding high temperatures.

Ducts that penetrate the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope shall be constructed airtight by sealing the penetration through the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote248:short] .)
Plumbing vent stack pipes that penetrate the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope shall be constructed airtight by

clauses.text: sealing the air barrier material to the vent stack pipe with a compatible sealant or sheathing tape, or
installing a rubber gasket or prefabricated roof flashing at the penetration of the plane of airtightness then sealing it and mechanically fastening it to the top plate.

content.text: Where a [REF:term:prt-wll:party wall] meets the plane of airtightness, that junction shall be constructed airtight by sealing any voids within the [REF:term:prt-wll:party wall] at the perimeter to the adjacent air barrier material and by

clauses.text: sealing all junctions between the structural components, or
covering the structural components with an air barrier material and sealing it to the adjacent air barrier material.

content.text: Where the concrete in a flat insulating concrete form wall acts as the air barrier, the continuity of the plane of airtightness shall be maintained between the concrete and adjacent air barrier materials.

articles.title: Trade-off Options for Above-ground Building Envelope Components and Assemblies

content.text: Subject to the limitations stated in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent6:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent8:short] , the trade-off options described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent2:short] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent4:short] apply only to above-ground [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope components and assemblies, or portions thereof, of a single [REF:term:bldng:building] .

The effective thermal resistance of one or more above-ground opaque [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assemblies is permitted to be less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] , provided

clauses.text: the total areas of all proposed and reference assemblies are equal,

the effective thermal resistance of one or more other proposed above-ground opaque [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assembly areas is increased to more than that required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] , and

the sum of the areas of all traded above-ground opaque [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assemblies divided by their respective effective thermal resistance is less than or equal to what it would be if all assemblies complied with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long]

content.text: The effective thermal resistance of one or more windows, as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent5:short] , is permitted to be less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7:long] , provided

clauses.text: the total areas of all traded windows are equal,
the traded windows are located in the same orientation,
the effective thermal resistance of one or more other windows is increased to more than that required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7:long] , and

the sum of the areas of all traded windows divided by their respective effective thermal resistance is less than or equal to what it would be if all windows complied with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7:long]

content.text: The effective thermal resistance of one or more portions of floor insulation or ceiling insulation in attics under sloped roofs in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] that are one [REF:term:tr:storey] in [REF:term:bldng-hg:building height] is permitted to be less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] , provided

clauses.text: the total area of fenestration, excluding skylights, and doors does not exceed 15% of the above-ground gross wall area as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3:long] ,
the floor-to-ceiling height measured from the top of the subfloor to the underside of the finished ceiling of the [REF:term:tr:storey] does not exceed 2.34 m ,
the distance measured from the top of the subfloor to the underside of the bottom chord of the truss or joist of the roof is not more than 2.39 m , and

the difference between the sum of the proposed areas of ceilings or floors divided by their respective proposed effective thermal resistance and the sum of the reference areas of ceilings or floors divided by their respective thermal resistance required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] is not more than the difference between 17% fenestration and door area and the proposed fenestration and door areas divided by the required effective thermal resistance values for windows and doors in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7:long]

content.text: The effective thermal resistance of windows shall be determined as RSI = 1/U-value.

The reduction in effective thermal resistance of above-ground opaque [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assemblies permitted by  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art11.sent4:short] shall result in an RSI value that is not less than

clauses.text: 55% of that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] for above-ground walls and joist-type roofs (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote254:short] ), and
60% of that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6:long] for other opaque assemblies.

content.text: The effective thermal resistances of above-ground opaque assemblies with embedded heating cables, pipes or membranes are not permitted to be traded.

The effective thermal resistances of doors and access hatches described in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent3:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.sent7:short] are not permitted to be traded.
This Subsection is concerned with the efficient use of energy by systems and equipment used for heating, ventilating and air-conditioning (HVAC).

Where HVAC systems, equipment or techniques other than those described in this Subsection are used, the [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the energy efficiency requirements of the [REF:standard:nrcc-necb] .

HVAC systems shall be sized in accordance with good practice as described in  Sections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote255:short] .)

Ducts shall be designed and installed in accordance with  Sections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote256:short] .)
Except for [REF:term:xht-dct:exhaust ducts] leading directly to the exterior, ducts and [REF:term:plnm:plenums] carrying conditioned air and located outside the plane of insulation shall

clauses.text: except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent4:short] , have all joints sealed against air infiltration and exfiltration with

subclauses.text: sealants or gaskets made from liquids, mastics or heat-applied materials,
mastic with embedded fabric, or
foil-faced butyl tape, and

clauses.text: except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent5:short] , be insulated to the same level as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long] for exterior above-ground walls.

content.text: Fabric-backed tape with rubber adhesives shall not be used as a primary sealant to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent3.clause1:medium] .

The underside of rectangular ducts installed under an insulated floor over an unconditioned space is permitted to be insulated to a lower level than required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent3:short] but not to less than 2.11 (m^{2}×K)/W , provided both sides of such ducts are insulated to a compensating higher thermal resistance so that the resulting heat loss does not exceed that of ducts complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art2.sent3:short] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote257:short] .)

Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent4:short] , every duct or opening intended to discharge air to the outdoors shall be equipped with

clauses.text: a motorized damper, or
a gravity- or spring-operated backflow damper.

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent3:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent4:short] and except in locations with fewer than 3500 heating degree-days as listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC:long] , every outdoor air intake duct or opening shall be equipped with a motorized damper that remains in the “open” position if the damper fails.

Where other regulations are in effect that do not permit dampers, air intakes and outlets need not comply with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent2:short] .

Air intakes and outlets serving HVAC systems that are required to operate continuously need not comply with  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent1:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art3.sent2:short] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote258:short] .)

articles.title: Piping for Heating and Cooling Systems

content.text: Piping for heating and cooling systems shall be designed and installed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect8:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote245:long] .)
Except for high-temperature refrigerant piping, all piping forming part of a heating or air-conditioning system shall be located

clauses.text: inside the plane of insulation, or

within or outside the plane of insulation, provided the piping is insulated to a thermal resistance not less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long] for exterior above-ground walls.

articles.title: Equipment for Heating and Air-conditioning Systems

content.text: Equipment for heating and air-conditioning systems shall be located

clauses.text: inside the plane of insulation, or
outdoors or in an unconditioned space, provided the equipment is designated by the manufacturer for such installation.

content.text: Except for manually fuelled solid-fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] , the supply of heating and cooling energy to each [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] , [REF:term:t:suite] or common space shall be controlled by thermostatic controls that activate the appropriate supply when the temperature in a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] fluctuates ±0.5°C from the set-point temperature for that space.
Where heating and cooling systems are controlled by separate thermostatic controls, means shall be provided to prevent these controls from simultaneously calling for heating and cooling.
Space temperature control devices used to control unitary electric resistance [REF:term:pc-htr:space heaters] shall conform to [REF:standard:csac828]

Controls required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art6.sent1:short] shall be designed such that lowering the set-point temperature on the thermostat for the heating system will not cause cooling energy to be expended to reach the lowered setting, and raising the set-point temperature on the thermostat for the cooling system will not cause heating energy to be expended to reach the raised setting.
Automatic devices or manually operated dampers, valves or switches shall be provided, as appropriate for the heating system used, to allow the heating of each zone to be adjusted.

Heat pumps equipped with supplementary heaters shall incorporate controls to prevent supplementary heater operation when the heating load can be met by the heat pump alone, except during defrost cycles.

Heat pumps with a programmable thermostat shall be equipped with setback controls that will temporarily suppress electrical back-up or adaptive anticipation of the recovery point, in order to prevent the activation of supplementary heat during the heat pump's recovery. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote262:short] .)
Where an HVAC system is equipped with a means for adding moisture to maintain specific humidity levels, an automatic humidity control device shall be provided.

articles.title: Heat Recovery from Dehumidification in Spaces with an Indoor Pool or Hot Tub

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent3:short] , spaces containing an indoor pool or hot tub shall be equipped with air exhaust systems conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent4:short] at design conditions. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect4.art2:long] )

Spaces containing an indoor pool need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:short] , provided a stationary mechanical or desiccant dehumidification system is installed that provides at least 80% of the dehumidification that would result from compliance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:short] .

Spaces containing an indoor pool or hot tub having a total water surface area of less than 10 m^{2} need not comply with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:short] , provided they are equipped with a cover having a nominal thermal resistance not less than 2.1 (m^{2}×K)/W .
Heat-recovery systems used to meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:short] shall

clauses.text: be capable of recovering at least 40% of the sensible heat from exhausted air when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:ahri1060] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote264:short] ), or
have a sensible-heat-recovery efficiency complying with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3:long] when tested in accordance with [REF:standard:csac439]

content.text: This Article applies where a self-contained mechanical ventilation system is installed whose principal exhaust component is equipped with heat-recovery capability. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote265:short] .)
Where an integrated mechanical system (IMS) with a heat-recovery ventilator provides the principal exhaust ventilation, the IMS shall

clauses.text: be tested in accordance with [REF:standard:csap.10] and
have a minimum overall thermal performance factor conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long]

content.text: When tested in conformance with the low-temperature thermal and ventilation test methods described in [REF:standard:csac439] heat-recovery ventilators described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent1:short] shall have a sensible heat-recovery efficiency of

clauses.text: at least 60% at an outside air test temperature of 0°C for locations with a 2.5% January design temperature greater than or equal to –10°C, and
at least 60% at an outside air test temperature of 0°C and at least 55% at an outside air test temperature of –25°C for locations with a 2.5% January design temperature less than –10°C.

content.text: The requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3:short] shall be met using a principal ventilation rate not less than that required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote266:long] .)

HVAC equipment and components shall comply with the performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote267:short] .)

Decorative gas-fired fireplaces and [REF:term:tv:stoves] are vented decorative gas [REF:term:pplnc:appliances] that are marked as such on their rating plate and that comply with [REF:standard:csa2.22]

Decorative gas-fired fireplaces and [REF:term:tv:stoves] shall not be used to satisfy heating requirements or as part of the heating system required by  Section [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33:long]
Does not include [REF:term:tv:stoves] with an oven whose volume is greater than 0.028 m^{3} .

See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art6.sent3:long] .

content.text: Natural gas and propane fireplaces shall be

clauses.text: direct-vent (sealed), and
pilot-on-demand, interrupted or intermittent ignition systems without a standing pilot light.

content.text: The heat source component of combined space- and service water heating systems that are not within the scope of [REF:standard:csap.9] shall meet the performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] for the applicable equipment type. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote268:short] .)
Space-heating systems that use solar thermal technology shall conform to the manufacturer's design requirements and installation procedures.
Service water heating systems that use solar thermal technology shall be installed in accordance with the [REF:standard:nrcc-npc] .
Hot water storage tanks associated with the systems referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art11.sent2:short] shall be installed in a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] .
This Subsection is concerned with the efficient use of energy by systems used to heat service water for household use as well as for indoor pools and hot tubs.

Where service water heating equipment or techniques other than those described in this Subsection are used, the [REF:term:bldng:building] shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the energy efficiency requirements of the [REF:standard:nrcc-necb] .

[REF:term:rvc-wtr-:Service water heaters] , [REF:term:blr:boilers] , pool heaters and storage tanks shall comply with the performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art2.table1:long] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote269:short] .)

Hot service water storage tanks not listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art2.table1:long] shall be covered with insulation having a minimum thermal resistance of 1.8 (m^{2}×K)/W .

content.title: Service Water Heating Equipment Performance Requirements

content.text: Except for components that are required to be installed outdoors, service water heating equipment shall be installed in a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote270:short] .)
Service water heating systems that use solar thermal technology shall conform to the manufacturer's design requirements and installation procedures.
Service water heating systems that use solar thermal technology shall be installed in accordance with the Book II (Plumbing Systems) of this Code.
Hot water storage tanks associated with the systems referred to in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art3.sent2:short] shall be installed in a [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] .
The first 2 m of outlet piping downstream and of inlet piping upstream leading from a storage tank or heating vessel shall be covered with piping insulation that is at least 12 mm thick.
All piping forming part of a continuously operating recirculating service water heating system shall be covered with piping insulation that is at least 12 mm thick.

Where piping forming part of the service water heating system is located outside the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope or in an unconditioned space, it shall be insulated to a thermal resistance not less than the effective thermal resistance required for the exterior above-ground walls.

Service water heating systems with storage tanks shall be equipped with automatic temperature controls capable of adjustment between the minimum and maximum temperature settings permitted for the intended use.
Heaters for indoor swimming pools shall be equipped with

clauses.text: a thermostat, and
a readily accessible and clearly labeled device that allows the heater to be shut off without adjusting the thermostat setting.

content.text: Pumps and heaters for indoor swimming pools shall be equipped with time switches or other types of controls that can be set to automatically turn off the pumps and heaters when their operation is not required. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote271:short] .)

This Subsection is concerned with modeling the energy performance of components, systems and assemblies, including heat gains from internal loads described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.sent4:long] , that are addressed in the scope of the prescriptive requirements in  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4:long] and that are installed in [REF:term:bldng:buildings] described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect1.art3.sent3:long] .
Internal loads other than those described in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.sent4:long] shall be excluded from the performance compliance calculations as they relate to

clauses.text: the lighting of unconditioned spaces,
exterior lighting, and
the ventilation of unconditioned spaces.

content.text: For the purpose of this Subsection, the term "reference house" shall mean a hypothetical replica of the proposed house design using the same energy sources for the same functions and having the same environmental requirements, [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] , climatic data and operating schedules, but made to comply with all applicable prescriptive requirements of  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long]  to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4:long] , not including  Tables [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table3:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.table4:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table3:long]

For the purpose of this Subsection, the term “proposed house” shall mean a modeled replica of the actual house under consideration, in which some elements covered in  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4:long] are specific to the actual house, while other elements not covered in those Subsections, but that are necessary for the calculation of the annual energy consumption, are assigned default values.
The performance compliance calculations shall determine the annual energy consumption of the proposed house and the house energy target of a reference house in accordance with

clauses.text: this Subsection, or
the EnerGuide Rating System, version 15, and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art3.sent2:short] .

content.text: Except as permitted by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art3.sent7:short] , the annual energy consumption of the proposed house in comparison to the house energy target of the reference house shall demonstrate a percent improvement in accordance with Table 9.37.6.3.-G. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote274:short] .)

Except for Tables 9.37.2.6.-C, 9.37.2.7.-D, and 9.37.2.8.-C, in establishing the house energy target, [REF:term:bldng:building] components, systems and assemblies shall be accounted for in accordance with the prescriptive requirements of Subsections 9.37.2. to 9.37.4. for the climate zone under consideration.

In establishing the annual energy consumption, [REF:term:bldng:building] components, systems and assemblies that are addressed in the scope of the prescriptive requirements of Subsections 9.37.2. to 9.37.4. shall be accounted for for the climate zone under consideration.

Where the construction techniques or [REF:term:bldng:building] components, systems or assemblies used are more energy-efficient than those prescribed by the prescriptive requirements, the performance compliance calculations are permitted to take this increased performance level into account in the determination of the annual energy consumption, provided it can be quantified and is not dependent on occupant interaction.

Both the proposed and reference houses shall be modeled using the same climatic data, [REF:term:l:soil] conditions, operating schedules in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4:long] and temperature set-points.
For log homes, the annual energy consumption of the proposed house shall not exceed the house energy target of the reference house. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote274:short] .)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.sent2:short] , the energy model calculations shall account for the annual energy consumption of systems and equipment required for

clauses.text: space heating,
ventilation,
service water heating, and
where installed, space cooling.

content.text: Redundant or back-up equipment for the systems and equipment listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.sent1:short] is permitted to be excluded from the energy model, provided it is equipped with controls and is not required to meet the space-conditioning load of the house. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote278:short] .)
The schedules used in the energy model shall

clauses.text: be based on a time interval not greater than one hour, where the energy model evaluates the performance of the house over hourly intervals, or
be applied in an hourly-bin model then averaged, where the energy model does not evaluate the performance of the house over hourly intervals.

content.text: The energy model calculations shall account for the loads due to heat gains from occupants, lighting and miscellaneous equipment, which shall be fixed for every day of the year, by

clauses.text: following the schedule provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art4.table1:long] , and
increasing the loads for each hour by 3.58 W per square metre of [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] in common spaces, if applicable.

content.title: Default Schedule for Internal Heat Gain Loads

table_notes.content: The schedule indicates at what time of day the heat gains from the metabolic activity of the occupants and occupant-dependent appliance, lighting and receptacle electrical loads are present; it does not account for heat gains from exterior lighting, lighting of unconditioned spaces, service water heating systems and HVAC equipment.
See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote276:short]

content.text: The energy model calculations shall account for the following space-heating temperature set-points:

clauses.text: 20°C in all living spaces above the [REF:term:bmnt:basement] ,
19°C in [REF:term:bmnt:basements] and common spaces, and
15°C in crawl spaces intended to be [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned spaces] .

content.text: The energy model calculations shall account for a space-cooling temperature set-point of 25°C in all [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned spaces] served by the cooling system.

The energy model calculations shall account for a thermostatic control that responds to fluctuations of ±0.5°C from the temperature set-point. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote279:short] .)
If a computer program is used to carry out the compliance calculations, the calculation methods employed in the energy model shall

clauses.text: be used for both the reference and proposed houses, and
be tested in accordance with [REF:standard:ashrae140] with variations in the computer program from the range recommended therein reported in accordance with Division C.

content.text: The proposed and reference houses shall both be modeled using the same approach and assumptions, except where [REF:term:bldng:building] components or energy efficiency features are permitted by this Subsection to be different.

The energy model calculations shall account for the effect of airtightness in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10.sent10:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect7.art3:long] , as applicable.
The energy model calculations shall account for heat transfer through elements separating [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from unconditioned space, the exterior or the ground.

To calculate the effect of heating and cooling consumption, the energy model calculations shall be performed using climatic data measured at time intervals no greater than one hour for one year (8 760 hours) based on the average of at least 10 years of measured data collected at the weather station nearest to the region in which the proposed house is located. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote280:short] .)

For urban regions with several climatic data sets and for locations for which climatic data are not available, the energy model calculations shall be performed using climatic data that best represent the climate at the [REF:term:bldng:building] site.
The energy model calculations shall account for ground reflectance by

clauses.text: increasing ground reflectance due to snow cover in a ratio of 30% without snow cover and 70% with snow cover, or
taking into account changes in ground reflectance throughout the heating season.

content.text: For each hour of the year, the energy model calculations shall account for heat transfer through wall assemblies, roof-ceiling assemblies, including attics where applicable, and exposed floor assemblies due to the thermal characteristics of the particular assembly and thermal bridging.

The following [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assemblies and components shall be addressed in the energy model calculations:
(See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long] .)

clauses.text: above-ground walls and roof-ceiling assemblies,
floors and walls in contact with the ground, and
doors, windows and skylights.

content.text: For each wall assembly, fenestration component, roof-ceiling assembly and exposed floor assembly, the energy model calculations shall account for

clauses.text: the area of the interior side of the insulated surface,
emissivity, and
the effective thermal resistance or overall thermal transmittance, as applicable.

content.text: The energy model calculations shall account for the effect that each assembly in contact with the ground has on below- [REF:term:grade:grade] heat transfer due to

clauses.text: the geometry of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] ,
[REF:term:l:soil] conditions (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part1.appendix.appnote2:long] ), and
the configuration of the insulation.

content.text: The energy model calculations shall account for heat transfer through fenestration separating [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned spaces] from the outdoors, including skylights, while accounting for both temperature difference and transmission of solar radiation based on

clauses.text: orientation as a function of azimuth and tilt of the surface,
area of frame opening and glazed area,
overall thermal transmittance, and
solar heat gain coefficient.

content.text: Where the energy model calculations account for the effect of thermal mass, the contents of the house shall be excluded. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote281:short] .)

The energy model calculations shall account for the presence of thermally active walls, floors and ceilings with embedded conditioning systems that form part of the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope.
Where skylights are installed in the roof, the gross roof area shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3.sent1:long] .
Skylights shall be considered to have no shading.
The energy model calculations shall account for the effects of exterior permanent and fixed shading only on solar heat gain from fenestration.
The ratio of fenestration area to opaque area of doors shall be the same for the proposed and reference houses. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote282:short] .)

The energy model calculations shall account for the energy consumption of each heating, ventilating and, where installed, cooling system for each hour of the year. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote283:short] .)
Each heating system and, where installed, cooling system shall be accounted for separately in the energy model calculations.
[REF:term:cnd-sp:Conditioned spaces] in both the reference and proposed houses shall be modeled as being

clauses.text: heated, where only heating systems are provided in the proposed house,
cooled, where only cooling systems are provided in the proposed house, or
heated and cooled, where complete heating and cooling systems are provided in the proposed house.

content.text: The performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] shall be used in the energy model calculations.

Where duct and piping losses are accounted for in the energy model calculations, they shall be included for both the proposed and reference houses and calculated the same way for both houses. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote284:short] .)
The same time periods shall be used in the simulation of the operation of the ventilation system for both the proposed and reference houses.
During the heating season, any solar and internal heat gains that cause an increase in space temperature beyond 5.5°C above the setpoint shall be

clauses.text: excluded from the energy model calculations, or
calculated as being vented from the house.

content.text: The energy model calculations shall account for the part-load performance of equipment, including electrical consumption.

The energy model calculations shall account for the heat-recovery efficiency of heat-recovery ventilators using a minimum of 2 data test points derived from testing in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3.clause1:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3.clause2:short] , as applicable.
The energy model calculations shall account for the energy consumption of all service water heating systems.
The performance requirements stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art2.table1:long] shall be used in the energy model calculations.

Where piping or standby losses are accounted for in the energy model calculations, they shall be included for both the proposed and reference houses, including their effect on space heating and cooling, and calculated the same way for both houses.
The energy model calculations shall use a supply cold water temperature, in °C, that is

clauses.text: equal to –0.002 (HDD) + 20.3 , where HDD < 7 999 ,
equal to 4.3, where HDD ≥ 8 000 , or
determined based on the ground and air temperatures in the climatic data file.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art8.sent8:short] , the energy model calculations shall use a service water delivery temperature of 55˚C. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote285:short] .)

For hot service water usage other than for showering, the energy model calculations shall take into account the service water heating use schedule presented in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art8.table1:long] using a load of

clauses.text: 97 L/ day for houses without a [REF:term:scnd-t:secondary suite] , or
65 L/day for each [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] in residential [REF:term:bldng:buildings] with two or more [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] .

content.title: Default Schedule of Service Water Heating Use

content.value: Distribution of Hourly Draws on Service Water Heating, L/h
Each [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] in residential [REF:term:bldng:buildings] with two or more [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] ( 65 L /day/ [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] )

content.text: The energy model calculations shall take into account daily hot service water usage for showering

clauses.text: at 7 a.m. for 15 mins for houses without a [REF:term:scnd-t:secondary suite] , or
at 7 a.m. for 10 mins for each [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] in residential [REF:term:bldng:buildings] with two or more [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] .

content.text: The energy model shall set the service water delivery temperature for showering to 41°C at the shower head, with a flow rate of 7.6 L/min .

articles.title: General Requirements for Modeling the Proposed House

content.text: Except where permitted by  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art12:long] , the energy model calculations for the proposed house shall be consistent with the proposed construction specifications for that house with regard to

clauses.text: fenestration and opaque [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assembly type, effective thermal resistance and areas,
HVAC system types and capacities, and
service water heating system types and capacities.

articles.title: Modeling Building Envelope of Proposed House

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10.sent2:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10.sent3:short] , the energy model calculations for the proposed house shall be consistent with the proposed construction specifications for that house with regard to

clauses.text: the area of the above-ground portion of [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls,
the effective thermal resistance of above-ground walls, ceilings below attics, roof assemblies and [REF:term:rm-jst:rim joists] ,
the maximum overall thermal transmittance of doors, as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art2.sent3:long] ,
the effective thermal resistance of below-ground walls and slabs-on-ground,
exterior walls, roof-ceiling assembly, doors, walls, exposed floors, and floors in contact with the ground,
distribution, orientation and area of fenestration and doors, as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3:long] ,
solar heat gain coefficient and overall thermal transmittance of fenestration, as calculated in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art2.sent3:long] ,
configuration of insulation in assemblies in contact with the ground, and
effective thermal resistance of [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls.

content.text: Except for penetrations, slab-on-ground edge insulation and assemblies with embedded heating pipes, where a [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope component or assembly covers less than 2% of the total area of the assembly type to which it belongs, its thermal characteristics are not required to be calculated as belonging to a distinct assembly, provided the area of the component or assembly is included in an adjacent assembly having the same orientation (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote287:short] .)

[REF:term:bldng:Building] envelope assemblies with the same thermal characteristics and orientation are not required to be calculated as distinct assemblies, provided their area is included in an adjacent assembly.
[REF:term:bldng:Building] envelope assemblies and components separating [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] from enclosed unconditioned space shall have a solar heat gain coefficient equal to 0.

Except as stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art6.sent9:long] , the energy model calculations for the proposed house shall account for the effects of exterior permanent and fixed shading devices, including fins, overhangs, and light shelves, on solar heat gain.
Where thermal mass is included in the energy model calculations for the proposed house, it shall be set as

clauses.text: the specified mass up to the inside edge of insulation in exterior walls, the mass of interior walls, the mass up to the centre-line of [REF:term:prt-wll:party walls] , and the mass of floors, as applicable,

the specified mass of the [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assembly, where the energy model calculations include a transient analysis of thermal transfer of the entire [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assembly, or
a default value of 0.060 MJ/(m^{2}×°C) .

content.text: Exterior walls, roofs and exposed floors shall have a solar absorptance of 0.4.
The orientation of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] of the proposed house as constructed shall be within 22.5° of the orientation used in the energy model calculations.
The airtightness used in the energy model calculations for the proposed house shall be

clauses.text: 3.2 air changes per hour at 50 Pa pressure differential with a pressure exponent of 0.67, where the construction complies with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25:long] ,

2.5 air changes per hour at 50 Pa pressure differential with a pressure exponent of 0.67, where it can be shown that the [REF:term:r-brrr:air barrier system] is constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect25.subsect3:long] and  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art9:long] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art10:long] , or
the airtightness determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect7.art3.sent1:long] expressed as

subclauses.text: the number of air changes per hour at 50 Pa pressure differential with a pressure exponent determined through a multi-point test, and
the equivalent leakage area.

content.text: For compliance with  Clause [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art10.sent9.clause3:medium] , a design airtightness value shall be assigned for use in the energy model until the actual airtightness has been measured.

articles.title: Modeling HVAC System of Proposed House

content.text: Where multiple HVAC systems serve a single space, the energy model calculations for the proposed house shall call each system in the order of priority established by the system control in the proposed house.
Where a heat pump is included in the proposed house, the energy model calculations shall include

clauses.text: the effect of the source temperature on the heat pump's efficiency, and
the temperature at which the heat pump shuts down.

content.text: Permanent supplementary heating systems that are operated by a thermostat or automatic control shall be included in the energy model calculations for the proposed house.

The performance characteristics of the heat-recovery ventilation system of the proposed house shall be as specified at not less than the principal ventilation rate required for a system designed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long]
The ventilation system shall be modeled as operating 8 hours a day at the principal ventilation rate.

The energy model calculations shall determine the required principal ventilation rate, in L/s, in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32.subsect3.art3:long] based on the number of bedrooms in the proposed house.
The energy model calculations may include duct and piping losses, taking into account the properties of the specified duct and piping insulation of the proposed house.
The energy model calculations shall include a heating system and, where installed, a cooling system sized according to the specifications for the proposed house.
The energy model calculations shall include the effect of part-load performance of equipment using

clauses.text: the same modeled part-load performance data used for the reference house as per [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.sent6.clause1:long] ,
the default part-load performance characteristics stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.sent6.clause2:long] , or
measured data for the specified equipment.

content.text: Where a heat-recovery ventilator is installed in the proposed house, the energy model calculations shall only account for the recovery of sensible heat using the efficiency ratings in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3:long] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote289:short] .)

Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent12:short] , where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house, the energy model calculations shall assume the circulation fan operates when the heating, cooling or principal ventilation system is operating. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote290:short] .)

Where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house and where the principal ventilation system in the proposed house is a separate, fully ducted ventilation system, the energy model calculations shall assume the circulation fan operates only when the heating or cooling system is operating.
Where the proposed house contains multiple HVAC systems, the circulation fan power shall be the sum of the circulation fan power capacity of each system.
The ventilation fan power consumption shall be modeled

clauses.text: as being 2.32 W/L/s for each ventilation fan on the exhaust side and, where applicable, on the supply side, or
as specified, where a heat-recovery ventilator is used.

content.text: Where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house, the energy model calculations shall determine the flow rate, in L/s, of the circulation fan in the reference house by multiplying the capacity, in W, of the heating system in the proposed house by

clauses.text: 0.0604 for heat pumps, and
0.0251 for all other types of heating systems.

content.text: Where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house, the energy model calculations shall determine the minimum electricity requirement, in W, of the circulation fan by multiplying the flow rate, in L/s, of the circulation fan in the reference house, determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent15:short] , by a factor of 2.30.
Where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house, the flow rate of the circulation fan shall be modeled as being the larger of

clauses.text: the flow rate of the circulation fan of the reference house, determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent15:short] , or
the flow rate of the circulation fan for the forced-air system specified in the design for the proposed house.

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent19:short] , where a forced-air system is installed in the proposed house, the power capacity of the circulation fan shall be modeled as specified in the design for the proposed house.

Where the design for the proposed house specifies a forced-air system with a circulation fan flow rate that is lower than the flow rate of the circulation fan in the reference house, as determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent15:short] , the electricity capacity, in W, of the circulation fan shall be modeled as being the larger of

clauses.text: the electricity capacity specified for the circulation fan in the proposed forced-air system, or
the minimum circulation fan electricity capacity determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent16:short] .

content.text: For natural gas-, oil-, propane- and wood-burning heating systems, the energy model calculations shall set the auxiliary electricity requirements, including that of combustion fans, to those specified for the proposed house.

articles.title: Modeling Service Water Heating System of Proposed House

content.text: The service water heating system used in the energy model calculations shall be sized as specified in the design for the proposed house.
The energy model calculations may include

clauses.text: piping losses, and
drain-water heat recovery, provided

subclauses.text: the calculation of the heat recovered is based on the performance of the drain-water heat-recovery unit specified, as determined in accordance with [REF:standard:csab55.1] using a drain-water inlet temperature of 35°C, and

where there are one or two above-ground showers, all of them are served by the drain-water heat-recovery unit, and where there are more than two above-ground showers, at least two of them are served by the drain-water heat-recovery unit.

articles.title: General Requirements for Modeling the Reference House

content.text: Except as provided in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art13.sent2:short] and  Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art14:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art16:long] , the energy model calculations for the reference house shall be consistent with the prescriptive requirements of  Subsections [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4:long] with regard to

clauses.text: fenestration and opaque [REF:term:bldng:building] envelope assembly types and areas,
HVAC system types and capacities, and
service water heating system types and capacities.

content.text: The energy model calculations for the reference house shall include the same values as those used for the proposed house with regard to

clauses.text: [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] ,
heated volume, and
number and types of rooms.

articles.title: Modeling Building Envelope of Reference House

content.text: The energy model calculations for the reference house shall include the same values as those used for the proposed house with regard to

clauses.text: the gross area of above-ground portion of [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] walls,
[REF:term:l:soil] conditions,
the orientation of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] , and
the ratio of fenestration area to opaque area of doors.

content.text: The energy model calculations for the reference house shall use the following values:

clauses.text: 0.060 MJ/(m^{2}×°C) for thermal mass,
a solar absorptance of 0.4 for the exterior walls, roofs and exposed floors,
0.26 for the solar heat gain coefficient of fenestration,
an airtightness of

subclauses.text: reserved,

revisions.text: 3.0 air changes per hour at 50 Pa pressure differential for attached zones, where the airtightness used for the proposed house is determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect38.subsect7.art3.sent1:long] using the unguarded method, and
reserved,
revisions.change_summary: Struck out '3.0 air changes per hour at 50 Pa pressure differential for attached zones, where the airtightness used for the proposed house is determined in accordance with Sentence 9.36.7.3.(1) using the unguarded method, and' and substituted 'reserved,'

subclauses.text: 2.5 air changes per hour at 50 Pa pressure differential, and

revisions.text: 2.5 air changes per hour at 50 Pa pressure differential otherwise, and
2.5 air changes per hour at 50 Pa pressure differential, and
revisions.change_summary: Struck out 'otherwise'

clauses.text: the pressure exponent used for the proposed house where this value is less than 0.67, otherwise, 0.67.

content.text: The effective thermal resistance and overall thermal transmittance values, as applicable, used in the energy model calculations for the reference house shall be determined for the applicable heating degree-day zone in accordance with

clauses.text: [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art6.table1:long] for walls, ceilings below attics, roof assemblies and [REF:term:rm-jst:rim joists] ,
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.table1:long] for doors, and
[REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] for below- [REF:term:grade:grade] walls and slabs-on-ground.

content.text: Except as provided in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art14.sent5:short] and [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art14.sent6:short] , the exterior walls, roof-ceiling assembly, doors, walls, exposed floors, and floors of the reference house that are in contact with the ground shall have the same area as those of the proposed house.
The area and orientation of fenestration and doors of the reference house shall be modeled as being equally distributed on all sides of the house.
The gross wall area and the area of fenestration and doors of the reference house shall be determined in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art3:long]

Windows and other glazed components in the reference house shall have a maximum overall thermal transmittance as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art7.table1:long] for the applicable heating degree-day category.
The configuration of insulation in assemblies of the reference house that are in contact with the ground shall be modeled as conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8:long]

[REF:term:fndtn:Foundation] walls shall be modeled using the applicable effective thermal resistance values in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.table1:long] and as conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect2.art8.sent2:long] .
The fenestration and door area to gross wall area ratio (FDWR) of the reference house shall be

clauses.text: for houses containing 1 or 2 two [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] ,

subclauses.text: as per the proposed house, where its FDWR is between 17% and 22%,
17%, where the FDWR of the proposed house is less than 17%, or
22%, where the FDWR of the proposed house is greater than 22%, and

clauses.text: for [REF:term:bldng:buildings] of [REF:term:rdntl-cc:residential occupancy] containing more than 2 [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] ,

articles.title: Modeling HVAC System of Reference House

content.text: Where multiple HVAC systems serve a single space, the energy model calculations for the reference house shall use the same order of priority as that used for the proposed house. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent1:long] .)
The energy model calculations for the reference house shall include the same features as those used for the proposed house with regard to

clauses.text: the principal heating and cooling energy sources, which are gas, electricity, oil, propane, wood or a heat pump,
the primary and secondary energy sources, which are gas, electricity, oil, propane, wood or a heat pump, and
the ventilation rate (see [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art11.sent6:long] ).

content.text: Except as required in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8.sent1:long] , the reference house shall be modeled without a heat-recovery ventilator.
The ventilation system shall be modeled as operating 8 hours a day.

The heating system and, where installed, the cooling system shall be sized in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect33.subsect5.art1:long] with regard to total heat output capacity and nominal cooling capacity. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote293:short] .)
The part-load performance of HVAC equipment in the reference house shall be calculated using

clauses.text: modeled part-load performance characteristics, where applicable, or

the performance values for each type of system multiplied by an adjustment factor from [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table1:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table2:long] or [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table3:long] as follows:

subclauses.text: for [REF:term:frnc:furnaces] , by multiplying the [REF:term:frnc:furnace] steady-state efficiency by the adjustment factor given in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table1:long] ,

for heat pumps and air conditioners, by multiplying the heat pump steady-state coefficient of performance by the adjustment factor given in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table2:long] , and

for [REF:term:blr:boilers] , combination space-heating and service water heating systems, and integrated mechanical systems, by multiplying the net-full-load heating efficiency by the adjustment factor given in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art15.table3:long] .

content.text: The performance of the HVAC equipment in the reference house shall be modeled

clauses.text: as conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] for the corresponding type, fuel source and capacity of equipment in the proposed house, or

where the HVAC equipment for the proposed house is not addressed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art10.table1:long] , as a gas warm-air [REF:term:frnc:furnace] with a minimum performance rating of 92% annual fuel utilization efficiency.

content.text: Where a heat-recovery ventilator is installed in the reference house, the energy model calculations shall only account for the recovery of sensible heat using the efficiency ratings in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art9.sent3:long] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote295:short] .)
The energy model calculations shall assume all ventilation and circulation fans required to be modeled in the reference house are equipped with permanent-split capacitor (PSC) motors.

Where a forced-air system is installed in the reference house, the energy model calculations shall assume the circulation fan operates when the heating, cooling or principal ventilation system is called for.
Where the reference house contains multiple HVAC systems, the circulation fan power shall be the sum of the circulation fan power capacity of each system.

The principal ventilation flow rate, in L/s, prescribed in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect32:long] shall be multiplied by 2.32 W/L/s to determine the ventilation fan power capacity, in W, to be used in the energy model calculations for each fan on the exhaust side and, where applicable, on the supply side.

Where a heat-recovery ventilator is required in the reference house in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect3.art8:long] , the ventilation flow rate, in L/s, in the zone served by the pool or hot tub shall be multiplied by 4.18 W/L/s to determine the heat-recovery ventilator power, in W, to be used in the energy model calculations.
Where a forced-air system is installed in the reference house, the system's capacity, in W, shall be multiplied by one of the following factors to determine the circulation fan flow rate, in L/s:

clauses.text: 0.0604 for heat pumps, and
0.0251 for all other types of heating systems.

content.text: Where a forced-air system is installed in the reference house, the circulation fan flow rate, in L/s, shall be multiplied by 2.30 W/L/s to determine the circulation fan power capacity, in W.

For natural gas-, oil-, propane- and wood-burning heating systems, the energy model calculations shall set the auxiliary electricity capacity, including that of combustion fans, to 208 W during operation.

articles.title: Modeling Service Water Heating System of Reference House

content.text: The energy source of the reference house's service water heating system, which is gas, electricity, oil, propane, wood or a heat pump, shall be the same as that for the system in the proposed house.
The service water heating system in the reference house shall be sized in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect31.subsect6:long] with regard to output capacity.

Except as required by [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect5.art16.table1:long] , the performance of the service water heating equipment in the reference house shall be modeled as conforming to [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect36.subsect4.art2.table1:long] for the energy source, capacity and type of service water heating equipment in the proposed house.

clauses.text: thermal transmittance of above-ground walls and roof-ceiling assemblies,
thermal transmittance of floors and walls in contact with the ground, or with space that is not [REF:term:cnd-sp:conditioned space] ,
thermal transmittance and solar heat gain of windows, doors and skylights,
air leakage through the [REF:term:ar-brr-ss:air barrier system] ,
internal heat gains from occupants and equipment, and
heat recovery from exhaust ventilation.

the target "percent improvement" is met or exceeded. (See Note A-9.36.6.3.(5)(b).)

content.text: Energy modeling shall be performed using a computer program that employs calculation methods that have been tested in accordance with [REF:standard:ansiashrae140] , "Evaluation of Building Energy Analysis Computer Programs" with variations in the computer program from the range recommended therein reported in accordance with Division C.

content.text: For [REF:term:bldng:buildings] conforming to the requirements of any of Steps 3 to 5, energy modeling shall account for the air leakage rate derived in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect38.subsect7:long] . (See Note A-9.36.6.4.(3).)

(See Note A-9.36.6.5.(1).)

content.text: The percent heat loss reduction shall be calculated by subtracting the annual gross space heat loss of the proposed house from the annual gross space heat loss of the reference house and dividing the result by the annual gross space heat loss of the reference house.

The percent improvement shall be calculated by subtracting the annual energy consumption of the proposed house from the house energy target of the reference house and dividing the result by the house energy target of the reference house.
