bc_amendments.content: 3.1.6.4.(1)Encapsulation of Mass Timber ElementsThe general intent of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:long] is that all exposed surfaces of the mass timber elements be encapsulated, including the upper surface of a mass timber floor assembly. However, the exposed surfaces in certain concealed spaces formed by or contained within mass timber elements are exempted from complying with this Sentence (see  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent4:long] ,  [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent2:medium]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art17.sent2:medium] , and Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art7:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art12:short] ). Moreover, the upper surface of a mass timber roof assembly need not be encapsulated where there is no concealed space above it. As well, the exterior side of a mass timber exterior wall assembly need not be encapsulated; however, the provisions of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9:long]  and Subsection [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3:long] for exterior walls still need to be considered.

3.1.6.4.(1)Encapsulation of Mass Timber ElementsThe general intent of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent1:long] , which generally applies for any building where a 50- or 70-minute encapsulation rating is otherwise required, is that all exposed surfaces of the mass timber elements be encapsulated, including the upper surface of a mass timber floor assembly. However, for some buildings, depending on the building height and occupancy, portions of mass timber elements are permitted to be exposed to varying degrees in accordance with the permissions stated in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent8:short] . Also, the exposed surfaces in certain concealed spaces formed by or contained within mass timber elements are exempted from complying with this Sentence (see  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art3.sent4:long] ,  [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art16.sent2:medium]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art17.sent2:medium] , and Articles [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art7:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art12:short] ). Moreover, the upper surface of a mass timber roof assembly need not be encapsulated where there is no concealed space above it. As well, the exterior side of a mass timber exterior wall assembly need not be encapsulated; however, the provisions of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9:long] and  Subsection [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3:long] for exterior walls still need to be considered.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Updated to reference Sentences 3.1.6.4.(3) to (8) instead of (3) to (6), and updated Article references

bc_amendments.content: 3.1.6.4.(3) to (6)Fire-Resistance Rating of Mass Timber with Exposed SurfacesPortions of mass timber elements required to have a fire-resistance rating are permitted to be exposed in accordance with the permissions stated in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:long]  to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent6:short] ; however, it is important to note that applying those permissions does not waive the requirement for these elements to have a fire-resistance rating.

3.1.6.4.(3) to (8)Fire-Resistance Rating of Mass Timber with Exposed SurfacesPortions of mass timber elements required to have a fire-resistance rating are permitted to be exposed in accordance with the permissions stated in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:long] to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent8:short] ; however, it is important to note that applying those permissions does not waive the requirement for these elements to have a fire-resistance rating. In the calculation of the total wall area of the perimeter of a suite or fire compartment in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent3:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent5:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent7:number] , the area of any wall openings, such as doors or windows, is included.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Updated note number to (3) to (8), updated sentence references to include calculation details for wall area in Sentences (3), (5) and (7)

bc_amendments.content: 3.1.6.4.(4)Exposed Surfaces of Mass Timber WallsThe primary objective of encapsulating mass timber elements is to limit the probability that these elements will significantly contribute to fire spread and fire duration in the event of a fire. Since thick wood members require a source of imposed heat flux to burn, the stipulation in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent4.clause1:long] that the exposed surfaces of mass timber walls face the same direction within a suite is intended to reduce the potential of re-radiation between burning mass timber surfaces that face each other, which could sustain flaming combustion into the decay phase of a fire if the sprinkler system failed to operate or to control the fire. Additionally, the maximum percentage of exposed surface area stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4:long] is low so that it is not sufficient to sustain a ventilation-controlled fire that might provide the radiation required to sustain flaming combustion into the decay phase of a fire if the sprinkler system failed to operate or to control the fire.

3.1.6.4.(4)Exposed Surfaces of Mass Timber WallsThe primary objective of encapsulating mass timber elements is to limit the probability that these elements will significantly contribute to fire spread and fire duration in the event of a fire. Since thick wood members require a source of imposed heat flux to burn, the stipulation in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4.sent4.clause1:long] that any portions of the exposed surfaces of different mass timber walls within a suite either face the same direction or have a minimum horizontal distance between one another. If the sprinkler system fails to operate or to control the fire, this directional orientation or minimum distance is intended to avoid or reduce the potential for re-radiation between portions of burning mass timber surfaces on different walls, and particularly those that either face or are in close proximity to one another, which could sustain flaming combustion into the decay phase of a fire. Additionally, if the sprinkler system fails to operate or to control the fire, the maximum percentages of exposed surface areas and maximum flame-spread ratings stated in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art4:long] are intended to be insufficient to sustain a ventilation-controlled fire that might provide the radiation required to sustain flaming combustion into the decay phase of a fire.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Updated to reference Clause 3.1.6.4.(4)(a) and expanded explanation about directional orientation and minimum distance requirements

bc_amendments.content: 3.1.6.6.Encapsulation MaterialsResearch has been conducted on different types of encapsulation materials, such as gypsum board, gypsum concrete and cement board. The results of tests using an intermediate-scale furnace and of cone calorimeter tests indicate that a combustible timber element protected with a 38 mm thick layer of gypsum-concrete topping or with two layers of 12.7 mm Type X gypsum board will not ignite or contribute significant heat to a fire until average temperatures of 325–380°C are attained at the interface between the encapsulation material or assembly of materials and the combustible substrate. These temperatures are consistent with the ignition temperatures of wood-based materials.

3.1.6.6.Encapsulation MaterialsResearch has been conducted on different types of encapsulation materials, such as gypsum board, gypsum concrete and cement board. The results of tests using an intermediate-scale furnace and of cone calorimeter tests indicate that a combustible timber element protected with a 38 mm thick layer of gypsum-concrete topping or with one (25 min) , two (50 min) or three (80 min) layers of 12.7 mm Type X gypsum board or two layers (70 min) of 15.9 mm Type X gypsum board will not ignite or contribute significant heat to a fire until the time at which average temperatures of 325°C to 380°C are attained at the interface between the encapsulation material or assembly of materials and the combustible substrate. These temperatures are consistent with the ignition temperatures of wood-based materials.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Updated layer specifications to include specific timing (25 min, 50 min, 80 min, 70 min) and board thickness details (12.7 mm and 15.9 mm Type X gypsum board)

bc_amendments.content: 3.1.6.6.(2)Protection of Gypsum Board from Foot TrafficWhere gypsum board is used as the encapsulation material on the top of a mass timber floor assembly, it should be protected from physical impact arising from normal pedestrian traffic that could damage it and possibly compromise its encapsulation rating.

3.1.6.6.(6)Protection of Gypsum Board from Foot TrafficWhere gypsum board is used as the encapsulation material on the top of a mass timber floor assembly, it should be protected from physical impact arising from normal pedestrian traffic that could damage it and possibly compromise its encapsulation rating.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Changed note number from A-3.1.6.6.(2) to A-3.1.6.6.(6)

bc_amendments.content: 3.1.6.9.(1) and (2)Exterior CladdingThe requirements in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9.sent1:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9.sent2:short] are intended to reduce the potential for fire spread on the exterior cladding of buildings of encapsulated mass timber construction through the use of noncombustible finishes on the exterior of the wall assembly or the use of a cladding/wall assembly that has been proven to resist flame propagation. These cladding/wall assembly combinations can be used as infill or panel-type walls between structural elements, or attached directly to a loadbearing structural system. Note that the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9:long] do not supersede the provisions in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3:long] regarding spatial separation and exposure protection.

3.1.6.9.(1), (2), (4) and (6)Exterior CladdingThe requirements in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9.sent1:long]  [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9.sent2:number] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9.sent4:number] and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9.sent6:number] are intended to reduce the potential for fire spread on the exterior cladding of buildings of encapsulated mass timber construction through the use of noncombustible finishes on the exterior of the wall assembly or the use of a cladding/wall assembly that has been proven to resist flame propagation as a function of increasing building height, including provisions to allow 100% combustible cladding where the height does not exceed 4 storeys. These cladding/wall assembly combinations can be used as infill or panel-type walls between structural elements, or attached directly to a loadbearing structural system. Note that the requirements in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect6.art9:long] do not supersede the provisions in  Subsection [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect3:long] regarding spatial separation and exposure protection.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Updated note number to include (4) and (6); added references to Sentences (4) and (6); added provision about 100% combustible cladding for buildings up to 4 storeys

bc_amendments.content: 3.1.11.5.(3) and (4)Fire Blocks in Concealed SpacesTo reduce the risk of fire spread in combustible concealed spaces within the types of buildings referred to in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect11.art5.sent3:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect11.art5.sent4:short] , fire blocking is required regardless of whether the horizontal concealed space is protected by sprinklers or not, unless the space is filled with noncombustible insulation so that any air gap at the top of the insulation is very small. (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.appendix.appnote42:long] for roof venting.)A 5- or 6-storey building constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art51:long] and buildings constructed in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art48:long] , [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art57:long]  or [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect2.art60:long] are required to be sprinklered in accordance with [REF:standard:nfpa13] (see [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect5.art12:long] ). [REF:standard:nfpa13] generally requires sprinklering of any concealed spaces of combustible construction or where large amounts of combustibles are present. However, [REF:standard:nfpa13] allows combustible concealed spaces not to be sprinklered in certain cases, including where concealed spaces are filled almost entirely with noncombustible insulation, where spaces contain only materials with a low flame-spread rating, and where limited access or the size of the space makes it impractical to install sprinklers. For certain types of construction in combustible concealed spaces that are not sprinklered, [REF:standard:nfpa13] mandates fire blocking beyond the minimum specified in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect11.art5.sent3:long] .

3.1.11.5.(3) and (4)Fire Blocks in Concealed SpacesTo reduce the risk of fire spread in combustible concealed spaces within the types of buildings referred to in  Sentences [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect11.art5.sent3:long]  and [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect1.subsect11.art5.sent4:short] , fire blocking is required regardless of whether the horizontal concealed space is protected by sprinklers or not, unless the space is filled with noncombustible insulation so that any air gap at the top of the insulation is very small. bc_amendments.content: 3.2.10.Fire Protection and Firefighting Assumptions for Residential Buildings with a Single Exit.The firefighting assumptions discussed in Note A-3 raise circumstances where additional firefighting capabilities and additional building protection measures may be required. The provisions in Subsection 3.2.10. for residential buildings with a single exit were developed with the expectation of a high level of capacity of the local fire department for fire prevention activities, fire suppression activities, the ability of the fire department to assist in egress of occupants in the event of an emergency, as well as a secure water supply for the function of the automatic sprinkler system and the manual fire suppression activities of a responding fire department.<bold>Fire Prevention</bold>Maintenance of fire safety systems is essential for all buildings but becomes increasingly important when redundancies, such as a second and separate exit, are reduced or eliminated. The provisions for residential buildings with single exit stairs were developed with the expectation that fire officials routinely enforce the British Columbia Fire Code to ensure that the inspection intervals specified within are carried out, and that follow up inspections resulting from observed non-compliances occur at expedited intervals. Building owners and managers are required to be actively involved in carrying out the maintenance and upkeep of the building's fire safety systems. Residential buildings with a single exit should not be located in jurisdictions where a high level of fire prevention oversight cannot be maintained.<bold>Fire Suppression</bold>The provisions for residential buildings with single exit stairs were developed with the expectation that a permanent, paid fire department is available to respond to a fire event twenty-four hours a day, every day. Firefighting personnel are expected to have a high level of training and the fire department is expected to be suitably equipped to provide fire suppression activities appropriate to the buildings and developments in their jurisdiction within tight response times. Residential buildings with a single exit should not be located in jurisdictions where a high level of fire suppression activities cannot be maintained.<bold>Egress and Safety of Occupants</bold>The premise of egress in the British Columbia Building Code is that occupants of residential buildings receive early notification of a fire event, and occupants are able to respond unassisted in such an event. Early notification however does not guarantee occupant self-evacuation and when redundancies, such as a second and separate exit, are reduced or eliminated, occupant response options are likewise reduced. The provisions for residential buildings with single exit stairs were developed with the expectation that the local fire department has a service level that can coordinate and assist occupants with moving to a safe place in a fire event. Building owners and managers must be actively involved in fire safety planning in conjunction with the local fire department. Residential buildings with a single exit should not be located in jurisdictions where a service level that includes search and rescue by firefighting personnel cannot be maintained.<bold>Water Supply</bold>The British Columbia Building Code requires an adequate water supply for firefighting be readily available and of sufficient volume and pressure to enable emergency response personnel to control fire growth so as to enable the safe evacuation of occupants and the conduct of search and rescue operations, prevent the fire from spreading to adjacent buildings, and provide a limited measure of property protection. As for any water-based fire protection systems or suppression activities, the water supply serving the building needs to be dependable over the life of the building through seasonal droughts and other eventualities. The provisions for residential buildings with single exit stairs were developed with the expectation of a highly dependable water supply would be available during construction and throughout the lifecycle of the building. Redundancies such as secondary or back up water supplies should to be considered to limit the probability that the water supply may become insufficient for an extended or even temporary period.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10 explaining fire protection and firefighting assumptions for residential buildings with single exit stairs

bc_amendments.content: 3.2.10.1.(4)Residential Buildings Not Permitted.The residential uses described in Sentence 3.2.10.1.(4) include short term as well as long term accommodations where Subsection 3.2.10. is not permitted to apply. For example, longer-term hotels and rooming houses sometimes referred to as single room occupancy hotels or single room accommodations with or without private bathrooms or kitchens are not permitted to apply Subsection 3.2.10.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10.1.(4) clarifying residential buildings not permitted under Subsection 3.2.10

bc_amendments.content: 3.2.10.2.(1) and (2)Automatic Sprinkler Systems.Automatic sprinkler systems serving a building to which Subsection 3.2.10. applies must be sprinklered in accordance with NFPA 13, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems," regardless of the permissions for other buildings to follow the NFPA 13R, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems in low-Rise Residential Occupancies," or the NFPA 13D, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems in One- and Two-Family Dwellings and Manufactured Homes," standards. All balconies and decks regardless of depth must be sprinklered.The requirement for sprinklers conforming to NFPA 13, "Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems," means that a fire alarm system described in Subsection 3.2.4. is also required.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10.2.(1) and (2) regarding automatic sprinkler system requirements for buildings under Subsection 3.2.10

bc_amendments.content: 3.2.10.2.(3)Exit Facility.The single exit facility serving a building to which Subsection 3.2.10. applies shall either be of noncombustible construction or shall be finished as an exit stair serving an unsprinklered high building described in Subsection 3.2.6. Should a fire event occur, protection of the exit stairs must not solely rely on the automatic sprinkler system.A 1 500 mm wide exit facility facilitates the movement and passing of people for regular use as well as in an emergency. The design of intermediate handrails, such as for widths exceeding 1 700 mm, should consider the movement of emergency personnel including their equipment on each side. The design of the exit facility must also consider misuse and proactively deter the storage or collection of materials so as not to obstruct passage and to minimize fuel load. For example, excess landing areas and alcoves in all exits (not limited to residential buildings with single exit stairs) must be carefully designed to deter any activities other than exiting and accessing floor areas as per Sentence 3.4.4.4.(6). Void spaces underneath stairs should be avoided. Landings must have signage to remind occupants that storage is not permitted in exit facilities.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10.2.(3) regarding exit facility design and construction requirements

bc_amendments.content: 3.2.10.2.(4)Exit Facility Discharge.Fire department access to buildings to which Subsection 3.2.10. applies must be provided to the principal entrance as well as to the access point most directly connected to the exit facility. As such, the exit facility discharge must be located to coordinate with the fire department access route described in Subsection 3.2.5.Designers should consider locating the exit facility discharge in close proximity to the principal entrance for the benefit of coordinating multiple access points with the fire department access route but also to avoid unintended use of the exit facility for package delivery or other material drop-off. There should be clear distinction between the principal building entrance (likely connecting to a lobby and elevator) and the exit facility discharge so that activities such as deliveries can be intuitively completed in the safe and intended manner. Locating the exit facility discharge in close proximity to the principal building entrance also reduces the potential that an access point is located in an isolated location of the building which could increase building and occupant security concerns.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10.2.(4) regarding exit facility discharge location and coordination with fire department access

bc_amendments.content: 3.2.10.4.(3)Suite Entry Doors.Sentence 3.2.10.4.(3) supersedes the permission in Article 3.1.8.12. to reduce the fire-protection rating of closures. Suite entry doors with less than a 45 min fire-protection rating are not permitted in buildings to which Subsection 3.2.10. applies, nor would these doors be permitted any undercuts such as described in Article 9.32.3.10.
bc_amendments.change_summary: Added Note A-3.2.10.4.(3) regarding suite entry door fire-protection rating requirements

To calculate, the designer shall take the number of units that meet the criteria of [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect8.subsect5.art1.sent1.clause1:long] and then design not less than 20 percent of those units to be adaptable. bc_amendments.content: As a result of the updating procedure for the 2010 edition of the Code, the 1-in-50 reference wind velocity pressures remained unchanged for most of the locations listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC.table2:long] ; both increases and decreases were noted for the remaining locations. Many of the decreases resulted from the fact that anemometers at most of the stations used in the previous analysis were installed on lighthouses, airport hangers and other structures. Wind speeds on the tops of buildings are often much higher compared to those registered by a standard 10 m tower. Eliminating anemometer data recorded on the tops of buildings from the analysis resulted in lower values at several locations.

As a result of the updating procedure, the 1-in-50 reference wind velocity pressures remained unchanged for most of the locations listed in [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixC.table1:long] . However, the reference wind velocity pressures for some locations were revised to reflect the availability of additional wind data. bc_amendments.content: 9.36.1.3.(6)ExemptionsExamples of buildings and spaces that are exempted from the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect37:long] include seasonally heated buildings, storage and parking garages, small service buildings or service rooms and unconditioned spaces in buildings and unconditioned buildings such as storage warehouses. However, note that, where a building envelope assembly of an exempted building is adjacent to a conditioned space, this assembly must meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect37:long] .

9.36.1.3.(5)ExemptionsExamples of buildings and spaces that are exempted from the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect37:long] include seasonally heated buildings, storage and parking garages, small service buildings or service rooms and unconditioned spaces in buildings and unconditioned buildings such as storage warehouses. However, note that, where a building envelope assembly of an exempted building is adjacent to a conditioned space, this assembly must meet the requirements of [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.sect37:long] .

bc-cc-t-ccbl.definition: means an area and its facilities, or both, as required by this Code, which is easy to approach, enter, exit, operate, participate in, pass to and from, and use safely and independently by [REF:term:bc-prsn-wth-dsblts:persons with disabilities] .

cc-t-xt.definition: means that part of a [REF:term:mn-f-gr:means of egress] within a [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] that provides access to an [REF:term:xt:exit] serving the [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] .

bc-dptbl-dwllng-nt.definition: means a [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] designed and constructed with some [REF:term:bc-cc-t-ccbl:accessible] features and which accommodates the future modification to provide more [REF:term:bc-cc-t-ccbl:accessible] features.

dfrzng.definition: means the adhesion of [REF:term:l:soil] to a [REF:term:fndtn-nt:foundation unit] resulting from the freezing of [REF:term:l:soil] water. (Also referred to as “frost grip.”)

grc-ccp.definition: (Group G) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof that is located on land that is associated with and devoted to the practice of farming, and is used for the purpose of producing crops, raising farm animals, or preparing, marketing, storing or processing agricultural products. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div1:short] .)

grc-ccp-nh.term: Agricultural occupancy with no human occupants (Group G, Division 4)
grc-ccp-nh.definition: means an [REF:term:grc-ccp:agricultural occupancy] that is not intended to be occupied by persons under normal use and is generally used for the storage of agricultural materials and by-products. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div2:short] .)

r-brrr.definition: means the assembly installed to provide a continuous barrier to the movement of air.

r-pprtd-.definition: means a structure consisting of a pliable membrane that achieves and maintains its shape and support by internal air pressure.

lrm-gnl.definition: means an audible signal transmitted throughout a zone or zones or throughout a [REF:term:bldng:building] to advise occupants that a fire emergency exists.

lrt-gnl.definition: means an audible signal to advise designated persons of a fire emergency.

ltrtn.definition: means a change or extension to any matter or thing or to any [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] regulated by this Code.

astc.definition: means a single number rating of the airborne sound attenuation of [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies separating two adjoining spaces, taking into account both the direct and flanking sound transmission paths. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7:short] .) (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote79:long] .)

pplnc.definition: means a device to convert fuel into energy and includes all components, controls, wiring and piping required to be part of the device by the applicable standard referred to in this Code.

rtn-grnd.definition: means a confined body of water under pressure in the ground.

mbl-ccpn.definition: (Group A) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] or the use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof by a gathering of persons for civic, political, travel, religious, social, educational, recreational or like purposes, or for the consumption of food or drink.

ttc-r-rf.definition: means the space between the roof and the ceiling of the top [REF:term:tr:storey] or between a dwarf wall and a sloping roof.

bc-thrt-hvn.definition: means the governmental body responsible for the enforcement of any part of this Code or the official or agency designated by that body to exercise such a function. Notwithstanding this definition, the Chief Inspector of Mines has the sole responsibility for administration and enforcement in respect to all [REF:term:bldng:buildings] , structures and site services used at a mine, as defined in the Mines Act.

brrr-fr.definition: means that a [REF:term:bldng:building] and its facilities can be approached, entered, and used by persons with physical or sensory disabilities.

bmnt.definition: means a [REF:term:tr:storey] or [REF:term:tr:storeys] of a [REF:term:bldng:building] located below the [REF:term:frt-tr:first storey] .

brng-rfc.definition: means the contact surface between a [REF:term:fndtn-nt:foundation unit] and the [REF:term:l:soil ] or [REF:term:rck:rock] upon which it bears.

blr.definition: means an [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] intended to supply hot water or steam for space heating, processing or power purposes.

br-wl-bnd.definition: means an imaginary continuous straight band extending vertically and horizontally through the [REF:term:bldng:building] or part of the [REF:term:bldng:building] , within which [REF:term:br-wl-pnl:braced wall panels] are constructed.

br-wl-pnl.definition: means a portion of a wood-frame wall where bracing, sheathing, cladding or interior finish is designed and installed to provide the required resistance to lateral loads due to wind or earthquake.

brchng.definition: means a [REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipe ] or chamber for receiving [REF:term:fl:flue] gases from one or more [REF:term:fl:flue] connections and for discharging these gases through a single [REF:term:fl:flue] connection.

bldng.definition: means any structure used or intended for supporting or sheltering any use or [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] .

bldng-r.definition: means the greatest horizontal area of a [REF:term:bldng:building] above [REF:term:grade:grade] within the outside surface of exterior walls or within the outside surface of exterior walls and the centre line of [REF:term:frwll:firewalls] .

bldng-hg.definition: (in [REF:term:tr:storeys] ) means the number of [REF:term:tr:storeys] contained between the roof and the floor of the [REF:term:frt-tr:first storey] .

bn-nd-pr.definition: (Group D) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] or use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof for the transaction of business or the rendering or receiving of professional or personal services.

ca.definition: means the provision of services other than [REF:term:trtm:treatment] by or through care facility management to residents who require these services because of cognitive, physical or behavioural limitations.

ca-cc.definition: (Group B, Division 3) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] or use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof, other than a [REF:term:hm-tp-ccpnc:home-type care occupancy] , where [REF:term:ca:care] is provided to residents. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div4:short] .)

cvt-wll.definition: means a construction of masonry units laid with a cavity between the wythes. The wythes are tied together with metal ties or bonding units, and are relied on to act together in resisting lateral loads.

chmn.definition: means a primarily vertical shaft enclosing at least one [REF:term:fl:flue] for conducting [REF:term:fl:flue] gases to the outdoors.

chmn-lnr.definition: means a conduit containing a [REF:term:chmn:chimney]  [REF:term:fl:flue] used as a lining of a [REF:term:mnr-r-cn:masonry or concrete chimney] .

clr.definition: means a device or assembly for closing an opening through a [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] or an exterior wall, such as a door, a shutter, a damper, wired glass or glass block, and includes all components such as hardware, closing devices, frames and anchors.

cmbtbl.definition: means that a material fails to meet the acceptance criteria of [REF:standard:ulcs114]

cmbtbl-c.definition: means that type of construction that does not meet the requirements for [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction] or [REF:term:ncps-mt-nstr:encapsulated mass timber construction] .

cmbtbl-dst.definition: means dusts and particles that are ignitable and liable to produce an explosion.

cmbtbl-fbr.definition: means finely divided, combustible vegetable or animal fibres and thin sheets or flakes of such materials which, in a loose, unbaled condition, present a flash fire hazard, including cotton, wool, hemp, sisal, jute, kapok, paper and cloth.

cmbtbl-l.definition: means a liquid having a [REF:term:flh-pnt:flash point] at or above 37.8°C and below 93.3°C .

cnd-sp.definition: means any space within a [REF:term:bldng:building] , the temperature of which is controlled to limit variation in response to the exterior ambient temperature by the provision, either directly or indirectly, of heating or cooling over substantial portions of the year.

cntrctr.definition: means a person who contracts with an [REF:term:wnr:owner] or their authorized agent to undertake a project, and includes an [REF:term:wnr:owner] who contracts with more than one person for the work on a project or undertakes the work on a project or any part thereof.

cntnd-r.definition: means a supervised area containing one or more rooms in which occupant movement is restricted to a single room by security measures not under the control of the occupant.

cktp.definition: means a cooking surface having one or more burners or heating elements.

bc-crdntng-rgstrd-prfsnl.definition: means a [REF:term:bc-rgstrd-prfssnl:registered professional] retained under  Clause [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect7.art2.sent1.clause1:number] of Division C to coordinate all design work and field reviews of the [REF:term:bc-rgstrd-prfssnl:registered professionals] who are required for a project.

dngr-gd.definition: means products, materials or substances that are [LIST:bulleted](See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div5:short] .)

dd-ld.definition: means the weight of all permanent structural and non-structural components of a [REF:term:bldng:building] .

dp-fndtn.definition: means a [REF:term:fndtn-nt:foundation unit] that provides support for a [REF:term:bldng:building ] by transferring loads either by end-bearing to [REF:term:l:soil] or [REF:term:rck:rock] at considerable depth below the [REF:term:bldng:building] , or by adhesion or friction, or both, in the [REF:term:l:soil] or [REF:term:rck:rock] in which it is placed. [REF:term:pl:Piles] are the most common type of [REF:term:dp-fndtn:deep foundation] .

dgnr.definition: means the person responsible for the design.

dtnt-cc.definition: (Group B, Division 1) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] by persons who are restrained from or are incapable of evacuating to a safe location without the assistance of another person because of security measures not under their control.

drct-vnt.definition: (as applying to a fuel-fired space- or water-heating [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] ) means an [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] and its venting system in which all the combustion air is supplied directly from the outdoors and the products of combustion are vented directly to the outdoors via independent, totally enclosed passageways connected directly to the [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] .

dst-bvg-a.definition: means a beverage that is produced by fermentation and contains more than 20% by volume of water-miscible alcohol.

dstr.definition: means a [REF:term:prcs-plnt:process plant] where [REF:term:dst-bvg-a:distilled beverage alcohols] are produced, concentrated or otherwise processed, and includes facilities on the same site where the concentrated products may be blended, mixed, stored or packaged.

dwllng-n.definition: means a [REF:term:t:suite] operated as a housekeeping unit, used or intended to be used by one or more persons and usually containing cooking, eating, living, sleeping and sanitary facilities.

ncps-mt-nstr.definition: means that type of construction in which a degree of fire safety is attained by the use of encapsulated mass timber elements with an [REF:term:ncps-rtng:encapsulation rating] and minimum dimensions for structural members and other [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies.

ncps-rtng.definition: means the time in minutes that a material or assembly of materials will delay the ignition and combustion of encapsulated mass timber elements when it is exposed to fire under specified conditions of test and performance criteria, or as otherwise prescribed by this Code.

xcvtn.definition: means the space created by the removal of [REF:term:l:soil] , [REF:term:rck:rock] or [REF:term:fll:fill] for the purposes of construction.

xht-dct.definition: means a duct through which air is conveyed from a room or space to the outdoors.

xt.definition: means that part of a [REF:term:mn-f-gr:means of egress] , including doorways, that leads from the [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] it serves to a separate [REF:term:bldng:building] , an open public thoroughfare, or an exterior open space protected from fire exposure from the [REF:term:bldng:building] and having access to an open public thoroughfare. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div6:short] .)

xt-lvl.definition: means the level of an [REF:term:xt:exit] stairway at which an exterior [REF:term:xt:exit] door or [REF:term:xt:exit] passageway leads to the exterior.

xt-tr.definition: (as applying to [REF:internal:nbc.divB.part3.sect2.subsect6:long] ) means a [REF:term:tr:storey ] having an exterior [REF:term:xt:exit] door.

xpng-bld.definition: means that part of the exterior wall of a [REF:term:bldng:building] that faces one direction and is located between ground level and the ceiling of its top [REF:term:tr:storey] or, where a [REF:term:bldng:building] is divided into [REF:term:fr-cmprt:fire compartments] , the exterior wall of a [REF:term:fr-cmprt:fire compartment] that faces one direction.

fctr-blt.definition: means a [REF:term:chmn:chimney] consisting entirely of factory-made parts, each designed to be assembled with the other without requiring fabrication on site.

frm-bldn.definition: means a [REF:term:bldng:building ] or part thereof that contains an [REF:term:grc-ccp:agricultural occupancy] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div7:short] .)

bc-fld-rvw.definition: means a review of the work[LIST:bulleted]that a registered professional in their professional discretion considers necessary to ascertain whether the work substantially complies in all material respects with the plans and supporting documents prepared by a registered professional.

fll.definition: means [REF:term:l:soil] , [REF:term:rck:rock] , rubble, industrial waste such as slag, organic material or a combination of these that is transported and placed on the natural surface of [REF:term:l:soil] or [REF:term:rck:rock] or organic terrain. It may or may not be compacted.

fr-blk.definition: means a material, component or system that restricts the spread of fire within a concealed space or from a concealed space to an adjacent space.

fr-cmprt.definition: means an enclosed space in a [REF:term:bldng:building] that is separated from all other parts of the [REF:term:bldng:building] by enclosing construction providing a [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] having a required [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] .

fr-dmpr.definition: means a [REF:term:clr:closure] consisting of a damper that is installed in an air distribution system or a wall or floor assembly and that is normally held open but designed to close automatically in the event of a fire in order to maintain the integrity of the [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] .

fr-dtctr.definition: means a device that detects a fire condition and automatically initiates an electrical signal to actuate an [REF:term:lrt-gnl:alert signal] or [REF:term:lrm-gnl:alarm signal ] and includes [REF:term:ht-dtctr:heat detectors] and [REF:term:mk-dtctr:smoke detectors] .

fr-ld.definition: (as applying to an [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] ) means the [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] contents of a room or [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] expressed in terms of the average weight of [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] materials per unit area, from which the potential heat liberation may be calculated based on the calorific value of the materials, and includes the furnishings, finished floor, wall and ceiling finishes, trim and temporary and movable [REF:term:prttn:partitions] .

fr-prtct.definition: means the time in minutes or hours that a [REF:term:clr:closure] will withstand the passage of flame when exposed to fire under specified conditions of test and performance criteria, or as otherwise prescribed in this Code.

fr-rtnc-.definition: means the time in minutes or hours that a material or assembly of materials will withstand the passage of flame and the transmission of heat when exposed to fire under specified conditions of test and performance criteria, or as determined by extension or interpretation of information derived therefrom as prescribed in this Code. (See  Sentence [REF:internal:nbc.divB.appendixD.appsect1.subsect2.article1.para2:long] in Appendix D of Division B.)

fr-rtrdn.definition: means wood or a wood product that has had its surface-burning characteristics, such as flame spread, rate of fuel contribution and density of smoke developed, reduced by impregnation with fire-retardant chemicals.

fr-prtn.definition: means a construction assembly that acts as a barrier against the spread of fire. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div8:short] .)

fr-tp.definition: means a system consisting of a material, component and means of support used to fill gaps between [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] or between [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] and other assemblies, or used around items that wholly or partially penetrate a [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] .

fr-tp-fl.definition: means a device intended for use in horizontal assemblies required to have a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] and incorporating protective ceiling membranes that operates to close off a duct opening through the membrane in the event of a fire.

frwll.definition: means a type of [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separation] of [REF:term:ncmbtbl-:noncombustible construction ] that subdivides a [REF:term:bldng:building] or separates adjoining [REF:term:bldng:buildings] to resist the spread of fire and that has a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] as prescribed in this Code and has structural stability to remain intact under fire conditions for the required fire-rated time.

frt-tr.definition: means the uppermost [REF:term:tr:storey] having its floor level not more than 2 m above [REF:term:grade:grade] .

flm-prd-.definition: means an index or classification indicating the extent of spread-of-flame on the surface of a material or an assembly of materials as determined in a standard fire test as prescribed in this Code.

flmmbl-l.definition: means a liquid having a [REF:term:flh-pnt:flash point] below 37.8°C and having a vapour pressure not more than 275.8 kPa (absolute) at 37.8°C as determined by [REF:standard:astmd323]

flh-pnt.definition: means the minimum temperature at which a liquid within a container gives off vapour in sufficient concentration to form an ignitable mixture with air near the surface of the liquid.

flght.definition: means a series of steps between landings. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div9:short] .)

flr-r.definition: means the space on any [REF:term:tr:storey] of a [REF:term:bldng:building] between exterior walls and required [REF:term:frwll:firewalls] , including the space occupied by interior walls and [REF:term:prttn:partitions] , but not including [REF:term:xt:exits] , [REF:term:vrtcl-rv:vertical service spaces] , and their enclosing assemblies.

fl.definition: means an enclosed passageway for conveying [REF:term:fl:flue] gases.

fl-cllr.definition: means the portion of a fuel-fired [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] designed for the attachment of the [REF:term:fl-pp:flue pipe] or [REF:term:brchng:breeching] .

fl-pp.definition: means the pipe connecting the [REF:term:fl-cllr:flue collar] of an [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] to a [REF:term:chmn:chimney] .

frcd-r-f.definition: means a [REF:term:frnc:furnace] equipped with a fan that provides the primary means for the circulation of air.

fndtn.definition: means a system or arrangement of [REF:term:fndtn-nt:foundation units] through which the loads from a [REF:term:bldng:building] are transferred to supporting [REF:term:l:soil] or [REF:term:rck:rock] .

fndtn-nt.definition: means one of the structural members of the [REF:term:fndtn:foundation] of a [REF:term:bldng:building ] such as a footing, raft or [REF:term:pl:pile] .

frt-ctn.definition: means the phenomenon that occurs when water in [REF:term:l:soil] is subjected to freezing which, because of the water/ice phase change or ice lens growth, results in a total volume increase or the build-up of expansive forces under confined conditions or both, and the subsequent thawing that leads to loss of [REF:term:l:soil ] strength and increased compressibility.

frnc.definition: means a [REF:term:pc-htng-:space-heating appliance] using warm air as the heating medium and usually having provision for the attachment of ducts.

g-vnt.definition: means that portion of a venting system designed to convey vent gases to the outdoors from the [REF:term:vnt-cnnc:vent connector] of a gas-fired [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] or directly from the [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] when a [REF:term:vnt-cnnc:vent connector] is not used.

grade.definition: means the lowest of the average levels of finished ground adjoining each exterior wall of a [REF:term:bldng:building] , except that localized depressions need not be considered in the determination of average levels of finished ground. (See [REF:term:frt-tr:First storey] and [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div10:short] .)

grndwtr.definition: means a free standing body of water in the ground.

grndwtr-.definition: (groundwater table) means the top surface of a free standing body of water in the ground.

guard.definition: means a protective barrier around openings in floors or at the open sides of stairs, landings, balconies, [REF:term:mzznn:mezzanines] , galleries, raised [REF:term:wlkw:walkways] or other locations to prevent accidental falls from one level to another. Such a barrier may or may not have openings through it.

ht-dtctr.definition: means a [REF:term:fr-dtctr:fire detector] designed to operate at a predetermined temperature or rate of temperature rise.

hv-tmbr-.definition: means that type of [REF:term:cmbtbl-c:combustible construction] in which a degree of fire safety is attained by placing limitations on the sizes of wood structural members and on the thickness and composition of wood floors and roofs and by the avoidance of concealed spaces under floors and roofs.

bc-hrtg-bldng.definition: is a [REF:term:bldng:building] which is legally protected or officially recognized as a heritage property by the Provincial government or a local government. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote2a:short] .)

hgh-hzrd.definition: (Group F, Division 1) means an [REF:term:ndtrl-cc:industrial occupancy] containing sufficient quantities of highly [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] and flammable or explosive materials which, because of their inherent characteristics, constitute a special fire hazard.

hm-tp-ccpnc.definition: (Group B, Division 4) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] or use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] consisting of a single detached housekeeping unit where [REF:term:ca:care] is provided to residents and may include the living space of the caregiver and their family. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div11:short] .)

hrzntl-x.definition: means an [REF:term:xt:exit ] from one [REF:term:bldng:building] to another by means of a doorway, vestibule, [REF:term:wlkw:walkway] , bridge or balcony.

hrzntl-r.definition: means a space such as an attic, duct, ceiling, roof or crawl space oriented essentially in a horizontal plane, concealed and generally inaccessible, through which [REF:term:bldng:building] service facilities such as pipes, ducts and wiring may pass.

mpdd-gr-.definition: means a supervised area in which occupants have free movement but require the release, by security personnel, of security doors at the boundary before they are able to leave the area, but does not include a [REF:term:cntnd-r:contained use area] .

ndrct-rv.definition: means a [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:service water heater] that derives its heat from a heating medium such as warm air, steam or hot water.

ndtrl-cc.definition: (Group F) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] or use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof for the assembling, fabricating, manufacturing, processing, repairing or storing of goods and materials.

ntrcnnct.definition: means superimposed [REF:term:flr-r:floor areas] or parts of [REF:term:flr-r:floor areas ] in which floor assemblies that are required to be [REF:term:fr-prtn:fire separations] are penetrated by openings that are not provided with [REF:term:clr:closures] .

lmtng-dt.definition: means the distance from an [REF:term:xpng-bld:exposing building face] to a property line, the centre line of a [REF:term:trt:street] , lane or public thoroughfare, or to an imaginary line between 2 [REF:term:bldng:buildings] or [REF:term:fr-cmprt:fire compartments] on the same property, measured at right angles to the [REF:term:xpng-bld:exposing building face] .

lv-ld.definition: means a variable load due to the intended use and [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] that is to be assumed in the design of the structural members of a [REF:term:bldng:building] . It includes loads due to cranes and the pressure of liquids in containers.

ldbrng.definition: (as applying to a [REF:term:bldng:building] element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own [REF:term:dd-ld:dead load] .

lw-hzrd-.definition: (Group F, Division 3) means an [REF:term:ndtrl-cc:industrial occupancy ] in which the [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] content is not more than 50 kg/m^{2} or 1 200 MJ/m^{2} of [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] .

mjr-ccpn.definition: means the principal [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] for which a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof is used or intended to be used, and shall be deemed to include the subsidiary [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancies] that are an integral part of the principal [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] . The [REF:term:mjr-ccpn:major occupancy] classifications used in this Code are as follows:

mnr-r-cn.definition: means a [REF:term:chmn:chimney] of brick, stone, concrete or masonry units constructed on site.

mn-f-gr.definition: means a continuous path of travel provided for the escape of persons from any point in a [REF:term:bldng:building] or contained open space to a separate [REF:term:bldng:building] , an open public thoroughfare, or an exterior open space protected from fire exposure from the [REF:term:bldng:building] and having access to an open public thoroughfare. [REF:term:mn-f-gr:Means of egress ] includes [REF:term:xt:exits] and [REF:term:cc-t-xt:access to exits] .

mchnl-vnt.definition: (as applying to a fuel-fired space- or water-heating [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] ) means an [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] and its combustion venting system in which the products of combustion are entirely exhausted to the outdoors by a mechanical device, such as a fan, blower or aspirator, upstream or downstream from the combustion zone of the [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] , and the portion of the combustion venting system that is downstream of the fan, blower or aspirator is sealed and does not include draft hoods or draft control devices. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div12:short] .)

mdm-hzrd.definition: (Group F, Division 2) means an [REF:term:ndtrl-cc:industrial occupancy ] in which the [REF:term:cmbtbl:combustible] content is more than 50 kg/m^{2} or 1 200 MJ/m^{ 2} of [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] and not classified as a [REF:term:hgh-hzrd:high-hazard industrial occupancy] .

mrcntl-c.definition: (Group E) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] or use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof for the displaying or selling of retail goods, wares or merchandise.

mzznn.definition: means an intermediate floor assembly between the floor and ceiling of any room or [REF:term:tr:storey] and includes an interior balcony.

ncmbtbl.definition: means that a material meets the acceptance criteria of [REF:standard:ulcs114]

ncmbtbl-.definition: means that type of construction in which a degree of fire safety is attained by the use of [REF:term:ncmbtbl:noncombustible] materials for structural members and other [REF:term:bldng:building] assemblies.

ccpnc.definition: means the use or intended use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof for the shelter or support of persons, animals or property.

ccpnt-ld.definition: means the number of persons for which a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof is designed.

pn-r-tr.definition: means a [REF:term:tr:storey ] in which at least 25% of the total area of its perimeter walls is open to the outdoors in a manner that will provide cross-ventilation to the entire [REF:term:tr:storey] .

bc-wnr.definition: means any person, firm or corporation controlling the property under consideration during that period of the application of [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.sect1.subsect1.art1.sent1:long] of this Code.

prttn.definition: means an interior wall 1 [REF:term:tr:storey] or part- [REF:term:tr:storey] in height that is not [REF:term:ldbrng:loadbearing] .

prt-wll.definition: means a wall jointly owned and jointly used by 2 parties under easement agreement or by right in law, and erected at or upon a line separating 2 parcels of land each of which is, or is capable of being, a separate real-estate entity.

prchd-gr.definition: means a free standing body of water in the ground extending to a limited depth.

bc-prsn-wth-dsblts.definition: means persons who have a permanent or temporary physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others.

pl.definition: means a slender [REF:term:dp-fndtn:deep foundation unit] made of materials such as wood, steel or concrete or a combination thereof, that is either premanufactured and placed by driving, jacking, jetting or screwing, or cast-in-place in a hole formed by driving, excavating or boring. (Cast-in-place bored [REF:term:pl:piles] are often referred to as [REF:term:cn:caissons] in Canada.)

plnm.definition: means a chamber forming part of an air duct system.

plmbng-t.definition: means a drainage system, a venting system and a water system or parts thereof.

pt-dtr-b.definition: means a building that the authority having jurisdiction has determined is necessary for the provision of essential services to the general public in the event of a disaster and includes buildings meeting these criteria but not limited to[LIST:bulleted](See Note A-1.4.1.2.(1).)

prvt-wg-.definition: means a privately owned plant for the treatment and disposal of sewage (such as a septic tank with an absorption field).

prcs-plnt.definition: means an industrial occupancy where materials, including flammable liquids, combustible liquids or gases, are produced or used in a process. (See Table 3.2.7.1. of Division B of the British Columbia Fire Code.)

prt-flr-spc.definition: means that part of a [REF:term:flr-r:floor area] protected from the effects of fire and used as part of a [REF:term:mn-f-gr:means of egress] from an [REF:term:ntrcnnct:interconnected floor space] .

pblc-crr.definition: means a corridor that provides [REF:term:cc-t-xt:access to exit] from more than one [REF:term:t:suite] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div14:short] .)

pblc-w.definition: means a sidewalk, [REF:term:trt:street] , highway, square or other open space to which the public has access, as of right or by invitation, expressed or implied.

rmp.definition: means a path of travel having a slope steeper than 1 in 20.

bc-rgstrd-prfssnl-f-rcrd.definition: means a <italic>registered professional</italic> retained to undertake design work and field review in accordance with [REF:internal:nbc.divC.part2.sect2.subsect7:long] .

rpr-grg.definition: means a [REF:term:bldng:building ] or part thereof where facilities are provided for the repair or servicing of motor vehicles.

rdntl-cc.definition: (Group C) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] or use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof by persons for whom sleeping accommodation is provided but who are not harboured for the purpose of receiving [REF:term:ca:care] or [REF:term:trtm:treatment] and are not involuntarily detained.

rtrn-dct.definition: means a duct for conveying air from a space being heated, ventilated or air-conditioned back to the heating, ventilating or air-conditioning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] .

rm-jst.definition: means the outermost member in floor framing, other than blocking, be it parallel, perpendicular or on an angle to the floor joists. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div15:short] .)

rck.definition: means that portion of the earth's crust that is consolidated, coherent and relatively hard and is a naturally formed, solidly bonded, mass of mineral matter that cannot readily be broken by hand.

run.definition: means the horizontal distance between two adjacent tread nosings on a stair. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote29.figure2:long] in [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote29:long] of Division B.)

ntr-drng.definition: means a drainage system that conducts sewage.

bc-scnd-t.definition: means a self-contained [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling unit] located within a [REF:term:bldng:building] or portion of a [REF:term:bldng:building][LIST:bulleted] (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div16:short] .)

rvc-rm.definition: means a room provided in a [REF:term:bldng:building] to contain equipment associated with [REF:term:bldng:building] services. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div17:short] .)

rvc-pc.definition: means space provided in a [REF:term:bldng:building] to facilitate or conceal the installation of [REF:term:bldng:building] service facilities such as chutes, ducts, pipes, shafts or wires.

rvc-wtr-.definition: means a device for heating water for plumbing services.

hllw-fnd.definition: means a [REF:term:fndtn-nt:foundation unit] that derives its support from [REF:term:l:soil] or [REF:term:rck:rock] located close to the lowest part of the [REF:term:bldng:building] that it supports.

mk-lrm.definition: means a combined [REF:term:mk-dtctr:smoke detector] and audible alarm device designed to sound an alarm within the room or [REF:term:t:suite] in which it is located upon the detection of smoke within that room or [REF:term:t:suite] .

mk-dtctr.definition: means a [REF:term:fr-dtctr:fire detector] designed to operate when the concentration of airborne combustion products exceeds a predetermined level.

l.definition: means that portion of the earth's crust that is fragmentary, or such that some individual particles of a dried sample may be readily separated by agitation in water; it includes boulders, cobbles, gravel, sand, silt, clay and organic matter.

sld-m.definition: means a single wythe or multi-wythe construction made of [REF:term:sld-m-u:solid masonry units] or semi-solid, cored, or hollow masonry units, the cells of which may or may not be filled with mortar or grout. In multi-wythe masonry construction, the space between the wythes consists of a mortar-filled collar joint or grout-filled space and the wythes may or may not be constructed of the same masonry materials.

sld-m-u.definition: means a concrete block or brick unit, a clay brick unit, or calcium silicate brick unit whose net solid area is at least 75% of its gross area. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div18:short] .)

stc.definition: means a single number rating of the airborne sound attenuation of a [REF:term:bldng:building] assembly separating two adjoining spaces, taking into account the direct sound transmission path. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div3:short] .) (See also [REF:internal:nbc.divBV2.part9.appendix.appnote79:long] .)

pc-htr.definition: means a [REF:term:pc-htng-:space-heating appliance] for heating the room or space within which it is located, without the use of ducts.

pc-htng-.definition: means an [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] intended for the supplying of heat to a room or space directly, such as a [REF:term:pc-htr:space heater] , fireplace or [REF:term:nt-htr:unit heater] , or to rooms or spaces of a [REF:term:bldng:building] through a heating system such as a central [REF:term:frnc:furnace] or [REF:term:blr:boiler] .

prnklrd.definition: (as applying to a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof) means that the [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof is equipped with a system of automatic sprinklers.

tg.definition: means a space that is designed primarily for theatrical performances with provision for quick change scenery and overhead lighting, including environmental control for a wide range of lighting and sound effects and that is traditionally, but not necessarily, separated from the audience by a proscenium wall and curtain opening.

trg-grg.definition: means a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof intended for the storage or parking of motor vehicles and containing no provision for the repair or servicing of such vehicles. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div19:short] .)

trg-tp-r.definition: means a [REF:term:rvc-wtr-:service water heater] with an integral hot water storage tank.

tr.definition: means that portion of a [REF:term:bldng:building] that is situated between the top of any floor and the top of the floor next above it, and if there is no floor above it, that portion between the top of such floor and the ceiling above it.

tv.definition: means an [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] intended for cooking and space heating.

trt.definition: means any highway, road, boulevard, square or other improved thoroughfare 9 m or more in width, that has been dedicated or deeded for public use and is accessible to fire department vehicles and equipment.

brfc-nvt.definition: means the appraisal of the general subsurface conditions at a [REF:term:bldng:building] site by analysis of information gained by such methods as geological surveys, in situ testing, sampling, visual inspection, laboratory testing of samples of the subsurface materials and [REF:term:grndwtr:groundwater] observations and measurements.

t.definition: means a single room or series of rooms of complementary use, operated under a single tenancy, and includes [REF:term:dwllng-n:dwelling units] , individual guest rooms in motels, hotels, boarding houses, rooming houses and dormitories as well as individual stores and individual or complementary rooms for [REF:term:bn-nd-pr:business and personal services occupancies] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div20:short] .)

ppl-dct.definition: means a duct for conveying air from a heating, ventilating or air-conditioning [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] to a space to be heated, ventilated or air-conditioned.

tpr-thr.definition: means a tread with non-parallel edges that increases or decreases its [REF:term:run:run] uniformly over its width.

thtr.definition: means a place of public assembly intended for the production and viewing of the performing arts or the screening and viewing of motion pictures, and consisting of an auditorium with permanently fixed seats intended solely for a viewing audience.

trtm.definition: means the provision of medical or other health-related intervention to persons, where the administration or lack of administration of these interventions may render them incapable of evacuating to a safe location without the assistance of another person. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div21:short] .)

trtm-cc.definition: (Group B, Division 2) means the [REF:term:ccpnc:occupancy] or use of a [REF:term:bldng:building] or part thereof for the provision of [REF:term:trtm:treatment] , and where overnight accommodation is available to facilitate the [REF:term:trtm:treatment] . (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div22:short] .)

nt-htr.definition: means a suspended [REF:term:pc-htr:space heater] with an integral air-circulating fan.

nprtctd-.definition: (as applying to [REF:term:xpng-bld:exposing building face] ) means a doorway, window or opening other than one equipped with a [REF:term:clr:closure] having the required [REF:term:fr-prtct:fire-protection rating] , or any part of a wall forming part of the [REF:term:xpng-bld:exposing building face] that has a [REF:term:fr-rtnc-:fire-resistance rating] less than that required for the [REF:term:xpng-bld:exposing building face] .

nf-cndtn.definition: means any condition that could cause undue hazard to the life, limb or health of any person authorized or expected to be on or about the premises.

nstbl-lqd.definition: means a liquid, including [REF:term:flmmbl-l:flammable liquids] and [REF:term:cmbtbl-l:combustible liquids] , that is chemically reactive to the extent that it will vigorously react or decompose at or near normal temperature and pressure conditions or that is chemically unstable when subjected to impact.

vpr-brrr.definition: means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour. (See [REF:internal:nbc.divA.part1.appendix.appnote7.div23:short] .)

vnt-cnnc.definition: (as applying to heating or cooling systems) means the part of a venting system that conducts the [REF:term:fl:flue] gases or vent gases from the [REF:term:fl-cllr:flue collar ] of a gas [REF:term:pplnc:appliance] to the [REF:term:chmn:chimney] or [REF:term:g-vnt:gas vent] , and may include a draft control device.

vrtcl-rv.definition: means a shaft oriented essentially vertically that is provided in a [REF:term:bldng:building] to facilitate the installation of [REF:term:bldng:building] services including mechanical, electrical and plumbing installations and facilities such as elevators, refuse chutes and linen chutes.

wlkw.definition: means a covered or roofed pedestrian thoroughfare used to connect 2 or more [REF:term:bldng:buildings] .
